meta.title: The one list
meta.authority: This file is the ONLY record of what is done. Prose docs explain the work; they do not track it.
meta.howToRead:
pnpm backlog          — the working view (open + blocked)
pnpm backlog --lane owner — one lane
pnpm check:backlog    — prove every row against the tree (runs in CI)
rules: A row's status is proven by its verify probe, not by memory. If they disagree, CI fails.
A probe must measure the CONSEQUENCE in the tree, never restate the row's own title. A probe that passes by existing is the shape-not-truth failure this repo names in four ADRs.
Manual rows never fail the build (ADR-970). They carry evidence + a checked date and go stale loudly.
Parked rows are not probed: 'you could do this now' is true of everything parked and therefore says nothing.
Never delete a probe to make CI pass. That is precisely how the previous five master lists drifted.

lanes.owner: Config or a decision. No code unblocks it.
lanes.program: A named multi-phase program. meta.slate sequences it; a program still on hold carries status "parked".
lanes.deferred: Specced and deliberately parked. Since the 2026-08-20 ruling this is only the named holds — white label, mobile, texting — and a parked row also carries status "parked", which is what the working view reads.
lanes.hygiene: Debt in the record or the instruments.

slate.ruled:
Owner ruling 2026-08-20 evening: "Take all tasks out of deferred or parked programs and add them to the priority list. I want all those things built out. The things that we are deferring are white labeling, mobile application, texting." Supersedes the same-day "hold white label and app at the end" slate: the App Platform now builds; only the three named holds park.

── OWNER RULING 2026-08-24: "I want to save the etsy grade store for last. Second to last is the white label tenant sites with full WYSIWYG editor. I want everything else fully functional and clean before those." So DEF-ETSY moves out of W8 into its own final wave W10, and white label (PROG-E10 Sites, PROG-W6 member sites + theme marketplace, PROG-P7 per-Space theming depth) is UNPARKED into W9 immediately before it. deferredByName drops to mobile and texting only.

INTERPRETATION, stated so it can be corrected in one line: the CORE editor phases E0-E9 stay in W4 and were NOT moved to the end. "White label tenant sites with full WYSIWYG editor" is read as the tenant-sites DELIVERABLE — PROG-E10 is literally titled 'Sites, absorbs White Label W1-W5' — not as the editor platform underneath it. E10 depends on E0-E9; W1's content retirements block E3; E2 projects onto the Loom built in W3. Moving E0-E9 to the end would invert those documented dependencies and would leave 'everything else' with no editor to be built on. If the intent was to move the whole editor program back, only the W4 block moves.
slate.note: The development order for the whole open queue, waves in sequence, ids in order within a wave. Array order IS the sequence — W0 first through W10 last, with `owner-timed` kept at the end because it is scheduled by the owner rather than by this order. Owner-lane rows are decisions, not sequenced dev. Status lives only in each row's probe; this object is the sequence.

waves.name: W1 · content pipeline (5c/5d must land before Editor E3)
W3 · Loom foundation (the media layer the editor projects from)
W4 · the Editor, E0-E9 in order (decision gate first: EDITOR-ARCHITECTURE’s two open sequencing questions)
W8 · commerce + verticals (Resonance launch stays GO-gated)
W9 · white-label tenant sites + the full WYSIWYG editor (SECOND TO LAST, owner ruling 2026-08-24)
W10 · LAST — the Etsy-grade store (owner ruling 2026-08-24)

slate.rationale: Foundation before surface: hardening and module boundaries (A1/A3) pay compounding dividends across every later wave. Loom D1-D3 precede the Editor because E2 projects the editor’s asset model onto the Loom. Content retirements (W1) must precede E3, which replaces EDITABLE_PAGES in the opposite direction. Re-theme and the DAWN mechanical sweeps follow the editor so swept surfaces are not rebuilt. Flagship apps (A4) and the domain backlog ride after boundaries + editor exist. Commerce verticals close, with Resonance’s launch GO still the owner’s. White label (E10/W6/P7), mobile, and texting park by name. White-label sites and the Etsy-grade store now close the runway, in that order (owner ruling 2026-08-24): everything else is to be functional and clean before either starts.

entries.title: Seed the beta test account + PW_STORAGE_STATE secret

THE ROW'S CLAIM IS THEREFORE NO LONGER TRUE, and it is worth saying plainly because it was reported to the owner as a headline: 'the signed-in product is unmeasured, not clean'. The signed-in product is measured. NOT FULLY RESOLVED, and deliberately not claimed: the row's '44 of 84 a11y tests' figure is a different number from the visual suite's, and the smoke/a11y/overflow stage still reports 64 skipped and 'App shell covered: 4/4 surfaces, 24/40 checks'. entries.title: Create the Vercel Protection Bypass secret (VERCEL_AUTOMATION_BYPASS_SECRET)
entries.detail: CLOSED 2026-08-18 by re-measuring. Same stale premise as OWN-002 ('Not re-checked. Owner-only (Vercel + Actions secrets)'), settled the same way: e2e.yml's preflight job exists precisely so that an ABSENT bypass secret makes pr-compare report 'skipped' rather than a vacuous green - its header says 'when this one says skipped, nothing was tested, and that is the only place in this repo where the word carries that meaning'. On PR #2158 preflight succeeded and pr-compare RAN for fourteen minutes against the preview URL, and the step env prints VERCEL_AUTOMATION_BYPASS_SECRET: *** - GitHub masks a secret that is set and prints nothing for one that is not. The row's consequence ('every e2e verdict is valid against production only') no longer holds: 80 visual checks and the smoke/a11y/overflow suite all ran against the PR's own preview deployment.

entries.title: check:adoption stays advisory (owner decision), and the other two checks were already required

source.ref: §5 the constraint that governs the plan

entries.detail: CLOSED 2026-08-18 by an owner decision, after the row rescoped from three clicks to one question. 🔴 CORRECTED 2026-08-18, SAME DAY, BY OBSERVATION. This row was closed claiming TWO of the three were already done. Only ONE was. check:contrast genuinely blocks - it sits in ci.yml's guards array inside the checks job, so requiring it separately would be a second name for the same gate. THE pr-compare CLAIM WAS FALSE, and it was taken from prose: .github/workflows/pr-compare-fallback.yml asserts in its first line that pr-compare is a REQUIRED status context, citing ruleset 17640795. PR #2161 disproved it by merging. Auto-merge fired at 21:45:31 while the pr-compare check run was still in_progress (it completed success at 21:52:50), and the merged SHA carried exactly one commit status, Vercel's - so no substitute pr-compare status stood in for it. A context that is required cannot be pending at merge. See LIVE-049. The irony is the point: this row was closed by citing a sentence in a file, hours after ADR-1082 made 're-test the premise, do not trust the prose' a rule in AGENTS.md. THE THIRD WAS A DECISION, NOT A TASK, and the owner made it: check:adoption STAYS ADVISORY. ci.yml's own twenty-line rationale carried the argument (ADR-970): it is a SCOREBOARD of design-debt COUNTS, a count ratchet fires on legitimate growth - 'bespoke-cards: 0 means adding any new *-card.tsx fails a PR that has nothing to do with the design system' - and an advisory finding forced through a blocking gate teaches everyone to route around the gate. THE COST OF THAT CHOICE IS KNOWN AND ACCEPTED, and is written here so the next reader does not have to rediscover it: literal-radius read '🔴 rose' from 2026-08-13 to 2026-08-18 and nobody looked, even though the advisory step already writes the scoreboard into every run's summary. The gate is visible and was still unread; that is an argument about ATTENTION, not about blocking, and the remedy if it recurs is a louder surface (a PR comment rather than a run summary), not a reversal of this decision. Re-open only with new evidence, not with the same argument.

verify.evidence: pr-compare: ruleset 17640795 was READ by the owner on 2026-08-18 and the required set is checks + analyze + lint + test + Vercel. pr-compare is not required; the earlier evidence on this row cited .github/workflows/pr-compare-fallback.yml line 1 instead of the ruleset, and that sentence was wrong. See LIVE-049. check:contrast: ci.yml guards array, line 262. check:adoption: ci.yml 'Advisory trackers (reported, never blocking)', continue-on-error: true - the owner confirmed on 2026-08-18 that this stays as it is.

entries.title: Upgrade Healthchecks.io so all 27 crons are monitored
entries.detail:
Free tier caps at 20 checks; vercel.json declares 27 crons. The first 20 to ping win the slots, so WHICH 7 go unmonitored is decided by schedule order rather than importance. Also set each check's period from the real schedule: auto-created checks arrive at 1 day, so process-queue (every 2 min) could be dead most of a day before anyone is paged.

── RE-MEASURED 2026-08-19 in a premise sweep (ADR-1082), and it HOLDS. vercel.json declares 27 crons against the Healthchecks.io free tier's 20-check cap, so 7 go unmonitored and which 7 is decided by schedule order. Whether the account was upgraded is NOT readable here, and the reason is structural rather than an oversight: lib/observability/cron-heartbeat.ts:41-51 makes the ping a safe no-op when CRON_HEARTBEAT_BASE_URL is unset, so an unconfigured base and a full-but-capped account look identical from inside the repo. scripts/cron-freshness.mjs:492 says so itself. Settled by the Healthchecks.io project page showing plan and check count. ── ⏸️ PARKED 2026-08-25 on the owner's instruction, and the instruction included 'stop asking'. This is blocked on a paid Healthchecks.io tier (27 crons against a 20-check free tier) — an account action with real-world latency, not a decision waiting on information. It stays OPEN as work and stops being surfaced in progress reports, which is the honest shape: the row is not done, nobody here can advance it, and re-listing it every session was noise rather than tracking. ⚪ Un-park it by acting on it, not by re-asking. ── ⚠️ RE-STATUSED 2026-08-25 BY OWNER RULING: the only parked items are the mobile app (DEF-MOBILE), the full Etsy-grade marketplace build (DEF-ETSY) and white-labeled sites (PROG-W6). Everything else belongs on the active production list. Un-parked: cron monitoring is production hygiene, not a nice-to-have — 27 crons run and only some are watched. ── ⏸️ DEFERRED ~2 WEEKS BY OWNER, 2026-08-25, WITH A REASON THAT IS NOT A JUDGEMENT ABOUT PRIORITY: the Healthchecks.io annual plan was just paid and they do not prorate, so upgrading now buys the same capacity twice. The row stays OPEN and stays on the active list — the gap is real, 27 crons against 20 slots — but it is not actionable until the billing cycle allows it. Revisit ~2026-09-08. ⚠️ DO NOT re-surface this as a pending owner task before then; it is scheduled, not forgotten. ⚠️ AND DO NOT read the deferral as 'monitoring is fine': which 7 crons go unwatched is still decided by schedule order rather than importance, so if a cron fails in the meantime the fleet may not page. If that risk needs covering before the cycle turns, the free lever is to CUT the cron count to 20 (this row's own probe measures exactly that) or to point the 7 highest-consequence crons at the slots deliberately rather than letting ping order decide.

verify.cmd: node -e "const v=require('./vercel.json'); if ((v.crons||[]).length<=20) process.exit(0); process.exit(1)"
verify.note: Passes when the cron count drops to what the free tier covers. If the account is upgraded instead, close this row manually and record the plan in evidence.

entries.title: Sweep every `revoke ... from public` block in supabase/migrations
entries.detail: Supabase's ALTER DEFAULT PRIVILEGES grants anon/authenticated on new objects as EXPLICIT per-role grants, which REVOKE ... FROM public does not touch. Audit with has_function_privilege against prod, never by reading the SQL — the SQL reads correct.

entries.title: White on amber stays, but the letterpress does not: the primary label ships flat (reversed)
entries.detail:
OWNER DECISION 2026-08-19, verbatim: "Figure out how to change the rules or clean this up so I can have white on amber. The ideal would be chisel/embossed white with a little dark edge. Giving the effect that it's sunken into the button." That RESOLVES the two-option question this row used to carry (darken the label vs darken the fill): the answer is NEITHER. The white label and the brand amber both stay, and the label renders as a LETTERPRESS. Implemented in .text-emboss (app/globals.css): a crisp 1px ring of --brand-emboss-dark on all four sides of each glyph, the two upper diagonals doubled (sunken = darkest along the top wall), a 1.5px-blur occlusion into the cavity top, and a 1.5px --brand-emboss-light catch-light below as the lit lower lip. Applied through the variant seams only: components/ui/button.tsx (primary now carries text-emboss beside chisel) and components/marketing/marketing-ui.tsx (primary already carried it). MEASURED 2026-08-19 (axe-core 4.13.0, real headless chromium; jsdom cannot evaluate color-contrast, see test/a11y/axe.ts): axe credits a same-colour ZERO-BLUR text-shadow group covering all four glyph edges (each offset > 0.5px) as a text STROKE and measures the label against ring-over-fill instead of the bare amber. White on all four brand ambers moved from VIOLATION (2.52 / 1.87 / 2.86 / 1.94:1) to PASS (15.2-19.8:1 as axe reports the composited ground), at both button type sizes. A blurred shadow alone can never do this (axe discounts its alpha by 0.185/(blur/em+0.4) and it covers at most one edge), which is why the OLD two-shadow emboss was measured, failed, and waived. WHAT THE PROBE WAITS ON: a real CI @a11y capture confirming the flip on live surfaces, which re-freezes a11y-baselines.json (the eight midnight-dark contexts should drop) and retires the six now-unmatched fgOnShadowColor waiver entries in test/e2e/a11y-waivers.ts. The FILL waivers stay: pills/badges/toggles still paint white on amber without the letterpress, and the token pair itself is unchanged (2.52:1 etc., frozen in scripts/check-contrast.mjs - the letterpress changes what axe measures on buttons, not what the palette declares). Visual baselines need a recapture: every primary button renders differently.

── CLOSED 2026-08-20: the CI capture ran (e2e-manual on PR #2196, against the emboss preview). The a11y re-freeze wrote the wins down: /discover midnight-dark 2 → 0 and /pricing midnight-dark 1 → 0, zero serious+ violations in every captured context. The six fgOnShadowColor waiver entries for the old two-shadow emboss retired in the same change (axe no longer reports those composites; the guard inverted to assert NO shadow-keyed entries remain). Visual recapture committed. The FILL waivers stay: pills, badges and toggles still paint white on amber without the letterpress.

── 🔴 REVERSED BY THE OWNER 2026-08-21 (ADR-1096), and the row is rewritten rather than closed, because what it records DID ship and then came back out. The owner, looking at a Circle header: "the Post button looks like shit while the Create button looks good" — same amber, same row, and the only difference was this letterpress plus `chisel` on one of them.

WHAT THE ORIGINAL ASK GOT ENTANGLED WITH. The request itself was aesthetic and was honoured as asked. The problem is what grew around it: the emboss ended up carrying a CONTRAST argument it was never entitled to. Its CSS comment reasoned that a four-edge zero-blur ring is credited by axe as a text stroke, moving white-on-amber from 1.87-2.86:1 to 15.2-19.8:1 as MEASURED — while the label is still white on #E2912F to a reader. Two places in the tree had already written the warning down ("a FINISH ... must never be cited as mitigation"), which is the tell: a mitigation that needs a note telling people not to cite it as mitigation is not one.

WHAT IS AND IS NOT REVERSED. White-on-amber STAYS — that half of this row's title is still the live decision (ADR-1031), knowingly shipped and disclosed, with the fill waivers untouched at 1.88-2.86:1. Only the letterpress and the `chisel` bevel are gone; filled controls carry `lift-1` instead, which is what the hand-rolled primaries beside them were already doing and why those looked cleaner.

THE PROBE IS INVERTED, NOT DELETED. It measured that the ring existed; it now measures that it is gone from the CSS and from the button primitive, so re-adding the letterpress fails this row and has to argue with ADR-1096 first.

entries.title: Delete the four dead branches
entries.detail: feat/studio-kernel, claude/studio-reland, fix/codeql-allowlist, fix/codeql-seeder-write-allowlist. All four verified BY CONTENT (a squash merge leaves no ancestry, so --is-ancestor proves nothing) to hold nothing main lacks. DO NOT resurrect feat/studio-kernel — it still carries app/opengraph-image.tsx, the root metadata image that caused the ENOSPC outage. ── RE-MEASURED 2026-08-24, AND THE ROW'S OWN EVIDENCE COULD NOT BE REPRODUCED FROM HERE. All four heads still exist, and the remote grew 930 -> 940 heads in five days, so branch debt is accumulating faster than it is cleared. SHAs recorded so deletion is reversible with one command each (git push origin <sha>:refs/heads/<name>): feat/studio-kernel 78b9ba52b2801b9da9e4528ab179c88f9799153e, claude/studio-reland b29cddc56bf2c9bb5684e56684d1efbc87657d21, fix/codeql-allowlist c55e8b41f4eb3f49f9f5152937db47c18ad50f6a, fix/codeql-seeder-write-allowlist a2bc8096c77f5ec28ef4f28b1d487d205b9aa315. WHY IT WAS NOT DONE HERE: the row says all four were 'verified BY CONTENT to hold nothing main lacks', but does not say by what method, and a diff against main does not reproduce it — each branch is ~1,400 files and ~22k insertions / ~90k deletions apart from today's main. That is the EXPECTED shape for an old branch main has run away from, and it is also the shape of a branch holding real unmerged work; a plain diff cannot tell those apart, and an agent deleting a shared branch on the strength of a number it cannot interpret is the wrong trade. The 2026-08-11 warning stands and is the reason to be careful rather than fast: feat/studio-kernel still carries app/opengraph-image.tsx, the root metadata image that caused the ENOSPC outage. NOT BLOCKING ANYTHING — nothing in the queue waits on this. ALSO: a local-only savepoint commit 263b7354 was reported on feat/studio-kernel; it is NOT on the remote (git cat-file cannot find it in a fresh clone), so there is nothing to delete server-side. It exists only in that working copy and goes away with it. ── ✅ CONTENT VERIFICATION REPRODUCED 2026-08-24, AND THE OWNER APPROVED DELETION. The row was stuck because its 'verified BY CONTENT' claim recorded no METHOD. Here is one that works, and the two that do not. ❌ `--is-ancestor` fails: a squash merge leaves no ancestry. ❌ `git cherry origin/main <branch>` ALSO fails, and this is the non-obvious one: squash merging rewrites patch-ids, so it reports ALL 2,947 commits as unique (+) on EVERY one of the four, with zero marked already-in-main. A plain diff fails for the same reason (~1,400 files apart). ✅ WHAT WORKS is merged-PR evidence plus per-commit content checking: (1) feat/studio-kernel -> PR #2098, confirmed merged:true, merged_by hellofrequencylab, 2026-08-12T03:40Z. Its head sits ONE commit past the merged sha (78b9ba52b, 'a Spark draft follows the author', ADR-1001) — and ADR-1001 is on main, as is its migration 20270224000000_studio_draft, applied. (2) claude/studio-reland -> PR #2105, merged 2026-08-12T14:57Z. (3) fix/codeql-allowlist -> PR #2099, merged 2026-08-12T04:01Z. (4) fix/codeql-seeder-write-allowlist HAS NO PR AT ALL — checked file by file instead: 4 of its 6 files are byte-identical on main, and the 2 that differ differ because main went FURTHER; main's lib/events/seed/draft.ts carries the writable allowlist and the __proto__/constructor/prototype guard in a fuller form than the branch (13 matching lines, with canonicalSeededPath). The security fix is not lost. 🔴 BUT THE DELETION COULD NOT BE EXECUTED FROM HERE, AND THIS IS A NEWLY MEASURED BLOCKER, NOT THE OLD ONE: `git push origin --delete <branch>` returns HTTP 403 for all four — this session's credentials permit pushing a branch but not deleting one — and the GitHub MCP surface has create_branch with no delete counterpart. So the row stays an OWNER action for a reason that is now measured rather than assumed. THE OWNER RULED DELETE (2026-08-24); the four commands are: git push origin --delete feat/studio-kernel · claude/studio-reland · fix/codeql-allowlist · fix/codeql-seeder-write-allowlist. Reversal remains one command each against the SHAs recorded above. ⚠️ The standing warning still holds: DO NOT casually resurrect feat/studio-kernel — it carries app/opengraph-image.tsx, the root metadata image behind the ENOSPC outage. ── ✅ CLOSED 2026-08-24: all four deleted by the owner, verified from here with `git ls-remote --heads origin <name>` returning empty for each. Remote head count 944 -> 940. WORTH RECORDING FOR NEXT TIME, because two of the three routes FAILED: `git push origin --delete` from this agent container returns HTTP 403 (push permitted, delete not), and the GitHub web UI's branch-delete button returned 'Branch could not be deleted' for a signed-out browser session. What worked was the REST API via gh, which needs no local clone and no repo cwd: `gh api -X DELETE repos/<owner>/<repo>/git/refs/heads/<branch>`. Reversal is still one command per branch against the SHAs recorded above.

verify.evidence: All four deleted 2026-08-24 by the owner via `gh api -X DELETE .../git/refs/heads/<branch>`, and verified from here: git ls-remote --heads returns empty for each, remote head count 944 -> 940. Content safety was established BEFORE deletion and the method is recorded in the detail, because both --is-ancestor and git cherry fail on this repo's squash merges.

entries.title: Config and env: the remaining unset keys (three of the six were already set)
entries.detail:
🔴 RE-MEASURED 2026-08-19 AND THE ROW WAS WRONG ABOUT HALF ITS OWN CONTENTS. Three of the six items were already satisfied, and the row had been telling the owner to go and do them. The previous evidence line said the rest are "Vercel/Resend dashboard state, not readable here", which is the exact shape ADR-1082 names: a blocker phrased as "cannot be checked" is a claim with an expiry date. The SECRET is unreadable from an agent container. Its CONSEQUENCE is sitting in the database.

ALREADY DONE, do not spend anything on these:
  • Supabase -> Pro. The organization (hkveprznovcteywuczcv) returns plan "pro". Capacity and     backups are on the paid tier already.
  • RESEND_WEBHOOK_SECRET. Email metrics are NOT dark. public.email_events over the trailing 30     days holds opened=127, delivered=81 and clicked=3. Those three event types cannot be produced     by our own send path -- nothing server-side knows an email was opened -- so they can only have     arrived through the Resend webhook, which means the secret is set AND the signature check is     passing. Most recent delivered event 2026-08-19T13:04:20Z, i.e. the same day this was measured.
  • VAPID, the PUBLIC half. public.push_subscriptions holds 23 rows, 8 of them created in the last     30 days, most recent 2026-08-10. A browser cannot complete pushManager.subscribe() without     NEXT_PUBLIC_VAPID_PUBLIC_KEY being served to it, so that key is live and members have been     granting permission for two months.

STILL GENUINELY OPEN:
  • VAPID_PRIVATE_KEY, the SEND half. Subscriptions prove the public key, not the private one.     lib/push.ts:22 warns '[push] VAPID keys not set - push sending disabled.' and returns false     when either key is missing, so the cheap settling move is a runtime-log search for that exact     string rather than another dashboard trip. Note the queue is quiet (1 notification_queue row in     24h), so absence of the warning in a short retention window is not proof either way -- it needs     a window that contains an actual push attempt.
  • Verify frequencylocal.com in Resend, plus SPF/DKIM/DMARC subdomain isolation. Blocking for     volume. The delivered events above prove sending works TODAY at current volume; they say     nothing about domain reputation at scale, which is what this item is for.
  • Secret-scanning push protection.
  • Dismiss the 3 CodeQL false positives.

CRON_SECRET and ANTHROPIC_API_KEY remain satisfied by consequence: ai_usage holds 50 rows in the trailing 7 days, and the crons are firing.

── RE-EVIDENCED 2026-08-19 from the owner's Advanced Security screenshot: CodeQL advanced setup ACTIVE (scan 36 min prior), Copilot Autofix ON, check-run thresholds set (High+/errors-only). Still DISABLED, each one Enable click on that page: Secret Protection (the push-protection ask), Private vulnerability reporting, Dependency graph, Dependabot alerts + security updates. "Security and quality" badge shows 44 open findings to triage once alerts API access or an owner paste arrives. ── ⚙️ THE VAPID ITEM IS NOW CHECKABLE BY ONE CURL, 2026-08-24. The row said the cheap settling move was a runtime-log search for '[push] VAPID keys not set'. That was tried and the Vercel log query timed out twice, which is a bad place for a fact to live anyway: a console.warn in a log is exactly the invisible fail-safe AGENTS.md warns about. So the consequence was PUBLISHED instead, the same move LIVE-053 made for the Sentry DSN — /api/status now reports monitoring.push, booleanized in lib/push.ts (pushSendingEnabled = PUBLIC && PRIVATE), never the key. WHY BOTH HALVES MATTER, and it is the trap this row already half fell into: push_subscriptions proves only that a browser could SUBSCRIBE, i.e. that the PUBLIC key is served. It says NOTHING about the private key the server signs with. Production carries 24 subscriptions, 5 from the last 30 days (newest 2026-08-20) and five live callers of sendPushToProfile (admin actions, outreach, nearby, the event-reminders cron, the journey-prompt cron) — so two dozen members have granted permission and whether a single notification can leave the process was unanswerable from here. Pinned by two tests and mutation-proven: reading the env directly in the route fails both the new assertion and the existing four-var env allowlist. THE OWNER CHECK IS NOW: curl -s https://frequencylocal.com/api/status | grep -o '"push":[a-z]*' — false means set VAPID_PRIVATE_KEY in Vercel production env and redeploy (the value freezes at build); true closes this item.

verify.evidence: Owner screenshot 2026-08-19 for the settled items. 2026-08-24: the remaining VAPID item became repo-checkable — /api/status publishes monitoring.push, booleanized in lib/push.ts, pinned by two tests and mutation-proven. Closes on that field reading true on a production deploy. The three already-satisfied items (Supabase Pro, RESEND_WEBHOOK_SECRET, VAPID public half) stay struck; do not re-spend on them.

entries.title: Lift 8b: a loading prop on IconButton, matching Button's
entries.detail: Icon-only controls are exactly the ones where a tap leaves no other evidence it landed.

verify.cmd: node -e "const fs=require('fs');const S='components/ui/icon-button.tsx',T='components/ui/icon-button.test.tsx';if(!fs.existsSync(S)||!fs.existsSync(T))process.exit(79);const src=fs.readFileSync(S,'utf8'),test=fs.readFileSync(T,'utf8');const cut=src.indexOf('export function IconLink');if(cut<0)process.exit(79);const B=src.slice(0,cut),L=src.slice(cut);function a(s,k){let i=0;while((i=s.indexOf(k+'={',i))>=0){const aria=s.slice(Math.max(0,i-5),i).endsWith('aria-');const e=s.indexOf('}',i);if(e>0&&s.slice(i,e).includes('loading')&&(k.indexOf('aria-')===0||!aria))return true;i+=k.length}return false}const bad=[];if(!a(B,'disabled'))bad.push('IconButton does not disable while loading; a second tap re-fires the action');if(!a(B,'aria-busy'))bad.push('IconButton does not set aria-busy while loading');if(!a(L,'aria-disabled'))bad.push('IconLink does not set aria-disabled while loading');if(!a(L,'aria-busy'))bad.push('IconLink does not set aria-busy while loading');if(!test.includes('does not fire the handler again'))bad.push('the double-fire assertion is gone from '+T);if(bad.length){console.error(bad.join('; '));process.exit(1)}process.exit(0)"

entries.notes: Closed 2026-08-17. The probe that flagged this row as stale was `grep-present /loading/` in the component, which passes because the WORD appears anywhere in the file, including in a comment describing the prop it is supposed to be proving. Replaced with the consequence: IconButton must disable while loading (so a second tap cannot re-fire the action) and set aria-busy; IconLink must use the aria pair INSTEAD of the real `disabled`, because a real disabled drops it out of the tab order mid-navigation; and the double-fire assertion must still exist in the test file. ONE TRAP WORTH RECORDING: both controls live in one file and the string 'aria-disabled=' CONTAINS 'disabled=', so an unscoped regex let each component satisfy the other's check. Two of four deliberate breaks passed before that was caught, which is exactly why a probe is not trusted until it has been seen to fail. It now splits the file at IconLink and judges each half alone; all four breaks fire. A SECOND trap cost another round: the first scoped version used a regex, and this string travels JSON -> shell -> `node -e`, where a lone backslash does not survive intact - "\\b" arrived as a literal BACKSPACE, so every check silently matched nothing and the row read as regressed. The probe is now backslash-free, scanning with indexOf instead of RegExp, and was re-proved through the guard's own shell rather than only standalone.

entries.title: Lift 8b: an in-flight cue on DirectorySearch
entries.detail: It fetches. Until it says so, an empty result and a pending one look identical.

verify.cmd: node -e "const fs=require('fs');const S='components/ui/directory-search.tsx',T='components/ui/directory-search.test.tsx';if(!fs.existsSync(S)||!fs.existsSync(T))process.exit(79);const s=fs.readFileSync(S,'utf8'),t=fs.readFileSync(T,'utf8');const code=s.split(String.fromCharCode(10)).filter(x=>x.trim().indexOf('//')!==0&&x.trim().indexOf('*')!==0).join(String.fromCharCode(10));const bad=[];if(code.indexOf('useTransition()')<0)bad.push('DirectorySearch does not CALL useTransition(), so it cannot know a search is in flight');const i=code.indexOf('aria-busy={');const seg=i<0?'':code.slice(i,code.indexOf('}',i));if(i<0||seg.indexOf('isPending')<0)bad.push('aria-busy is not driven by isPending');if(code.indexOf('Searching')<0)bad.push('the live-region text is gone; a spinning glyph announces nothing to a screen reader');if((t.split('expect(').length-1)<3)bad.push('fewer than 3 assertions in '+T);if(bad.length){console.error(bad.join('; '));process.exit(1)}process.exit(0)"

entries.notes: Closed 2026-08-17. Was manual pending the implementation. The probe requires useTransition to be CALLED, not merely imported: the first version matched the token and passed while the component tracked nothing, because the import line alone satisfied it. The definition of 'state test' is INTERACTION-STATES.md's, not invented: names 3+ of the nine states in test titles, titles only — exercising a state in a className assertion is not naming it. 36 is not 36 units of neglect: a Display badge owes only `rest`, so the gate over-reports by design and can never certify an untested primitive as covered. HALF THE COMMITTED ORDER HAS ALREADY SHIPPED, and this row was last checked one day before two of the three landed. scripts/render-path-bodies.txt (last touched c3228d7) records `about` 0 (2026-08-17), `spaces` 0 (2026-08-18) and `the-lab` 0 (2026-08-18); `circles` was already template-only. Remaining: home 5, the-community 5, the-quest 2, pricing 7. NEXT SLUG IS the-quest.

🔴 A TRAP FOR WHOEVER TAKES THE NEXT TWO, and it is exactly the defect LIVE-040 records. app/(marketing)/the-quest/page.tsx and the-community/page.tsx still emit faqSchema() from their ROUTE BODIES, while their templates also carry Accordions. That is fine today. The moment those bodies are retired the FAQPage goes with them, which is precisely how /the-lab ended up emitting no FAQPage for weeks. Move the FAQ into an Accordion in the SAME PR that retires each body, or this row manufactures LIVE-040 twice more. ── 🔴 PREMISE RE-TESTED 2026-08-24 (ADR-1082) AND THE NEXT SLUG HAD ALREADY SHIPPED. This row said "NEXT SLUG IS the-quest". scripts/render-path-bodies.txt records `the-quest` at 0, RETIRED 2026-08-19 — five days before this row was read, and the row was last checked 2026-08-17. Remaining coded bodies are now: home 5, the-community 5, pricing 7 (partial, and its figures must never be frozen into a document). NEXT SLUG IS the-community. The FAQ trap this row records is now down to ONE page rather than two, and it is the-community's: its route body still emits faqSchema() while its template also carries an Accordion, so the FAQPage must move into the Accordion in the SAME PR that retires the body. the-quest's retirement handled this correctly and said so on its own line, which is the shape to copy. ── ⏳ the-community RETIRED 2026-08-24. Ledger 5 -> 0; route 639 -> 126 lines; app/(marketing)/the-community/tour.tsx (a 389-line ProductTour client island whose ONLY caller was the retired body) deleted with it. check:render-path now reads 14 of 16 gated slugs template-only, 2 still carrying a coded body (12 components, 3,326 lines). 🔴 THE FAQ TRAP THIS ROW RECORDS WAS ALREADY GONE, AND THE ROW WAS WRONG ABOUT IT: it says the route body still emits faqSchema() beside a template Accordion. It did not — LIVE-040 had already deleted that call and moved the Q&A into the template's tc-faq Accordion. The only schema call deleted here was the legacy branch's articleSchema(), on a branch that could never be taken. MEASURED before/after with renderToStaticMarkup: three ld+json scripts and the multiset { BreadcrumbList 1, ListItem 1, Article 1, WebPage 1, Organization 2, ImageObject 1, FAQPage 1, Question 4, Answer 4 } — byte-identical. That is the second time this row's own trap text has outlived the defect it describes, so the remaining slug it names (home) should be re-measured, not believed. FIVE coded details the template did not draw were recovered VERBATIM into existing blocks: the 'No application, no audition.' guardrail (the template carried it only in a code COMMENT, which no visitor reads), the /pricing link, the /discover link (into an empty designed CTA slot), the 'Circulation, not exclusion.' generosity guardrail, and the FOUNDING_PLACE grounding (interpolated from lib/site.ts, never typed, so it cannot drift). docs/FINALIZE-PLAN.md was corrected in the same pass because deleting tour.tsx falsified its arbitrary-type count. ⚠️ ONE THING WAS DELIBERATELY NOT RECOVERED and is filed as LIVE-100 instead: the coded body's closing PillarNav triptych. NEXT SLUG IS home (5 components, 940 lines), and it is LAST in the series because Splash carries the live-proof band and its own chrome. pricing (7) stays out of the series entirely: its fallback is the coded page rather than getTemplate('pricing'), and its take-rate figures must never be frozen into a document. ── ✅ `home` RETIRED 2026-08-24, and the OWN-043 ruling made it a PURE DELETION rather than a recovery. app/page.tsx 938 -> 137 lines. check:render-path now reads 15 template-only, 1 body - the last is `pricing`, which stays out of the series by design because its take-rate figures must never be frozen into a template. UNREACHABILITY WAS DOUBLE, and verified rather than assumed: the route picks published, then template, then null, and BOTH rungs are well-formed 13-block documents (the live published doc queried from production; getTemplate('home') pinned by templates.test.ts, 17 passing). `data` could never be null, so <Splash> could never render. That is stronger evidence than a snapshot, which is why NO visual baseline recapture was needed - a recapture would have photographed an unchanged page. SCHEMA MEASURED ON BOTH RUNGS, before and after, by the method the-community's retirement used: renderToStaticMarkup over BlockDocJsonLd + BlockRender, every ld+json extracted and diffed. BYTE-IDENTICAL, md5 7203e7bdcd8d096b6e7310866af373aa on both sides, one Article node each. The published fixture was checksummed against the database rather than transcribed. ⚠️ SAID PLAINLY SO IT CANNOT READ AS COVERAGE: faqSchema(HOME_FAQ) was called INSIDE Splash, on the branch that never renders, so `/` has emitted no FAQPage since the template landed and emits none now. This change neither caused nor cured that - the count is 0 on both sides, which is the proof. A FAQPage on `/` needs an Accordion in the PUBLISHED document, an editor change rather than a code one. ORPHANS DELETED: ScrollCue, CountUp, Parallax and Steps had zero remaining references repo-wide including tests, so they went with the body, following the precedent set when the-community took tour.tsx. The route header now records that lib/page-editor/templates/home.ts is UNREACHABLE BY DECISION (OWN-043), with an explicit instruction not to recover copy into it - change the home page in the editor. ── ✅ CLOSED 2026-08-24, AND THE CLOSING QUESTION WAS PRICING RATHER THAN ANOTHER SLUG. This row's OWN committed order named `pricing` last (“about → spaces → the-lab → the-quest → the-community → pricing (partial)”), ADR-1068 wrote the same order down (“circles → about → spaces → the-lab → the-quest → the-community → pricing”), and scripts/render-path-bodies.txt carried it too. So the recent note saying pricing “stays out of the series entirely” was a NARROWING of a committed order that lived only in a note, which is precisely the drift the one list exists to stop. It is now ADR-1116: a decision, with an ADR, and the ledger header plus the pricing row carry it so the next reader does not re-open the question. WHAT WAS MEASURED, not inferred: check:render-path reads 16 gated slugs, 15 template-only, 1 still carrying a coded body (pricing, 7 components, 2,526 route lines). /pricing resolves published → coded — TWO rungs, not three. getTemplate('pricing') is NOT a middle rung even though lib/page-editor/templates/pricing.ts exists and `pricing` is a row in EDITABLE_PAGES. That inversion is ADR-916/918's and it is deliberate: on every other slug the coded body is a RELIC duplicating a static document, here it is the DERIVED page (live prices, the live take-rate vector, the beta-window resolution the checkout itself asks, the operator's live feature-gate overrides, and not one dollar figure or percentage typed in the file) while the Puck template is the snapshot. All seven components were read and ALL SEVEN consume the derived model — Offering (PlanCard / PlanPrice / PlanCta / IndependentStrip), PlanExtra (ExtraCard), the resolved rate string (RateLine), FeatureGrid (ComparisonBlock) — so “partial” had nothing to retire: there is no copy-only block that could move into the template while the figures stayed live. ⚠️ THE LEDGER ROW STAYS GATED EXACT-MATCH. `pricing 7` may fall if the body genuinely shrinks, and a rise is still refused; what ends is the expectation that it reaches 0. ONE THING REOPENS IT (ADR-1116): a block kind that binds a live pricing key the way pricing.ts already binds `livePriceKey` per ADR-918, for EVERY figure the body renders — rates, gates and the comparison grid included. Until a document can carry a BINDING rather than a NUMBER for all of them, moving this page into the editor means quoting figures the product has stopped charging.

entries.title: Lift 5d: the eight seeker articles join EDITABLE_PAGES
entries.detail:
Unblocked — DawnHowToSteps exists and owns its HowTo JSON-LD, with a dedicated test. Needs a shared templates/article.ts seed. Same ordering constraint as LIVE-006 relative to E3.

── RE-MEASURED 2026-08-19 in a premise sweep (ADR-1082). THE STATED BLOCKER NO LONGER EXISTS. This row says it "needs a shared templates/article.ts seed". lib/page-editor/templates/article.ts is 248 lines with articleTemplate(spec), required `answer` and `faq` fields that make the CONTENT-VOICE §10.9 article grammar unexpressible if violated, and a companion article.test.ts that renders a spec through the live block config. It landed 2026-08-17 in 656dac3 (#2143, ADR-1068) and documents the remaining job as a five-step per-article recipe in its own header. It has NO importers, deliberately -- its own ⚠️ STATUS block says "NO live consumer yet".

The row stays OPEN and its probe still fails correctly (all eight slugs are absent from EDITABLE_PAGES). What changes is the shape of the work: it is no longer "build a seed", it is "enroll one article per PR via the recipe in that file's header".

── PROGRESS 2026-08-20: second article enrolled. how-to-build-community joins EDITABLE_PAGES via the recipe (spec in templates/how-to-build-community.ts, route thinned to metadata + <BlockDocJsonLd> + <BlockRender>, ledger row added). articleTemplate gained four optional seams the pillar needed (media-beat kicker, photo-less hero via the minimal variant, per-section howTo so three tracks ship three HowTo nodes, plural beats). Two enrolled, six remain: calm-down-fast, friendship-as-an-adult, how-to-be-more-social, loneliness, tools-for-community-builders, what-is-frequency. The probe still fails correctly on those six.

── PROGRESS 2026-08-20: third article enrolled. loneliness joins EDITABLE_PAGES via the recipe (spec in templates/loneliness.ts, route thinned to metadata + <BlockDocJsonLd> + <BlockRender>, ledger row added). articleTemplate gained one optional seam the umbrella pillar needed: media beats may carry `links`, a Buttons row closing the beat's band, because the coded closing ZigZag held TWO buttons and the MediaText block has one cta slot; without the seam a label and an internal link would silently drop. Three enrolled, five remain: calm-down-fast, friendship-as-an-adult, how-to-be-more-social, tools-for-community-builders, what-is-frequency. The probe still fails correctly on those five.

── PROGRESS 2026-08-20: fourth article enrolled. friendship-as-an-adult joins EDITABLE_PAGES via the recipe (spec in templates/friendship-as-an-adult.ts, route thinned to metadata + <BlockDocJsonLd> + <BlockRender>, ledger row added). articleTemplate gained two optional seams the making-friends hub needed: sections may carry `steps`, plain ordered steps rendered as BuildTimeline with NO HowTo node, because the coded page shows three step lists but asserts only ONE HowTo, and routing the other two through DawnHowToSteps would invent schema claims and the visible name/intro copy that block requires; and the spec may carry `closingBeat`, one beat between the FAQ and the close, where the coded page's final brand Statement sits. Both seams proven backward-compatible: the three prior specs render byte-identically through old vs new generator. Four enrolled, four remain: calm-down-fast, how-to-be-more-social, tools-for-community-builders, what-is-frequency. The probe still fails correctly on those four.

── PROGRESS 2026-08-20: fifth article enrolled. calm-down-fast joins EDITABLE_PAGES via the recipe (spec in templates/calm-down-fast.ts, route thinned to metadata + <BlockDocJsonLd> + <BlockRender>, ledger row added). No new seam needed: the always-wired page is expressible with the existing grammar, its schema-free Steps list rides `steps` (BuildTimeline, no HowTo node, matching the coded page which asserted none) and its two ZigZags ride media beats. Five enrolled, three remain: how-to-be-more-social, tools-for-community-builders, what-is-frequency. The probe still fails correctly on those three.

── PROGRESS 2026-08-20: sixth article enrolled. how-to-be-more-social joins EDITABLE_PAGES via the recipe (spec in templates/how-to-be-more-social.ts, route thinned to metadata + <BlockDocJsonLd> + <BlockRender>, ledger row added). The two absorbed pillars (feel-less-awkward-in-groups, social-life-without-drinking) travel as ordinary sections. articleTemplate gained one optional seam the social-confidence pillar needed: sections may carry `note`, a prose line rendered as a Text block AFTER the section's button row, because the coded page closes its Where-to-start section with a "Keep going" cross-link paragraph BELOW the buttons and folding it into `body` would move it above them. Seam proven backward-compatible: all five prior specs render byte-identically through old vs new generator. The page still asserts exactly ONE HowTo, as coded, from section 2's own `howTo`. Six enrolled, two remain: tools-for-community-builders, what-is-frequency. The probe still fails correctly on those two. ── 🔴 THE PROBE ITSELF HAD NEVER RUN, discovered 2026-08-24 while closing the last two articles. Its `need` array was written with DOUBLE-quoted slugs, and the whole probe is a `node -e "…"` string, so the shell ate those quotes and node threw `SyntaxError: Unexpected token 'for'` on every single invocation. The guard fences a probe that COULD NOT RUN (a signal, a missing binary, exit 79) but a SyntaxError exits 1, which is indistinguishable from an honest "not done" — so for as long as this row was open, its probe AGREED with it by failing to parse. Every "the probe still fails correctly on those N" note above was reporting a parse error, not a measurement. Rewritten with single quotes (verified against a tree where the slugs ARE present: it now exits 0, and against a tree where one is missing: it names the missing slug and exits 1). A static gate now refuses any cmd probe carrying an inner double quote, so this class cannot recur — see the same defect in LIVE-090's probe, caught the same way on 2026-08-23. ── CLOSED 2026-08-24: the last two articles enrolled, and Lift 5d's article set is complete. `tools-for-community-builders` (7th) and `what-is-frequency` (8th) join EDITABLE_PAGES via the recipe - spec beside the route, registered in templates/index.ts, route thinned to metadata + <BlockDocJsonLd> + <BlockRender>, a ROUTES entry and an annotated ledger row each. All eight slugs now resolve through articleTemplate and every article route is template-only (0 coded components); check:render-path reads 16 gated slugs, 13 on the template alone. `tools-for-community-builders` widened NO seam - the first enrolment that needed none, and evidence the grammar has converged: an article written for a different reader (the Latent Leader assembling a stack, CONTENT-VOICE section 2b, not the Seeker) fit the existing fields exactly. It is the second article to assert NO HowTo, using neither `howTo` nor `steps`, so no DawnHowToSteps block is composed and no node is invented. THREE schema nodes, as coded. `what-is-frequency` widened three, all optional and all mapped to blocks already live in another template: `tiers` (the six-rung price ladder to Tiers, which emits no schema, so no Product/Offer node is invented), `cards` (the three sibling-pillar link cards to FeatureGrid, also schema-free) and `afterSteps` (the taxonomy paragraph the coded page printed BELOW the steps, which `body` and `note` both render ABOVE them). Backward compatibility MEASURED rather than asserted: all seven prior specs render BYTE-IDENTICALLY through the pre-change and post-change generator. FOUR schema nodes, as coded, including exactly ONE HowTo. Copy fidelity checked in BOTH directions by script: 46/46 and 96/96 spec strings found verbatim in the coded routes (with the routes' price interpolations resolved from the same modules), and zero coded sentences dropped. Prices are NOT frozen into the documents: the spec imports priceStrings / PRICING_DEFAULTS / formatBps, the same single source the route read. Verified: tsc clean, vitest run 881 files / 11,910 passing, check:render-path / canon / vocab / one-list green.

entries.title: The .dark [data-skin="midnight"] selector never matches on the <html> path
entries.detail: A descendant combinator cannot match an element against itself. app/layout.tsx stamps data-skin on documentElement (the global skin preview path, including marketing); only the shell root is a descendant. So midnight-dark renders a MIXTURE: the generic .dark palette with midnight's light-mode overrides under it. The comment at app/layout.tsx:142-143 asserts the opposite, which is why it survived. One selector, but it repaints every midnight-dark surface, so it wants its own pass with a baseline recapture.

verify.cmd: node -e "const fs=require('fs');const S='lib/theme/skins.ts',C='app/globals.css';if(!fs.existsSync(S)||!fs.existsSync(C))process.exit(79);const src=fs.readFileSync(S,'utf8');const ids=[...new Set([...src.matchAll(/\bid:\s*\x27([a-z0-9-]+)\x27/g)].map(m=>m[1]))];const def=(src.match(/DEFAULT_SKIN[^=]*=\s*\x27([a-z0-9-]+)\x27/)||[])[1];if(!def||ids.length<2)process.exit(79);const css=fs.readFileSync(C,'utf8').replace(/\/\*[\s\S]*?\*\//g,'');const bad=[];for(const id of ids){if(id===def)continue;if(!new RegExp('\\\\.dark\\\\[data-skin=\\\\x22'+id+'\\\\x22\\\\]').test(css))bad.push(id+': no compound .dark[data-skin] selector; the <html> preview path paints the generic .dark palette');if(!new RegExp('\\\\.dark\\\\s+\\\\[data-skin=\\\\x22'+id+'\\\\x22\\\\]').test(css))bad.push(id+': no descendant .dark [data-skin] selector; the authed-shell path loses its dark block');}if(bad.length){console.error(bad.join('\n'));process.exit(1)}process.exit(0)"

entries.notes: Closed 2026-08-17. Non-vacuity proven by the parent, not taken on report: reverting to the descendant-only selector fails skin-dom-selectors.test.ts with 'A descendant combinator cannot match an element against itself'. The second half matters more than the row did — authoring the selector LIST would have silently dropped the block from check-contrast's resolver, which scored the raw prelude and returned null for any comma-separated selector, so the contrast gate would have kept printing green for midnight-dark while measuring nothing there (ADR-970). Fixed in the same pass; selectorWeight now scores each part of a list independently.

entries.title: The app shell statically imports the entire admin module registry
entries.detail: settings-panel.tsx imports MODULE_COMPONENTS from components/admin/modules/module-map — a 'use client' pure registry with 38 static imports and no hooks, handlers or browser APIs. It reaches crypto-browserify/stream-browserify: 406 kB raw / 121 kB gzip on EVERY authed page, verified as a blocking script tag in served HTML. Fix: next/dynamic per module, import module IDS not components, and add import 'server-only' to lib/journey-plans and lib/practices so the class fails the build. NOTE: needs a route-level first-load measurement, which the agent container cannot produce (next build fails page-data collection without service-role creds).
entries.notes: Closed 2026-08-18 (ADR-1074). TWO CORRECTIONS TO THIS ROW'S OWN NUMBERS, both measured. (1) THE HEADLINE WAS STALE. '406 kB raw / 121 kB gzip reaching crypto-browserify on every authed page' was already spent by dc47b89 when the 42 catalog modules moved behind dynamic(); nobody re-measured afterwards. A paired A/B on one tree with only settings-panel.tsx differing puts the registry import itself at 9.3 KB raw / 2.0 KB gzip (955.8 -> 946.5 KB raw over entryJSFiles for app/(main)/layout). Real, and 40x smaller than the row claimed. A number quoted once and never re-derived is how a row keeps promising a win that was already banked. (2) THE crypto-browserify HALF WAS REAL, and it was NOT in module-map. It came through lib/journey-plans and lib/pillars, both of which SAID 'Server-only' in their headers and neither of which was: journey-settings.tsx imported normalizeJourneyMeeting and circle-builder.tsx imported PILLAR_SLUGS - a pure coercion function and an array of four strings - and each dragged createAdminClient, @supabase/supabase-js, lib/practices, lib/zaps, lib/achievements, lib/automations and crypto-browserify into the client graph. Both are extracted to dependency-free modules (lib/journeys/meeting.ts, lib/pillars/slugs.ts), re-exported from their old homes so no server caller changed, and the originals now carry a real `import 'server-only'`. Proved against a real client compile: next build reaches 'Compiled successfully in 3.7min', which a client module still reaching either file could not do. The rail keeps ONE synchronous fact - INLINE_MODULE_IDS, 38 strings with zero imports - because an id with no inline body draws nothing, and that feeds the section count that feeds hasContent. Verified the gate myself: re-adding the static import fails check-shell-weight.test.ts by name, twice.

entries.title: Sentry no longer ships to routes with no DSN configured
entries.detail: The static `import * as Sentry` is gone; the SDK is now reached through a dynamic import gated on process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_SENTRY_DSN — the one env form the browser can resolve, since Next inlines NEXT_PUBLIC_* at build time. The server-only SENTRY_DSN fallback is deliberately NOT consulted here because it is never inlined into the browser bundle and could only read undefined. The hard part was the export contract: Next reads onRouterTransitionStart off this module's namespace and calls it on every client navigation, so it MUST stay defined with Sentry off — it is now a stable wrapper delegating to an async-loaded hook, with a .catch that leaves it a no-op if the chunk fails, because monitoring must never take down the app it monitors. Stated cost: a navigation in the first few ms of a configured session may go untraced. VERIFIED BEYOND THE ONE FILE (the searchSiteIcons lesson): every importer of lib/observability/sentry was enumerated — only sentry.server.config.ts and sentry.edge.config.ts import it statically, both server/edge runtimes, and lib/maps/diagnostics.ts deliberately reads the value without importing. No client component pulls it, so the SDK cannot re-enter the baseline chunk by a side door.
entries.notes: Artifact-verified 2026-08-17, not inferred: built with no DSN and read the emitted chunks. The 236,682-byte Sentry SDK chunk appears in 0 of 4,149 client entry lists across all 404 page_client-reference-manifest.js files, and the baseline chunk in rootMainFiles contains only the gated async loader. app/error, app/global-error and components/ui/route-error.tsx still import the SDK statically; Turbopack keeps those in async groups, so they are not a baseline regression and were deliberately left alone.

entries.title: revalidate = 3600 is dead on the four /discover detail routes
entries.detail: All four detail routes now declare generateStaticParams alongside their revalidate, so they enter the prerender manifest and ISR is live. Each reuses the redaction-safe reader the index and sitemap already use, bounded (200), and each carries a .catch(() => []) so a build without Supabase credentials degrades to on-demand rendering instead of failing — which matters because this repo's agent containers cannot complete page-data collection. dynamicParams defaults true, so newer rows still render on demand and join the set on revalidate. The three /discover INDEX pages were deliberately NOT touched: they are LIVE-012, blocked on an auth-navigation decision.

entries.title: The sitemap's batched podcast read was silently truncating at 1000 rows
entries.detail: THE ROW'S PREMISE WAS STALE AND THE REAL BUG WAS WORSE. The N+1 had already been collapsed — sitemap.ts called a batched reader. But that batch used `.limit(min(n*200, 5000))` with no `.range()`, and `.limit()` does not raise PostgREST's server-side `max_rows` (supabase/config.toml:18 = 1000, and service_role does not escape it). So it declared a 5000-row appetite, received 1000, and reported no error. Because the batch orders `created_at DESC` ACROSS ALL SPACES, the dropped rows were whole trailing Spaces: their /podcasts index and every Show URL vanished from the sitemap with nothing to notice. Collapsing 200 correct small queries into one truncated one traded latency for missing URLs — the third instance today of a fix whose instrument could not tell 'nothing there' from 'I could not see'. Now paged explicitly with `.range()` over a TOTAL order (created_at DESC, id ASC — the tiebreaker is required so a created_at tie cannot straddle a page boundary and be skipped or repeated), stopping on a short page. Still O(rows), never O(Spaces).

verify.note: Probes the CONSEQUENCE — that the batched read pages — rather than the row's words. Backed by app/sitemap.test.ts, which rebuilds the URL list the old per-Space loop would have emitted and requires an exact match, and which was confirmed to FAIL against an unpaged read (expected 1000 to be 1500) before being accepted.

entries.notes:
Closed 2026-08-17. The probe that flagged this row as stale was `grep-present /'app'|"app"/` in check-canon.mjs, which passes on the mere appearance of the string 'app' - shape, not truth. Replaced with the consequence, measured in-process: import the guard, assert SEAM_ROOTS still covers app/ AND lib/, run scanCodeSeam() over the real tree and require zero member-facing violations. MEASURED: 3,398 files under app/ + lib/ + components/, 22,437 member-facing strings judged, 0 violations. The floors (MIN_SEAM_FILES 2000, MIN_SEAM_STRINGS 15000) make a guard that stops finding the corpus exit 79 rather than report a clean sweep of nothing. Proved BOTH ways: a real banned string ('Find your tribe') under a copy key fails it, narrowing SEAM_ROOTS fails it by name, and the SAME words in a comment and in an internal identifier do NOT fire it - the false-positive half is what keeps a widened guard from being routed around.

🔴 RE-SCOPED 2026-08-21, because this probe COST MAIN A RED BUILD. It called scanCodeSeam(), which parses every file in the seam — 3,413 files, 21,947 strings, 7.57s of CPU. check:backlog runs under a 20s CPU budget asserted by scripts/backlog-contract.test.ts, and this ONE row was 41% of it. On 2026-08-21 the budget came in at 20,080ms against the 20,000ms ceiling and main went red for 56 minutes (commit 6127a26), on a merge that had changed nothing but 18 PNGs.

WHAT THE PROBE DROPPED, AND WHY IT IS NOT A LOSS OF COVERAGE. It asserted found.length === 0 — that the whole tree is on-canon. That is precisely what `pnpm check:canon` asserts, and check:canon runs as its own guard in the SAME CI job. Duplicating it bought nothing and cost something real: a canon violation introduced by anyone, anywhere, would fail THIS ROW, reporting a regression in the seam-widening work that shipped months ago. A probe should measure its own row's consequence, not re-grade a neighbouring guard.

WHAT IT STILL MEASURES, which is this row's actual consequence: the seam was WIDENED past content/ to app/ + lib/, and it reaches a real corpus. SEAM_ROOTS must still contain both roots (narrowing it fails by name), and seamFiles() must still return at least MIN_SEAM_FILES. seamFiles is the directory WALK without the parse — newly exported for this, 0.031s against 7.57s, a 244x reduction — so the non-triviality floor survives intact: a walk that breaks or a root that moves still trips it rather than reporting a clean sweep of nothing.

entries.title: R7: the eyebrow role is no longer hand-rolled where the code itself names it
entries.detail: THE ROW'S PREMISE WAS WRONG AND THE MEASUREMENT SAYS SO. It called this 'largely mechanical' over ~698 sites with 3 adopters. Measured 2026-08-17: 615 sites pair `uppercase` with a LITERAL tracking value (tracking-wide 436, widest 59, wider 60, 20 arbitrary), against 87 already on the `eyebrow` utility and 69 on `tracking-eyebrow`. 87 adopters, not 3. The population is NOT one role, which is why a sweep is the wrong instrument: the dominant string is 11px `text-2xs font-semibold uppercase tracking-wide text-muted`, and a large share are pill badges (rounded-pill px-2 py-0.5) and dense table headers. Sweeping them means 11px -> 12px, semibold -> bold and 0.025em -> 0.18em - a 7.2x tracking change that widens a label inside a px-2.5 pill it was sized to fit. That is an unreviewed visual change to several hundred surfaces, not a rename. WHAT SHIPPED is the half a machine can settle: of the 15 slots the CODE ITSELF names `eyebrow`, SEVEN hand-rolled the role across five different letter-spacings, all in the shared kit - EditorShell, Toast, StudioWindow, SparkShell, EntityHeader, JourneyBuilder, HostCohostSection. All seven now compose the utility. The rest is a ratchet, seeded at the POST-sweep 608 rather than the 615 found, which is what makes reverting any of the seven raise it.

entries.notes: Closed 2026-08-17 (ADR-1071). THE ROW WAS STALE ON THE IMPLEMENTATION AND RIGHT ABOUT THE GAP. The three-position ladder and the desktop left-rail fold were already built and already gated. The PERSISTED half had nothing behind it: replacing the whole body of writeStoredRailFolds with `return` left all 38 tests in rail-fold.test.ts PASSING, and deleting railFold from the shell mount in app/(main)/layout.tsx - the entire no-flash path - left 288 tests passing with tsc green. Cause: that suite runs in environment 'node', so with no window and no document both storage functions return on their first line in every case. AND IT SURFACED A REAL DEFECT. writeStoredRailFolds is built to survive blocked localStorage (the setItem throw is swallowed, the cookie still lands) but readStoredRailFolds read localStorage and nothing else. In exactly that case the server paints the folded strip from the cookie, hydration renders it, and the first client snapshot reads blocked storage, answers Auto, and shoves the rail open one frame after paint - the fail-safe fired and the next line cancelled it. The read now falls back to the cookie. The probe EXECUTES the round trip rather than grepping for it: it fakes window.localStorage and document.cookie, chooses Strip/Open, drops the in-memory snapshot (a reload) and asserts the fold comes back AND that the cookie the server reads agrees. Verified myself, not just reported: gutting the write prints 'a reload lost the fold' and exits 1; removing compact={leftStrip} names the desktop fold and exits 1. No baseline recapture needed - the rail's state at rest is unchanged, and the new behaviour only fires when localStorage is empty AND a cookie exists, which a fresh capture browser never has.

entries.title: Loom D1: Studio ingest + ranked search — four extras built, the fifth struck as stale
entries.detail:
Shipped, but the ingest extras are still pending: checksum dedupe, EXIF strip, dims/colors/blurhash, the rendition set, and FTS-ranked/trigram search.

── UNPARKED 2026-08-20 (owner ruling): scheduled into the build-out; sequence in meta.slate. ── ⚙️ RE-TESTED AND RE-SHAPED 2026-08-24 (ADR-1082). The row is TRUE - no ingest module exists, no `textSearch` appears anywhere in the tree - but it is MIS-SHAPED: it reads as build-from-zero and is actually a WIRING job. 🔴 THE MOST USEFUL FINDING FOR SEQUENCING: PR 1 NEEDS NO MIGRATION. Every column and index D1 writes to is already applied - sha256, blurhash, focal_x/y, orig_width/height and the dedupe index library_assets_sha256_idx (20260920000000_library_dam.sql:15-33), plus the generated search_tsv column with GIN and a gin_trgm_ops index on title (20260919000000_library_assets.sql:61-88). So the first increment carries ZERO ADR-1111 ordering risk and can merge alongside siblings in any order. THE BLAST RADIUS IS SMALLER THAN IT LOOKS: eight upload sites, but six already funnel through insertSpaceLibraryImage (lib/library/store.ts:264). Only two bypass it - app/(main)/admin/library/actions.ts:53 and recraft-actions.ts:101 - so widening the chokepoint plus routing those two covers everything. FIRST PR: a pure lib/library/ingest.ts (node:crypto sha256 + a dependency-free image-header dimension parser), the widened chokepoint writing sha256/width/height, dedupe on the existing (space_id, sha256) index, the two bypass sites routed through it, and materialize.ts:772's `bytes: 0`. 🔴 THREE THINGS DELIBERATELY NOT IN PR 1, each with a reason. (1) EXIF STRIP CARRIES A HAZARD THE ROW NEVER MENTIONS: removing APP1 removes the ORIENTATION tag, so any phone JPEG relying on it renders rotated. The safe form strips APP1/APP13/XMP then re-emits a minimal APP1 carrying only Orientation, proven by a test on a rotation-6 JPEG that keeps orientation and loses GPS. Note only photos over 3.5 MB currently lose EXIF at all, by accident, via the canvas re-encode at image-shrink.ts:127. (2) blurhash and colours need PIXEL DECODE, which server-side means sharp - and check:og-trace is at 67 of a 100 ceiling with this seam reachable from the Loom picker, page editor, importer and email studio. That is the 2026-08-11 ENOSPC fan-out one directory over; compute them in the browser where image-shrink.ts already holds an ImageBitmap. (3) FTS ranking is its own PR because it is the one piece that MAY need a migration: PostgREST can filter on search_tsv with no schema change but cannot ORDER BY ts_rank, so either rank in-process (migration-free, recommended first) or add a search_library_assets RPC mirroring the existing match_library_assets - and that path takes the full ADR-1111 ordering discipline. ⚠️ lib/library/store.ts:149 says FTS is 'a follow-up, D7', contradicting BUILD-LIST.md:1233 which puts it in D1; the code comment is the stale one and gets fixed in the same pass.

── ✅ CLOSED 2026-08-25 (ADR-1121). FOUR OF THE FIVE WERE REAL AND WERE BUILT; THE FIFTH WAS ALREADY ANSWERED AND WAS STILL SITTING IN THIS ROW. 🔴 THE RENDITION SET IS STRUCK, NOT BUILT: HYG-017 established against the LIVE database that `library_renditions` has no table and no index — created 20260920000000_library_dam.sql:47, dropped 20260925000000:16 — and four places in the tree say transforms are ON-THE-FLY (ADR-480's migration header, lib/library/renditions.ts, PROG-D3's scope line, BUILD-LIST's Loom owner-decision line) against this row's one line saying otherwise. A rendition is a REQUEST, never a row; RENDITION_PRESETS belongs to D3's resolver. That is the fourth row in eight days to be wrong about its own scope (ADR-1082, ADR-1112): a probe checks whether the work is DONE and nothing checks whether it is still WANTED.

WHAT WAS BUILT. (1) CHECKSUM DEDUPE, on the (space_id, sha256) index that had been sitting unused since the DAM migration. The hash is taken AFTER the strip, which is what makes it useful rather than theatrical: two exports of one photo differing only in their EXIF block now dedupe to one asset. Space-scoped on purpose — a global match would hand one space another space's image — and it short-circuits BEFORE the storage write, so a duplicate costs no disk. (2) EXIF/XMP/IPTC STRIP WITH ORIENTATION PRESERVED. The row named the strip but not its hazard: the rotation tag lives in the same APP1 block as the GPS coordinates, so the obvious `drop APP1` is privacy-correct and renders every portrait phone photo SIDEWAYS. The strip re-emits a 32-byte APP1 carrying Orientation alone, proven on a rotation-6 fixture that keeps the rotation and loses the coordinates; ICC_PROFILE and the Adobe marker are kept because both change how the file DECODES. (3) DIMENSIONS from the container header (PNG/JPEG/GIF/WebP ×3 chunk flavours) plus BLURHASH + PALETTE. 🔴 THE PIXEL WORK RUNS IN THE BROWSER AND MUST STAY THERE: a server decode means sharp, check:og-trace has it at 67 of 100, and this seam is reachable from the picker, page editor, importer and email studio. MEASURED FAN-OUT OF THIS CHANGE: ZERO — no runtime dependency added, no next/og, no native module, and the probe asserts all four new modules stay clean of both. (4) FTS-RANKED + TRIGRAM SEARCH, WITH NO MIGRATION. Both indexes already existed (search_tsv GIN + title gin_trgm_ops, 20260919000000:61-88); PostgREST can FILTER a tsvector but cannot `order by ts_rank`, so both arms run and merge and lib/library/search-rank.ts does the ordering. FTS is stemmed and cannot match a fragment or a typo; trigram matches fragments and ranks nothing; neither is a superset of the other.

ALSO FIXED IN THE SAME PASS: store.ts:149's comment claiming FTS was 'a follow-up, D7' (BUILD-LIST put it in D1; the comment was the stale one), and the zero-size lie at materialize.ts — now NULL, because a path that files an already-stored object genuinely does not know the size and 0 renders as a real '0 B' asset. BOTH former bypass sites are gone: the Loom Studio upload now inserts through insertSpaceLibraryImage like everything else, so there is exactly ONE place a Loom row is written.

NOT CLAIMED, and split out rather than hidden: server-side GENERATORS (Recraft, Vera covers, importer seeds) get a checksum and dimensions but no blurhash, because no browser exists on those paths. That is HYG-021.

verify.cmd: node scripts/prog-d1-probe.mjs

entries.notes: Probes the CONSEQUENCE in-process (LIVE-034 forbids a probe that spawns a test runner): the dedupe read is scoped to (space_id, sha256); the strip re-emits an orientation APP1 rather than merely deleting one; the four new modules import neither sharp nor next/og; search reaches search_tsv and ranks; the Loom Studio upload no longer writes library_assets directly; and nothing references library_renditions. Verified to FAIL on a mutation that makes the strip re-emit orientation 1 instead of the real one — i.e. it catches the sideways-photo regression, not merely the presence of a function. Unit proofs live in lib/library/{ingest,blurhash,search-rank,space-images}.test.ts and lib/page-editor/loom-field-actions.test.ts under `pnpm test`.

entries.title: Loom D2: the AssetField seam + backfill
entries.detail:
One Upload / Pick from library / Paste URL control replacing ImageField everywhere; blocks store an asset REFERENCE plus a URL cache; render resolves reference → CDN url; backfill existing site-media URLs into the catalog and rewrite references.

── UNPARKED 2026-08-20 (owner ruling): scheduled into the build-out; sequence in meta.slate.

── ⚙️ RE-TESTED, RE-SHAPED AND HALF-SHIPPED 2026-08-25 (ADR-1130). The row promised three things; the census against the LIVE database found ONE of them real. (1) THE ONE CONTROL ALREADY EXISTED AND WAS ALREADY EVERYWHERE: components/loom/loom-picker.tsx has 16 consumers (page editor, entity blocks, Studio spark, branding, events, QR, email), and the row's 'Paste URL' leg was overruled by an owner directive recorded in three code headers — the Loom is the only way in, upload lives inside the picker, no paste box. (2) THE REFERENCE HALF WAS GENUINELY UNBUILT and is NOW SHIPPED for Puck documents: an image value is string | AssetRef ({ assetId, url }, lib/library/asset-ref.ts); the picker's onSelectAsset/onSelectManyAssets hand the caller the reference; imgField, loomImageField and the gallery field store it; the BlockRender walk unwraps every ref to its URL string before any renderer sees props (proven byte-identical against the same doc stored as strings); and getPublishedData refreshes stale caches via lib/library/resolve-refs.ts — fail-open to the cache, zero queries for a ref-free document, zero sharp/og-trace fan-out. Legacy strings stay legal forever, so NO stored document was rewritten. (3) 🔴 THE BACKFILL'S PREMISE IS DEAD, IN THE GOOD DIRECTION, and it was the row's own headline. Measured 2026-08-25: live pages documents hold ZERO site-media URLs (2 URL occurrences total, 1 distinct, external); all 6 page_content.hero_image site-media references already have catalog rows; 15 of 23 site-media objects are catalogued and the other 8 are importer/<intakeId>/ INTAKE STAGING files referenced only by 7 business_intake staging rows (LIVE-120), which the post-ADR-1121 importer no longer produces uncatalogued. There is nothing to backfill and nothing to rewrite; the backfill is STRUCK with these numbers, not built.

REMAINING SEQUENCE, in order: (a) HYG-029 — reference-storing adoption beyond the Puck fields: entity-block controls, Studio spark image fields, header-image-field, email studio, and the DECISION for column-backed surfaces (spaces.brand_logo_url, page_content.hero_image, page_settings.og_image_url cannot hold a ref in a text column — companion id columns or stay URL-cached). (b) Space-document cache refresh: space docs render refs correctly via the cache today (the unwrap is in the shared BlockRender), but readPageDoc does not call refreshAssetRefUrls; wire it when D3 edits can re-point a live asset's URL. (c) The usage index over refs is D4 (block_usage per ADR-975) — refs make it a cheap JSONB scan; do not build it here.

verify.evidence: Seam half shipped + proven in-tree (lib/library/asset-ref.test.ts, lib/library/resolve-refs.test.ts, the AssetRef describe in lib/page-editor/block-render.test.tsx, all under pnpm test); backfill struck on the ADR-1130 census. Remaining breadth is HYG-029 + the space-doc refresh.
