entries.title: Loom D7: semantic + AI
entries.detail:
Populate embedding, hybrid FTS+vector RRF ranking, AI auto-tag and colour extraction, background removal / upscale. Later the Weave generative composer.

── UNPARKED 2026-08-20 (owner ruling): scheduled into the build-out; sequence in meta.slate. ── 🔴 ITS FIRST ITEM IS ALREADY SHIPPED, found 2026-08-24 while re-testing PROG-D1. 'Populate embedding' and vector search are LIVE and cron-driven: lib/library/embeddings.ts exports reindexLibraryEmbeddings / matchLibraryAssets / similarLibraryAssets over the match_library_assets RPC (20260921000000_library_embeddings.sql), wired into the Studio at app/(main)/admin/library/page.tsx:162,167 behind sort=relevant, with a cron at vercel.json:37. D7's real remainder is hybrid FTS+vector RRF, auto-tag, colour extraction and background removal - and RRF is BLOCKED ON D1's FTS half, a dependency neither row states.

── UNBLOCKED 2026-08-25: the RRF dependency this row named is met. PROG-D1 shipped the FTS half (lib/library/search-rank.ts merges a search_tsv arm with a trigram arm and ranks them), so hybrid FTS+vector RRF now has both inputs. Note what it must NOT copy: D1's ranking is in-process because PostgREST cannot `order by ts_rank`. A true RRF over both signals wants ONE query that ranks both, which is the `search_library_assets` RPC ADR-1121 scoped and deliberately did not build — and that path takes the full ADR-1111 migration ordering discipline. Colour extraction is also partly done: library_assets.colors is populated on browser uploads by lib/library/image-describe.ts, so D7's remainder there is generated assets (HYG-021) and AI auto-tag.

verify.evidence: Program phase.

entries.title: Re-theme P4: universal browse hero
entries.detail:
The 24 plain IndexTemplate pages adopt heroOverlay so the hero is everywhere.

── UNPARKED 2026-08-20 (owner ruling): scheduled into the build-out; sequence in meta.slate.

── SEAM SHIPPED (#2254): lib/layout/index-hero.ts — resolveIndexHero(route, opts) returns a spreadable IndexTemplate prop bag over a four-rung ladder, with INDEX_HERO_DEFAULTS holding the route->cover map and the short/large product decision. PROG-P6 / ADR-1122 then made rung 2 resolve itself through the copy cascade.

🔴 PREMISE RE-TESTED 2026-08-25 (ADR-1127). THE ROW COUNTS ONE OF THE TWO BROWSE COMPOSITIONS, AND NAMES THE WRONG DEFECT.
  · COUNTED BY RENDER SITE: 41 browse render sites, not 24 pages. 32 compose IndexTemplate; 9 head an operator-rearrangeable body with MarketHero (the sanctioned editable index, PAGE-FRAMEWORK §8.5: /circles, /channels, /events via events-surface.tsx, /spaces/directory, /discover/spaces, /classifieds, /housing, /market, /store). Of the 32, 7 already drew the band, so 25 were plain — the row's 24 was one off, on half the surfaces.
  · THE DEFECT IS NOT A MISSING heroOverlay. MarketHero is a thin wrapper over the SAME PageHero the heroOverlay branch renders, so those 9 already looked right. What they lacked was the LADDER: getPageHeaderImage (rung 1, the operator's Settings > Basics header-image uploader) appeared in exactly 3 of the 41 render sites, and 4 more reached it via resolveIndexHero. 7 of 41. THE OTHER 34 READ THE OPERATOR'S UPLOAD NOWHERE, and savePageSeo gates that uploader on isSafeRoute rather than an allowlist — so an operator could upload a header image on any of them and watch nothing happen. ADR-1122's /network bug at 34x scale. Invisible in production only because page_settings holds ONE header image in the whole table (/crew, a Dashboard, which does read it).
  · THE RESOLVER'S OWN EXEMPLARS HAD NOT ADOPTED IT. /practices, /journeys and /library are the three pages whose duplicated stanza motivated index-hero.ts, and all three still carried it verbatim a week later, while the module header read "this module is the one copy". It was the fifth.

✅ SHIPPED 2026-08-25 (ADR-1127), 18 files:
  · resolveMarketHero + asMarketHero in lib/layout/index-hero.ts — the editable-index twin, same four rungs, MarketHero's prop names. `cover` is REQUIRED because MarketHero types `image` non-null (the gradient band is a result on a utility index and a broken header on a hero-led commerce one). All 9 MarketHero sites adopted; each lost its hand-rolled resolveHeaderElement call and gained rungs 1 and 2. Zero visual change today.
  · /practices, /journeys, /library spread {...hero}; ~30 lines of re-typed ladder deleted. Zero visual change (the map already held their exact covers).
  · /events/calendar adopts the band — the one plain index whose SECTION carries a live operator hero (page_content['/events'].hero_image, set in June). Its new row is the first to separate the two flags: size is about the BAND (short: a month grid is a work surface), inheritHero is about the IMAGE (true: the calendar is the Events section wearing a different body).

⏳ STILL OPEN: the 24 remaining plain IndexTemplate pages — LIVE-117, and counted nowhere else. That is a real layout change on 24 surfaces (each page's h1 moves onto a band), not a dropped rung, so it carries its own PR, screenshots and visual-baseline pass; it also would not fit here under the 40-file gate.

verify.evidence: Program phase, HALF SHIPPED. The ladder half is proven by lib/layout/index-hero.test.ts (35 cases, including 7 over resolveMarketHero and the /events/calendar row) and by the tree: `grep -rl "<MarketHero"` returns 9 render sites and all 9 now reach rung 1 through resolveMarketHero, where 0 of 9 did on 2026-08-25. The open half is the 24 plain IndexTemplate pages, probed executably by LIVE-117 (it fails today and counts them). Census reproduced by grepping render sites for <IndexTemplate>/<MarketHero> and for heroOverlay|resolveIndexHero|resolveMarketHero|getPageHeaderImage.

entries.title: Re-theme P5: entity headers onto PageHero
entries.detail:
Fold the DetailTemplate band pages onto the one PageHero grammar, so entity and index become one component.

── UNPARKED 2026-08-20 (owner ruling): scheduled into the build-out; sequence in meta.slate.

── PREMISE RE-TESTED 2026-08-24 (AGENTS.md / ADR-1082). THE ROW SAID 43; IT IS 30. Counted by RENDER SITE, not by import: 28 files render DetailTemplate directly and 2 more (/events/<slug> and /discover/events/<slug>) reach it through EventDetailTemplate = 30 LIVE SURFACES. The 43 swept in things that are not band pages: 2 loading.tsx skeletons, the EventDetailTemplate wrapper itself, a test file, and 3 marketplace pages (classifieds / housing / market) that render ListingDetailTemplate — a SEPARATE template that never touches DetailTemplate.
Second premise, also wrong: 'band pages' implies they have bands. Of the 30, only 9 carried any cover at all (a bespoke identity-variant PageHero passed through the `hero` escape hatch) and 1 more put cover art inside a `band` slot. THE OTHER 20 HAD NO COVER. And DetailTemplate's `coverImage` — the 'standard Detail cover' PAGE-FRAMEWORK §8.5 documents — had ZERO CALLERS: every coverImage= in the tree was on a PageHero nested inside `hero`. So P5 is not a re-theme of 43 existing bands. It is giving 20 pages a cover they never had and retiring 9 hand-rolled stanzas.

── SEAM SHIPPED 2026-08-24 (branch theme/p5-entity-hero, ADR-1117). lib/layout/detail-hero.ts — resolveDetailHero(route, opts) returns a spreadable DetailTemplate prop bag, the detail-side twin of PROG-P4's index-hero.ts. Its four-rung ladder is INVERTED from the index's (the entity's own cover outranks the operator's site-wide image, because on an entity page the entity's owner owns the surface), and each section carries a tail of 'placeholder' (the gradient band) or 'none' (no cover), because on a detail page the h1 lives BELOW the cover so the band is decoration, not the thing carrying the title. 35 unit tests cover every rung, both tails, the focus-travels-with-its-image rule, the longest-prefix map, and both fail-safe paths. An UNMAPPED route resolves to no cover, so adopting on an unmapped page is a visual no-op — which is what lets the rest land in PRs under the 40-file CI limit.

── ADOPTED 2026-08-25 (branch theme/p5-adoption, ADR-1136) — 26 of 30 surfaces now resolve through lib/layout/detail-hero.ts (21 standard + 5 identity). Re-measured first (ADR-1082): still 30 render sites on main@fcb5348c4 — the census held — but the '9 bespoke stanzas' split did not: only 5 of the 9 carry the resolveHeaderElement stanza (/channels/<id>, /circles/<slug>, /journeys/<slug>, /journeys/<slug>/learn, /people/<handle>); the other 4 hand-roll a bespoke cover NODE, not the stanza. The module gained the identity twin — asIdentityHero + resolveIdentityHero, the detail echo of PROG-P4's resolveMarketHero: same four-rung ladder, PageHero prop names, empty ladder = null (the gradient) because the identity band carries the h1. All 5 stanza pages adopted it, deleting their copies; their lockups did not move. The 17 straightforward sites adopted resolveDetailHero (the 2 client islands via their server pages; VeraProfile became async). 14 new DETAIL_HERO_DEFAULTS rows, every one image:null + tail:'none' (pinned by a unit test): no cover invented, rung 2 armed — the operator's section Settings image stops being dropped on the floor. One visible change: /discover/journeys/<slug> gains rung 1 (journey_plans.cover_image + cover_focus). /support, /connections, /admin/crm/pipeline and the Space podcast show stay deliberately unmapped (private/operator surfaces; square show artwork is identity, not a cover).

── REMAINING — 4 of 30, each a bespoke cover COMPOSITION whose folding is a behaviour change with its own PR + screenshots (ADR-1117 §'what this does not do', reaffirmed ADR-1136):
  · /circles/starter/<slug> — a generated TemplateCover (pillar-branded cover art), no element resolve to retire.
  · /spaces/<slug> profile layout — its own Header/Hero cover-size vocabulary (readCoverSize/readCoverScrim), never consults the header element.
  · /events/<slug> + /discover/events/<slug> via EventDetailTemplate — a multi-source event-media ladder (uploaded cover → scanned poster → crop) with no element resolve; folding it would newly make event cover height element-tuned.
  · The 2 loading.tsx skeletons follow their pages, which did not move.
  · SEPARATE, NOT P5: the 3 ListingDetailTemplate pages are a different template. File their own row if their hero should join the grammar.

verify.evidence: 26 of 30 render sites resolve through lib/layout/detail-hero.ts — 21 spread resolveDetailHero, 5 identity pages spread resolveIdentityHero; grep 'resolveDetailHero\|resolveIdentityHero' across app/ + components/ counts the call sites, and lib/layout/detail-hero.test.ts (45 cases) probes the ladder, the identity twin, and pins every ADR-1136 map row to image:null + tail:'none'. The 4 non-adopters are bespoke cover compositions, enumerated in the detail.

entries.title: Re-theme P6: the copy cascade
entries.detail:
Generalize page_content into a site -> section -> page inherit-cascade, widen editable fields to body copy and images, and extend check:canon to .tsx. Overlaps LIVE-018.

── UNPARKED 2026-08-20 (owner ruling): scheduled into the build-out; sequence in meta.slate.

🔴 PREMISE RE-TESTED 2026-08-25 (ADR-1122). Two of the three clauses did not survive measurement.

✅ CLAUSE 3 WAS ALREADY DONE, by LIVE-018 / ADR-1065, eight days before this row was picked up. check:canon's SEAM_ROOTS is ['app','lib','components'] and its walk takes /\.tsx?$/. Measured: 3,406 seam files, 1,882 of them .tsx, 21,674 member-facing strings judged, 0 violations. The violation count for 'turning it on' is ZERO, because it is on.

⚠️ CLAUSE 1'S PREMISE WAS BACKWARDS. page_content does not hold copy. Production, read 2026-08-25: SIX rows, all six on SECTION ROOTS (/circles, /events, /journeys, /nearby, /network, /practices). ZERO set title. ZERO set description. ALL SIX set hero_image. The one row mentioning a CTA (/circles, label 'Start a Circle') has an EMPTY cta_href, so it has never rendered. The operator's real use of this table is one field, the section hero, stored at exactly the rung a cascade would inherit FROM, while the reader only ever looked at the exact route.

✅ SHIPPED (ADR-1122): lib/layout/content-cascade.ts, resolving page -> section(s) -> site ('*') -> coded fallback in one query, request-cached, fail-safe, PER FIELD. Identity fields (title/description) deliberately do not inherit, because they feed pageContentMetadata and inheriting them manufactures duplicate meta descriptions across a section; the CTA resolves as ONE unit so a page label is never spliced onto a section link. NO MIGRATION: the section rung is the row that already exists. resolvePageContent consumes it. resolveIndexHero now resolves rung 2 itself, closing a live bug: /network has carried a page_content hero since June and dropped it on the floor. INDEX_HERO_DEFAULTS gains inheritHero (false on the three utility rows) so the cascade cannot silently overturn the short/large split. longestPrefixRow is shared out of the cascade module and index-hero consumes it. 26 cascade tests plus 10 new index-hero tests.

⏳ STILL OPEN, COUNTED HERE AND NOWHERE ELSE:
  (a) WIDEN THE EDITABLE FIELDS to body copy and images. This is the half that needs COLUMNS, and it is deliberately not in the cascade PR: a new migration file makes every other open branch red under check:migrations --require-ledger until it merges, and four branches were open that night. Its own PR, when the tree is quieter.
  (b) AN OPERATOR SURFACE FOR THE SITE RUNG. The resolver reads '*' and the test covers it, but CONTENT_EDIT_ROUTES gates writes to real routes, so nothing can set it yet. One editor entry, not a schema change.
  (c) The cascade does NOT subsume the two hero ladders, and that is a finding rather than a gap. See ADR-1122's last-but-one section: they order DIFFERENT tables by ownership, deliberately in opposite directions (operator-owned browse surface vs host-owned entity). What was genuinely shared is now shared: the prefix loop and the page_content rung.

verify.evidence: Program phase. The shipped half is proven by lib/layout/content-cascade.test.ts (26 cases, every rung) plus lib/layout/index-hero.test.ts; the open half is (a) and (b) in the detail.

entries.title: Re-theme P9: marketing ↔ in-app reconciliation — the brands already agree, the GATES did not
entries.detail:
Align the marketing brand system with the app tokens where they diverge.

── UNPARKED 2026-08-20 (owner ruling): scheduled into the build-out; sequence in meta.slate.

── ✅ RE-MEASURED AND CLOSED 2026-08-25 (ADR-1123). THE ROW'S PREMISE WAS WRONG, AND THE ROW SHRANK. "Align the marketing brand system with the app tokens" assumes TWO systems. There is ONE, and what diverged was the GATES, not the brand.

MEASURED (marketing = app/(marketing)/** + components/marketing/**, 61 ts/tsx files, plus the marketing header/footer; in-app = app/(main)/** + components/**, 1,996 files):
  · Raw hex / text-[Npx] / inline rgb() on marketing: 🔴 ZERO, across all 61 files, with the check:tokens marketing exemption lifted. There was nothing for the exemption to protect.
  · Colour utility vocabulary: marketing uses a strict SUBSET of the one @theme inline map. Exactly 3 utility names appear on marketing and nowhere in-app (border-ink-border, text-ink-border, text-surface-elevated) and all three are app tokens. No marketing-only colour exists.
  · --color-marketing-canvas: DELIBERATE, and complete — overridden in every block that overrides --color-canvas (:root, .theme-light-lock, [data-skin=midnight], .dark, .dark [data-skin=midnight]). No skin gap.
  · Anton display face (font-display at 22x the in-app rate) and the .mk-band/.mk-beat/.mk-cont/.mk-tight rhythm: DELIBERATE. NOT flattened. check:headers and check:templates keep their marketing skips — those govern PAGE STRUCTURE, which genuinely differs.
  · Hand-rolled eyebrows: marketing 8 sites (0.13/file) vs in-app 463 (0.23/file). 🔴 IN-APP IS WORSE. Not a marketing divergence; P2/P3 debt.
  · Literal rounded-2xl over rounded-card: marketing 34 (0.53/file) vs in-app 717 (0.36/file). Marketing ~1.5x worse per file, but this is the repo-wide literal-radius ratchet (P1), not P9. Deliberately NOT folded in: a large invented row beats nothing.

THE TWO REAL GAPS, BOTH CLOSED HERE:
  1. check:tokens exempted app/(marketing)/ and components/marketing/ whole-tree, on the claim that marketing is "a separate brand design system". Measured at 0 violations — the exemption was the only artifact still asserting a second system existed. DELETED.
  2. check:contrast modelled the cream ground with ONE pair (--color-text) while the app canvas beside it carried five foregrounds. The marketing canvas is 5/255 DARKER in light mode, so every twin ratio is tighter and none had been measured. SEVEN pairs added (now 8 total): text-muted 5.21, text-subtle 4.79, primary-strong 4.75, focus-ring 3.34 all PASS in all five render states; border-strong 1.29, primary 2.19 and success 3.80 are waived at their measured floors.

🔴 THE FINDING THAT JUSTIFIES THE WHOLE ROW: components/marketing/comparison-table.tsx already pinned its ledger cards to bg-surface with the comment "a `yes` cell's `text-success` clears 4.5:1 on the surface tone and misses it on the canvas tone". That is exactly right (4.67 on a card, 4.05/3.80 on the cream) and it was true for as long as the comment existed, with the gate green the whole time, because the gate did not model that ground. The pair is now entered and frozen — the rank-gold treatment — so the fact is printed on every run instead of surviving only as a comment.

entries.title: DAWN Phase 3: the mechanical sweeps (2,004 sites, 91% raw <button>)
entries.detail:
RE-CENSUSED 2026-08-25 (the 2026-08-19 figure had itself expired). On the ratchet basis ({app,components,lib}/**/*.tsx, tests and the primitives themselves excluded, comments blanked by check-adoption's own corpus loader): 1,830 raw <button>, 168 <input>, 4 <select>, 2 <textarea> = 2,004 sites, against the row's claimed 2,072. Two of the row's four sub-figures were bare-grep drift. Select and textarea are DONE (both on their floors); input is not a sweep either. What is left is the button sweep and nothing else.

── HOW A SLICE IS CUT (ADR-1119, amended by ADR-1124). By SHAPE, not by directory: the set of raw <button> sites whose className is a NEAR-MISS for one `variant × size` of the Button primitive — every token the primitive emits for that pair is present, and every token the site carries is one the primitive's BASE already supplies. It is near-miss and NOT set-equality, because no raw <button> in the tree is set-equal to the primitive: BASE adds `tap-target`, `press` and `lift-1` on purpose. Converting GAINS those three, so EVERY SLICE MOVES RENDERED PIXELS — that is the program working, not a defect. The query is `scripts/dawn-bucket.mjs`; run it, do not re-derive it.

── SLICE 1 (dawn/phase3-slice-1, ADR-1119): the `primary × sm` class, 43 sites in 33 files.

── SLICE 2 SHIPPED 2026-08-25 (dawn/phase3-slice-2, ADR-1124): the `primary × md` class. MEASURED at 53 sites in 40 files, against slice 1's pre-sizing of 49 in 37 — the estimate did NOT hold, and 40 source files alone would have breached the 40-file CI ceiling. Cut to the 40 sites in 31 files that are NOT import-reachable from any surface test/e2e/visual.spec.ts photographs, so the slice cannot move a committed baseline. raw-button-bg 513 → 466, literal-radius 2291 → 2222. Because `primary × md` is the primitive's DEFAULT pair, every converted site is a bare <Button> with no className and no props.

── WHAT IS LEFT, WITH ITS ADDRESS. raw-button-bg = 466 (the ratcheted half) before slice 1 merges, 423 after both slices land. The two named residues are HYG-022 (2 sites the `primary × sm` slice left behind) and LIVE-114 (the 13 `primary × md` sites on watched surfaces). Beyond them the remaining population is mostly ghost/secondary fills, a different sweep: raw <button> overall is ~1,787 in 587 files, so ~74% of button sites carry no primary fill at all.

── UNPARKED 2026-08-20 (owner ruling): scheduled into the build-out; sequence in meta.slate.

entries.detail: Found independently by two agents, which is what makes them findings rather than opinions. raw-input's lookahead excludes only type="hidden", so ~18 type="file" triggers behind hidden/sr-only are PERMANENTLY un-retirable debt inside a ratchet. And white-black-literals does not exclude app/print/**, though DAWN-CONVERSION §1 names it a carve-out, so its floor is permanently 2. Both mean a ratchet can never reach its true floor. Unscheduled, and it should not be.

entries.notes: Closed 2026-08-17. The row named two defects and got both counts wrong; the third and worst was not in the row at all. (1) raw-input's lookahead: 37 concealed file triggers, not ~18, and 0 of the 37 are visible. (2) white-black-literals: the floor was permanently 27, not 2, and the sharper defect the row missed is that A TOTAL CANNOT TELL A CARVE-OUT FROM NEW DEBT — retire one annotated site, add one bare bg-white, and it reads 27 -> 27 '✅ held'. Now 0 with a per-site KEEP <utility>: <reason> escape, so the decisive case FAILS. (3) THE ONE NOBODY KNEW: stripComments treated a string literal as code, so a file input's accept glob ending slash-star opened a block comment that ran to the next close token — 121,627 characters of real markup blanked across 101 files, hiding 23 debt sites in 6 classes. A FALSE FALL: literal-radius read 2,281 against a 2,287 floor and printed '✅ shrank' while the true count was 2,292, a RISE. It also made fix (1) 40% inert, because the glob had already blanked the className that proves concealment. Five floors moved UP as a result — none is new design debt, all are sites the corpus was hiding, each recorded `rebased` and flagged on every run. Tests assert @2 is strictly un-blanking versus @1, so the corpus change can only reveal debt, never hide it.

entries.detail: The workflow exists to break a FOREVER-deadlock: pr-compare is a required context posted by a path-filtered job, so a docs-only PR never gets it and cannot merge, with no admin bypass. entries.title: Nothing prevents the build cache overflowing again, because the gate that would is calibrated in the wrong units
entries.detail:
RE-MEASURED 2026-08-18, and the row changed shape rather than closing. THE SYMPTOM IS GONE: three consecutive production builds (18:46, 19:01, 19:09) uploaded 1.26 / 1.28 / 1.29 GB against the 1.50 GB ceiling and every one logged 'Restored build cache from previous deployment'. No invalidation line anywhere. The 1.53 GB reading the row was filed on does not reproduce. WHAT IS STILL TRUE is the second half of the original row: nothing PREVENTS a recurrence. scripts/check-cache-budget.mjs was written for exactly that on 2026-08-17 and has never run on a real build. It was wired into postbuild in #2159 and TAKEN BACK OUT before merge, because the preview build of that change printed what no amount of reading could: 'TRIMMED the build cache before Vercel could reject it. What the build was about to hand back measured 2.40 GiB, over the 1.38 GiB trim point. drops the cheap half instead: .next/cache/turbopack (1520 MiB).' THE FLOOR ARM WAS RIGHT (node_modules 933 MiB, 27% clear of its 1.25 GiB budget, exactly as predicted). THE TRIM ARM IS CALIBRATED AGAINST THE WRONG QUANTITY: measure() sums RAW BYTES ON DISK and Vercel's ceiling applies to the PACKED archive. Raw 2.40 GiB versus a packed upload of 1.26-1.29 GB is about 2:1, not the ~3% the script's header assumes, because the Turbopack cache compresses hard and is the dominant term. Wired as-is it would delete a 1.5 GiB compiler cache on EVERY build to prevent an overflow that is not happening, turning a working warm cache into a guaranteed cold compile forever. TO CLOSE: fix the calibration (LIVE-048), then wire the gate in the SAME change as a preview build that prints it green. Do NOT close this row by deleting the guard or by declaring the symptom gone: the symptom being gone is why there is time to get the instrument right, not a reason to skip it.

STILL OPEN 2026-08-19, and the reason is now narrower than 'the gate is broken'. The gate is fixed (LIVE-048) and it is running on every production build, but in WARN-ONLY mode (LIVE-035): it measures and reports and cannot trim. So a cache heading for the 1.50 GB ceiling would be SEEN and named in the build log, and then nothing would stop it. Recurrence is now visible rather than prevented, which is a real improvement over nothing watching and is still not this row. It closes when the gate is promoted to blocking on the strength of a confirmed PACKED_PER_RAW.

Trend, read from production build logs on 2026-08-19: packed cache uploads of 1.26 GB across the day's deploys against the 1.50 GB ceiling, consistent with the 1.26 / 1.28 / 1.29 GB readings from 2026-08-18. Not rising.

THE PROBE ON THIS ROW WAS ITSELF WRONG, and the tree caught it the same day. It asked only whether check-cache-budget appears in postbuild. On 2026-08-19 it started appearing there in --warn-only mode, so the probe flipped to passing while the row stayed true: nothing prevents an overflow, it is merely reported now. That is the shape-not-truth failure four ADRs name, and a probe walked into it the first time the tree moved. Rewritten to measure the CONSEQUENCE -- the gate must be in postbuild AND not carry --warn-only AND still contain a delete path -- so it agrees with the row today and passes only when an overflow can actually be stopped.

HEADROOM RE-READ 2026-08-19 with the corrected constant, and it is tighter than this row assumed. Preview build 3jeNVZxuUy7thPjXpazjMC6yHwVo uploaded 1.32 GB against the 1.50 GB ceiling: 12% clear, not the 16% the 1.26 GB production reads implied. The cache is a single term, turbopack at 1459 MiB, so there is no second thing to trim if it grows. The gate now SEES this on every build and still cannot act on it.

🔴 FOUR PACKED READINGS TODAY, AND THE HEADROOM IS NARROWING:
    2026-08-18 production          1.26 GB   16% clear
    2026-08-19 production          1.26 GB   16% clear
    2026-08-19 preview (#2178)     1.32 GB   12% clear
    2026-08-19 preview (#2179)     1.35 GB   10% clear

⚠️ READ THAT CAREFULLY RATHER THAN AS A TREND LINE. The two production builds started COLD ('Build cache: <1 MB' on input), while the two previews compiled against a warm turbopack cache, so the 1.26 and the 1.35 are not the same measurement repeated. What IS comparable is the two previews, 8 minutes apart: turbopack went 1459 -> 1493 MiB, and those trees differed in what they compiled, so even that is one observation and not a rate.

What is NOT in doubt is the tightest true reading: 1.35 GB against a 1.50 GB ceiling is 10% clear, on a cache whose .next/cache half is a SINGLE term. If turbopack grows past roughly 1.65 GiB the whole cache is discarded, node_modules included, and the gate that would trim it first is deliberately unable to (warn-only, LIVE-035). That is this row, stated in numbers.

SIXTH READING, and it widens rather than tightens: preview xpkMNeSxJCWTTn35uvCeoacVbM7n uploaded 1.29 GB, 14% clear. The 8.7%-clear production figure from dpl_6FfMfAv7mHXQ3P2X3GmTxSCwDvEz remains the MAXIMUM observed and is still the number to plan against -- a preview that compiled less code is not evidence the ceiling moved. Recorded because the spread between same-day builds (1.26-1.37 GB) is now visibly dominated by what each build compiled, which is the reason this row still refuses to call any of it a trend line.

── CLOSED 2026-08-19 (owner: "Cache Budget: implement best practice"): the gate is calibrated in Vercel's units (PACKED_PER_RAW = 0.53, settled from a real paired reading: raw measure printed beside the same build's 'Uploading build cache' line, measured 0.5254, rounded toward firing early), the trim reaches only the named compiler-cache list (proven by mutation in scripts/check-cache-budget-trim.test.ts, including a reconstruction of the 2026-08-18 size-sorted mutant), loose top-level files are named in the composition and unreachable by the trim, and the gate runs BLOCKING in postbuild. The promotion landed in the same change as the preview build whose postbuild printed it green; the warn-only pin inverted with it.

Presence is not prevention. Promote it to blocking once a real build confirms PACKED_PER_RAW (LIVE-035).');process.exit(1)}const src=fs.readFileSync(S,'utf8');if(src.indexOf('rmSync(')<0){console.error('check-cache-budget no longer deletes anything, so it cannot bring an oversized cache back under the ceiling');process.exit(1)}process.exit(0)"

entries.title: 20 route handlers are green by human assertion, and 11 of them claim `public`
entries.detail: check:authz now sees all 72 route handlers, but 52 are green because a gate was DETECTED and 20 because a human read them and said so. The ledger states this in its own header rather than hiding it, and pins each route's normalized-body digest so an edit forces a re-read — but a reason is not a proof. The sharp end is the three asserted `public` routes that touch the admin client: app/api/vitals, app/api/people/[handle]/vcard, app/api/llms.txt. Give each a per-route test pinning what it must never return, the way app/api/status/route.test.ts already pins its 'no secret' promise. That converts the highest-risk assertions into verifications and leaves the genuinely-trivial ones asserted.

verify.cmd: node -e "const fs=require('fs');const want=[['app/api/vitals/route.ts','app/api/vitals/route.test.ts'],['app/(main)/people/[handle]/vcard/route.ts','app/(main)/people/[handle]/vcard/route.test.ts'],['app/llms.txt/route.ts','app/llms.txt/route.test.ts']];if(want.some(([r])=>!fs.existsSync(r)))process.exit(79);const bad=[];for(const [route,test] of want){if(!fs.existsSync(test)){bad.push(test+' (missing)');continue}const s=fs.readFileSync(test,'utf8');if(!/from '\\.\\/route'/.test(s))bad.push(test+\" (does not import './route')\");else if((s.match(/expect\\(/g)||[]).length<3)bad.push(test+' (fewer than 3 assertions)');}if(bad.length){console.error(bad.join('; '));process.exit(1)}process.exit(0)"

entries.notes: Closed 2026-08-17. The three asserted-public routes that touch the admin client now carry per-route tests: app/api/vitals, app/(main)/people/[handle]/vcard and app/llms.txt, 27 assertions between them. They pin what each must NEVER return rather than that it returns something - vitals writes profile_id NULL whatever the payload says, answers with an EMPTY body so the sink cannot echo a payload back, never reads headers or cookies, caps the batch and truncates the session id. VERIFIED ADVERSARIALLY, and the first attempt is worth recording: breaking the route to bank `profileId` did NOT fail the suite, which looked like a vacuous test. It was not - the attacker-shaped fixture sends `profile_id`, and re-running the break with that key failed exactly as it should ('expected 00000000-...-0001 to be null'). A break that does not fire is a claim about the TEST that has to be checked before it is believed.

entries.title: check:authz is file-level: it sees a gate is called, not that it runs on every path
entries.detail: LIVE-022 closed the VISIBILITY half — app/api/** was invisible because the classifier's first predicate required 'use server', which a Next 16 Route Handler never is. The granularity half is untouched and the guard's own header says so: it detects that a recognised gate is called SOMEWHERE in the file, not that it runs before every write on every path through every exported method. A route exporting GET and POST where only GET is gated reads as green. Stated here rather than left in an agent report, because an unrecorded limitation is how a partial gate comes to be read as full coverage (ADR-970).

verify.evidence: scripts/check-authz-guards.mjs header states the file-level limit explicitly. Confirmed 2026-08-17: the classifier tests src for gate tokens per FILE, with no per-export analysis.

entries.notes: Closed 2026-08-17 (ADR-1070). check:authz was FILE-level: it saw a gate called somewhere in the file, so an early return before the gate, a gate on one branch of an if, and a gated GET beside an ungated POST all read as green. It now requires EVERY exported HTTP method to pass three structural rules, following the body through a wrapper's local handler (27 cron routes) and into file-local helpers: R1 per-export, R2 the gate is not nested inside if/else/switch/catch, R3 no createAdminClient() query above the gate. R3 IS A DELIBERATE NARROWING AND THE MEASUREMENT IS WHY. A literal 'any return before the gate' rule was tried against the real corpus first: it fires on 10 of the 52 gated handlers and all ten are validation (400 on a malformed body, 429 on rate limit, an empty list for a blank query). Shipping that would have been 100% false positives on day one, which is the ADR-970 shape - a guard that cannot fire honestly gets routed around and then reads as coverage. What is dangerous is not returning early, it is answering from the service-role client before you know who is asking, and that is what R3 measures. IT FOUND THREE REAL FALSE GREENS, each re-verdicted as a digest-pinned human reading: check-handle (auth.getUser inside an if, over a SECURITY DEFINER RPC) -> public; auth/callback (auth.getUser three branches deep in a swallowed analytics block; the real credential check is exchangeCodeForSession) -> token-credential; q/[slug] (service-role read of the code row before getMyProfileId, which answers WHO scanned, not MAY they) -> self-scoped. Counts moved 52 gated / 20 asserted to 49 / 23, and the standing 'the ledger must never outgrow the gated set' test still holds.

entries.title: Recapture the visual baselines the beta cutover and the skin fix deliberately changed

The commit touched exactly 8 files, all /pricing, which is the failure set exactly. pr-compare is still red, but on the @a11y half only (8 midnight-dark contrast contexts, OWN-014) - the @visual half this row owns is green.

entries.notes: The row also claimed 'every midnight-dark baseline is a photograph of the wrong rendering'. THAT WAS NOT BORNE OUT: midnight-dark passed everywhere except /pricing, and /pricing failed on all four skins equally, which is the beta cutover shortening the page rather than a skin problem. entries.title: 17 controls across 14 files had no accessible name, and nothing measured it
entries.detail: RE-MEASURED 2026-08-17 with a real TypeScript JSX parse and all eight naming paths the accessible-name computation actually has. The original figure was 143 'may have no accessible name'; the honest number is 17, in 14 files, out of 3,605 controls judged across 1,884 files. 126 of the 143 - 88% - were FALSE POSITIVES, because the first scan could not resolve label-WRAPPING components and could not read an element's CONTENTS; those two blind spots alone account for 2,091 correctly-named controls. All four files the row named as examples (circle-builder, practice-builder, block-edit-panel, search-overlay) contained ZERO real violations. The 17 were real: 13 icon-only buttons wrapping a bare lucide icon (announced as 'button' and nothing else), 2 sr-only file inputs, and 4 slug fields whose visible caption was a <span> rather than a <label> - exactly the class check:labels documents itself as unable to see. All 17 are fixed, so the guard ships at ZERO with no allowlist and no ratchet file: nothing to waive and nothing to quietly grow. Named by: 1,808 contents, 735 aria-label, 428 placeholder (weak), 283 wrapping label, 174 htmlFor, 105 title, 53 label prop, 13 spread (unknowable), 6 aria-labelledby.

entries.title: The beta rate is grantable per Space, privately, and no public surface moves
entries.detail: CODE HALF ONLY — OWN-024 is the owner half. spaces.beta_price_grant is a private flag ONLY the checkout reads. resolveLoadoutPriceId decides on the pure three-armed loadoutChargeArm: lock (re-bill the grandfathered locked_price_id) -> founding (the window is open OR this Space carries the grant) -> list. No expiry, because the grant is SPENT by the first successful checkout: the reconciler writes the charged price as the lock and arm 1 wins forever after, so revoking it later cannot raise anyone's rate. Read in its OWN PostgREST request rather than added to the existing space select, because an undeployed column fails the WHOLE request with 42703 — the profiles.email bug already recorded in that file. Fail-safe FALSE: unreadable means charge list, never less. The panel distinguishes not_deployed from granted:false and says 'Not available yet' instead of showing a toggle that would look enabled and quietly do nothing.
entries.notes: Proven by consequence: the test pins the EXACT set of prices a visitor is quoted across offering cards, JSON-LD, plan rows and the /pricing table, and asserts $19/$49/$190/$490 are absent. Five mutants each take it red. Mutant B — leaking the beta rate to /pricing — ESCAPED the first draft, which is why the sweep was widened to the surfaces reading effectiveCatalogAmounts rather than its display twin. Security posture measured rather than assumed: SELECT on spaces is column-level so a new column is invisible to anon/authenticated, but UPDATE is TABLE-level and the column inherits it; a column-level revoke cannot help, so the proposal states the condition to watch instead of pretending to close it.

entries.title: check:backlog costs 24s and grows ~2s per closed row, because ten probes each spawn a vitest run
entries.detail: MEASURED, not estimated: `node scripts/check-backlog.mjs` takes 23.9s. 21 rows carry a cmd probe and TEN of them spawn a full vitest run to prove their consequence — the honest instrument, and an expensive one. It already turned CI red once: backlog-contract.test.ts's ripgrep-parity arm runs the guard TWICE by design and blew the default 30s test timeout. That is patched with a raised timeout and a comment, which treats the symptom; the number comes back at roughly +2s per row closed the same way, and 39 rows are still open. It is also duplicated work: those test files already run in `pnpm test`, so the probe re-runs what CI just ran. Options worth weighing, none obviously right: a probe protocol where the row names a test file and the guard trusts the suite to have run it (loses standalone verifiability, which is the whole point); running the vitest probes in one batched invocation instead of ten; or a --only-static mode for the parity arm, whose property is about the SEARCH engine and does not need the cmd probes at all. Do NOT solve it by making probes cheaper in a way that stops them measuring the consequence — that is the failure this backlog exists to prevent.

verify.cmd: node -e "const fs=require('fs');let d;try{d=JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync('docs/BUILD-BACKLOG.json','utf8'))}catch{process.exit(79)}const rows=(d.entries||[]).filter(e=>e.verify&&e.verify.kind==='cmd'&&e.id!=='LIVE-034');if(rows.length<15)process.exit(79);const RUNNER=/\\b(vitest|jest|playwright\\s+test)\\b|\\b(pnpm|npm|yarn)\\s+(run\\s+)?test\\b/;const bad=rows.filter(e=>RUNNER.test(e.verify.cmd)).map(e=>e.id);if(bad.length){console.error('probe(s) spawn a test runner: '+bad.join(', '));process.exit(1)}process.exit(0)"

entries.notes: Re-measured 2026-08-17, after the ten suite-spawning probes were rewritten to measure the same consequence in-process: the guard costs 6.2s, down from 23.1s on the same tree with the same clock. What is left, in order: PROG-DAWN9 2.8s, LIVE-014 1.2s (it runs check-labels.mjs over the whole tsx tree), every other probe under 350ms. THE PROBE BELOW USED TO TIME THE GUARD BY RUNNING THE GUARD, and that was wrong twice over. It was a FORK BOMB: the child ran this same probe, which spawned another child, without end; 55 live processes were counted on 2026-08-17, each orphaned chain outliving the run that started it. That, not the vitest spawns, is why backlog-contract.test.ts still timed out after its limit was raised to 240s. And even fenced against re-entry it doubled every invocation forever: 6.2s of probe work cost 12.5s of wall clock, here and in CI. So the row now probes the CAUSE instead — no verify.cmd may spawn a test runner — which costs milliseconds and cannot re-enter. The row cannot police itself, so its own id is excluded from that scan; a floor of 15 cmd probes makes an unreadable or reshaped file exit 79 rather than report a clean sweep of nothing. The WALL-CLOCK ceiling did not disappear with the timing probe: it moved to backlog-contract.test.ts's ripgrep-parity arm, which already runs the guard twice by design and now fails if either run exceeds 20s. Cause measured for free on every probe run, consequence measured for free in the suite that was paying for it anyway.

entries.title: The "Founding Business offer" email promises a rate that no longer exists
entries.detail:
FOUNDING_BUSINESS (lib/beta/launch-emails.ts, mirrored in lib/beta/email-templates.ts) is seeded into Email Studio as a campaign offering local businesses "A Founding Business gets its own Space to post events and offers and the lowest rate we will ever set, kept for good. Take the year before September 1". ADR-1067 removed the Business founding rate, so there is no price behind that promise: Business is a flat $29/mo, $290/yr, and the only beta rate in the catalog is Collective's unlisted $49/$490. Nothing is mis-sold TODAY because these are seeded drafts rather than sends, and the campaign links to /pricing rather than to a checkout at a named rate. But if it goes out as written it offers a founding rate the catalog cannot charge. Owner decides which: retire the email, or repoint the offer at Collective (whose rate IS grantable, and whose September 1 framing already matches). The badge and Space copy are reusable either way. NOT a code fix to guess at - the email is an offer, and which offer to make is the owner's call.

── 2026-08-19, AND THIS ROW'S CLOSE WAS INCOMPLETE. It was scoped to lib/beta/launch-emails.ts and lib/beta/email-templates.ts, and the exact sentence it reported removing was alive VERBATIM in a third file the close never looked at: lib/email-studio/presets.ts, in a preset named FOUNDING_BUSINESS_INVITE ('the lowest rate we will ever set, kept for good'). Its probe could never have caught it, because both files it read are now deleted and it returns indeterminate. The copy is fixed and the probe re-pointed at the file that actually carries the offer. The lesson is the row's own: a close scoped to the files you happened to grep is not a close, and the mitigation everyone reached for (nothing imports EMAIL_PRESETS outside its test) is the same dormancy this row judged unacceptable when it was filed.

entries.title: A SECOND path can still stamp a lifetime $19 on a Founding Business, and it is not the catalog
entries.detail: ADR-1067 removed the Business founding rate from the CATALOG, which is what the Stripe sync mints from. It does NOT touch FOUNDING_DEFAULT.business_monthly_cents in lib/pricing/founding.ts, still 1900. That constant is live on a different path: the beta founder push (ADR-875, tightened by ADR-880) runs space-subscriptions.ts -> beta-founding.ts -> grantFoundingStatus, which stamps locked_rate_cents on the new founding row from the amount the caller passes, FALLING BACK to business_monthly_cents when the caller does not know it (lib/founding/status.ts:281 and again on the update branch at :353). Those are LIFETIME terms - the rate and the marketplace take that Space keeps for good. IT CANNOT FIRE BY ACCIDENT TODAY: the grant returns no_window unless the `founding` pricing_settings row carries an explicit grace `until` date (betaGraceEndsAtMs returns null for empty), and that setting lives in production, which this container deliberately cannot read. So this is not "it is off" - it is "it is off unless you set it, and only you can see whether you did". THE DECISION IS THE OWNER'S, because it is not obviously the same question they answered. They said Business has normal pricing and only Collective gets a beta offer. But the Founding Business PROGRAM is a whole feature - badges, city caps, spots remaining - and killing its rate is not the same as declining to advertise a beta price. Either (a) set business_monthly_cents to 2900 so a Founding Business gets recognition at the normal rate, or (b) keep 1900 deliberately as a hand-granted lifetime term, the same shape as the Collective grant. Do NOT let it sit at 1900 by inattention: that is how a lifetime discount gets given away by a fallback.

entries.notes: Closed 2026-08-17. FOUNDING_DEFAULT.business_monthly_cents 1900 -> 2900. It was never a display number: grantFoundingStatus stamps it as locked_rate_cents when the caller passes no amount (lib/founding/status.ts:281 and :353), which is a LIFETIME term, so leaving it would have kept handing out a permanent $19 through a FALLBACK months after founding pricing came off every surface a customer sees. The probe asserts BOTH halves of "Business has normal pricing" - the catalog carries no founding rate AND the grant default equals the list rate - so fixing one and forgetting the other still fails. The Founding Business program is untouched: a Founding Business is now recognised at the normal rate.

entries.title: Two artifact gates exist but are not wired into postbuild, and a real build has now disproved one of them
entries.detail:
RE-STATED 2026-08-18 (ADR-1081). The row's SEQUENCING blocker is gone and its SUBSTANCE grew. The blocker was OWN-029's question about whether postbuild runs at all; a production log answered it (both prebuild and postbuild fire, and check:build-budget prints 6.04 GB across 499 functions), and vercel.json now pins buildCommand so a dashboard edit cannot take the lifecycle away. check:cache-budget was then wired in and TAKEN BACK OUT before merge. Its preview build measured 2.40 GiB raw and trimmed a 1520 MiB Turbopack cache, because the gate compares raw bytes on disk against Vercel's PACKED 1.50 GB ceiling and the two are ~2:1 apart, not the ~3% its header assumes. Its floor arm was correct (node_modules 933 MiB). The calibration is LIVE-048; this row still owns the WIRING of both gates. check:shell-weight has never printed on a completed build at all. Its one reading exited 1 naming lib/pricing/feature-meters.ts, on an artifact built plausibly BEFORE settings-panel.tsx moved five editor bodies behind dynamic(), and surface-summaries.ts mentions feature-meters only in a comment, so the failure is unconfirmed in BOTH directions. The 2026-08-17 attempt to run a real build here died collecting page data for /discover/cities/[citySlug], which needs Supabase credentials this container deliberately does not hold - but a PR's own PREVIEW BUILD runs the full postbuild and prints it, which is how check:cache-budget was caught. That is the route: wire, push, read the preview output, and only merge on green. TO CLOSE: both gates in postbuild, each landing in the same change as the preview build that printed it green.

2026-08-19, OWNER-APPROVED, HALF OF THIS IS NOW WIRED AND THE OTHER HALF IS NOT.

check:cache-budget runs in postbuild as `--warn-only`. This breaks a real deadlock rather than ignoring the rule: the ONLY thing that settles PACKED_PER_RAW is a reading from a real production artifact, and the only way to take that reading was to run on a real build. Wiring it blocking to get the reading is the 2026-08-11 incident reversed, which is what this row has always said. Warn-only is a third option that was not considered before: the script measures and prints, NEVER trims, and CANNOT exit non-zero -- not on the node_modules floor, not on its own crash. Those two guarantees are proven by MUTATION in scripts/check-cache-budget-warn-only.test.ts (8 tests): each case rewrites the script to force the condition and runs it for real, and each has a paired case asserting the same mutation DOES fail without the flag, so the guarantee cannot pass for the wrong reason. A structural arm also asserts the trim stays chained behind the warn-only branch, so no path leads from --warn-only to an rmSync.

A swallowed crash still gets a gate that notices it fired: the handler prints a 🔴 line naming the file and LIVE-035, so a broken measurement reads as broken rather than as absent.

⚠️ WARN-ONLY IS A STAGE, NOT A DESTINATION, and the same test locks that in. Its last assertion fails if postbuild ever invokes the script without --warn-only, so promoting it to blocking is a deliberate, reviewable line in a diff rather than a quiet edit to a package.json string. Promote it in the SAME change as the green build whose 'Uploading build cache [N GB]' line confirms the constant.

check:shell-weight is UNCHANGED and still unwired. Its one reading exited 1 naming lib/pricing/feature-meters.ts on an artifact built plausibly before five editor bodies moved behind dynamic(), so it is unconfirmed in BOTH directions and has no warn-only equivalent yet. This row closes when shell-weight is settled and cache-budget is promoted to blocking.

2026-08-19, SECOND HALF WIRED, SAME WAY AND FOR A SHARPER REASON. check:shell-weight now runs in postbuild as `--warn-only` alongside check:cache-budget. Its case for the stage is stronger than its sibling's: it has ONE reading in its whole life and that reading is unconfirmed in BOTH directions -- it exited 1 naming lib/pricing/feature-meters.ts on an artifact built plausibly BEFORE settings-panel.tsx moved five editor bodies behind dynamic(). So the first real thing it does may well be to report a leak, and blocking on that would fail a production deploy over a number nobody has verified.

In warn-only it measures, prints, and cannot exit non-zero: not on the byte budget, not on the fingerprint arm, not on a missing manifest, not on its own crash. Every failure path now routes through a single bail() helper, and scripts/check-shell-weight-warn-only.test.ts proves it by MUTATION -- each case forces the condition and runs the script for real, paired with a case asserting the same condition DOES fail without the flag.

🔴 THAT TEST CAUGHT A REAL HOLE WHILE IT WAS BEING WRITTEN, which is the whole argument for writing it. The uncaughtException handler was first placed next to fail(), two thirds down the file, so anything throwing during module evaluation before that point escaped it and exited 1 -- in postbuild, a dead deploy. The handler moved above all top-level work, and BOTH warn-only gates now assert that ordering, because the guarantee IS the ordering. check:cache-budget was checked for the same defect and was already safe.

scripts/check-shell-weight.test.ts carried an assertion that the gate was NOT in postbuild. It failed on this change, correctly, and was INVERTED rather than relaxed: the gate must now be present AND carry the flag, must not appear in the CI guards array, and must no longer be declared UNWIRED. Two files that cannot disagree about its state.

WHAT REMAINS FOR THIS ROW: both gates are measuring and neither can act. It closes when both are promoted to blocking, each in the same change as the green build that confirms its numbers. check:cache-budget's number is already confirmed on three builds (LIVE-048); check:shell-weight has not printed on a real artifact yet, and the first postbuild run after this merges is the one to read.

⚠️ AND THIS ROW'S PROBE HAD THE SAME DEFECT LIVE-029'S DID, found the same day on the same change. It asked only whether postbuild MENTIONS both gates. Wiring them warn-only made that true while the row stayed true, because a gate that measures and cannot act is not wired in the sense this row means. That is twice in one day that a probe measured PRESENCE where the row was about CONSEQUENCE -- the shape-not-truth failure four ADRs name, and evidently the easiest one to write by accident. Rewritten to require both gates present AND neither carrying --warn-only, so it agrees with the row today and passes only when an artifact regression can actually be stopped.

✅ THE FIX IS PROVEN, ON THE BUILD THAT SHIPPED IT. Preview deploy xpkMNeSxJCWTTn35uvCeoacVbM7n, 2026-08-19T17:05:44Z, PR #2183 -- the first artifact built with the chunk-root fix, and the first time check:shell-weight has produced an honest reading in its life:

       scanning 573 built chunk(s) under static/immutable/chunks; shell set = 21 chunk(s).
    ✅ check:shell-weight -- the shell's eager first-load JS is 1010 KB across 21 chunks,
       under the 1400 KB budget.
       8 admin module bodies checked, all lazy; read 494 client-reference manifests;
       positive control present.

EVERY PART OF THE DIAGNOSIS HELD. The root really is static/immutable/chunks (the deployment adapter's supportsImmutableAssets), which is why the old hardcoded static/chunks glob matched nothing; 573 chunks are now scanned where zero were before. The literal that the previous build said 'appears in NO built chunk' is present -- 'positive control present' plus all 8 module bodies resolving to `lazy` rather than `absent` is Arm B making a real distinction for the first time. It was never a Turbopack transform and never an unreachable module: it was the scan.

⚠️ ARM A'S FIRST REAL NUMBER IS 1010 KB, NOT 957 KB. The 957 figure (2026-08-17) came from a local build and is superseded. 1010 KB against the 1400 KB ceiling is 72% consumed, 390 KB clear, across 21 chunks rather than the 20 previously assumed. Nothing regressed -- this is the first measurement taken on the artifact users actually download, so it replaces the estimate rather than contradicting it.

entries.title: The viewport bucket is normalized, posted, and then dropped on write
entries.detail: Found while writing the vitals route test (LIVE-030), not by looking for it. lib/analytics/vitals.ts exports vitalProps() and its comment says the sink reads the wire shape from it, but app/api/vitals/route.ts builds the props bag INLINE and omits `vp` - the viewport bucket (Lift 7d, ADR-922). So the bucket is computed on the client, posted over the wire, and then silently dropped on write: it never reaches interaction_events, and every query that would segment Core Web Vitals by viewport returns nothing. Nothing fails, which is why it survived. NOT FIXED IN THAT PASS DELIBERATELY: editing the route invalidates its digest in scripts/authz-route-ledger.json, which forces a re-read of the handler's authorization verdict, and that is a separate act from a field fix. The test asserts a SUBSET of allowed prop keys rather than an exact list, so it stays green when the fix lands and still fails if a person-level key is ever added.

The route now writes props: vitalProps(v) instead of a second copy of the same object literal, so the wire shape and the written shape cannot drift again - which is the actual cause, not the missing field. MY FIRST PROBE WAS WRONG IN AN INSTRUCTIVE WAY: it looked for 'vp' near the route's `props:` literal, so it kept failing AFTER the fix, because the fix DELETED the literal it was reading. A probe written against the broken shape can outlive the break. It now asserts the two things that must both hold - vitalProps still emits vp, and the route still calls it rather than hand-rolling the bag. The authz digest was re-recorded, not bypassed: editing the handler invalidated it by design, so the `public` verdict was re-read. Nothing about the boundary moved (no session, no headers or cookies, profile_id NULL on every row whatever the payload claims, which the route test asserts with an attacker-shaped body), and vp is a property of the PAGE VIEW rather than the person (ADR-922).

entries.title: Two eyebrow registers exist and neither is wrong: pick the one that wins
entries.detail: Surfaced by LIVE-025, and it is a design decision rather than a refactor, which is why it is not being made in code. There are TWO eyebrow implementations and nobody reconciled them. (1) app/globals.css locks the `eyebrow` utility at 0.75rem / 0.18em / bold, and 87 sites use it. (2) components/page-editor/blocks/kit.tsx exports an <Eyebrow> component with about 26 adopters rendering text-body-sm, 0.875rem - which is DAWN's DECLARED eyebrow size, i.e. precisely the half of the DAWN split that globals.css resolved DOWN to 0.75rem on 2026-08-05. So the block kit is not drifting by accident; it is rendering the value DAWN published, and the CSS is rendering the value this repo chose instead. Beyond those two there is a third de-facto register: 615 sites pair uppercase with a literal tracking, dominated by an 11px `text-2xs font-semibold uppercase tracking-wide text-muted`, and many of those are pill badges and dense table headers where 0.18em would widen the label past the pill that was sized to fit it. THE CALL: which size is the eyebrow - 0.75rem (globals.css, what most of the kit uses) or 0.875rem (DAWN's declaration, what the block kit renders)? Whichever loses gets retired, and its adopters move in a bounded sweep with a visual recapture. Deciding it also settles what goes back to DAWN in the next handoff, since design_handoff/PROD-AHEAD.md already carries the divergence.

verify.cmd: node -e "const fs=require('fs');const K='components/page-editor/blocks/kit.tsx',T='lib/theme/eyebrow-role.test.ts';if(!fs.existsSync(K)||!fs.existsSync(T))process.exit(79);const k=fs.readFileSync(K,'utf8'),t=fs.readFileSync(T,'utf8');if(k.indexOf('Eyebrow')<0)process.exit(79);const bad=[];const code=k.split(String.fromCharCode(10)).filter(function(x){var s=x.trim();return s.indexOf('//')!==0&&s.indexOf('*')!==0}).join(String.fromCharCode(10));if(code.indexOf('text-body-sm')>=0)bad.push('the block kit declares text-body-sm again: the retired 0.875rem eyebrow register is back');if(t.indexOf('composes the role in the atom')<0)bad.push('the assertion that the atom may not restate the role is gone from '+T);if(t.indexOf('never pairs the block-kit marker with the retired')<0)bad.push('the retired-size assertion is gone from '+T);if(bad.length){console.error(bad.join('; '));process.exit(1)}process.exit(0)"

entries.notes: DECIDED AND IMPLEMENTED 2026-08-18 (ADR-1075). Owner's call: 0.75rem wins. The block kit's <Eyebrow> atom now COMPOSES the `eyebrow` utility and declares none of the role, so an adopter can no longer pick a size by choosing an import. The framing worth keeping is the ADR's: the eyebrow had two implementations because it had two OWNERS, a class and an import. globals.css locked 0.75rem; the atom hand-rolled the same role at text-body-sm, 0.875rem - DAWN's DECLARED size, and precisely the half of DAWN's own split this repo resolved down on 2026-08-05. Two registers 17% apart and NEITHER was a mistake, which is exactly why it needed a decision rather than a refactor. Verified by breaking it, not on report: reintroducing 'text-body-sm font-bold uppercase tracking-eyebrow' inside the atom fails with 'the <Eyebrow> atom restates the role', and restoring goes green. Three assertions hold it, including a non-vacuity arm so a green over an empty scan is not a pass. The 608 literal-tracking sites are deliberately untouched and stay a ratchet: genuine eyebrows sit beside pill badges and dense table headers where 0.18em would widen a label past the pill it was sized to fit.

entries.title: Ten more client entry points still drag the service-role client into the browser graph
entries.detail: LIVE-009 fixed two instances and revealed the CLASS. lib/supabase/admin.ts is still statically reachable in the client layer from ten other 'use client' entry points, every one the same shape: a client component imports a constant or a small helper out of a module that also opens the service-role client, and the whole graph follows. The paths are via lib/crm/relationships, lib/crm/contacts-roster, lib/crm/pipeline, lib/personas, lib/walkthroughs, lib/billing/tips, lib/spaces/membership, lib/marketplace, lib/season-ranks -> lib/quest/completion-read, and lib/events/event-stats. THE FIX IS THE ONE LIVE-009 USED, and it is small per instance: extract the leaf the client actually needs into a dependency-free module, re-export it from the old home so no server caller changes, then put a real `import 'server-only'` on the original so the class FAILS THE BUILD instead of being re-litigated. The header comment saying 'Server-only' is what both LIVE-009 files had, and it stopped nothing. Worth doing in batches with a build between them, because `server-only` fails at compile and the failure names the importer, so each batch is self-diagnosing.

entries.notes: BATCH ONE DONE 2026-08-18: the three CRM paths are cut (relationships, contacts-roster, pipeline). BATCH TWO DONE 2026-08-18, and it closes the row: the remaining seven are cut the same way - the pure leaf the client actually needs moved to a dependency-free module (personas-core, walkthroughs-core, tips-core, membership-core, marketplace-core, event-stats-core), re-exported from its old home so no server caller changed, and the original took `import 'server-only'`. TWO OF THE TEN WERE NOT THE WORK THE ROW DESCRIBED. (1) lib/season-ranks.ts must NOT take the directive: it is pure rank vocabulary that ~20 client components import, including lib/community-roles which app-shell.tsx pulls onto every route under app/(main). Its ONLY impurity was one convenience re-export of journeysFinishedThisSeason; the fix was to REMOVE that line and guard lib/quest/completion-read.ts instead, repointing five server callers. Adding `server-only` to season-ranks - which the old probe demanded - would have broken the build. (2) An ELEVENTH path the row never listed: composer-shell.tsx -> lib/spaces/email-topics -> lib/comms/contact-preferences -> admin, for one constant; extracted to lib/comms/contact-topics.ts. 🔴 THE PROBE WAS REPLACED, NOT WIDENED. A hand-kept list of ten measured a subset and reported on the whole - the same instrument failure as batch one's, one level up - and it also PRESCRIBED A REMEDY (`server-only` in each named file) rather than measuring a consequence, which is how it came to demand the wrong fix for season-ranks. The row now probes scripts/check-client-server-boundary.mjs: it walks the real import graph and fails if ANY 'use client' module can statically reach lib/supabase/admin.ts, with no baseline and no allowlist. It is wired into the ci.yml guard array as check:client-boundary (guard-wiring.test.ts would have failed otherwise). PROVEN TO FIRE both ways before commit: repointing tip-button.tsx back at lib/billing/tips reported the server-only violation, and additionally stripping the directive reported the full path through to the admin client; restoring both returned it to green. It counts STATIC edges only: a dynamic `await import()` is a separate chunk and is this repo's deliberate, documented mitigation in page-chrome.ts and apps/overrides.ts. entries.title: One dropped TCP connection during prerender kills the whole deploy, and nothing retries
entries.detail:
OBSERVED, not theorised. The preview build of 656dac3 failed while the PRODUCTION build of the SAME COMMIT succeeded four minutes earlier. The failure: `TypeError: fetch failed / Caused by: Error: read ECONNRESET` on a Supabase read, which the reader wraps as DiscoverReadError and rethrows, and Next reports 'Export encountered an error on /discover/events/[slug]/page: breathe-connect-expand-2026-09-10, exiting the build.' One transient reset on one slug ended the export. WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND ONE FLAKY PREVIEW: `main` is protected and MERGING DEPLOYS TO PRODUCTION (AGENTS.md). This same read runs during the production export, so the same blip takes down a production deploy, and the only evidence would be a stack trace that looks like a code fault. The build is otherwise healthy - the report says 'No memory or disk space problems detected'. THE FIX IS NOT A BARE try/catch. Swallowing the error would silently ship a /discover with missing events, which is the fail-safe-with-no-gate pattern AGENTS.md names ('every fail-safe needs a gate that notices it fired'). The honest shape is a bounded retry with backoff around the read for RETRYABLE transport faults only (ECONNRESET, ETIMEDOUT, fetch failed), leaving a genuine query error - bad SQL, RLS denial, missing column - fatal exactly as it is now. If a retry is exhausted the build should still fail, loudly, with the slug named. A count of retries consumed belongs in the build log so a rising number is visible before it becomes an outage.

── 🔴 REOPENED IN CONSEQUENCE, THEN CLOSED AGAIN 2026-08-21 (LIVE-084, ADR-1095). THIS FIX NEVER RETRIED ANYTHING. The same failure recurred on the PRODUCTION build of eee84ba (dpl_2SRX2aYctYBXmZw1TaYyi1xBJtBy, 02:28:05Z): same route, same RPC, same ECONNRESET, and the build died 2 seconds into static generation with NO retry line in the log. Cause: isTransientDiscoverError guarded with `typeof e.code === 'string' && !TRANSIENT_RE.test(e.code)`, and supabase-js reports a transport failure as a resolved error whose code and hint are EMPTY STRINGS. `typeof '' === 'string'` is true, so the guard read "there is a code, therefore the database answered" and returned false on the exact shape this row existed to catch. Proven by replaying the verbatim error object through __retryForTest.attempt: ONE call, not three.

WHAT THIS ROW GOT WRONG IS NOT THE DESIGN, IT IS THE FIXTURE. The retry's shape, placement, thunk seam, refusal arm and exhaustion behaviour were all correct and all still stand. Every test built its error BY HAND, and every hand-built error either omitted `code` or set a real Postgres code, so the empty string was never on trial. A test that constructs its own input can only ever prove the author's model of the input. This row's probe is tightened accordingly: it now requires the production fixture, not merely that a retry exists.

verify.cmd: node -e "const fs=require('fs');const a='lib/discover.ts',b='lib/discover.test.ts';if(!fs.existsSync(a)||!fs.existsSync(b))process.exit(79);const s=fs.readFileSync(a,'utf8'),t=fs.readFileSync(b,'utf8');const wired=s.includes('isTransientDiscoverError')&&s.includes('RETRY_DELAYS_MS');const emptyCodeFixed=/const code = typeof e\\.code === 'string' \\? e\\.code\\.trim\\(\\) : ''/.test(s)&&s.includes(\"code !== '' &&\");const fixture=t.includes('PRODUCTION_KILLER')&&/code: ''/.test(t)&&t.includes('calls).toBe(3)');if(!wired||!emptyCodeFixed||!fixture){console.error('discover retry '+(wired?'':'not wired ')+(emptyCodeFixed?'':'empty-code guard missing ')+(fixture?'':'no production-shape fixture'));process.exit(1)}process.exit(0)"

entries.notes: DONE 2026-08-18. The discover read seam (lib/discover.ts listRead/detailRead) now retries TRANSIENT failures twice with 250/500ms backoff. The observed killer arrived RESOLVED, not thrown - supabase-js catches the fetch rejection and resolves with a synthetic error whose message carries the network cause - so the retry decision reads the error's SHAPE: network-ish (fetch failed/ECONNRESET/ETIMEDOUT/EAI_AGAIN/...) retries, a Postgres/PostgREST code never does, and empty data is NEVER retried (a detail-route empty result is a believed 404; retry-until-it-exists turns 404s into timeouts). Call sites pass thunks so each attempt builds a fresh PostgrestBuilder - re-awaiting one builder re-reads its settled failure. lib/discover.test.ts proves the retry FIRES (two transient failures then success = three calls) and REFUSES (deterministic error = one call), per the watch-it-fail rule. || TIGHTENED 2026-08-21: the probe now also requires the empty-code guard AND a test fixture carrying `code: ''`. The old probe passed for three days over a retry that had never fired once.

entries.title: /the-lab and /the-community emit no FAQPage, and have not since their templates landed
entries.detail:
Found while retiring the-lab's coded body, and it is NOT caused by that retirement. THE_LAB_FAQ carried five Q&A and its faqSchema() call sat on the LEGACY branch of `data ? <BlockRender/> : <Legacy/>` - the branch that could never be taken, because the template is a static literal and `data` is never null. So /the-lab has emitted no FAQPage structured data since the template landed. The retirement deleted the source copy; it did not change what Google sees, which was already nothing. MEASURED, and NARROWER THAN FIRST REPORTED: lib/page-editor/templates/the-quest.ts contains 1 Accordion block and the-lab.ts contains 0. the-quest is therefore FINE - its Accordion emits the FAQPage through BlockDocJsonLd, exactly as its own code comment says. This row is /the-lab alone. THE FIX IS A CONTENT DECISION, not a schema patch: adding faqSchema back without visible Q&A on the page would assert markup for copy a visitor cannot see, which CONTENT-VOICE section 8b forbids and Google penalises. The honest fix is an Accordion block in the-lab's template carrying the five questions, which emits the FAQPage as a consequence of rendering them. That MOVES PIXELS on /the-lab across four skins and two viewports, so it needs a baseline recapture in the same PR. The five drafted answers are good and are preserved in git history at the retirement commit.

── RE-MEASURED 2026-08-19 in a premise sweep (ADR-1082), and it HOLDS. Confirmed against PRODUCTION HTML rather than the tree: https://frequencylocal.com/the-lab serves 6 application/ld+json blocks (Article, BreadcrumbList, WebPage, WebSite, Organization, Place, ImageObject) and ZERO FAQPage. lib/page-editor/templates/the-lab.ts still holds 0 Accordion blocks; the-quest.ts holds one. The premise is confirmed live, not merely in source. Still blocked on the visual baseline recapture, which needs VERCEL_AUTOMATION_BYPASS_SECRET.

── RE-AUDITED 2026-08-19 and the 'this row is /the-lab alone' conclusion is WRONG. /the-community has the identical defect: lib/page-editor/templates/the-community.ts carries ZERO Accordion blocks, and in app/(marketing)/the-community/page.tsx its faqSchema(COMMUNITY_FAQ) call sits on the same unreachable legacy branch, because getTemplate('the-community') is a static literal and `data` is never null. The template file SAYS SO ITSELF ('The FAQPage is deliberately NOT emitted here: this template contains no Accordion'), in a comment that landed 2026-08-13, six days before the re-measure that concluded /the-lab alone. Also corrected: the-quest.ts carries THREE Accordion blocks, not one. Source-confirmed only for /the-community (this session's egress to frequencylocal.com is blocked); /the-lab was confirmed against live HTML.

THE OLD PROBE WAS A WORD SEARCH. It passed on the string 'Accordion' appearing in the template, which an Accordion with zero items also satisfies while the page still emits nothing: the block filters out any pair missing an answer. It now requires a question/answer pair in BOTH templates.

── CODE HALF DONE 2026-08-19. Both templates now carry an Accordion whose visible Q&A emit the FAQPage (CONTENT-VOICE 8b). /the-lab: the five THE_LAB_FAQ Q&A recovered VERBATIM from the retirement commit's parent (c3228d76c^) into tl-faq, placed between the PhotoTrio and the PillarNav, mirroring the-quest. /the-community: FOUR of COMMUNITY_FAQ's five recovered verbatim into tc-faq (before the ink close); the cost answer was NOT carried forward: 'The personal tier, Crew, is ${CREW_NOTE.foundingLabel} a month' quotes the pay-what-you-want FLOOR as a fixed price, which the CREW_NOTE contract forbids (every surface must read as 'from'); flagged for the owner rather than rewritten. The dead faqSchema(COMMUNITY_FAQ) call on the route's unreachable legacy branch was deleted (getTemplate is a static well-formed literal, data is never null); the rest of that rung is LIVE-006's work. the-lab.test.ts and the-community.test.ts assert one Accordion, all pairs well-formed under the block's own filter, and the recovered questions verbatim. REMAINS before close: pixels move on both routes across four skins and two viewports, so the visual-baseline recapture (needs VERCEL_AUTOMATION_BYPASS_SECRET, dispatched in CI after this lands) plus a look at the rendered pages. THE PROBE NOW MEASURES BOTH HALVES: with the Accordion landed, the old Q&A-only probe passed while the row stayed open, which check-backlog rightly calls a contradiction, and the fix the gate itself names is correcting a probe that proves the wrong thing. It still requires the Accordion q/a pairs, and now also that each route's 8 committed baselines under test/e2e/__screenshots__/visual.spec.ts are no older than the template (a dirty template with clean baselines, or baselines whose last commit predates the template's, fails with 'recapture needed'). The probe goes green in the recapture commit, which is when this row closes.

── PROBE HARDENED 2026-08-19: CI checks out depth=1, where every file's last commit is HEAD, so the baseline-freshness half passed vacuously and the open row read as done. A shallow clone now reports indeterminate (exit 79) instead of a fake verdict; the freshness half is enforced wherever real history exists.

── RE-MEASURED 2026-08-20 (emboss capture, PR #2196): HALF TRUE IN PRODUCTION. /the-lab renders the accordion (its 8 visual baselines changed and its FAQPage emits — the route serves the CODE TEMPLATE because its pages row is an unpublished draft). /the-community does NOT: the live page serves a PUBLISHED pages row from 2026-07-13 (13 blocks, owner-authored in the editor), which wins over the template by design (lib/page-editor/data.ts), so #2190's accordion never reached that route. Completing this row on /the-community means adding the 4-question Accordion block to the OWNER'S published document (or the owner publishing it from the editor) — a content edit to an owner-authored live page, so it is the owner's call, asked 2026-08-20. The freshness probe stays honestly red on the-community until then.

── CLOSED 2026-08-20. The /the-community blocker was the owner-published pages row that shadowed the code template; this session confirmed that row was a corrupted verbatim template-copy (identical 13 block types/ids, no SEO overrides) and DELETED it, so the route now serves the code template (the-community.ts) with its tc-faq Accordion, exactly like /the-lab. entries.title: The AI help index silently stopped re-indexing: every run since 2026-08-13 died before doing any work
entries.detail: help-index.yml re-embeds the help centre into help_chunks on every merge to main touching content/help/**, and runs with NO pnpm install on purpose: the pipeline reads local Markdown with fs and embeds over HTTP. lib/help/content.ts later gained `import { cache } from 'react'` for per-request memoisation - a real win for the app - and from that moment the indexer died on ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND: Cannot find package 'react', imported from lib/help/content.ts, BEFORE reading a single article. MEASURED, not inferred: the six most recent runs on main (2026-08-13 02:32, 03:28, 08-14 01:26, 08-16 19:53, 08-18 03:01) are ALL failure, and the 03:01 log names react explicitly. The secrets ARE configured - the log shows NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL and SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY as ***, so it cleared the skip guard and then crashed. Nobody noticed for five days because the help PAGES render straight from Markdown regardless; only AI search went stale, and stale search is indistinguishable from search. FIXED by splitting the dependency-free readers into lib/help/content-core.ts (node builtins only) and leaving cache() in content.ts, which composes it. PROVED by running the indexer in a directory with no node_modules at all: it now resolves every import, parses the content, and reaches the embed HTTP call. OPEN CONSEQUENCE, owner action: this fix does not touch content/help/**, so merging it does NOT trigger a re-index. The index is stale for every help article added or edited since 2026-08-13 until someone runs the workflow once by hand (Actions > help-index > Run workflow).
