entries.title: The midnight skin's dark overrides never match on the <html> path
entries.detail:
PREMISE EXPIRED, and the row's own probe was the dangerous part. RE-MEASURED 2026-08-19: app/globals.css:772-773 already authors the dark override as a SELECTOR LIST — the compound .dark[data-skin="midnight"] for the <html> path AND the descendant .dark [data-skin="midnight"] for the shell-root path. git blame dates the compound line to 656dac3, 2026-08-17, two days before this row was still being carried as open. The row claimed three descendant-form selectors; there is exactly ONE rule block, and the other two matches are COMMENTS (globals.css:611 and :634), which is how the count of three was arrived at. The row also said app/layout.tsx:142-143 asserts the opposite of the behaviour; it now reads 'the skin CSS selectors match both <html> and the shell div', which is correct. No pixels move and no baseline recapture is needed, because the work shipped two days ago.

THE PROBE WAS WRONG IN THE DIRECTION THAT BREAKS THE PRODUCT, which is why this is worth more than a status flip. It required ZERO occurrences of .dark [data-skin= and failed while any remained. But the descendant form is REQUIRED: data-skin lands on two different elements (the pre-paint script writes the freq-skin preview onto documentElement, the authed shell re-stamps it on the shell root), so deleting the descendant selector to satisfy the probe would have silently killed midnight-dark on the authed shell — the same class of failure as LIVE-008, in the mirror. A row whose probe can only be closed by breaking the code is worse than an unprobed row: it reads as an instruction. Anyone working the list top-down would have done it.

THE CONSEQUENCE IS ALREADY MACHINE-PROVEN, and by something better than a grep. lib/theme/skin-dom-selectors.test.ts (written for LIVE-008) parses the real selector list out of the real sheet and feeds it to a real selector engine in jsdom, against BOTH DOM shapes, for EVERY registered skin, plus a light-mode leak check. It runs in pnpm test. skins.test.ts alone would not have caught this: it greps globals.css for the words '.dark [data-skin="<id>"]', which is shape, not truth, and its own neighbour's header says so.

THE NEW PROBE measures both halves statically: for every non-default id in lib/theme/skins.ts it strips comments, splits the skin's dark selector list, and requires the compound AND the descendant form to each be present. Verified to fail both ways before being committed — delete the compound and it reports the <html> preview path, delete the descendant and it reports the authed shell root. It does not spawn a test runner (LIVE-034).

verify.cmd: node -e "const fs=require('fs');const S='lib/theme/skins.ts',C='app/globals.css';if(!fs.existsSync(S)||!fs.existsSync(C))process.exit(79);const ids=[...fs.readFileSync(S,'utf8').matchAll(/id:\\s*'([a-z0-9-]+)'/g)].map(m=>m[1]).filter(i=>i!=='default');if(!ids.length)process.exit(79);const css=fs.readFileSync(C,'utf8').replace(/\\/\\*[\\s\\S]*?\\*\\//g,'');const pre=[...css.matchAll(/(?:^|[};])\\s*([^{}@;]+?)\\s*\\{/g)].map(m=>m[1].replace(/\\s+/g,' ').trim());const bad=[];for(const id of ids){const sels=pre.filter(p=>p.includes('[data-skin=\"'+id+'\"]')&&p.includes('.dark')).flatMap(p=>p.split(',')).map(s=>s.trim()).filter(Boolean);if(!sels.some(s=>s==='.dark[data-skin=\"'+id+'\"]'))bad.push(id+': no compound .dark[data-skin] — the dark block no-ops on the <html> preview path');if(!sels.some(s=>s==='.dark [data-skin=\"'+id+'\"]'))bad.push(id+': no descendant .dark [data-skin] — the dark block no-ops on the authed shell root');}if(bad.length){console.error(bad.join('\\n'));process.exit(1)}process.exit(0)"

entries.title: Sign-in has no loading state, no rate limit, and loses the deep link
entries.detail: CLOSED 2026-08-18. Three of the four things this row named are fixed; the fourth was ALREADY fixed and the row had not caught up. (1) NO PENDING STATE, and this was the correctness half rather than the polish half: pressing Send magic link made the page sit still for as long as the mail provider took, the instinct is to press again, and a second press makes Supabase issue a NEW one-time token and INVALIDATE the first - so a member who taps twice out of impatience kills the link they are about to open, and nothing on screen explains why. Both forms now submit through app/sign-in/submit.tsx, a client leaf whose useFormStatus drives Button's loading prop: aria-busy, disabled as the re-entrancy guard, and the label left untouched so the control cannot change width (INTERACTION-STATES section 4, rules 3 and 4). (2) NO RATE LIMIT: three buckets now - by IP (the spray, and account enumeration), by lower-cased mailbox (the inbox flood, and the Supabase mail quota; without the case fold the per-address ceiling is free to double), and a looser IP bucket on the Google path, which sends no mail of ours. All three pass whenUnconfigured 'allow', a NEW option on lib/rate-limit.ts. That option is the load-bearing decision: the limiter FAILS CLOSED in production when Upstash is absent, which is right for a public write and catastrophic here, because one expired KV token would deny every sign-in and every sign-up on a product that is otherwise up (ADR-1041). (3) THE ERROR BOX rendered decodeURIComponent(searchParams.error) straight onto the page. React escapes it, so it was never script injection; it is CONTENT injection, which on a login form is the more useful attack - anyone could send /sign-in?error=Your%20account%20is%20locked.%20Call%20555-0100 and the product rendered that sentence, in its own error styling, on its own sign-in page. Two of the three writers also passed Supabase's raw error.message through, putting a vendor's wording on the one screen a member is most likely to give up on. The query string now carries a CODE from a closed set and app/sign-in/errors.ts owns the words; an unrecognised code renders our generic line, which is what CLOSES the surface rather than narrowing it. (4) DEEP-LINK CARRY was already done, and the row's own premise was stale: #2132 taught proxy.ts to set ?next=, and /sign-in has re-validated it into the fq_post_login cookie ever since. Same stale-blocker shape as LIVE-012, found the same way - by reading the code before acting on the row. Still NOT in scope, each a separate decision: passwords/passkeys as a third door (owner), the PKCE cross-device magic-link failure (needs a flow design, not a patch), and Captcha stays OFF (the client sends no token; enabling it breaks sign-in).

entries.title: The beta induction is renamed Funnels and moved to /join, so the front door was replaced, never removed
entries.detail:
CLOSED 2026-08-19 by ADR-1090, and the closing shape is not the one the row predicted. The row guarded a teardown-at-launch: delete app/onboarding/beta/** together with a replacement sign-up route, never alone. What actually happened is the owner re-decided the feature's fate: the induction is not throwaway, it IS the sign-up platform, named Funnels, and its honest home is /join. The rename moved app/onboarding/beta/** to app/join/(induction)/** and folded the /beta/<slug> splash into app/join/[slug], with permanent 308s from every old URL (next.config.ts). Nothing was deleted alone; the front door moved and the old addresses forward to it.

BOTH PROBE HALVES NOW HOLD, AND FOR THE RIGHT REASON: app/onboarding/beta is gone because its contents live under app/join, and app/join is a real sign-up route — the walk from /join/<slug> (splash) through /join (induction) to /join/complete (account created) was read end-to-end in the rename PR. There is still no separate /sign-up route and none is needed: Funnels are the standard sign-up path this row said had to exist before the beta-named directory could go.

THE ROW'S ORIGINAL PREMISE ('it says so itself: TEMPORARY, deleted at launch') EXPIRED with the owner's Funnels directive — the temporary framing was ADR-068's, and ADR-1090 supersedes it for the machinery (the Beta PROGRAM copy, BETA_MEMBERS_GET_CREW and the /beta page, is what still flips at GA). The probe is kept verbatim: it still fails if anyone ever removes app/join without a replacement under app/sign-up or app/(marketing)/join, which is this row's rule outliving its subject.

entries.title: app_instances: keep it dark until E0, or retire it until E0 re-creates it

The table shipped ahead of its code: 0 rows, tenancy policies applied, and exactly one non-generated reference in the tree (components/admin/library/apps-lane.tsx). E0 absorbs A2 and builds its writers, so the decision is cheap and binary: leave the empty policied table in place as E0's landing pad (costs nothing, risks a second library_usages — a table someone assumes is live because it exists), or drop it and let E0 re-create it from its migration. Either answer closes this row; what must not continue is the unowned middle.

That reference is a JSX COMMENT, not a read: "{/* TODO(LP3/LP5): wire library_usages ... The where-referenced backbone lands with app_instances. */}". A tree-wide `grep "from('app_instances')"` returns nothing, and the table holds 0 rows.

So the "drop it and let E0 re-create it" option is cheaper than this row prices it: deleting the table breaks no code path, because no code path touches it. The decision is unchanged and still the owner's; only the cost of one side of it moved.

── DECIDED 2026-08-19: owner said "Do best practice," which the row's own text defines: a policied empty table nothing reads is a second library_usages waiting to be trusted, so it is DROPPED and E0 re-creates it with its writers. entries.title: ADR-914 reversed the sell-wall: the Market is open to free members, the Crew gates stay
entries.detail: ADR-914 (2026-07-30) reversed ADR-913 the SAME DAY: a free Member CAN sell, tickets and donations and payouts, day one, no upgrade, and the principle is "never gate the transaction, gate the repeat". The rate became a seven-rung ladder: free Member 10%, Crew 8%, free Space 10%, Business 5%, Collective 3%, Non Profit 0%, Independent 0%. THE DOC HALF IS DONE (2026-08-19): the false bodies were corrected IN PLACE, reversed claims struck through with dated notes citing ADR-914, rates verified against NETWORK_TAKE_RATE_DEFAULT (lib/billing/pricing-keys.ts:194-202, mirrored by lib/pricing/defaults.ts take_rate). Fixed: COMMUNITY-COLLECTIVE-STRATEGY.md (the "rungs are gone" amendment paragraph, the section-4 tier table's "Does not sell"/"cannot sell"/Collective 5% cells, the buy-down bullet, and the struck "billing_live OFF" status line); COLLABORATION-AND-UPGRADE-FUNNEL.md (section 4 Sell row "RSVPs only" cells now 10%/10%, section 3 "Selling IS a wall" paragraph reversed, Collective 3%, section 5 "today the walls only bite once billing turns on" struck, banner "billing_live OFF" struck); and the sweep's third teachers: PRICING-OPERATIONS.md (rule 3 "a free Member cannot sell", the ladder table, the console Member % bullet), OPERATOR-FUNNELS.md section 7 break-even premise, COMMUNITY-COLLECTIVE-BUILD-PLAN.md section A point 2, BUSINESS-SPACE-BACKEND-SURVEY.md take-rate model paragraph. Help center was already right (content/help/spaces/plans-and-pricing.md teaches ADR-914). WHAT REMAINS IS THE OWNER DECISION THE ROW ALWAYS WAS: (a) the Crew-gates half - PRICING.md's ADR-908 Crew table still gates hosting past one Circle, publishing past one Journey or three Practices, charging for an event, and entry points, four help articles tell members so, and that is the "membership fully accessible" question (ADR-1084); (b) the two hard Market walls that contradict ADR-914 in live code (app/(main)/market/sell/page.tsx "Selling is a paid feature", app/(main)/marketplace/commerce-actions.ts redirect('/upgrade')), recorded as OPEN in VALUE-LADDER.md and left standing here because opening the Market is a product call, not a doc fix. Deciding the sell-wall docs and deciding the Crew gates was one decision, not two - the docs now teach ADR-914; the gates await the owner. ── ✅ OWNER RULING 2026-08-24: open the Market, leave the five Crew feature gates alone. Blast radius measured first — the Market held 2 listings in the entire product, and 15 of the 16 free members have never logged in (0 lifetime Gems, 20 lifetime Zaps across all 16), so no wall here was costing anything measurable. It was still a live contradiction with a written ADR, which is why it moved. THREE hand-rolled isPaid(realMembershipTier) walls removed, all OUTSIDE FEATURE_GATES where no gate audit or /pricing cell could see them: market/sell/page.tsx (the 'Selling is a paid feature' FocusTemplate), marketplace/commerce-actions.ts createMakerProductAction (redirect('/upgrade')), and A THIRD THE ROW NEVER NAMED — draftMakerProductCopyAction, whose only rationale was mirroring the creation gate, and which would otherwise have left a Vera door that silently did nothing for the member who may now list. None was replaced by a gate key: the ruling is that there is no wall here to make visible. THE RATE DOES THE WORK THE WALL PRETENDED TO, traced end to end: checkout threads the payee's REAL membership_tier into memberTakeRateCents -> memberNetworkTakeRateBps, resolving a free seller to memberFree (1000bps, 10%) and Crew to member (800bps, 8%), 0% on the seller's own audience. The lookup asks isPaid, an ALLOW-LIST, so null/undefined/a typo all price at the HIGHER rung — ADR-914's deliberate direction, re-verified. ⚠️ TWO THINGS FOUND AND DELIBERATELY LEFT, both reported rather than smuggled in: canTakePayments('profile') is false, so a member listing is connect-only and no member Market sale settles in-app yet — an owner_kind rule, not a tier, so a Crew member is blocked identically; and canReceivePayouts gates Stripe onboarding on role-or-persona, so a plain free Member cannot open the funnel ADR-914 wants triggered at first sale. Opening the Market opened the LISTING; the SALE still needs those two. check:templates baseline raised by one through the sanctioned path with a reason: market/sell's FocusTemplate WAS the wall, so the page now joins classifieds/new and services/new as a server page delegating to a Spark.

entries.notes: Probed in-process rather than by spawning the 15-test free-seller suite, because LIVE-034 forbids a verify.cmd that runs a test runner. The mutation-proven suite (app/(main)/marketplace/free-seller.test.tsx, 15 tests, exercising the REAL page function and the REAL server action against a free-tier profile) runs in `pnpm test` and is the actual guard. The probe measures both directions the ruling has: the walls are gone AND the rate that replaces them is still 1000bps AND the five gates that were ruled to STAY are still there — so a later change that quietly re-walls, zeroes the free rung, or drops a Crew gate all fail it.

entries.title: The check:backlog cost ceiling is asserted on wall clock, so a loaded box fails it instead of a slow probe
entries.detail: OBSERVED 2026-08-18, once, in a full `pnpm test` run: 'check:backlog took 23.8s, over its 20s budget. Something added expensive work to a probe.' Nothing had. MEASURED on the same tree, unloaded: origin/main 13.38s and 13.39s, the branch under test 13.49s and 13.50s. Three probes added that day (OWN-029, LIVE-029, LIVE-035, all single-file reads) cost about 110 ms between them, 0.8%, against 6.5s of headroom. A second full run of the identical tree passed. THE ASSERTION MEASURES THE WRONG QUANTITY. It spawns check:backlog and times its WALL CLOCK, from inside a suite that is at that moment running 838 test files across 4 cores. What it reads is contention, and contention is not a property of any probe. Its own message then sends the next reader hunting for expensive work that does not exist, and tells them - correctly, for the failure it was designed for - that raising the number is not the fix. So the honest failure mode and the noisy one are indistinguishable, on the one gate whose whole job is telling those two apart. The budget itself is right and should stay: LIVE-034 closed a real 24s regression and the ceiling is what stopped it recurring. What needs to change is the CLOCK. Measure the guard's CPU time rather than its elapsed time, or run this one assertion outside the parallel pool. NOT A FIX: raising GUARD_BUDGET_MS, which would blind the gate to the growth it exists to catch. CLOSED 2026-08-19. The clock is now CPU time, read from /proc/self/stat cutime+cstime, which is the CPU of REAPED CHILDREN and therefore captures the guard AND all ~60 probe subprocesses. process.cpuUsage() would NOT have worked: it reports only the measuring process, which is asleep inside execFileSync the whole time. MEASURED on a 4-core box with and without six spinning cores: wall 9.26s/9.61s unloaded vs 18.57s/17.29s loaded (nearly double), childCPU 12.04s/12.54s unloaded vs 12.50s/12.11s loaded (flat within 4%). 18.6s of wall against the old 20s ceiling is exactly how a green tree failed at 23.8s. Budget kept at 20s, now of CPU, against a measured 12.1-12.5s baseline. Linux-only, and it SKIPS elsewhere rather than falling back to the wall clock: asserting the wrong quantity is what produced the false failure, and a gate that cannot measure honestly on a platform should say nothing there (ADR-970). The probe sentinel moved from GUARD_BUDGET_MS to GUARD_BUDGET, because the constant is GUARD_BUDGET_CPU_MS now and the old sentinel would have exited 79 (cannot look) on the fixed tree.

entries.title: check:cache-budget's trim killed two builds: wrong threshold units, and it can delete the fetch cache
entries.detail: MEASURED, not suspected. The gate was wired into postbuild in #2159 and its preview build printed: 'TRIMMED the build cache before Vercel could reject it. What the build was about to hand back measured 2.40 GiB, over the 1.38 GiB trim point. drops the cheap half instead: .next/cache/turbopack (1520 MiB).' The wiring was reverted before merge. THE DEFECT: measure() sums raw bytes on disk; Vercel's 1.50 GB ceiling applies to the packed archive. On the same tree, raw 2.40 GiB versus a packed upload of 1.26-1.29 GB is about 2:1. The script's header asserts the two 'have run ~3% apart', and that sentence is the whole bug - everything downstream of it is arithmetic. Turbopack's cache compresses hard and is the dominant term, so the error scales with the half that grows. CONSEQUENCE, MEASURED RATHER THAN ESTIMATED, and it is worse than 'builds get slower'. The one trim this gate ever ran emptied .next/cache on claude/cache-gate, and the NEXT TWO BUILDS ON THAT BRANCH BOTH DIED: each compiled in ~2.4 minutes and then hung in 'Collecting page data using 3 workers', hitting BUILD_EXCEEDED_MAXIMUM_TIME at 46 minutes. Every other build that day was green, including four production deploys. A CONTROL separated the two suspects: claude/build-pin carried the identical vercel.json buildCommand line and nothing else, on a branch cut from main so its build restored a healthy cache, and it reported 'Build Completed in /vercel/output [59s]'. 59 seconds against two dead builds. The pin is exonerated; the emptied cache is the cause. A SECOND DEFECT, and it is the one that makes this M rather than S: .next/cache is not only Turbopack's compiler cache, it also holds the INCREMENTAL FETCH CACHE. Page-data collection prerenders hundreds of routes that each read Supabase; warm those reads are local, cold every one goes to the network and the build never finishes. The trim drops directories BIGGEST-FIRST rather than by name - deliberately, so a future growth elsewhere is still caught - and that generality is exactly what lets it delete the half the build cannot proceed without. Fixing the threshold is necessary and NOT sufficient: whatever the number becomes, the trim must drop the compiler cache BY NAME or drop nothing. The floor arm is unaffected and was correct: node_modules 933 MiB against 1.25 GiB. TO CLOSE, BOTH HALVES. (a) Make the trim drop only what is safe to lose - name the compiler cache rather than sorting by size - so a firing trim can never take the fetch cache with it. (b) Express the trim point in the units Vercel applies. Measuring the packed size means packing, which is not free on a build; the cheaper honest route is a calibration constant derived from SEVERAL real builds - raw measured by this script, packed read off the build log's 'Uploading build cache [N GB]' line - carried in the file with its measurements and its date, so it can be re-checked rather than trusted. Then re-wire under LIVE-035, in the same change as a preview build that prints it green. NOT A FIX: raising TRIM_AT_GIB to a number that happens to stop it firing, which would leave the units wrong and the gate blind at a different size. A NOTE ON THIS ROW'S OWN PROBE, because it made the mistake twice while being written. First it matched the word 'calibration', which the commit had just added to the file's header explaining the bug - a grep that passes by existing. Rewritten to require a declared CONSTANT, it then matched nothing even with the constant present: it stripped block comments first, and this file's header documents the globs Vercel caches (node_modules/**, .next/cache/**), so a slash next to a star opened a comment that ran to the next close token and blanked the declaration. That is the same defect CORPUS_BASIS strip-comments@2 was written for in the adoption scanner. It now strips line comments only.

verify.note: ── PROBE TIGHTENED 2026-08-24 (HYG-016). It used to assert 'exactly one rmSync in the file', a PROXY for the invariant that actually matters: deletes INTO .next/cache are restricted to the named compiler list and can never reach the fetch cache. When check:cache-budget gained a second, unrelated delete — orphaned pnpm store entries under node_modules/.pnpm — the proxy fired and the invariant was untouched. It now classifies every rmSync by its TARGET: exactly one may name cacheDir/.next/cache and it must sit inside the COMPILER_CACHE_DIRS loop, and every other delete must name node_modules/.pnpm. That is strictly stronger than the count it replaced — the new delete path is pinned too, so an edit that repoints it at the cache fails this row rather than passing it.

entries.notes:
Closed 2026-08-19 (ADR-1086). BOTH defects, because fixing either one alone still leaves a gate that kills builds. (a) THE TRIM NAMES THE COMPILER CACHE. COMPILER_CACHE_DIRS is turbopack, rspack, webpack, swc, read out of next/dist/build/webpack-config.js rather than guessed, and the trim loop iterates THAT list instead of the size-sorted cacheParts. A directory it does not name cannot be removed however large it grows, so the incremental fetch cache is out of reach by construction rather than by ordering. NEVER_TRIM_DIRS (fetch-cache, images) is the second belt: if a future edit ever puts a protected name into the compiler list, the whole trim refuses to run and says so, instead of quietly repeating 2026-08-18. Anything under .next/cache the file does not recognise is now REPORTED and KEPT, which is the honest version of the generality the biggest-first loop was reaching for. (b) THE THRESHOLD IS IN VERCEL UNITS. PACKED_PER_RAW = 0.50 converts raw bytes on disk to the packed archive Vercel weighs, and the trim point is TRIM_AT_PACKED_GB = 1.50 GB ceiling minus a 0.10 GB reserve, in decimal GB because that is what Vercel prints. DERIVATION, carried in the file with its date: raw 2.40 GiB = 2.58 GB measured by this script on preview build GyKdz12oPgfc5roSqmv6F8Nq3nyK, against packed uploads of 1.26 / 1.28 / 1.29 GB on three production builds and 1.33 GB on claude/build-pin, all 2026-08-18. That is 0.49-0.52, rounded to 0.50. IT IS MARKED PROVISIONAL IN THE FILE AND THE WEAKNESS IS NAMED RATHER THAN AVERAGED AWAY: the raw reading and the packed readings come from DIFFERENT builds of equivalent trees, because the one build that had a raw reading had its cache trimmed before it was packed. So every run now prints the raw figure and the ratio it applied, next to an instruction to compare them with the "Uploading build cache [N GB]" line the same build prints. The first green preview build under LIVE-035 is what settles it. Sanity check on the number: the 2026-08-18 preview build measured 2.40 GiB raw, which this arithmetic puts at 1.29 GB packed, against a 1.40 GB trim point. The gate would NOT have fired, which is what the production upload lines say actually happened. PROVED ON FIXTURES, sparse files so the sizes are real to lstat and free on disk. A 3.63 GiB tree drops turbopack only, stops the moment the estimate is under the trim point, and leaves fetch-cache, images, swc and an unrecognised directory standing. A tree whose fetch-cache alone is 2 GiB drops both compiler caches, is still over, and says STILL OVER instead of deleting the fetch cache. With the two lists deliberately overlapped, nothing is deleted at all. The floor arm is untouched and still exits 1 at 1.27 GiB of node_modules. The closing line now states which side of the ceiling the estimate lands on in BOTH directions, because the first draft printed a green "under the ceiling" over a number that was over it. THE PROBE MEASURES THE CONSEQUENCE, and it was run against seven mutants: the pre-fix file (fails on every arm), fetch-cache added to the compiler list, the loop put back on cacheParts, the calibration constant renamed to something unnamed, TRIM_AT_PACKED_GB reverted to TRIM_AT_GIB, fetch-cache dropped from NEVER_TRIM_DIRS, and the file deleted (79, cannot tell). It is static, spawns no test runner, and strips LINE comments only, because this file documents globs like node_modules/** and a block-comment strip blanks the declarations. Its sharpest arm is structural rather than textual: the file's ONLY rmSync must sit inside a loop over COMPILER_CACHE_DIRS. NOT DONE HERE, DELIBERATELY: the gate stays OUT of postbuild and out of every workflow. LIVE-035 owns the wiring and the rule it is keeping is the one this file already broke once, that a build-blocking gate which has never seen a real artifact is the 2026-08-11 incident reversed. NOT VERIFIABLE FROM THIS CONTAINER: the constant itself. No build here can produce a packed figure, so 0.50 rests on two readings taken from different builds, and the file says so in the comment rather than presenting it as measured.

✅ THE CONSTANT IS SETTLED, 2026-08-19, AND IT WAS WRONG IN THE UNSAFE DIRECTION. The warn-only stage (LIVE-035) produced what this row said it could not have: a SINGLE build that printed both halves. Preview build 3jeNVZxuUy7thPjXpazjMC6yHwVo, on the very PR that wired warn-only, measured 2.34 GiB raw (node_modules 933 MiB + turbopack 1459 MiB) = 2.513 GB decimal, and Vercel then printed 'Uploading build cache [1.32 GB]'. 1.32 / 2.513 = 0.5254.

The provisional 0.50 UNDER-estimated the packed size by 5.1%. That is the dangerous direction: the gate would have believed it had more headroom than it did and trimmed LATER than intended, and a cache that reaches Vercel over the ceiling is discarded WHOLE, node_modules included. The 2026-08-18 defect erred the other way and merely cost a cold compile. Both errors were real; only one of them loses the install cache.

PACKED_PER_RAW is now 0.53, rounded UP from the measured 0.5254 on purpose, because over-estimating costs a cold compile and under-estimating costs the whole cache. The limit that has NOT changed: it is still a whole-archive ratio, and node_modules and the Turbopack cache do not compress alike, so a tree whose mix moves a long way from this one can still drift. Every run prints the raw figure so the pair can be re-read on any build.

⚠️ HEADROOM IS TIGHTER THAN THE EARLIER READINGS SUGGESTED. 1.32 GB against the 1.50 GB ceiling is 12% clear; the 2026-08-18 production reads of 1.26 GB looked like 16%. That gap is exactly what LIVE-029 is about, and it is the argument for promoting the gate to blocking.

CONFIRMED ON A SECOND BUILD, INDEPENDENTLY, MINUTES LATER. Preview build BFrLfowMz2KHy4u39JDdizF1aacZ (PR #2179) is the first build to RUN the corrected 0.53, and it predicted its own upload exactly:

    estimated  1.35 GB packed  (2.37 GiB raw = 2.545 GB, node_modules 933 MiB + turbopack 1493 MiB)
    actual     1.35 GB

Two builds, taken 8 minutes apart on different trees with different cache sizes: ratios 0.5254 and 0.5305, mean 0.528. 0.53 sits between them, which is what a settled constant looks like rather than one fitted to a single reading. The whole-archive caveat stands, because both builds carried a similar MIX (933 MiB node_modules against ~1.4-1.5 GiB turbopack); a tree that moves that ratio can still drift.

THIRD READING, SAME DAY, AND THE CONSTANT PREDICTED IT TOO. Preview build BTHo48M7P15rSJmZvsqjR7VDNsci: raw 2402 MiB (node_modules 933 + turbopack 1469) = 2.519 GB, predicted 1.33 GB at 0.53, uploaded 1.33 GB. True ratio 0.5281.

    build                              raw        predicted   actual   ratio
    3jeNVZxuUy7thPjXpazjMC6yHwVo       2.34 GiB   1.33 GB     1.32 GB  0.5254
    BFrLfowMz2KHy4u39JDdizF1aacZ       2.37 GiB   1.35 GB     1.35 GB  0.5305
    BTHo48M7P15rSJmZvsqjR7VDNsci       2.35 GiB   1.33 GB     1.33 GB  0.5281

Three builds, three different cache sizes, measured ratios spanning 0.5254-0.5305 with a mean of 0.528. 0.53 predicts two of them exactly and the third within the printed digit, and it sits inside its own evidence rather than on the edge of it. The whole-archive caveat is unchanged: all three carried a similar MIX (933 MiB node_modules against 1.46-1.49 GiB turbopack), so a tree that moves that ratio can still drift.

FIFTH READING, AND THE FIRST WHERE PREDICTION AND ACTUAL APPEAR IN THE SAME LOG. Preview xpkMNeSxJCWTTn35uvCeoacVbM7n, 2026-08-19T17:05:43Z: raw 2.28 GiB (node_modules 933 MiB + turbopack 1404 MiB), gate predicted 1.30 GB at 0.53, and the build's own 'Uploading build cache' line 70 seconds later read 1.29 GB. True ratio 0.5273.

Five builds, both targets, ratios 0.5254 / 0.5305 / 0.5281 / 0.5316 / 0.5273 -- span 0.006, mean 0.5286. The constant is settled; 0.53 has never been off by more than 0.01 GB on a real artifact. This is the half of LIVE-048 that is DONE. What remains is the other defect: the trim must drop the compiler cache BY NAME, because .next/cache also holds the incremental fetch cache and removing that is what hung two builds at BUILD_EXCEEDED_MAXIMUM_TIME.

entries.title: pr-compare is not a required check, and the file that said otherwise now records what is
entries.detail: CLOSED 2026-08-18. STEP (a) IS DONE AND IT IS THE ONLY STEP NOBODY IN THE REPO COULD DO: the owner opened ruleset 17640795 and read the required set off the settings page. IT IS FIVE CONTEXTS - checks, analyze, lint, test, Vercel. pr-compare is NOT among them, which confirms the observation this row was filed on: PR #2161 merged on auto-merge at 21:45:31 while its pr-compare check run was still in_progress, finishing green seven minutes after the merge, with exactly one commit status (Vercel's) on the merged SHA. STEP (b): .github/workflows/pr-compare-fallback.yml no longer opens by calling pr-compare REQUIRED. Its header now leads with the reading, the date, the set, and the merge that disproved the old claim, and it keeps the PR #2107 deadlock history in the past tense as the reason the workflow is NOT deleted - the deadlock returns the moment anyone re-requires the context, and this file is what makes that a one-checkbox change. STEP (c): docs/WORKFLOW.md rule 4 now carries the set and is named as the only authority on it, because the whole failure was a workflow comment being cited instead. TWO CONSEQUENCES ARE WRITTEN DOWN THERE RATHER THAN LEFT TO BE REDISCOVERED. First, 'auto-merge on green' promises compile + lint + typecheck + test + a deployed preview, and promises NOTHING about pixels; a PR that moves rendering is exactly what rule 4 sends to a human. Second, and this was found in the same reading and was not what the row went looking for: 'Require branches to be up to date before merging' is UNCHECKED. A PR merges on the CI it ran against ITS base, not against current main, so two PRs that each pass alone can still break main together. That is a defensible setting for one developer on auto-merge (the alternative serialises every merge behind a fresh run) and it is now a known property with a stated mitigation rather than a surprise. WHAT THIS ROW COST, KEPT HERE ON PURPOSE: it was filed because OWN-004 had been closed hours earlier by citing a sentence in a workflow header, on the same day ADR-1082 made 're-test the premise, never trust the prose' a rule in AGENTS.md. The prose had been wrong since the requirement was removed, and every PR merged on auto-merge that day merged on a narrower gate than the repo's own documentation described.

entries.title: Record payment is a one-way money button with no confirm and no undo, and it cost a year tonight
entries.detail: HAPPENED, not hypothesised. The owner pressed 'Record payment' on an active agreement while asking whether they should, and it extended paid_through from 2027-07-27 to 2028-07-27 - claiming a second $490 year the member had not paid. It took a guarded database UPDATE to put back, because THERE IS NO UNDO IN THE UI. TWO THINGS ARE MISSING AND THEY ARE DIFFERENT. (1) NO CONFIRM: the button fires on a single click with no dialog and no before/after, on a field that is money. components/ui/confirm-submit-button.tsx already exists for exactly this and is used on deletes; a renewal is at least as consequential as a delete, and unlike a delete it looks harmless. (2) NO CORRECTION PATH: once an agreement is active the panel renders a read-only summary plus that one button. The paid-through date input exists ONLY on the create form, which is unreachable forever after. So the single control the screen offers is the one that cannot be reversed, and the operator's only exit is a person with database access. WHY IT WILL RECUR IF LEFT: this is a once-a-year action per Space, so nobody builds a habit around it, and the failure is silent - no error, no email, just a wrong date that surfaces when a renewal reminder does not arrive and a member is not asked for money they owe. THE FIX, and the smaller half is the important one: a confirm step naming BOTH dates ('extend Temple of Aset from July 27 2027 to July 27 2028?') would have stopped this outright. An edit path for an active agreement is the second half and can follow. NOT A FIX: a toast after the fact, which tells you what happened without letting you undo it. CLOSED 2026-08-19. Both halves shipped, and the smaller one first as the row asked. (1) CONFIRM: Record payment now opens a Dialog naming BOTH dates ("moves paid-through from July 27 2027 to July 27 2028"), with the new date computed by addInterval, the SAME pure helper the server writes with, so the sentence a human reads and the value the database takes cannot drift. (2) CORRECTION PATH: correctPaidThrough (lib) + correctPaidThroughAction (server action) + a Correct date dialog set the date directly on an active agreement, deliberately unbounded because a repair is as likely to move a year back as a day forward. Both clear the three reminder stamps, which is the fail-safe direction: the ladder derives from paid_through, so a date moved BACKWARD must be able to raise its reminders again. Five tests lock it, including the round trip (record then correct returns the original date) and the refusal of a bad date with no write.

entries.title: The operator-seat switch could activate a price the owner had never set, and did
entries.detail: HAPPENED. The first live catalog sync minted EIGHT products instead of six; the extra was Operator seat, four prices at $9/$90, in the live account, with billing_live also true. The placeholder skip had not failed: catalog_operator_seat_active was true in production, so isCatalogItemInertPlaceholder correctly stopped skipping and the sync correctly minted what it was told. The gap is that ACTIVATION and AMOUNT were never compared. CATALOG.operator_seat carries placeholder:true and a documented stand-in amount; ADR-803 added the switch for use AFTER the owner sets a real amount, and nothing enforced the order. Turning the switch on while no operator amount existed shipped the stand-in as a real, chargeable price. Stripe Prices are IMMUTABLE, so it could only be archived, never corrected, which is exactly why the guard has to sit before the write. FIXED: setOperatorSeatActive(true) now refuses while pricing_settings has no catalog.operator_seat override, and says what to do instead; turning it OFF stays always allowed because that direction is safe. PRODUCTION REPAIRED the same day: flag off, the four operator_seat rows deleted from pricing_stripe_prices, and the Stripe product plus all four prices archived. Nothing was ever charged (0 customers, 0 subscription items).

entries.title: Every public practice URL was a uuid, and each of those pages disowned itself
entries.detail: FOUND while re-measuring OWN-012, which turned out to be already done: all 20 practices are public and /discover/practices renders 20 cards. The SEO goal behind that row was still not achieved, for a different reason. listPublicPractices, librarySearch and getRankedPractice all read the practices_ranked VIEW, which does not expose slug (RANKED_COLS strips it, and selecting it empties the view outright). So every row came back with slug: undefined and the p.slug ?? p.id fallbacks downstream silently resolved to the uuid. Measured on production 2026-08-19: the live sitemap advertised twenty /discover/practices/<uuid> URLs, every card on the index linked the same way, and each of those pages declared its canonical as the /discover/practices/<slug> URL via getPublicPractice, which reads the TABLE. Google was handed twenty addresses and told on arrival at every one that it was not the real address. 18 of the 20 practices have slugs sitting unused in the table. FIXED with slugsForPractices(ids), one keyed read mirroring tagsForPractices, wired into all three readers. The uuid fallback is deliberate and STAYS: a practice with no slug must still be reachable. The bug was never the fallback, it was that the slug was never fetched so the fallback was the only path.

verify.cmd: node -e "const fs=require('fs');const s=fs.readFileSync('lib/practices.ts','utf8');if(!/async function slugsForPractices\(/.test(s)){console.error('slugsForPractices is gone');process.exit(1)}const calls=(s.match(/slugsForPractices\(/g)||[]).length;const attaches=(s.match(/slug: slugById\.get\(/g)||[]).length;if(calls<4||attaches<3){console.error('a practices_ranked reader stopped attaching the slug: '+(calls-1)+'/3 calls, '+attaches+'/3 attaches');process.exit(1)}process.exit(0)"

entries.title: /feed has thrown a Supabase this-loss TypeError in production for six weeks and nothing recorded it
entries.detail:
FOUND 2026-08-19 by a runtime-health read after the five merges of that night, not by a gate. Vercel groups exactly one production runtime error for the project: TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'rest'), route /feed, first seen 2026-07-09T21:45:33Z and last seen 2026-08-19T04:36:35Z, 1 occurrence and 1 user in the trailing 6h. It is PRE-EXISTING: the last occurrence is 68 minutes BEFORE the first merge of that run (05:44), so none of #2166-#2170 introduced it. The frames are minified: at c (.next/server/chunks/ssr/lib_1b8tszi._.js:2:11541), at async gw (.next/server/chunks/ssr/app_(main)_view-as-actions_ts_073-c-k._.js:74:6517), at async l (.next/server/chunks/ssr/0anw_next_dist_0ns0ns1._.js:2:10950), digest 3920664382.

DIAGNOSIS, and it is not the obvious one. The first reading was the practice-streak rest window (StoredStreak.rest, the 'life happens' pause), because /feed reads it and the word matches. That is WRONG on the code: readStored() coalesces with (meta?.practiceStreak ?? {}) and getPracticeStreak() always returns a constructed object, so neither ps.rest nor stored.rest can throw. 'rest' is a SUPABASE-INTERNAL property. In @supabase/supabase-js dist/index.mjs the SupabaseClient constructor sets this.rest (line 664) and exactly three methods read it: from() -> this.rest.from (690), schema() -> this.rest.schema (700), rpc() -> this.rest.rpc (730). So the error is one of those three called with a lost `this` — a client method used as a bare value rather than invoked on its client.

WHAT THE TREE DOES NOT EXPLAIN. There is no such site in source. Swept app/, lib/ and components/ for a destructured or unbound client method: no `const { from } = client`, no `.from` / `.rpc` / `.schema` appearing as a value rather than a call, and the one deliberate rebinding is correct (lib/analytics/insights-read.ts:52 returns db.rpc.bind(db)). No runtime Proxy wraps a client outside tests. All four factories (admin/server/public/client) return the client directly. So closing this needs something the repo cannot supply on its own: a source-mapped frame, or a repro.

WHY IT IS WORTH A ROW RATHER THAN A SPECULATIVE PATCH. It is rare (1 user), pre-existing, on a route this run did not touch, and every candidate fix would be a guard added blind — the shape-not-truth move this repo names in four ADRs. It is recorded instead so it stops being invisible: a real production error ran unrecorded for six weeks, which is exactly the 'every fail-safe needs a gate that notices it fired' rule with no gate at all.

NEXT STEP for whoever picks it up: Vercel retains no log LINES this far back (a runtime-logs query over the 04:20-04:50 window on 2026-08-19 returned nothing, only the aggregated error group survives), so wait for the next occurrence and read it fresh, or map app_(main)_view-as-actions_ts_073-c-k._.js:74:6517 against the deployed build's source map to name `gw`. Do not raise a guard until the call site is named.

RE-READ 2026-08-19 over a 12h window, and the read added a frame the first one did not print. The THROW SITE is at c (.next/server/chunks/ssr/lib_1b8tszi._.js:2:11541) — a lib_ chunk — called from gw in the (main) chunk, under Next's render path (0anw_next_dist). That CORROBORATES the Supabase attribution and narrows where to look: @supabase/supabase-js and everything under lib/ bundle into the lib_ chunk, while the component that reads a practice-streak `rest` window lives in components/. A one-character minified name at column 11541 of a lib_ chunk is the shape of a bundled one-line method, which is exactly what SupabaseClient.from/schema/rpc are. It does NOT name the CALLER, which is still the thing needed, and it is still not grounds for a guard.

NOT A RECURRENCE. The same read shows last=2026-08-19T04:36:35Z, unchanged, count 1 over 12h — one event, rendered with a fuller stack, not a second hit. Eight production deploys shipped between 05:44 and 11:27 that day and none of them produced a new occurrence, and no OTHER error group exists for the project over the window. Twelve quiet hours is not evidence at a rate of roughly one hit per six weeks, so this closes no faster than the row already said.

CALL SITE NAMED 2026-08-19, and the mechanism is now reproduced rather than inferred. A node probe against the installed @supabase/ssr confirms the exact string: an ALIAS call (const rpc = client.rpc; rpc(...)) throws TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'rest'), while an INLINE paren-cast call ((client.rpc)(...)) does NOT — tsc/swc emit client.rpc(...), so `this` survives. That is why the earlier sweep for a bare .rpc VALUE missed it: every site writes `const rpc = admin.rpc as unknown as Fn`, and the grep filter dropped lines without `.rpc(`.

The site matching the stack is app/(main)/messages/popover-actions.ts:108 — `const rpcAll = supabase.rpc as unknown as (...)`, invoked at :118 inside fetchMessagesSummary's Promise.all, guarded by roomIds.length > 0. Every frame fits: it is a 'use server' module under app/(main) (the chunk Turbopack named after view-as-actions.ts, another 'use server' file in the same group); fetchMessagesSummary is async (at async gu) and is dispatched by Next (at async l in next/dist); SupabaseClient.rpc is SYNCHRONOUS, so it throws as a non-async top frame (at c) inside bundled vendor code. The ROUTE SPREAD is the clincher: VeraLauncher calls prefetchDockSummary() in a mount effect from the (main) layout, so the action fires from whatever page the shell is on — /settings, /feed, /messages, /messages.rsc. The roomIds.length > 0 guard explains the 9 users (only members of at least one room reach it), and components/messages/dock-chat.tsx:34 swallows it in a bare catch, which is exactly why it ran six weeks unseen while the server logged every one.

Ten sites shared the shape and all ten are now bound (x.rpc.bind(x), the pattern lib/analytics/insights-read.ts:52 already used): messages/page.tsx:259, messages/popover-actions.ts:108, api/webhooks/stripe/route.ts:89, billing/bundle-invites.ts:457+534, billing/bundle-seats.ts:196, billing/tickets.ts:423, achievements.ts:76+157, gems.ts:71. The two inline paren-casts (popover-actions.ts:38, :170) are correct as written and were left alone. scripts/check-detached-client-methods.test.ts is the gate that notices: it fails on the alias shape (proven against the literal broken line as a fixture) and passes clean on the tree.

POST-FIX READ 2026-08-19T16:05Z, and it carries something worth writing down. The group is UNCHANGED at count=20, users=9, last=2026-08-19T04:36:35Z -- which is 10 hours BEFORE the fix deployed at 14:46Z, so there have been no new occurrences, and that proves nothing yet at a natural rate of roughly 20 hits a week.

⚠️ WHAT IS NEW IS THAT THE GROUP SHOWS THREE DISTINCT DIGESTS, and only one of them is the stack this fix explains:
    digest 2220602272  at c (lib_1b8tszi._.js) <- at async gu (app_(main)_view-as-actions_ts_...)
    digest 467657171   at C (_0g12mbf._.js:2:4256)   -- SINGLE FRAME, different chunk
    digest 3553111027  at E (_0g12mbf._.js:2:4788)   -- SINGLE FRAME, different chunk

The first is the popover-actions.ts call site, now bound. The other two are single-frame stacks in a DIFFERENT chunk and are not explained by the ten sites this fix bound. They are historical samples from the same aggregated group rather than new hits (the count and last-seen did not move), so they may well be the same defect seen through an older deployment's chunking. But they are not accounted for, and saying so is cheaper than discovering it later.

THIS MAKES THE CLOSE CONDITION FALSIFIABLE RATHER THAN JUST QUIET: if a post-fix occurrence appears carrying digest 467657171 or 3553111027, the fix is INCOMPLETE and there is at least one more unbound site in a chunk this sweep did not reach. If a clean week passes with no occurrence of any digest, it is done.

── OBSERVABILITY HALF SHIPPED 2026-08-20: /api/status now publishes monitoring.sentry (booleanized from lib/observability/sentry.ts, never the DSN), so "is the recorder on in this deployment?" is one curl - the fail-safe finally has a gate that notices it is off. The recorder itself stays off until the OWNER sets NEXT_PUBLIC_SENTRY_DSN in Vercel production env and enables a Sentry new-issue alert; the repo can neither do nor verify that, but the curl now proves whichever state holds. Fix half unchanged: bound alias on main since f41c577 (#2175), regression locked by lib/gems.test.ts (#2198) + scripts/check-detached-client-methods.test.ts, and a full repo sweep found zero remaining detached aliases. ── CHECKPOINT 2026-08-24 (day 5 of the 30-day silence window; NOT closed). Fresh Vercel runtime read, 7d, routes /feed /settings /messages: the 'rest' group's last occurrence is still 2026-08-19T04:36:35Z, ~10 hours BEFORE f41c577 landed at 14:46Z, and its lastDeployment is dpl_DGzaYAzyPLDxbBDtrpmfzfeufMQX — the pre-fix preview this row already identified. Zero occurrences on any post-fix deployment. Three code legs re-verified today: lib/gems.ts:71 carries admin.rpc.bind(admin); app/(main)/messages/popover-actions.ts:108 carries supabase.rpc.bind(supabase); and a fresh tree-wide sweep for a client method aliased as a VALUE rather than invoked found none (the two lib/menus/actions.ts hits are immediate db.from<…>(…) CALLS, not aliases). lib/gems.test.ts's mock reads this.rest like the real SupabaseClient, so the bind cannot be removed silently. DELIBERATELY LEFT OPEN: this row's own close condition is 30 days of silence counted from 2026-08-19T14:46Z, and 5 days of quiet on an app with 23 active members and ~5 hits in six weeks is suggestive, not sufficient. Closing on it would be the 'closed without the probe ever passing' failure this list exists to prevent. Next checkpoint due 2026-09-18. ── 🔴 THE ROW CONTRADICTED ITSELF ABOUT ITS OWN CLOSE CONDITION, corrected 2026-08-24. The verify block said '7d of zero occurrences'; the detail's checkpoint said '30-day silence window, next checkpoint 2026-09-18'. By one half the row was 2 days from closing, by the other 25. A row whose close condition depends on which half you read is the drift the one-list rules exist to prevent. SETTLED ON 30 DAYS, the defensible number at roughly 5 hits over 6 weeks: a 7-day silence is inside the natural gap between occurrences and would close the row on noise. Both halves now say 30. ── CODE HALF RE-VERIFIED 2026-08-24 and it has EXPIRED: all ten alias sites are bound at HEAD, and an independent receiver-agnostic sweep for any .rpc/.from/.schema/.storage/.channel used as a value across app/ lib/ components/ hooks/ found ZERO detached aliases. The only .rpc-as-value hits are inline paren-casts, which keep `this`. Production is silent on every post-fix deployment; the last occurrence is ~10h BEFORE the fix deployed. What remains open is the clock, not the code. ── ⚠️ THE GATE HAD A REAL BLIND SPOT, closed here. check-detached-client-methods.test.ts matched receivers by NAME SHAPE (supabase|admin|client|db|sb). Measured against every variable in the tree assigned from a client factory: matched admin(775) db(308) supabase(223) client(1); MISSED q(4) dbc(4) dbh(2) ub(2) d(2) base(2) cfg(1) handle(1) - eight real client-holding names over 18 sites. None was detached, so this fixed no bug; it fixed the gate, which is the point (ADR-970: a fail-safe that cannot notice the next occurrence reads as coverage without being coverage). The guard now ALSO resolves, per file, the names that file assigns from a client factory, so spelling no longer decides whether the gate can see. File-scoped on purpose: `base` is a client in one file and a URL string in another, and a repo-wide name list would re-admit the false positives the narrow receiver test exists to avoid. Mutation-proven: removing the widening turns the new control red naming the missed variable. ── CHECKPOINT 2026-08-25 (day 6 of 30; NOT closed). Picked up as 'find the lost-this site' and the premise re-test showed it had EXPIRED before work began — the ADR-1082 pattern this row itself warns about: the site was already named, bound, gated and its recorder made checkable days earlier. Re-verified fresh rather than trusting the record: (1) every bind site present at HEAD (app/(main)/messages/popover-actions.ts:108, messages/page.tsx:260, lib/gems.ts:71, lib/achievements.ts:76+157, lib/billing/bundle-invites.ts:457+535, bundle-seats.ts:198, tickets.ts:435, api/webhooks/stripe/route.ts:89, lib/zaps.ts:261, insights-read.ts:52); (2) scripts/check-detached-client-methods.test.ts green, 5/5, including the receiver-resolution widening; (3) a fresh Vercel 7d runtime read: the 'rest' group's last occurrence is STILL 2026-08-19T04:36:35Z on the pre-fix deployment dpl_DGzaYAzyPLDxbBDtrpmfzfeufMQX — count=2, users=2 in this sampling window, and BOTH sampled stacks carry the explained frames (async gw and async gv in the view-as-actions chunk; digests 3920664382 and 2377037220 — note the second differs by one digit from the 2377037020 the 08-24 verify recorded, so one of the two readings mis-transcribed it; either way the stack shown IS the explained one). Neither once-unaccounted digest (467657171, 3553111027) appears. ONE CORRECTION to the record: the bind content reached origin/main via #2193 (4d7ad1c92), which absorbed #2175's branch commit f41c5777f — that SHA is NOT an ancestor of main, so anything pinning 'since f41c577' should pin the content, not the SHA; the 14:46Z deploy clock start is unaffected. Zero post-fix occurrences on any deployment. Only the clock is open; due 2026-09-18. 2026-08-25: the premise was re-tested (ADR-1082) and HOLDS - all ten sites bound at HEAD, guard green, and a receiver-agnostic sweep across five detach shapes finds zero. Only the silence clock is open. The re-test also found three shapes the GUARD could not see (non-assignment positions, a formatter-wrapped assignment, and two unscanned roots); all three were empty and all three are now closed with mutation-proven arms (ADR-1154).

verify.evidence: Close condition is 30 DAYS of zero occurrences of this digest family on deployments carrying the fix (clock start 2026-08-19T14:46Z, so due 2026-09-18). Re-read 2026-08-25 (day 6): 7d window shows count 2, users 2, route /feed, last 2026-08-19T04:36:35Z on the PRE-fix deployment dpl_DGzaYAzyPLDxbBDtrpmfzfeufMQX — zero post-fix occurrences. Both sampled digests (3920664382, 2377037220) carry the explained view-as-actions stack; the two once-unaccounted digests (467657171, 3553111027) do not appear. Code half re-verified same day: all bind sites present at HEAD and scripts/check-detached-client-methods.test.ts passes 5/5. Only the silence clock is open.

entries.title: A practice could reach the sitemap with no slug, and two did
entries.source: Full-repo audit 2026-08-19 (the practices half of the SEO sweep behind OWN-013)
entries.detail:
MEASURED IN PRODUCTION 2026-08-19: 20 approved public practices, 18 with a slug. app/sitemap.ts:295 advertises /discover/practices/${p.slug ?? p.id}, so the other two shipped RAW UUIDS to crawlers while every other practice shipped a keyword slug. The fallback is deliberate and stays -- a slugless practice must remain reachable -- but it is SILENT, which is the failure this repo names in AGENTS.md: a fail-safe with no gate that notices it fired.

ROOT CAUSE, and it is not the obvious 'the backfill missed them'. 20260627010000_practice_slugs.sql added the column, backfilled every row that existed, and created a PARTIAL unique index (where slug is not null). Two days later 20260629000000_seed_season_1_stretch.sql inserted more practices through pg_temp.upsert_practice(...), which never sets a slug. The backfill had already run and NULLs do not collide under a partial index, so nothing errored. forkPractice() in lib/practices.ts had the same omission, so the hole was not historical: any fork later made public would have done it again.

FIXED IN TWO LAYERS, because either alone is thin. (a) The APP path: forkPractice now mints via uniquePracticeSlug(src.title), the same helper createPractice always used, so the clean short slug stays an app concern. (b) The DATABASE path: migration 20260819141841 adds the practices_fill_slug BEFORE INSERT OR UPDATE trigger, which no writer can bypass -- not a future seed migration, not an admin script. The trigger does NOT probe for a free slug: a SECURITY INVOKER probe reads practices through the caller's RLS, so a member who cannot see the row holding 'nature-witnessing' would be told the name is free and practices_slug_key would then reject the INSERT, turning a cosmetic omission into a failed creation. It appends 12 hex of the row's own id instead, unique by construction, no query, and it can never fail a write. That shape is self-identifying, so a slug carrying an id fragment is a visible signal that a write path forgot.

THE MIGRATION IS NAMED FOR THE VERSION THE LEDGER RECORDED, not a hand-picked one. Applying through the Supabase MCP stamps schema_migrations with the APPLY-TIME wall clock and ignores any filename version -- the defect scripts/maintenance/ledger-parity.mjs exists to catch. Parity verified by hand at 621 repo .sql files against 621 ledger rows, because check:migrations could not be executed in that container.

NOT DONE HERE, DELIBERATELY: the two live rows are NOT backfilled. See LIVE-055 -- they turned out to be duplicates, and minting slugs for them would have cemented two duplicate public library entries.

verify.cmd: node -e "const fs=require('fs');const P='lib/practices.ts';if(!fs.existsSync(P))process.exit(79);const S=fs.readFileSync(P,'utf8');const i=S.indexOf('export async function forkPractice(');if(i<0)process.exit(79);const rest=S.slice(i+1);const e=rest.indexOf('\nexport ');const body=e<0?rest:rest.slice(0,e);const bad=[];if(body.indexOf('uniquePracticeSlug(')<0)bad.push('forkPractice inserts a practice without minting a slug, so a fork that is later made public reaches app/sitemap.ts as a raw uuid');const migs=fs.readdirSync('supabase/migrations').filter(f=>f.endsWith('.sql'));const trig=migs.filter(f=>fs.readFileSync('supabase/migrations/'+f,'utf8').indexOf('practices_fill_slug')>=0);if(!trig.length)bad.push('no migration creates the practices_fill_slug trigger, so the database has no net under the app path');else{const t=fs.readFileSync('supabase/migrations/'+trig[0],'utf8');if(!/create\\s+trigger\\s+practices_fill_slug/i.test(t))bad.push('practices_fill_slug is named but no trigger is created from it');if(!/before\\s+insert\\s+or\\s+update/i.test(t))bad.push('the practices_fill_slug trigger does not fire on both insert and update');}if(bad.length){console.error(bad.join('; '));process.exit(1)}process.exit(0)"

entries.title: Two public practices are exact-title duplicates of an older seeded one
entries.source: Fell out of LIVE-054 -- the slugless rows were the symptom, not the defect
entries.detail:
The two practices with no slug are not merely unslugged. Each is an exact-title DUPLICATE of an older seeded practice that already holds the clean slug and carries all the engagement:

  Nature Witnessing  ec0161ea-9bbd-427a-91b7-2ecb22895638  2026-06-17  slug set  18 logs  created_by null (system seed)
                     1516f5c4-2047-4dae-b6a2-1b0daada1ea9  2026-06-18  no slug    0 logs  created_by c1d40f58
  One Small Reach    b5b1009a-2761-4354-82f2-edbeb06bd624  2026-06-17  slug set  12 logs  created_by null (system seed)
                     ef2b62fb-6d03-45e7-9eec-8662d37a5861  2026-06-21  no slug    0 logs  created_by c1d40f58

Both duplicates are is_public=true, status=approved, is_demo=false, remixed_from null, zero logs. So the public library advertises 20 entries where 18 were intended, and two of them are dead copies.

WHY THIS IS NOT FOLDED INTO LIVE-054. Minting slugs for the newer pair would cement the duplicates under permanent id-suffixed URLs, which is worse than the uuid it replaces. Retiring one is what merge_practices(from_id, to_id) (20260828000000) exists for: it re-points adoptions and logs, records the old slug as a redirect, and archives + unpublishes + stamps merged_into on the source. Here there is nothing to re-point (0 logs) and no old slug to redirect, so the merge is close to free.

IT IS STILL A CURATION CALL, NOT A MECHANICAL ONE. Which of two public practices survives is a library decision with member-visible effect (two entries leave the public library), and the repo puts merges behind an operator review surface (listReviewQueue / needsAttention in lib/practices/clean.ts) rather than behind a script. The evidence says the newer pair are the copies: the survivors are the system-seeded rows, they are a day older, they hold every log, and they own the clean slug.

TO CLOSE, once an operator confirms the direction:
  select merge_practices('1516f5c4-2047-4dae-b6a2-1b0daada1ea9','ec0161ea-9bbd-427a-91b7-2ecb22895638');
  select merge_practices('ef2b62fb-6d03-45e7-9eec-8662d37a5861','b5b1009a-2761-4354-82f2-edbeb06bd624');
then re-read: zero practices with a null slug, and 18 approved public practices.

CLOSED 2026-08-19 on the owner's direction: retire the newer copies. Both merges ran through merge_practices(), the RPC 20260828000000 provides, so nothing was deleted and nothing was hand-written.
  merge_practices('1516f5c4-2047-4dae-b6a2-1b0daada1ea9','ec0161ea-9bbd-427a-91b7-2ecb22895638')
  merge_practices('ef2b62fb-6d03-45e7-9eec-8662d37a5861','b5b1009a-2761-4354-82f2-edbeb06bd624')
Both returned old_slug null, which is correct: the duplicates never had a slug, so there was no URL to redirect and no practice_slug_redirects row was written.

THE MEMBER COUNT IS THE PART WORTH READING. Each duplicate carried ONE member_practices row, so this was not a no-op on people. merge_practices de-duplicates before re-pointing (it deletes the source row where the same profile already holds the canonical, then re-points the rest), and the canonical counts came out UNCHANGED at 2 and 1. Both adopters were already on the canonical, so nobody lost an adoption and nobody ended up with two.

A SIDE EFFECT WORTH RECORDING, because it is the first production evidence that LIVE-054's net works: merge_practices archives the source with an UPDATE, which fired the new practices_fill_slug BEFORE UPDATE trigger, and the two archived rows minted 'nature-witnessing-1516f5c42047' and 'one-small-reach-ef2b62fb6d03'. That is the id-suffixed shape the trigger is designed to produce, it is self-identifying, and it cannot reach the sitemap because both rows are now is_public=false.

verify.evidence: Measured against production immediately after the merges, 2026-08-19: `select count(*) filter (where is_public and status='approved') , count(*) filter (where is_public and status='approved' and slug is null), count(*) filter (where merged_into is not null) from practices` -> 18 public approved, 0 with a null slug, 2 merged rows. The library went 20 -> 18 and app/sitemap.ts now advertises zero uuid practice URLs. Both retired rows read is_public=false, status='archived', merged_into set to their canonical, 0 logs, 0 members. Re-open only if a public practice with a null slug appears again, which LIVE-054's trigger now makes impossible at the database layer.

entries.title: The chat dock swallows its warm failure, which is why LIVE-053 ran six weeks unseen
entries.source: Fell out of LIVE-053 -- the reason nobody saw a 20-hit production error
entries.detail:
components/messages/dock-chat.tsx:34 wraps prefetchDockSummary() in a bare `catch { /* best-effort warm */ }`. The intent is right -- a failed warm must not break the shell -- but the implementation discards the error entirely, so the member sees an empty dock and NOTHING anywhere records that the call failed. The server logged all 20 occurrences of LIVE-053 and no human or gate ever read them, for six weeks, across 9 users.

This is precisely the rule in AGENTS.md: every fail-safe needs a gate that notices it fired. A swallowed error is an invisible regression.

TO CLOSE: keep the fail-safe, but make it audible. Report the failure to the client error channel the rest of the app uses rather than dropping it, so a warm that stops working surfaces as a signal instead of as an empty dock. The probe below fails while a bare catch remains.

CLOSED 2026-08-19. The fail-safe is KEPT and made audible: the catch still swallows, because a failed warm must not break the shell and the dock refetches on open, but it now reports through Sentry.captureException with tags {surface: messages-dock, phase: prefetch} -- the same channel app/error.tsx, app/global-error.tsx and components/ui/route-error.tsx already use. The probe is deliberately scoped to prefetchDockSummary rather than to the file: the handle-search catch at the bottom of the same component swallows an AbortController abort, which is expected control flow rather than an error, and a file-wide rule would have demanded reporting it. What this row is about is a SERVER EXCEPTION being dropped, not every catch.

entries.title: Does a Collective Space get 3 operator seats, or the owner plus 3?
entries.detail:
One sentence from the owner closes this. The seat wall began enforcing on 2026-08-19 (ADR-1087) and its own header was wrong about who spends a seat: it said 'the owner holds no member row', and ALL 19 non-root Spaces hold an ACTIVE space_members row for their own owner_profile_id at role 'admin'. So the owner is counted.

For Free and Business (allowance 1) that is right either way: the rung is meant to be the owner alone, and teammates start at Collective. For COLLECTIVE (allowance 3) it decides whether the Space gets owner + 2 teammates (today) or owner + 3 (if usedSeats excluded the owner, as the comment claimed). Three Spaces are on Collective and each holds owner + 1, so none is at the wall yet and there is no hurry, only a decision.

The code was deliberately NOT changed when this was found: either answer is defensible, and moving a paying Space's seat total on the strength of a stale comment is guessing in the expensive direction. The fix, once decided, is one filter in usedSeats or one number in PLACEHOLDER_METER_LIMITS.space_team, plus the comment.

── ANSWERED 2026-08-19, owner verbatim: "Owner + 2, total of 3." Today's behaviour is the intended one: the space_team allowance of 3 counts three operator humans INCLUDING the owner's own admin row, so usedSeats stays exactly as written and no code changed. The stale header claim ('the owner holds no member row') was already corrected when the question was filed; the seats.ts header now records the decision instead of the question.

entries.title: The approval spine survived its console, and ten of its twelve transitions now have no caller
entries.detail:
Removing the Beta Command Center (2026-08-19) deleted every UI that drove the approval spine, but not the spine: it moved to lib/outbound/ because assertApproved still gates every real campaign send from sendCampaignNow. What has no caller any more is the TRANSITIONS: markReady, approve, pause, cancel, recordTestSend, listReadyForApproval, listOutboundByStatus, listPhaseOutbound, groupReadyByPhase, armPhase.

THEY WERE KEPT ON PURPOSE AND THAT IS THE PROBLEM TO RESOLVE, not a mistake to revert. Seven campaigns rows carry a non-null phase_id (measured in production 2026-08-19, of 12 total). assertApproved refuses anything that is not approved or scheduled, so deleting approve() would mean those seven rows can NEVER clear the gate again: a trap, not a cleanup. campaigns.phase_id is now a dangling column, nothing writes it, and its foreign key went with beta_phases.

Two honest ways to close, and it is a judgement call: give the spine a small review surface on the CRM Marketing tab (the route the revalidatePaths now point at), or clear the residual phase_id values and delete the transitions. Either resolves it; leaving it is how a spine with no surface becomes load-bearing folklore.

── RESOLVED 2026-08-19, owner decision: the spine got its surface, not the axe. An approval queue panel now composes into the CRM Marketing tab (the route every transition's revalidatePath already pointed at): components/admin/crm/approval-queue.tsx lists everything `ready` (listReadyForApproval), everything `paused` (a hold is an open decision), and the phase-carrying `draft` strays, and its per-row actions delegate through thin 'use server' wrappers (app/(main)/admin/crm/marketing/actions.ts) to the spine's own approve/pause/cancel/markReady, which still self-gate on approverGate and write the audit row. The seven stranded phase_id rows take the ordinary path now: markReady puts a stray draft up for review, then approve arms it or cancel kills it, so assertApproved is clearable again without touching the database by hand. recordTestSend/listPhaseOutbound/groupReadyByPhase/armPhase still have no surface caller by choice: the queue reviews per item, and arming a whole phase blind is the opposite of review. The probe is the old one inverted: it fails if approve, pause or cancel loses its last importer outside lib/outbound/.

entries.title: A view-as read on /feed can hand practice-streak an undefined stored state (production TypeError, 1 hit)
entries.detail: Production runtime error group, digest 3920664382: TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'rest') on /feed, stack through app/(main)/view-as-actions.ts into lib/practice-streak.ts. count=1 user=1, first 2026-07-09, last 2026-08-19. The public read path guards with (meta?.practiceStreak ?? {}), but several internal call sites read stored.rest on a parameter the view-as impersonation path can apparently pass as undefined. Rare, real, and cheap to harden: find the call site that forwards undefined (or make the internal readers total). NOT the LIVE-053 clean-week pair (467657171/3553111027 have not recurred). — 2026-08-20 re-test: the premise was wrong on both names. Reproduced the deployed Turbopack chunks byte-for-byte: the throwing frame lib_1b8tszi._.js:2:11541 is awardGems's `await rpc('award_gems_atomic', …)` in lib/gems.ts, and the calling frame app_(main)_view-as-actions_ts_073-c-k._.js:74:6517 is `await awardGems(profile.id, 'daily_login')` in dailyCheckIn (app/(main)/checkin-actions.ts) — the once-per-member-day check-in POSTed from whatever page the shell is on, hence /feed. 'view-as-actions' is only the merged action-chunk's name; lib/practice-streak.ts is not in the stack at all (readStored() normalizes every meta read; no path can pass an undefined stored). Mechanism: the pre-#2175 alias `const rpc = admin.rpc as unknown as (…)` detached `this`, and SupabaseClient.rpc reads `this.rest` — the LIVE-053 mechanism at the lib/gems.ts site (different digest because different frames). ALREADY FIXED on main by f41c5777f (#2175, 2026-08-19 14:46Z): the alias is bound. The last hit (2026-08-19T04:36Z) came from preview deployment dpl_DGzaYAzyPLDxbBDtrpmfzfeufMQX of branch claude/agenthandoff-2026-08-19-z1zayi, cut from 5d79b440a BEFORE the fix — it is not evidence the fix failed, and stale pre-fix preview branches can still re-fire the digest. Regression test added: lib/gems.test.ts now uses a `this`-sensitive client mock (from/rpc read this.rest like the real SupabaseClient) plus an explicit daily_login-path test — proven to fail with the exact production TypeError against the pre-fix gems.ts (f41c5777f~1) and pass on main. The 30-day silence clock counts only deployments carrying f41c5777f. ── CHECKPOINT 2026-08-24 (day 5 of the 30-day silence window; NOT closed). Fresh Vercel runtime read, 7d, routes /feed /settings /messages: the 'rest' group's last occurrence is still 2026-08-19T04:36:35Z, ~10 hours BEFORE f41c577 landed at 14:46Z, and its lastDeployment is dpl_DGzaYAzyPLDxbBDtrpmfzfeufMQX — the pre-fix preview this row already identified. Zero occurrences on any post-fix deployment. Three code legs re-verified today: lib/gems.ts:71 carries admin.rpc.bind(admin); app/(main)/messages/popover-actions.ts:108 carries supabase.rpc.bind(supabase); and a fresh tree-wide sweep for a client method aliased as a VALUE rather than invoked found none (the two lib/menus/actions.ts hits are immediate db.from<…>(…) CALLS, not aliases). lib/gems.test.ts's mock reads this.rest like the real SupabaseClient, so the bind cannot be removed silently. DELIBERATELY LEFT OPEN: this row's own close condition is 30 days of silence counted from 2026-08-19T14:46Z, and 5 days of quiet on an app with 23 active members and ~5 hits in six weeks is suggestive, not sufficient. Closing on it would be the 'closed without the probe ever passing' failure this list exists to prevent. Next checkpoint due 2026-09-18. ── ✅ CLOSED 2026-08-24 ON A RE-TEST (ADR-1082), NOT ON THE CLOCK. Two independent findings. FIRST, the title's mechanism cannot happen: lib/practice-streak.ts readStored() (:216-224) coalesces EVERY field - `meta?.practiceStreak ?? {}`, then `rest: ps.rest ?? null` - so it can never return undefined nor an undefined `rest`. Every reader goes through it (:131,:276,:366,:548,:627); no exported function accepts a StoredStreak parameter, so there is no path that forwards an unnormalised value; and both consumers are total on nullish anyway (pauseCoveredDays :89-90, isResting :107-108). The `'rest'` in the production message is SupabaseClient.this.rest, never StoredStreak.rest. SECOND, the underlying defect was fixed on 2026-08-19 and re-proved here by mutation rather than trusted: reverting lib/gems.ts:71 to the unbound shape turns the guard red with the literal production string 'Cannot read properties of undefined (reading rest)'. `app/(main)/view-as-actions.ts` contains no practice-streak, no .rpc and no .from - it was only Turbopack's name for a merged server-action chunk, which the row's own 2026-08-20 re-test had already suspected. Nothing here was ever a practice-streak defect.

verify.cmd: node -e "const fs=require('fs');const P='lib/practice-streak.ts';if(!fs.existsSync(P))process.exit(79);const s=fs.readFileSync(P,'utf8');const m=s.match(/function readStored\\(\\)?[\\s\\S]*?\\n\\}/)||s.match(/function readStored[\\s\\S]*?\\n\\}/);if(!m){console.error('readStored is gone; the normalisation this row closed on no longer exists');process.exit(1)}if(m[0].indexOf('ps.rest ?? null')<0){console.error('readStored no longer coalesces rest, so an undefined stored state can reach a reader again');process.exit(1)}process.exit(0)"
verify.note: Measures the CONSEQUENCE the row is closed on: that stored state is normalised at the single read point. Fails if readStored is deleted or stops coalescing `rest`.

entries.title: createCircle bottom-up path cannot forge a circle/announcement as another profile
entries.detail: Server actions are POST endpoints reachable outside the UI (Next data-security guide, node_modules/next/dist/docs/01-app/02-guides/data-security.md L281). createCircle's ungated bottom-up branch (topical_channel_id present, no authorizeAction) took host_id straight from client form input, then wrote circles.host_id, a memberships row, and a 'Started a new circle' posts.author_id from it - a member could forge a circle, self-join and an announcement authored as an arbitrary victim profile. check:authz read the action as self-guarded because it DOES call authorizeAction (just conditionally) - the 'right guard, wrong scope / client-supplied id' shape the gate cannot see. Fixed: on the bottom-up path host_id is forced to caller.id; only the gated admin path (host+/community ops) may assign a different host. topical_channel_id is FK-checked by the DB (circles_topical_channel_id_fkey).

entries.title: ADR-907 claim tokens: migrate the four column-based minters, or formally drop the plan
entries.detail: ADR-907's hashed claim_tokens system ('use this for EVERY new claim flow') has zero production callers a year on. Every live claim flow still mints PLAINTEXT tokens onto anon-readable entity columns: lib/spaces/claim.ts (mintSpaceClaimToken), lib/listing-seeder/claim.ts, lib/events/event-drafts.ts; readers at app/events/claim/[token], app/listings/claim, app/spaces/claim compare on those columns. ADR-907 recorded the owner declining to migrate the four existing columns 'now', but that deferral was tracked only in the superseded BACKLOG.md, so nothing probes it. Owner's call: migrate the four flows onto claim_tokens, or formally retire ADR-907 and delete lib/claims/tokens.ts. Not a security emergency (tokens are random and single-use) but the plaintext-on-anon-readable-column shape is the reason ADR-907 exists. ── RETIRED UNIMPLEMENTED 2026-08-24 on the owner ruling, and the reason is a premise that HALF expired. This row's stated justification was 'the plaintext-on-anon-readable-column shape is the reason ADR-907 exists'. The anon-readable half is CLOSED: measured against production 2026-08-24, has_column_privilege('anon', …, 'claim_token', 'SELECT') is FALSE on all four of spaces, events, listings and market_listings — migrations 20270127000000, 20270128000000 and 20270129000000 did exactly that, and nobody had circled back to re-read the row against them. Meanwhile claim_tokens held 0 rows and lib/claims/tokens.ts had 0 importers outside itself, a year on. So the system was deleted (tokens.ts + its tests) and the empty table dropped by migration. ⚠️ THE RESIDUAL RISK IS NAMED RATHER THAN CLOSED: tokens stay PLAINTEXT AT REST, so anyone with service-role or direct DB access sees the live unredeemed ones (16 rows carry a token on spaces, 9 still unclaimed). That is a different threat model from the anon one ADR-907 was written for, and retiring ADR-907 does not address it. The four plaintext minters and the three reader routes are deliberately UNTOUCHED so those 9 live tokens keep working.

verify.evidence: Retired on the owner ruling 2026-08-24. Verified before deleting: 0 rows in claim_tokens, 0 non-test importers of lib/claims/tokens.ts outside lib/claims/, and has_column_privilege('anon', …, 'claim_token','SELECT') false on all four tables. The row's own cmd probe now passes (the file is gone). Manual because the RESIDUAL risk — plaintext at rest — is a judgment the repo cannot probe: it is not a defect, it is an accepted exposure with a named threat model.
