entries.title: db-tests flips to a required PR check
entries.detail: The owner said "I'll add it now" (2026-08-19). Branch protection is owner-only and no tool in this environment can read it — but per the ADR-1082 rule the CONSEQUENCE will print where the secret cannot: the next PR where a red db-tests visibly blocks merge (or where the merge box lists db-tests among required checks) is the proof. Flip this row on that sighting, citing the PR. 2026-08-25: db-tests made its first real catch (ADR-1150), which is the strongest argument yet for the flip - it is the only gate in CI that applies every migration to an empty database, so it is the only one that can see a fresh-apply defect at all. ✅ DONE 2026-08-25: the owner flipped it. Ruleset `main` (17640795) now lists SIX required checks - checks, analyze, lint, test, Vercel and db-tests - confirmed from the settings screen showing 'Ruleset updated' with db-tests present and bypass list still empty. ⚠️ THE FLIP CREATES A DEADLOCK AND THIS ROW IS ONLY SAFE WITH ITS OTHER HALF: db-tests.yml is path-filtered to supabase/**, and GitHub renders a required-but-never-posted context as 'Expected - Waiting for status to be reported' and blocks the merge FOREVER. PR #2107 hit exactly that with pr-compare on 2026-08-12 and could not be merged by ANY means, because bypass_actors is null on this ruleset - it does not exempt admins either. .github/workflows/db-tests-fallback.yml closes it, modelled line for line on pr-compare-fallback.yml, and scripts/db-paths.mjs reads the path list OUT of db-tests.yml through the parser both fallbacks now share (a second copy would drift, and a path missing from the copy means a migration-touching PR gets a free green on the one gate that could have caught it).

verify.cmd: node -e 'const fs=require("fs");const w=".github/workflows/db-tests-fallback.yml";if(!fs.existsSync(w)){console.error("db-tests is a REQUIRED context but its fallback workflow is gone - every pull request that touches no migration will block forever, which is the PR #2107 deadlock");process.exit(1)}const s=fs.readFileSync(w,"utf8");if(!/"context": "db-tests"/.test(s)){console.error("the fallback no longer posts the db-tests context, so a no-migration PR has nothing to satisfy the required check");process.exit(1)}if(/^\s+db-tests:\s*$/m.test(s)){console.error("the fallback declares a JOB named db-tests - two check runs would share the name and a stub could overwrite a red migration gate");process.exit(1)}if(!fs.existsSync("scripts/db-paths.mjs")){console.error("the fallback has no path script, so its path list is restated and can drift from db-tests.yml");process.exit(1)}const d=fs.readFileSync("scripts/db-paths.mjs","utf8");if(!/import\s*\{[^}]*\}\s*from\s+..\/workflow-paths\.mjs./.test(d)){console.error("db-paths no longer reads the shared parser, so there are two glob matchers that can disagree");process.exit(1)}'
verify.note: Measures the CONSEQUENCE of the required flip rather than the flip itself, which is owner-only and unreadable here: a required db-tests with no fallback is the PR #2107 forever-deadlock, so the fallback existing, posting the right CONTEXT, NOT declaring a job of the same name, and reading its path list through the shared parser are the four things that keep the flip safe. The flip itself is evidenced below. ⚠️ The last arm matches the IMPORT STATEMENT, not the string 'workflow-paths' — the first version matched anywhere in the file and so was satisfied by db-paths.mjs's own header comment describing the shared parser. A probe that a comment can satisfy measures prose, not behaviour.

entries.title: 38 exported server actions have no production caller — triage each to wire, delete, or a recorded keep
entries.detail:
Re-derived 2026-08-20 at db4d0b1: 38 exported functions in 'use server' files with zero non-test references outside their own file (36 with zero references anywhere; getSpaceRailBundle and listLoomImages carry live test references only). SEVERITY REFRAMED the same day by #2213's independent verification, which this row absorbs: 37 of 38 self-guard (requireAdmin / requireStaffCap / authorizeEditor / getMyProfileId / …) and fail closed, so those are NOT open doors — the cost is dead code, stale-comment drift, and seven half-built features silently rotting. #2213's per-name reads to carry into the triage: seven are DEAD-PENDING-UI (requestEventHost, startBundleCheckout, startSpacePlanCheckout [billing-gated], nudgeStreakMate, createDealForProfile, draftOfferingBlurbAction, countSpaceEmailAudience) — real backends of intended features, deleting discards real work; and it reads the manage/layout/* set as NOT superseded because SpacePageBuilder (components/entity-blocks/profile-page-builder.tsx via SpacePageModule) still renders — yet none of those 8 action names have any textual caller, so ADJUDICATE that first: establish what SpacePageBuilder actually invokes before touching the set. The SpaceUpdates trio lands per OWN-035's ruling. OUTCOME CONTRACT: every name ends wired (gains a caller), deleted, or a RECORDED keep — removed from this row's probe list in the same PR with the rationale written into this row. #2213's 'conservative outcome: keep all 32' was a holding position in prose; this row exists so the per-name fates stop living there.

── ADJUDICATED 2026-08-20, later the same day, by a per-name triage pass with the function bodies open. Two corrections to the paragraph above. (1) #2213 was wrong that all self-guard: getGamificationSummary(profileId?) at app/(main)/crew/gamification-actions.ts:169 runs getMyProfileId ONLY when no profileId is supplied, then reads profiles/user_achievements/streaks via createAdminClient — so a bare POST with an arbitrary profile id returns any member’s zaps, streaks and season rank with no session at all. Verified by direct read this session. It is superseded (the widgets self-fetch) and deletes FIRST. (2) The manage/layout dispute resolves against #2213’s read: SpacePageBuilder rendering does not mean these eight names have callers — each has a NAMED wired successor (block order/hide → saveSpaceGridLayout in the grid builder; setSpaceHero → the setSpaceHeroLook + setSpaceHeaderCta split; uploads → the universal Loom picker; setSpaceServices → the Shop catalog; the preset/default pickers never mounted). Triage outcome: 24 DELETE (21 deletions + 3 un-exports of delegate-only helpers: requestCollaboration, updateRecordingAction, saveSpaceProfileLayout), 8 WIRE (seenWalkthroughAction, exitSpacePreview, nudgeStreakMate, eraseSparkDraftsAction, deleteBrandStyle, deleteListingIntake, requestEventHost, reseedSpaceBlockCopy), 6 OWNER (the SpaceUpdates trio → OWN-035; startBundleCheckout — the deliberate 2026-08-12 createBundleCheckout mount whose purchase UI is the missing half, deletion would reverse that recorded decision; startSpacePlanCheckout — evidence says ADR-811 loadout superseded it but it is a revenue path; setWebsitePublished → rides the PROG-E10 ruling).

── CLOSED 2026-08-20. All 38 names resolved, none by a recorded keep: 24 deleted (21 outright + 3 un-exported delegate-only helpers), 8 wired to the UI half each was built for, 6 by owner ruling this evening — SpaceUpdates retires its UI and its three actions while the table stays per C3.5 (OWN-035 ruling: retire UI, keep table), the household bundle gains its purchase control on /settings/billing (the missing half of the 2026-08-12 mount), startSpacePlanCheckout goes as ADR-811-superseded, and setWebsitePublished goes until PROG-E10 restores it with Sites. The probe passes with the map intact, which is the outcome contract this row wrote for itself: every name wired, deleted, or recorded — and nothing needed the recorded arm.

entries.title: The 11 unreachable layout modules get a mount or a retirement
entries.detail: Re-verified still true 2026-08-20 (HYG-009): four community module ids are registered only under ROUTE_MODULE_IDS['*'] (lib/widgets/module-routes.ts:57, the Epic 1.7 note) and the fallback never resolves because every registered route has its own entry; eight entity-* rows sit under '/spaces/*' with no page mounting <PageModules> — the profile renders lib/entity-blocks instead (lib/widgets/modules.ts:658,693). Two registries imply reachability nothing delivers. Decide once: retire the '*' set and the eight entity rows, or mount the profile Layout editor (Epic 1.7). Deciding is the work; leaving both registries lying is the defect. ── 🔴 PREMISE RE-TESTED 2026-08-24 (ADR-1082) AND IT IS STALE ON TWO COUNTS, with a third error in its citation. (1) IT IS 11, NOT 12. `entity-cta` gained a real mount at app/(main)/spaces/[slug]/(profile)/book/page.tsx:7, rendered at :38 inside <Suspense> on the live /spaces/<slug>/book route. That landed in #2193 on 2026-08-19 - ONE DAY BEFORE this row's own 2026-08-20 re-verification, which still counted it. Same pattern as LIVE-012 and LIVE-043 in ADR-1082: a PR nobody circled back to. (2) THE CITE IS WRONG. lib/widgets/module-routes.ts:57 does not declare the `*` fallback and has no fallback at all; :57 is a comment about the entity-profile family. The `*` set is lib/widgets/modules.ts:658 plus the last-resort `?? COMMUNITY_MODULE_IDS` at :727. (3) THE DECISION IS NO LONGER BALANCED - the mount branch is CLOSED. The row offers 'retire, or mount the profile Layout editor (Epic 1.7)', but app/(main)/spaces/[slug]/(profile)/page.tsx:9 cut the profile over to SpaceProfileModules (ADR-508 U3), a separate engine with a functional superset of every entity block. RETIRE all 11; keep the entity-cta COMPONENT and drop only its dead /spaces/* registration. ── ⚠️ AND THE DEAD REGISTRIES ARE NOT COSMETIC, which this row assumed. They leak into two operator surfaces: the Layout editor's 'All pages' scope (components/admin/page-settings/layout-editor.tsx:121) renders toggles for the 4 dead community blocks and SAVES them to a page_settings row that can never render, because moduleAssignments filters by the route's own id set (lib/page-settings/layout.ts:126) - exactly the 'settings that do not make sense' trap module-routes.ts was written to prevent, one layer up; and routeChainForScope (lib/apps/for-scope.ts:45-47) has no `space` entry, so both global and space scopes fall through to ['*'] and surface those blocks in the admin rail. ── 🔴 TWO TRAPS FOR WHOEVER WORKS IT: deleting the '*' key alone RESURRECTS the dead set through the `?? COMMUNITY_MODULE_IDS` fallback at modules.ts:727, which must become `return []`; and lib/widgets/modules.test.ts:321 counts a module reachable if it appears in ANY route set including '*' and /spaces/*, so it passes today on all 11 dead modules - shape-not-truth, and it must be replaced rather than trusted. Collateral that dies with the retirement, all verified single-consumer: components/widgets/entity/entity-empty.tsx and lib/spaces/profile-presence.ts. KEEP lib/spaces/profile-stats.ts (still live via content-data.ts:23) and entity-cta-link.tsx. Bundle note: app-shell.tsx imports neither page-modules.tsx nor lib/widgets/registry.tsx, so check:shell-weight is not at risk either way - mounting would have cost server function weight, not the client shell. ── ✅ RETIRED 2026-08-24. All 11 gone: the four community blocks and the seven entity blocks, their ROUTE_MODULE_IDS keys ('*' and '/spaces/*' deleted whole), their registry bindings and their component files, plus the verified single-consumer collateral (entity-empty.tsx, lib/spaces/profile-presence.ts). entity-cta's COMPONENT survives - it is genuinely mounted at the /book route - and only its dead registration went. BOTH TRAPS HANDLED: moduleIdsForScope now returns [] rather than falling through to COMMUNITY_MODULE_IDS (and both id constants are deleted, so the fallback cannot be re-typed by accident), and modules.test.ts's reachability suite - which passed today on all 11 dead modules because it counted any appearance in any route set - is replaced by one that drives the real guard, with a mutation control that re-registers the community set and must fail. BOTH OPERATOR LEAKS CLOSED: the Layout editor lost its 'All pages' scope, and routeChainForScope returns [] for a scope kind with no URL section. NEW PROBE scripts/check-module-reachability.mjs, wired through VITEST_ENFORCED: for every ROUTE_MODULE_IDS key with no <PageModules> mount, each id's bound component must be imported somewhere under app/. entries.title: The block palette is scoped per surface
entries.detail: Re-verified still true 2026-08-20 (HYG-009): one shared config feeds derivePickerGroups on every editor surface (lib/page-editor/config.tsx:30; components/page-editor/mobile/data-ops.ts:55), so a marketing page's palette offers the entire 17-block Profile category and Space content blocks that cannot bind there. Fix: a per-surface category allowlist (page kind -> category keys) passed into derivePickerGroups on both the desktop and mobile paths. ── CLOSED 2026-08-24. lib/page-editor/palette-scope.ts declares EditorSurface ('marketing' | 'space') and SURFACE_CATEGORIES, an exhaustive Record of category allowlists; derivePickerGroups takes the surface and both editors pass it through a REQUIRED prop. THE PREMISE HELD BUT CORRECTED THE ROW ON THREE POINTS. (1) The Profile category is 18 blocks, not 17. (2) An unbindable block dropped on a marketing page is a SILENT NO-OP, not a crash — measured by rendering all 20 profile+spaceContent blocks with no metadata.space: 13 render ZERO bytes, 3 render an empty wrapper, and 5 render fine from their own props. So an operator could place, save and PUBLISH a section a visitor never sees, with no error anywhere: worse than a crash for detectability, milder for blast radius, and it means the blanket 'Profile is illegal on marketing' claim was too strong. (3) The leak was BIDIRECTIONAL and the row named one direction: the 6 circles blocks read metadata.circlesIndex and render zero bytes on a Space page. Marketing was over-offered by 30 blocks, Space by 6. Blast radius checked before narrowing: all 16 EDITABLE_PAGES templates use only sections/content/media/productStory/circles, so zero existing documents lose anything. THE FAIL-SAFE IS OPEN BY DESIGN — an unrecognised surface offers the FULL palette, never an empty one, because an over-wide palette is cosmetic while an empty one is an editor that cannot author anything and reads as broken with no operator recovery. Four things notice the open path (an exhaustive Record, a required prop at both mounts, a source-shape pin on both call sites, and a test asserting the union of allowlists is EXACTLY the config's category set). Mutation-proven five ways, including the subtle one: moving placed.add(t) below the allowlist check re-leaks all 30 blocks through the 'More' group while looking correct.

entries.notes: Probes the POLICY in-process rather than spawning the suite (LIVE-034 forbids a probe that runs a test runner). The 15-test suite with its five mutation proofs is the real guard and runs in `pnpm test`. Follow-up worth its own row: the `circles` category binds only on the /circles slug, so marketing is still over-wide by 6 blocks on the other 15 pages; slug-level scoping needs a 16-row map beside EDITABLE_PAGES. Second: SpaceArrangement is a preset-only region that is uncategorized, so it rides the 'More' group on every surface and probably belongs out of the palette entirely.

entries.title: The market-listing opt-out reaches the Tickets rail
entries.detail: Re-verified still true 2026-08-20 (HYG-009): the host's 'List this event publicly' opt-out is honored on the index (lib/commerce/index-data.ts:487) but listTicketedEventProjections (lib/commerce/ticket-projection.ts:129,208) selects rows without applying listableOnly, so an opted-out ticketed event still surfaces on the Market Tickets rail. Apply listableOnly to the projection rows before shaping cards. ── PATH CORRECTED 2026-08-24: this row cites lib/commerce/index-data.ts:487 as where the opt-out IS honoured, and that file does not exist. The live site is app/(main)/events/index-data.ts:516, which calls listableOnly from lib/events/market-listing.ts:56. The defect itself re-verified TRUE the same day: lib/commerce/ticket-projection.ts still never applies it, and that file’s own header (line 5) claims it "reads listable" events, so the comment is false as well as the behaviour. ── CLOSED 2026-08-24. listableOnly now runs on the projection, and the docstring that already CLAIMED to return listable events is true. Two details beyond the one-line fix: (1) the read went WIDE (limit*2, capped 200) and the cap moved after the filter, because a filter applied after .limit() lets an opted-out event eat a visible card slot — the same ordering the /events browse surface uses for this rule; (2) the filter runs before the tier/space/profile reads, so those batch over fewer rows. Five tests, verified as a real control: the opt-out test FAILS against the pre-fix line and passes after. They also pin the fail-open default, since listed is the default and only an explicit false opts out.

entries.title: 13 header destinations were unreachable on a phone, and operator menu edits never reached mobile
entries.detail: 🔴 FOUND 2026-08-24 while triaging HYG-010. RE-MEASURED BEFORE THE WORK (ADR-1082) and the row was wrong about itself in BOTH directions: it said twenty, itemised fifteen, and the true count is THIRTEEN. Four of the six /discover/* surfaces it named (circles, events, journeys, topics) were in fact reachable, because the sheet also rendered a hand-kept DISCOVER_NAV block covering them; and it missed /spaces/directory and /what-is-frequency, which were not. The thirteen: /discover/partners, /discover/practices, the Spaces directory, all five /for/* doors, /pricing, /what-is-frequency, /help, /privacy, /terms. ── THE CAUSE was real as stated: marketing-mobile-menu.tsx mapped headerTriggers() FLAT, and those are the PARENTLESS trigger nodes, so every child destination under them never rendered on a phone. The second defect was real too: marketing-header.tsx passed only `light` to the sheet, so PrimaryNav got the DB-backed menu and the sheet got the code default, and an operator's edit in the Menu manager reached the desktop and never a phone. ── FIXED (ADR-1118): the sheet takes the SAME headerMenu prop PrimaryNav takes and renders it through categoryTriggers (lib/menus/project.ts, the panel-or-link decision EXTRACTED from mega-menu.tsx so bar and sheet cannot disagree). A dropdown becomes a collapsible group holding everything the desktop panel holds, child columns folded in via flattenCategoryTree; a single-link category stays a plain link. The DISCOVER_NAV block is gone - all five of its links are rows of the menu itself. ── The unmerged remote branch `claude/mobile-menu-popover-fixes` the row warned about does NOT touch either file and is behind main. ── NOT DONE, filed instead: SiteHeader (/discover/*, /help) has no phone nav AT ALL, which is a larger surface than this row named (LIVE-110); DISCOVER_NAV is now an orphan export (HYG-019).

Fails if the sheet still projects the registry triggers flat (that projection IS the bug), if it stops using the shared panel-or-link projection or the category flatten (either would silently drop children again), if MarketingHeader stops handing it the DB-backed headerMenu (the operator-edit half), or if the header menu stops declaring any of the thirteen destinations by name - read out of the registry through menu-drift.mjs::codeLeaves, not grepped for. entries.title: The public header offered "Spaces directory" and landed on the marketing page, because a dropdown carries no landing
entries.detail: FOUND 2026-08-24 during the HYG-010 triage. RE-MEASURED BEFORE THE WORK (ADR-1082). Both member-facing claims HELD exactly: /spaces/directory sat in synced_default_keys with no live row (the sync is inserts-only and skips anything already in that set, so the engine could never resurrect it), and a live row labelled 'Spaces directory' pointed at /spaces. The COUNT was an apples-to-oranges comparison: 26 counts registry NODES (6 triggers + 20 children), the DB stores ITEMS, and the comparable code figure was 22 - so the drift was ONE extra row and ONE changed href, not three missing pages. ── THE CAUSE, which no one had connected: a dropdown trigger carries NO href of its own, so a landing page that is not also a ROW inside its own panel has no path from the header at all. /spaces and /the-community were both in that state. docs/MENU-AUDIT-2026-08-06.md row 3 found the Spaces half, called it 🔴, and routed the repair to the DB - and the repair that landed RELABELLED the directory row instead of adding a landing row. A code-shaped defect repaired in data produces a lie in the UI, and the code defect survives. ── FIXED (ADR-1118): both triggers now lead with their own landing in HEADER_TRIGGER_SEEDS, and the directory row points at /discover/spaces - the PUBLIC twin. Not /spaces/directory: robots.ts disallows that app-shell twin so it cannot cannibalise the canonical, and the (main) layout already redirects a signed-out visitor off it. The data correction (scripts/adr-1118-header-spaces-directory.sql, idempotent) was RUN against production 2026-08-24 and re-read: 24 live rows, 'Spaces' -> /spaces then 'Spaces directory' -> /discover/spaces, and /spaces/directory dropped from the baseline. ── THE DRIFT CHECK the row asked for is scripts/maintenance/menu-drift.mjs, wired into the weekly sweep on the ledger-parity pattern and scoped to `header`, NOT the admin_header HYG-010 named (that surface has zero DB rows and the check would have guarded an empty set, ADR-970). Its headline finding is the one no count can make: a live row whose LABEL matches a code default but whose HREF does not. Proven on real production payloads both ways - exit 1 on the pre-correction read naming the mislabel, exit 0 on the post-correction read.

verify.cmd: node -e "const fs=require('fs'); const R='lib/nav/registry.ts',M='scripts/maintenance/menu-drift.mjs',W='.github/workflows/maintenance.yml'; if(!fs.existsSync(R)||!fs.existsSync(M)||!fs.existsSync(W))process.exit(79); const f=[],TWINS=['/spaces/directory','/partners','/journeys']; if(!/menu-drift\\.mjs/.test(fs.readFileSync(W,'utf8')))f.push('the weekly header drift check is not wired into the maintenance sweep'); import(require('url').pathToFileURL(process.cwd()+'/'+M).href).then(function(m){ const trig=m.codeTriggers(fs.readFileSync(R,'utf8')); if(trig.length<5)process.exit(79); trig.forEach(function(t){ if(t.items.length&&!t.items.some(function(i){return i.href===t.href}))f.push('the \"'+t.label+'\" dropdown does not contain its own landing '+t.href+', so that page has no path from the header'); [{label:t.label,href:t.href}].concat(t.items).forEach(function(i){ if(TWINS.indexOf(i.href)>=0)f.push('the public header links '+i.href+', a robots-disallowed app-shell twin'); }); }); if(f.length){console.error(f.join('; '));process.exit(1)} process.exit(0); }).catch(function(e){console.error('probe could not run: '+e.message);process.exit(1)});"
verify.note: Measures the two invariants that were violated, by EXECUTING the registry projection (menu-drift.mjs::codeTriggers), not by grepping: every dropdown trigger must contain its own landing among its items, and no header node may point at a robots-disallowed app-shell twin (/spaces/directory, /partners, /journeys). Plus the weekly drift check must stay wired into the maintenance sweep. Negative-controlled: removing the Spaces landing row and repointing the directory at the twin reproduces both messages. Spawns no test runner (LIVE-034). The DB half is not probed here on purpose - no repo probe can read production, which is exactly why the weekly check exists and why this probe demands it stay wired.

entries.notes: The invariant also runs in `pnpm test`: lib/nav/registry.source.test.ts holds both arms with the failure story attached, and scripts/maintenance/menu-drift.test.ts reconstructs the exact live mislabelled row - an earlier draft of the comparison excused it because /spaces is itself a code default elsewhere, and reported a clean sweep. Live DB re-read 2026-08-24 after the correction: menu-drift exits 0. Five stale baseline keys (/for/coaches, /for/product-businesses, /for/service-businesses, /classifieds, /market) were LEFT in place and are reported as advisory: removing a key restores the sync's willingness to re-inject that href and would quietly overwrite a past operator delete, and failing on them would have made the instrument red on the day it shipped.

entries.title: The Create Event cover uploader still writes to storage from the browser, and it is failing live
entries.detail: REPORTED BY THE OWNER 2026-08-20 and confirmed in the logs the same hour: a member could not add an event photo (it 'kept freezing') and got an RLS failure editing details. Both are one defect. app/(main)/events/new/event-form.tsx:469 renders <ImageUpload folder='event-covers'> with NO uploadFn, so the cover goes straight from the browser to the event-media bucket, whose INSERT policy is granted to {authenticated} and requires split_part(name,'/',1) = auth.uid(). EVIDENCE, not inference: edge log 2026-08-20T20:51:25Z shows POST 400 /storage/v1/object/event-media/86a4ca9f-f2e7-4ad9-b1ca-7032487187fc/event-covers/1787259085047.png from Safari (macOS), and the postgres log at 20:51:27Z shows 'new row violates row-level security policy for table objects'; a second identical pair at 20:01:27Z. The path DOES carry the caller's uid, so the denial means the request reached Storage WITHOUT the session (anon) - the exact failure two other call sites already diagnosed and fixed by routing server-side (lib/spaces/... and app/(main)/events/[slug]/social-actions.ts:205 both carry the comment). The reporter's account is healthy: profile linked, confirmed, signed in 19:16Z, community_role host, and the RLS predicates all resolve true when simulated. Both failures came from Safari while every successful upload in the same window is Chrome. FIX: give the create-event cover the same server-side uploadFn the gallery beside it already uses (uploadEventGalleryImage), i.e. a gated action that writes with the admin client and returns the stored PATH - note ImageUpload's uploadFn branch currently calls onChange with res.url, so mode='path' needs the action to return a path (or the branch to respect mode) before this can be wired; that seam is part of the fix, not a detour. The same audit should sweep every other ImageUpload mount lacking uploadFn. FIXED 2026-08-20, same evening it was reported. The create-event COVER now routes through uploadNewEventImage, a new gated server action beside uploadEventGalleryImage: it mirrors the create flow own baseline authorization (getMyProfileId non-null, matching createEvent and the /events/new page guard - the per-target circle/space checks in createEvent gate PLACEMENT and cannot be evaluated before an event exists), writes with the admin client under the caller own profile prefix with a UUID name, validates folder against a two-value allowlist, and reuses the gallery action GALLERY_MIME + 10MB gates so the bucket can never reject what the action accepted. The uploadFn/mode seam was fixed properly rather than worked around: the branch used to call onChange with res.url unconditionally, which would have written the literal string undefined?t=... into cover_image_path, so uploadFn now returns a ServerUploadResult and a pure valueFromServerUpload(mode,res) resolves it - URL mode byte-identical to before, path mode never cache-busted (a query string breaks getPublicUrl). A SECOND instance of the same defect was found and fixed in the same pass: the create-event GALLERY (MultiImageUpload at event-form.tsx:498) had no upload prop and did the identical uid-prefixed browser write. The full 13-mount ImageUpload audit is in the PR: every other mount is either uploadFn-routed or URL-mode behind the Loom picker (whose uploads are already service-role server-side), so the hidden direct-browser input is unreachable there. Tests carry a negative control: 10 of 12 wiring assertions fail against pre-fix main.

verify.cmd: node -e "const fs=require('fs');const F='app/(main)/events/new/event-form.tsx';if(!fs.existsSync(F))process.exit(79);const t=fs.readFileSync(F,'utf8').replace(/\\/\\*[\\s\\S]*?\\*\\//g,'').replace(/^\\s*\\/\\/.*$/gm,'');const i=t.indexOf('<ImageUpload');if(i<0)process.exit(0);const seg=t.slice(i,t.indexOf('/>',i)+2);process.exit(seg.includes('uploadFn')?0:1)"

entries.notes: Probe measures the consequence at the reported site: the create-event cover uploader must carry an uploadFn (the server-routed branch) rather than falling through to the direct-browser write. Exits 79 if the file moves, so a rename reads as cannot-look rather than fixed.

entries.title: The events listing horizon is an operator setting, and it ships uncapped

source.ref: the hardcoded 60-day ceiling (owner report: Lumi’s event was nowhere to be found, 2026-08-20)

entries.detail: A host published a gathering 64 days out and it never appeared on /events. The cause was a hardcoded 60-day ceiling in app/(main)/events/index-data.ts (`const future = now + 60 days`), applied to all three of the loader's reads. Nothing anywhere explained the omission — not the listing, not the event page, not the host's own library — which is the worst failure this surface has. Owner ruling 2026-08-20: "Remove that cap for now. Make it a setting in the admin." SHIPPED: platform_settings.events_listing_horizon_days (0 = no cap, and 0 is the default, the missing-row reading, and the fail-safe on any read error), read through eventsListingHorizonDays() in lib/platform-flags.ts, set from /admin/events > Listing horizon. The loader omits its upper bound entirely when uncapped rather than substituting a far-future sentinel, because a sentinel is a hardcoded 60 wearing a bigger number. The row budget (SERIES_WIDE_READ, ADR-897) still bounds every read; removing the date ceiling did not remove the row ceiling, and the rows a full budget drops are the furthest out because each query orders by starts_at ascending.
entries.notes: In-process (grep-absent), not a spawned cmd: the guard has a 20s child-CPU budget and its failure message says to measure in-process rather than spawn. Measures the CONSEQUENCE — the hardcoded 60-day arithmetic is absent from the loader. Re-introducing a literal ceiling fails it. The wired half (eventsListingHorizonDays feeding a nullable bound) is pinned by lib/platform-flags.test.ts, which is where a behavioural assertion belongs.

entries.title: The creator of an event draft can open it
entries.detail: Owner report 2026-08-20: a member composed an event with the Vera composer and it was "nowhere to be found". The composer (app/(main)/events/event-spark.tsx:386) routes through saveDraft -> createEventDraft, which writes status='draft' and host_id=null on purpose (ownership is the question the publish step asks: 'mine' sets host_id, 'posted' mints a claim token). getEventCapabilities selected only host_id/scope_type/scope_id/space_id, so posted_by_profile_id granted nothing; with host_id null the composer matched no arm of the event rule, canManage was false, and the draft guard at app/(main)/events/[slug]/page.tsx:443 called notFound() ON THE CREATOR'S OWN ROW. /drafts was the only door, and it wears no badge by explicit design (lib/nav/my-frequency.ts:32-38). FIXED: the poster of an UNPUBLISHED draft leads it. The publish boundary is enforced by the caller, which passes draftPosterId null the moment status is 'published' — never widen it past publish, because a published 'posted' event is deliberately NOT the poster's, it is waiting to be claimed by the organizer it describes. This grants nothing new: lib/events/event-drafts.ts already scopes getMyDraft and listMyUnfinishedEventDrafts on posted_by_profile_id + status='draft'. It stops the capability layer disagreeing with the draft layer.
entries.notes: In-process (grep-present), not a spawned cmd: scripts/backlog-contract.test.ts caps check:backlog at 20s of CHILD CPU and says to measure in-process rather than spawn. The probe pins that the seam EXISTS on both sides (the resolver arm and the caller that feeds it). The half that actually matters — that the grant does NOT survive publish — is a behavioural assertion, so it lives in lib/core/capabilities.test.ts where it can be executed rather than pattern-matched, and it is mutation-checked there.

entries.title: Public Space surfaces stop rendering drafts and private events
entries.detail: Found in the events-visibility sweep, 2026-08-20. listEventsForSpace reads through the SERVICE-ROLE client, so RLS is bypassed and its own query is the only gate there is — and it had none: space_id, plus an optional start date. SpaceEvent.status has carried the comment "public readers filter on it" since the field was added and NOT ONE public reader did, so an unpublished draft or a `private` event on a Space rendered on that Space's PUBLIC profile: components/widgets/entity/entity-offerings.tsx:23 (Upcoming sessions), entity-cta.tsx:138, lib/spaces/content-data.ts:570 (the SpaceEvents block) and lib/spaces/profile-stats.ts:53 (the public hero stat, whose very next line applies publishedOnly to practices "so drafts must not be counted" — events were missed). FIXED by making the SAFE read the default: status='published' AND visibility in (public,unlisted) AND removed_at is null unless the caller passes includeUnpublished. Exactly one caller opts out, the operator's own Space console calendar, which badges drafts on purpose. A contract written in a comment that nothing enforces is not a contract, and nine callers each remembering to filter is the same bet nine times.
entries.notes: In-process (grep-present) for the same child-CPU reason. Pins that the opt-out parameter exists, which can only be true if the gate it guards exists. The rest of the contract — the three predicates land on the query, the opt-out is opt-IN, and no public reader uses it — is executed in lib/events/store.test.ts and lib/events/space-events-gate.test.ts, which assert behaviour instead of text.

entries.title: The profile Associations panel read zero for every member: the space wall stopped matching anything
entries.detail: SCOPE CORRECTED ON CONTACT — this was filed as the Events tile and it was all FOUR tier-A tiles. lib/people/associations.ts re-applies the Space wall by hand on four reads (circles, events, practices, journey_plans) because 20260711090000_space_content_isolation.sql puts it in RESTRICTIVE policies that never fire on the admin client, so the app-code predicate IS the gate. It was spelled .is(space_id, null), written when null meant "not in a Space". 20260712030000_content_space_id_default_root.sql then added a BEFORE INSERT trigger stamping every new row space_id to the ROOT tenant, and null quietly came to mean "written before that migration". Measured against production 2026-08-20: 0 of 7 circles, 0 of 20 practices, 0 of 12 journey_plans and 1 of 59 events had a null space_id. The whole "what this person built" panel read zero for every member on the platform, and it read zero the way a correct empty state reads, so nothing looked broken. A FIFTH site had the same bug in memory: app/(main)/people/[handle]/page.tsx filtered c.space_id === null for the Circle Up achievement chip. FIXED: one named rule (unwalledSpaceFilter for queries, the pure exported isUnwalledSpaceId for rows) admitting null OR root, used at all five sites. NOT A WIDENING OF THE WALL: can_view_space_content returns true for any space whose visibility is not private, and root is network, so root-owned content was already RLS-readable by anyone; only PRIVATE-Space content stays out, which is the entire purpose. Root resolution failing degrades to the null-only arm, which under-counts rather than over-shares.
entries.notes: In-process (grep-present) for the child-CPU budget (HYG-012). Pins the BOTH-ARMS filter string, which is the half that was missing; the null-only arm alone is the defect. The rest of the contract is executed: lib/people/space-wall.test.ts mutation-checks the pure rule from both directions, and components/profile/profile-associations-wiring.test.ts counts the four call sites and pins the page’s use of the shared helper.

entries.title: Tonight stops disappearing at 5pm Pacific: the member-facing event floors use community midnight

source.ref: HOME_TZ / dayInZone, the floor the correct surfaces use

entries.detail: SCOPE MEASURED ON CONTACT: filed as nine sites; the full count of raw-instant starts_at bounds across app/lib/components is 28. events.starts_at stores the wall-clock as UTC PARTS, so a lower bound of new Date().toISOString() is wrong twice — it drops an event THE MOMENT IT STARTS rather than at the end of its day, and it drops TONIGHT ENTIRELY once UTC rolls past midnight (about 5pm Pacific), because now-in-UTC-parts has already become tomorrow. FIXED, the member-facing set (12 bounds across 8 files): lib/events/store.ts listEventsForSpace upcomingOnly — which alone feeds entity-offerings, entity-cta, the SpaceEvents block, profile-stats, profile-presence, the Space dashboard and the manage rail counts; components/feed/feed-list.tsx x2; app/(main)/nearby/page.tsx x2; lib/nearby/map-pins.ts; lib/quest/next-gathering.ts (a query bound AND its in-memory twin, which had the identical bug in JS); lib/spotlight/data.ts; lib/events/membership-included.ts; and app/(main)/circles/[slug]/manage/events-section.tsx x3 — that last one an operator surface where, after 5pm, tonight vanished from the host's own management list. All now share upcomingEventFloor() (lib/events/upcoming-floor.ts). DELIBERATELY NOT SWEPT, because each genuinely means "from this instant" rather than "today": the recurrence materialiser (lib/event-recurrence.ts), member metering (lib/pricing/member-meter-usage.ts), Space directory counts (lib/spaces/discovery.ts), event matching (lib/events/matching.ts), the broadcast send window (lib/spaces/broadcast-audience.ts), the Space access gate (lib/events/space-event-access.ts), and the CRM/lead operator widgets. Every one is a count or a gate, not a "what is on today" list. WHY THE HELPER IS ITS OWN MODULE: lib/events/series.ts has ZERO IMPORTS on purpose so it stays client-importable without dragging tz-lookup into the bundle, and its own header calls the caller-supplied floor "not an oversight, it is the seam". upcoming-floor.ts is the server-side half of that seam, so the seam survives and callers get one function instead of two lines to get out of step.
entries.notes: In-process (grep-present) for the child-CPU budget (HYG-012). Points at five of the eight swept files rather than one, so removing the helper from any single high-traffic surface fails it. The behavioural half — that the floor stays on TODAY after UTC has rolled over, which is the actual bug — is executed in lib/events/upcoming-floor.test.ts with the clock injected, so it pins the 5pm boundary instead of waiting for it.

entries.title: The RSVP reminder cron has no status gate, so a draft can email its RSVPs
entries.detail: Found in the sweep, 2026-08-20. app/api/cron/event-reminders/route.ts:125-131 selects reminder candidates with a starts_at band and .eq('is_cancelled', false) and NOTHING ELSE — no status, no removed_at. An unpublished draft that somehow carries RSVPs will send reminder emails for an event that exists on no public surface. Compare lib/events/follower-reminders.ts:264-278, the sibling cron, which does gate on status='published' AND visibility='public'. One predicate closes it. FIXED 2026-08-20: the candidate select gains .eq(status, published) AND .is(removed_at, null) — removed_at because a moderator-removed event is the same one-way failure as a draft. A member cannot un-RSVP from an event they cannot open.
entries.notes: In-process (grep-present) to stay inside the guard’s child-CPU budget. One predicate closes this row, and its presence in the candidate select IS the consequence.

entries.title: The Stripe platform profile answers were reviewed; Stripe limits what can be changed
entries.detail: Owner action, one dashboard edit, no deploy. The Connect platform profile completed 2026-08-20 answers "Your accounts will collect payments directly from buyers using DIRECT charges", with losses_collector=stripe, fees_collector=account and dashboard=full — the STANDARD-account responsibility set. The codebase is the opposite on every axis: accounts are created as EXPRESS (lib/billing/connect.ts, accounts.create type:'express'), which fixes fees on the platform, losses on the platform and the Express dashboard on the account; and every charge is a DESTINATION charge (transfer_data.destination + application_fee_amount in lib/billing/tips.ts:95-96, lib/billing/tickets.ts:395-396, lib/billing/space-membership-checkout.ts:112, lib/commerce/checkout.ts:195-197), settling on the PLATFORM's balance. There is no Stripe-Account header anywhere in lib/ or app/. The second acknowledgement the owner signed the same day ("You'll be liable for seller losses. Stripe will hold reserves on your account.") describes the code correctly; the profile answers do not. Nothing mis-settles today, because a per-charge API call decides how a charge settles, not a profile default — but Stripe has been told this platform runs a model it does not run, which mis-calibrates its risk view and makes any future support conversation start from a false premise. FIX THE PROFILE, NOT THE CODE (ADR-1093): destination charges are right for this product, and rewriting four channels to satisfy a dashboard answer would be the tail wagging the dog. Change the business-model answer to the destination/separate-charges option and let the responsibility rows follow. ── BLOCKER RE-TESTED 2026-08-24, AND IT HOLDS (ADR-1082 asks for this rather than a restatement). The owner ruled "do whatever gets it working appropriately", which is the FIX THE PROFILE, NOT THE CODE direction this row already carries: destination charges are correct for this product and rewriting four settlement channels to satisfy a dashboard answer would be the tail wagging the dog. What an agent CAN do was then checked rather than assumed: this environment holds no Stripe credential (no STRIPE_* in the process env, no .env beyond .env.example), and the Connect platform profile's business-model answers are dashboard state with no read on the public API even with a key — unlike OWN-007/OWN-008, whose consequence was printed in an advisor read, this one has no consequence anywhere a repo or a log can see it. So it stays `manual` and owner-only, on evidence rather than on the phrase. THE OWNER ACTION IS UNCHANGED AND IS ONE EDIT: in the Stripe dashboard's Connect platform profile, change the business-model answer from "your accounts collect payments directly from buyers" (direct charges) to the destination/separate-charges option, and let losses_collector / fees_collector / dashboard follow it. No deploy, no code change. ── ✅ CLOSED 2026-08-24 BY THE OWNER, AND THE ROW'S PREMISE WAS WRONG IN A WAY WORTH RECORDING. This row (and ADR-1093) read the **Platform profile** page as the live declaration Stripe acts on. It is not. Stripe says so on the page itself: 'This shows historical information you provided during Connect onboarding. Current integration details and updates are in platform setup.' So every value this row quoted — business model 'Sellers will collect payments directly', losses_collector stripe, fees_collector account, dashboard full — is a record of what was ANSWERED during onboarding on 2026-08-20, not a description of the current configuration. The editable settings live at Settings > Connect > platform setup, a different page. The owner went there on 2026-08-24 and reports THE OPTIONS STRIPE OFFERED WERE LIMITED: the change was made as far as Stripe permits, and the historical profile still displays the original answers because that is what a historical record does. WHAT THIS MEANS, HONESTLY: the mismatch this row names is REAL and the fix was NOT fully available. The ruling stands — fix the profile, not the code — but 'fix the profile' is bounded by what Stripe's form allows, so what remains is a limitation to be aware of rather than an outstanding task. The code side is unchanged and correct: Express accounts, four destination-charge sites, zero Stripe-Account headers. NOTHING MIS-SETTLES EITHER WAY, because a per-charge API call decides how a charge settles, never a profile default. Independent signal from the same session: the Connect overview shows gross payment volume $0.00 and 0 new accounts over the trailing twelve months, so no money has ever moved through Connect and none of this has been exercised in production. RE-OPEN only if Stripe later exposes the business-model answer as editable, or if a settlement behaves unexpectedly.

verify.evidence: Closed by the owner 2026-08-24 after reviewing the live settings at Settings > Connect > platform setup and finding Stripe's options limited. The row's original premise was corrected in the same pass: the Platform profile page is HISTORICAL by Stripe's own statement on it, not the live declaration this row and ADR-1093 treated it as. Repo half unchanged and still correct (express account create, four destination-charge call sites, zero Stripe-Account headers). Connect gross volume $0.00 / 0 accounts, so nothing has been exercised. ADR-1093 amended with the same correction.

entries.notes: Deliberately manual (ADR-970): the profile lives in someone else’s dashboard and has no repo-visible consequence, so a mechanical probe here could only re-measure the code side, which is not what this row is about.

entries.title: The root Space stops reading as a real host: one resolver, ten sites, one named exception

source.ref: hostingSpaceId’s root guard, and its one caller

entries.detail: Owner report 2026-08-20: "it said it was under Frequency. It should have been under Lumi's personal account as she created it." hostingSpaceId() (lib/events/belonging.ts:57-65) is the function that gets this right — it returns null when the resolved space IS the root, because a BEFORE INSERT trigger (supabase/migrations/20260712030000_content_space_id_default_root.sql) stamps EVERY event's space_id to root, so treating it as a real host labels personal events with the platform's brand AND points the membership-tier and payout lookups at the platform tenant. It has exactly ONE caller: app/(main)/events/[slug]/page.tsx:396. TEN other readers re-derive the pair by hand as `host_space_id ?? space_id` with NO root guard, counted 2026-08-20 and including the money and access paths: lib/billing/tickets.ts:224, lib/events/ticket-tiers.ts:142, lib/events/ticket-space-access.ts:31, lib/events/space-event-access.ts:120, lib/events/crm-access.ts:275, lib/events/event-share.ts:315, lib/spaces/broadcast-audience.ts:122, app/(main)/events/[slug]/manage/broadcast-actions.ts:88 and broadcast-section.tsx:30 (both route member email through the space), app/(main)/events/actions.ts:965. Four of those ten decide who may READ an event's data or WHO GETS PAID, so on a root-stamped event they resolve to the platform tenant. Live count the same day: 32 of 58 events are root-stamped. CLOSED 2026-08-20. A new server module (lib/events/host-space.ts) is the ONE async door to the rule, so belonging.ts stays pure and no site has a reason to hand-roll the fallback again. NINE sites now exclude root: the members-only ticket gate and its configuration-time guard (an unbuyable ticket, refused for a reason nobody could act on), the Space access context, the "is this event hosted by THIS space" authorization check (an operator on the ROOT console passed it on other members' personal events), CRM stewardship over attendees (a root steward inherited access to every personal event's attendee list), event sharing, both broadcast lanes, and the Space-broadcast audience filter. A TENTH site was found only because a per-file scan had stopped at the first match: recordBuyerAsContact (lib/billing/tickets.ts) filed EVERY buyer of EVERY personal event as a contact of the platform's own Space. ONE site was deliberately left alone and is now named rather than inline: feeBearingSpaceId, because lib/billing/tickets.ts prices Space-hosted, personal and PLATFORM-hosted as three distinct cases, and collapsing root to null there would reprice the platform's own sales as personal ones. It is spelled as a branch rather than a ??-chain so the guard can sweep the whole tree without carving out a file. On the broadcast audience the direction of the trade-off is the argument: before the guard, a send from the root console addressed every event on the platform; after it, it addresses none. Too few recipients is a missing email; too many cannot be recalled.
entries.notes: The probe is grep-absent over app/lib/components with no path exclusions, which is only honest because the one legitimate implementation was written not to match (see feeBearingSpaceId). lib/events/host-space.test.ts carries the behavioural half, including a case proving the branch form and the ??-chain agree — that equivalence is what lets the guard hunt the chain everywhere.

entries.title: The check:backlog CPU budget is reshaped: a per-probe ceiling, and a total that scales with probe count
entries.detail:
Found 2026-08-20 when scripts/backlog-contract.test.ts failed a PR at 20.2s against its 20s child-CPU budget. It has now failed FOUR builds (20.2s, 20.3s, 20.6s). The original framing — eleven probes wastefully re-reading the same tree — was right about the reading and WRONG about the remedy. Both cheap fixes were tried and MEASURED, and both failed:

(1) MEMOISING the file listing and contents inside check-backlog.mjs: bought nothing measurable (19.98s baseline vs 20.61s memoised on the same loaded machine, against run-to-run noise of about +/-1s). A parent-process cache can only help the IN-PROCESS kinds, and those mostly point at single named files; all eleven expensive probes are `cmd`, i.e. separate node processes that cannot see parent memory.

(2) CONVERTING the eleven to the in-process grep kinds — the fix this row originally prescribed. The harness was extended with `exclude` and `stripComments` to make it possible, and then reading the eleven showed the premise was false: only THREE (OWN-036, OWN-037, LIVE-071) are pattern matches. The other eight are COMPUTATIONS, not greps — LIVE-012 walks app/discover checking auth calls per file against an allowlist, LIVE-020 imports check-function-grants.mjs and audits 400+ migrations through it, LIVE-038 carries an ALLOWED set, LIVE-054 parses a named function's body, LIVE-058 collects exported symbol names, LIVE-062 checks a per-file map of 38 action names, LIVE-066 pairs modules with importers. None of them can become a regex over paths without measuring something weaker than what the row claims. Converting the three that CAN saves about 75ms against a 600ms overage.

SO THE HONEST FINDING IS THAT THERE IS NO WASTE LEFT TO REMOVE. The budget is measuring a genuinely expensive and genuinely necessary set of checks that has grown past the number someone picked when it was smaller. The guard's own message says "Raising this number is not the fix" — that advice assumed waste existed, and the measurements above say it does not.

🔴 THIS IS AN OWNER CALL, NOT A CODE CHANGE, and it is deliberately left open rather than resolved by an agent raising a build gate on its own authority. The options: (a) raise GUARD_BUDGET_CPU_MS with the measurement recorded beside it and an ADR saying why; (b) run the probes concurrently — this cuts WALL clock but not CPU, so it does not move this number; (c) split the guard so the eight computational probes run on their own schedule; (d) accept that adding probed rows now costs a budget conversation each time.

── OWNER RULING 2026-08-21: option (a) is chosen in a specific shape — A PER-PROBE CEILING PLUS A COUNT-SCALED TOTAL, not a raised constant. The reasoning is that the guard's own failure message already says what it cares about ("something added expensive work to a PROBE"), and a fixed total does not measure that: it measures how many rows the backlog has, so every honest new row pushes it up and the gate fires for a reason unrelated to the thing it exists to catch. THE SHAPE: (1) no SINGLE probe may exceed a per-probe CPU ceiling — that is the real regression signal, and it stays valid however long the list gets; (2) the TOTAL budget scales with the number of probes, so adding a normal row is free and only an abnormal one trips it. check-backlog.mjs needs to report per-probe timings for (1) to be assertable — a summary line the test parses is enough, and it is useful to a human reading the output too. Land the constants from a real measurement, the way PACKED_PER_RAW was settled, and write the numbers into the ADR beside them. NOT STARTED: the owner asked to stop and close the thread on 2026-08-21; this row now carries the decision so the next session implements rather than re-litigates. ── STEP 1 LANDED 2026-08-24, STEP 2 DELIBERATELY NOT. The owner's ruling needs check-backlog.mjs to report per-probe timings before the per-probe ceiling is assertable, so that half is built and shipping: each probe is now bracketed by a /proc/self/stat cutime+cstime read (the same quantity the contract test budgets, and the only load-independent one per LIVE-047), and the guard prints `probe-cost: n=… totalCpuMs=… maxCpuMs=… slowest=…` plus the three most expensive probes by name. LOCAL MEASUREMENT, three runs, variance under 0.3%: n=111, total 8.32-8.56s, worst single probe PROG-DAWN9 at 2.02-2.09s, then LIVE-014 850ms and LIVE-018 520ms. Average 75ms. 🔴 THE CONSTANTS ARE NOT SET FROM THAT, AND THIS IS THE WHOLE REASON THE ROW STAYS OPEN. CPU time is load-independent but it is NOT hardware-independent: a slower core burns MORE cpu-seconds for identical work. This row's own history proves the gap — CI failed at 20.2/20.3/20.6s CPU while contemporaneous local readings of the same tree were 12.0-13.4s, about 1.6x. Today's local 8.5s therefore says nothing safe about what CI will read, and a count-scaled total derived from it would be roughly 1.6-2.4x too tight the first time a loaded runner saw it — which is precisely the failure this row exists to end, re-created with better instrumentation. AGENTS.md settles the method: a build-blocking gate that has never seen a real artifact is the 2026-08-11 incident with the roles reversed, so wire it in the same change as the run that proves it and read what it prints. PACKED_PER_RAW was settled exactly this way, by a paired reading. STEP 2, once CI has printed the line on a real run: set PER_PROBE_CEILING from the observed worst probe with headroom (locally that is ~2.1s, so roughly 2x it), replace the flat 20s with BASE + PER_PROBE_ALLOWANCE x n derived from the CI total, and record both numbers and the local:CI ratio in an ADR beside them. The flat 20s assertion is UNTOUCHED in this change: instrumentation cannot fail a build, so nothing here can break CI while the real number is being collected. ── STEP 2 LANDED 2026-08-24 (ADR-1107), FROM A PAIRED CI/LOCAL READING. The instrumentation shipped in step 1 printed on a real CI run (`checks`, run 32753212940, commit e64ac53b2): n=111 totalCpuMs=8530 maxCpuMs=2150 slowest=PROG-DAWN9, against three local runs of the same tree at n=111, total 7690-8560, max 1960-2090. 🔴 THE 1.6x THIS ROW ASSUMED IS NOT THERE: CI:local measures 1.00-1.11 on this pair, so the gap it recorded (CI 20.2s vs a contemporaneous local 12.0-13.4s) is not a property of today's runners. The constants are still set from the CI half, generously, because that is the assumption most likely to expire. A second measurement settled the shape: PROBES ARE ~96% OF THE GUARD (guardCpuMs 8360/8000 against a probe total of 8080/7690, so ~300ms is the guard walking the tree for the in-process kinds), which is what makes a budget built from the probe reading assertable against the whole-guard number. Landed: PER_PROBE_CEILING_MS=4500 (2.1x the worst CI probe), BASE_CPU_MS=2000 (~7x the measured non-probe work), PER_PROBE_ALLOWANCE_MS=180 (2.3x the 77ms CI average; 22.0s at n=111). The flat GUARD_BUDGET_CPU_MS is GONE. Two further things the shape needed: check:backlog now also self-reports `guard-cost: guardCpuMs=…`, because vitest's default reporter swallows a PASSING test's console.log and a number readable only by breaking a build cannot be what a build-blocking constant is set from; and both printed lines are fail-safes, so the contract test fails when either stops firing and cross-checks the self-report against the same quantity measured from outside the process. BOTH NEW ASSERTIONS ARE MUTATION-PROVEN: +7000ms on the reported worst probe fails the ceiling with its own message, and deleting the guard-cost line fails the presence assertion. ── CI READING REPLICATED the same afternoon on an unrelated run (32756093205, the supporter-rung branch, 90 minutes later, different runner): n=111 totalCpuMs=8510 maxCpuMs=2120, against the first reading's 8530/2150 — 0.2% and 1.4% apart. Two readings is not a distribution, but it rules out the first having been a fluke of one runner, which is the specific way a single-sample constant goes wrong.

verify.cmd: node -e "const fs=require('fs');const T='scripts/backlog-contract.test.ts',G='scripts/check-backlog.mjs';if(!fs.existsSync(T)||!fs.existsSync(G))process.exit(79);const t=fs.readFileSync(T,'utf8'),g=fs.readFileSync(G,'utf8');const bad=[];if(t.indexOf('GUARD_BUDGET_CPU_MS')>=0)bad.push('the flat GUARD_BUDGET_CPU_MS is still in backlog-contract.test.ts');if(t.indexOf('toBeLessThan(PER_PROBE_CEILING_MS)')<0)bad.push('the per-probe ceiling is not asserted');if(t.indexOf('BASE_CPU_MS + PER_PROBE_ALLOWANCE_MS * probeCount')<0)bad.push('the total does not scale with the probe count');if(t.indexOf('guard-cost: guardCpuMs=')<0)bad.push('the contract test no longer requires the guard-cost line');if(g.indexOf('guard-cost: guardCpuMs=')<0)bad.push('check-backlog.mjs no longer self-reports guard-cost');if(bad.length){console.error(bad.join('; '));process.exit(1)}process.exit(0)"

entries.notes: Zero-cost row on purpose (manual, no probe): the finding is that probes are expensive, so filing it must not make it worse. Do not re-attempt the memoisation or the blanket conversion — both were measured, both are recorded above with their numbers, and both failed for structural reasons that have not changed.

entries.title: The calendar collapses repeating events into a Repeats strip

source.ref: the month grid that drops the recurrence fields it is handed

entries.detail:
Owner report 2026-08-20: "The only events that should be suppressed on the calendar are recurring weekly events. I want any event to show within a year of it being loaded but I don't want repeating events jamming the calendar." MEASURED the same day: 17 of the 20 upcoming events are occurrences of two weekly series (Breathe Connect Expand, Meld Community Cowork). 85% of the calendar is two events repeating.

OWNER-SPECIFIED DESIGN (multiple choice, 2026-08-21):
  • A Repeats STRIP sits between the month header and the grid, one chip per series, labelled with the series name AND its cadence ("Breathe Connect Expand · Thursdays"). Chips, not bare icons — an unlabelled icon fails the skeptic test because a member cannot tell what it is without clicking.
  • Clicking a chip DOT-HIGHLIGHTS that series' dates in the grid (it does not filter the grid down, and it does not hide anything). Clicking the chip's name opens the event.
  • In the cells: the NEXT occurrence of each series renders as a normal card; every later date gets a small dot rather than a card. So "what is on this Thursday" stays answerable at a glance while ~16 of the 17 repeat cards leave the grid.
  • SCOPE IS /events/calendar ONLY. The master .ics already collapses a series to one RRULE entry, /events index cards already fold through collapseSeriesRows, and Space/Circle lists are explicitly out of scope for this row.

THE GROUNDWORK ALREADY EXISTS, which is most of why this is M and not L. supabase/migrations/20261203000000_calendar_feed_recurrence.sql already added recurrence_type, recurrence_until and parent_event_id to public_calendar_feed — precisely so the .ics routes could collapse a series — and app/(main)/events/calendar/page.tsx reads that feed and then DROPS all three when it builds its CalendarEvent objects. lib/events/series.ts already has collapseSeries, seriesKey and SeriesGroup, which every other surface uses. This is wiring, not building.

⚠️ TWO TRAPS. (1) parent_event_id IS THE GROUPING KEY, NOT recurrence_type: the materialised child occurrences all carry recurrence_type 'none' and only the anchor knows the cadence, so grouping on cadence finds nothing. (2) "WITHIN A YEAR" AND "REPEATING" FIGHT EACH OTHER TODAY: occurrences are materialised rows and only 60 days ahead (HORIZON_DAYS in lib/event-recurrence.ts), so raising the listing horizon shows one-off events a year out but repeats simply stop existing past 60 days. Owner ruling: COMPUTE the strip's future dates from the anchor's recurrence_type + recurrence_until for display, and decide separately later whether to raise the materialiser. Those computed dates are display-only and cannot be RSVP'd or ticketed until the materialiser catches up — say so in the UI rather than letting a member click into nothing.

RELATED, ALREADY DONE: the listing horizon is an operator setting (LIVE-073) and is currently set to 365. ── SEQUENCED 2026-08-24 into W0: it was filed after the 2026-08-20 slate was ruled and sat in no wave. Placed near-term because the owner reported it directly and specified the design; move it if that is the wrong wave. ── BUILT 2026-08-24. ⚠️ ONE PREMISE OF THIS ROW WAS WRONG AND THE FIX IS PART OF THE CHANGE: the owner ruling says compute the future dates "from the anchor's recurrence_type + recurrence_until", but the anchor is NOT IN THE FEED. public_calendar_feed() floors at now() - 1 day, so an established series' anchor row aged out months ago. Measured against production the same day: all 8 loaded rows of each live weekly series are children reading recurrence_type 'none' / recurrence_until null, and 0 anchors were present, so the cadence existed nowhere the page could reach. listSeriesAnchors() (lib/events/store.ts) now reads the anchors back BY ID, gated to published + public + not cancelled + not removed + not demo + a real cadence (the master-feed gate minus its date floor, re-applied in JS by seriesAnchorIsLive), and hands them to the pure plan. Everything else shipped as specified: chips carry name + cadence, the chip name links to the next date, the cadence half is an aria-pressed HIGHLIGHT (nothing is filtered or hidden), the next date keeps its card, later dates are dots, computed dates past the 60-day horizon are hollow dots with UI copy saying they open for RSVP about two months ahead, and the materialiser is untouched. NOT VERIFIED IN A BROWSER: no build or e2e was run for this change.
entries.notes: In-process (grep-present) for the child-CPU budget (HYG-012). The pattern MOVED from parent_event_id to planCalendarRepeats when the row was built, and it measures more, not less: the page cannot call planCalendarRepeats without handing it the feed rows WITH their recurrence columns (it took the three-column widening of listPublicCalendarEvents to type-check at all), and the plan is what groups the series. The grouping half — parent_event_id and never recurrence_type, the trap this row names — is pinned behaviourally by lib/events/calendar-repeats.test.ts against a fixture copied from production: mutating the key to recurrence_type fails 8 of its 19 tests, run 2026-08-24. A grep for parent_event_id in the route file would now pass on a COMMENT, which is the shape-not-truth failure the rules name.

entries.title: A Space's Circles have no page: the menu item is an anchor and the noun URL is an owner 404

source.ref: the tab that did not exist

entries.detail:
REPORTED BY THE OWNER 2026-08-21: "when someone clicks on a space's circles ... right now no page shows up". Confirmed in one sweep and it was never a bug, it was a hole. The profile menu's "Circles" was an ANCHOR: deriveSectionNav maps the stored SpaceCommunity block to #circles, so it scroll-jumped to a six-item teaser on Home and only appeared when that block was in the saved layout. /spaces/[slug]/circles already existed and looked exactly right, but it was the owner console opening with `if (!caps.canEditProfile) notFound()`, so the most obvious click on a Space profile ended in a 404. ADR-1091 C3.4 had deleted the old Community tab and left a 308 to the Space ROOT, which is why nothing filled the gap.

BUILT 2026-08-21 (ADR-1094). The public tab lives in the (profile) route group so the cover, identity row and menu come from that layout; the owner console moved to /spaces/[slug]/manage/circles, outside the group, which is the split Shop already runs (public /shop, console /settings/shop). OWNER RULING the same day: hide the tab at zero for VISITORS (the honest-empty rule Calendar, Collaborators and Shop follow) and keep it for a MANAGER, because the empty state is where "Start your first circle" lives. 'circles' joins DEDICATED_TAB_ANCHORS or the Home anchor sits in the menu beside the real tab, which is the "two Reviews" bug a second time. The tab ships zero client JS of its own (format + sort are plain Links over searchParams) and the filter row renders only at 8+ circles. ROOT notFound()s: stampCircleSpaceId stamps every personal circle to the root tenant, so without the guard the root Space's profile would have listed the platform's private circles. The /spaces/:slug/community 308 re-points from the Space root to the tab it always meant.

verify.cmd: node -e "const fs=require('fs');const P='app/(main)/spaces/[slug]/(profile)/circles/page.tsx';const C='app/(main)/spaces/[slug]/manage/circles/page.tsx';if(!fs.existsSync(P)||!fs.existsSync(C))process.exit(1);if(fs.existsSync('app/(main)/spaces/[slug]/circles'))process.exit(1);const n=fs.readFileSync('lib/spaces/profile-nav.ts','utf8');const okNav=n.includes(\"'circles'\")&&n.includes('${base}/circles')&&n.includes(\"new Set(['reviews', 'circles'])\");const cfg=fs.readFileSync('next.config.ts','utf8').includes(\"destination: '/spaces/:slug/circles'\");const mod=fs.readFileSync('lib/admin/modules/space-modules.ts','utf8').includes('/manage/circles');process.exit(okNav&&cfg&&mod?0:1)"

entries.notes: The probe measures the CONSEQUENCE, not the title: the public page exists, the console has MOVED (the old directory is gone, so a stray copy fails the row), the nav points at a page rather than an anchor and suppresses the duplicate, the 308 lands on the tab, and the admin rail deep-links to the new console path.

entries.title: An unlisted circle renders on its Space's public page, and is counted in a public stat

source.ref: listCirclesForSpace and its four public callers

entries.detail:
Found while sweeping the Circles surfaces for LIVE-082, 2026-08-21. listCirclesForSpace reads through the SERVICE-ROLE client, which holds BYPASSRLS and never sees circles_access_restrictive, and applies no visibility filter of its own. Its COLS string did not even SELECT `unlisted` or `access`, so a caller could not have applied the rule if it had remembered to. FOUR public callers reached for it and all four filtered on status alone: getSpaceCommunity (the public Home block), EntityCommunity (the entity profile module), resolveProfileStats (the PUBLIC hero's "Circles N") and spaceHasContent (the has-content gate). So an unlisted circle rendered on a Space's public page and was counted in a public number. This is exactly the failure lib/circles/visibility.ts predicts in its own header block.

FIXED 2026-08-21 (ADR-1094): listPublicSpaceCircles owns the rule and applies BOTH filters IN THE QUERY. In-query matters as much as in-one-place: filtering a CAPPED page in JavaScript lets a hidden row eat a visible row's slot, so a Space with one unlisted circle showed five cards in a six-slot block with nothing to explain the gap. AXIS 2 is deliberately NOT filtered (a listed closed circle is the lead funnel of ADR-1015; canEnterCircle on the circle's own page is the door), but CircleCard now badges it with its CIRCLE_ACCESS_LABEL and swaps Join for "See what's inside", because canJoinCircle refuses every closed mode and offering Join was a lie. listCirclesForSpace stays raw and is documented as the OWNER-surface read.

LIVE BLAST RADIUS: MEASURED 2026-08-21, against production, because a row that says "unmeasured" is a claim with an expiry date (ADR-1082) and this one cost a single query. 7 circles exist. 6 sit on the ROOT tenant (spaces.slug='frequency', type=root, visibility=network) and 1 on a real business Space (danieltyack: active, listed, open). By status: 2 active, 3 draft, 2 forming. EXACTLY ONE row was actually leaking: an ACTIVE, UNLISTED circle on the root tenant, which getSpaceCommunity rendered on /spaces/frequency, the platform's own public profile. No REAL Space was publishing a hidden circle, so the member-facing damage was nil and the hero "Circles N" was correct everywhere it mattered. access is 'open' on all 7, which re-confirms the LIVE-059 reading and is why the earlier note refused to let that reading stand in for this one: it is axis 2 and this is axis 1. The defect was real, its reach was one row, and the fix is the same either way. ── ⚙️ PROBE NARROWED 2026-08-24, IN THE SAME CHANGE THAT MADE IT NECESSARY. This row's probe readFileSync's each of its `callers`, and LIVE-067's retirement DELETES two of them - components/widgets/entity/entity-community.tsx and lib/spaces/profile-presence.ts. readFileSync on a missing file THROWS, so the probe would exit non-zero and check:backlog would report this DONE row as a regression - verified by running it on the retirement tree before fixing it: 'LIVE-083 says DONE, tree says NOT DONE'. The two surviving callers (lib/spaces/content-data.ts, lib/spaces/profile-stats.ts) still exercise the same guarantee: both must call listPublicSpaceCircles and neither may call listCirclesForSpace. 🔴 THE GENERAL HAZARD, worth more than this instance: a probe that names FILES couples one row to every future deletion elsewhere, and the coupling is invisible until a `done` row goes red in someone else's PR. Prefer naming the IMPORT that must be absent or the EXPORT that must exist over naming a file that may be retired.

verify.cmd: node -e "const fs=require('fs');const s=fs.readFileSync('lib/circles/store.ts','utf8');const hasCols=/const COLS =[\\s\\S]{0,400}unlisted/.test(s)&&/const COLS =[\\s\\S]{0,400}access/.test(s);const hasReader=s.includes('export async function listPublicSpaceCircles')&&s.includes(\"or('unlisted.is.null,unlisted.eq.false')\");const callers=['lib/spaces/content-data.ts','lib/spaces/profile-stats.ts'];const clean=callers.every(f=>{const t=fs.readFileSync(f,'utf8');return t.includes('listPublicSpaceCircles')&&!t.includes('listCirclesForSpace')});process.exit(hasCols&&hasReader&&clean?0:1)"

entries.notes: The probe measures the CONSEQUENCE both ways: the columns are selected (so the rule is askable at all), the reader exists and carries the exact axis-1 predicate, and NO public caller still imports the raw read. Re-adding listCirclesForSpace to any of the four fails the row. The rule's behaviour is proven separately by lib/circles/store.test.ts, whose axis-1, before-LIMIT and own-unlisted-circle cases fail against the pre-fix tree.

entries.title: The discover retry never fired: an empty `code` was read as a database answer, and it killed a production deploy
entries.detail:
OBSERVED ON PRODUCTION, not theorised. The production deploy of eee84ba (#2235) FAILED: `DiscoverReadError: discover read failed: public_event_by_slug` while prerendering /discover/events/breathe-connect-expand-2026-09-03, caused by `TypeError: fetch failed / read ECONNRESET`. One transient packet loss on one of 297 static pages ended the whole export (dpl_2SRX2aYctYBXmZw1TaYyi1xBJtBy, 2026-08-21T02:28:05Z).

LIVE-039 SHIPPED A RETRY FOR EXACTLY THIS ON 2026-08-18 AND IT HAD NEVER FIRED. The tell was in the log: `attempt()` console.errors a line on every retry, the failure came 2 seconds into static generation, and there was no retry line at all. Root cause, one expression:

    if (typeof e.code === 'string' && !TRANSIENT_RE.test(e.code)) return false

supabase-js does not THROW a transport failure, it RESOLVES an error whose code and hint are EMPTY STRINGS, because the request never reached PostgREST and there is no PostgREST code to report: { message: 'TypeError: fetch failed', details: '...read ECONNRESET...', hint: '', code: '' }. `typeof '' === 'string'` is true and TRANSIENT_RE.test('') is false, so the guard concluded "a code is present, therefore the database gave a deterministic answer" and refused to retry the one shape the retry was written for. The absence of a code, expressed as an empty string, was read as the presence of one.

PROVEN BEFORE FIXING: the verbatim error object from the build log, replayed through __retryForTest.attempt, called the query ONCE. Fixed by trimming the code and treating blank as absent, so classification falls through to the message text where 'fetch failed' matches; `details` joined the searched text as well, since that is the field carrying the causal chain. The code arm still returns false for any real Postgres code, so widening the text cannot make a deterministic failure retryable, and two tests pin that.

SECOND SITE, same route, fixed in the same pass: app/discover/events/[slug]/opengraph-image.tsx called getPublicEventBySlug (a throwing detailRead) with no catch, while its circles counterpart had always used `.catch(() => null)`. The OG card already renders a branded fallback for a missing event, so it had a designed empty state and no reason to be able to end a build. The PAGE keeps throwing on purpose: swallowing there would answer a crawler with a real 404 on a sitemapped URL.

REACH OF THE FIX (surveyed, not assumed): attempt() is the ONLY throwing read in the entire prerendered set, and it is reached UNGUARDED by five detail routes (events/[slug], circles/[id], topics/[slug], places/[citySlug], cities/[citySlug]) and six prerendered index pages (/discover and its events, circles, topics, places, cities indexes). Every one of them was relying on a retry that never ran; one expression restores it for all of them. Also swept in the same pass: generateStaticParams in cities/[citySlug] and places/[citySlug] were the only two in app/discover missing the `.catch(() => [])` their siblings carry (LIVE-011), so a params read could end the export before a single page rendered.

BLAST RADIUS: the deploy that died was DOCS-ONLY (#2235 changed one file, docs/BUILD-BACKLOG.json), so production kept serving e13b6b9 and no member saw anything. That is luck, not safety: the same blip on the same route would have taken down any deploy, and `main` is protected precisely because merging deploys to production.

ADR-1095 records the decision and the durable rule. Open and NOT fixed here, filed as its own concern: app/sitemap.ts leans on one outer catch, so a single discover blip silently empties the whole dynamic sitemap with nothing noticing (DEPLOY-SAFETY §6, the fail-safe-with-no-gate shape).

verify.cmd: node -e "const fs=require('fs');const s=fs.readFileSync('lib/discover.ts','utf8');const og=fs.readFileSync('app/discover/events/[slug]/opengraph-image.tsx','utf8');const t=fs.readFileSync('lib/discover.test.ts','utf8');const guard=s.includes(\"code !== '' &&\")&&!/typeof e\\.code === 'string' && !TRANSIENT_RE/.test(s);const ogSafe=og.includes('getPublicEventBySlug(slug).catch(');const proven=t.includes('PRODUCTION_KILLER')&&/code: ''/.test(t);process.exit(guard&&ogSafe&&proven?0:1)"

entries.notes: The probe measures the CONSEQUENCE three ways: the empty-code guard is present AND the exact pre-fix expression is gone, the events OG read is caught like its circles twin, and the test file carries the production fixture. Re-introducing the old guard fails the row. The behavioural proof lives in lib/discover.test.ts, whose three new cases fail against the pre-fix tree (verified by checking out lib/discover.ts at eee84ba and re-running: 3 failed, 9 passed).

entries.title: A popup opened inside a Space renders in the HOST theme, because the portal lands outside AccentScope
entries.detail:
Found while sweeping the popup surfaces for theme uniformity, 2026-08-21. A Space's page theme is NOT established on the document root: AccentScope renders a plain DIV carrying data-space-theme plus the five --color-primary* custom properties inline, inside the profile subtree, and both the [data-space-theme] CSS blocks and the accent overrides hang off THAT node. Dialog and WizardModal both createPortal(..., document.body), which lands their subtree OUTSIDE that div, so a Spark or a Dialog opened from a themed Space page rendered in the HOST amber and the HOST fonts. StudioWindow, which does not portal, inherited correctly. Two sibling surfaces, opposite behaviour.

WHY NO GATE COULD SEE IT: every token involved is legal. The popup was not painting a wrong colour, it was resolving a CORRECT token against the wrong ancestor. check:tokens, check:contrast and the adoption ratchet all measure the class a site writes, and every class here was already right.

FIXED 2026-08-21 (ADR-1097): the opener leaves a hidden aria-hidden sentinel rendered IN PLACE, and a ref callback on the portaled root reads the sentinel's nearest [data-space-theme] ancestor and mirrors the theme id and the five accent properties onto that root. A REF CALLBACK, not useEffect+setState: it is a DOM mirror settled before paint, so state would cost a second render and trip the repo's set-state-in-effect lint. The INLINE style is read rather than getComputedStyle, so a host default is never copied down and frozen; absent an override the token simply keeps inheriting.

THE PORTAL IS NOT THE BUG AND MUST NOT BE REMOVED. dialog.tsx documents why it exists: inside a transformed or clipped ancestor (the sliding admin rail is the live case) a `fixed inset-0` overlay is trapped by that ancestor's containing block and renders as a narrow sidebar panel instead of covering the viewport. Deleting the portal would trade an invisible palette bug for a visible layout one.
entries.notes:
The probe measures the CONSEQUENCE in three places: the hook still reads a themed ancestor and copies the accent properties AND still does so without useEffect/useState (re-introducing the effect shape fails the row), BOTH portaling popups are wired to it while still portaling, and the negative-control test file survives. Behaviour is proven separately by components/ui/portaled-space-theme.test.tsx, whose two theme-carrying assertions fail against the pre-fix tree while its two guard assertions (still portals to the document body; nothing applied outside a Space) pass on both trees.

COMMENTS ARE STRIPPED BEFORE THE CODE CHECK, and the first version of this probe is why: the hook's header explains at length WHY it is a ref callback and not `useEffect` + `setState`, so the probe read the words out of the prose arguing against them and failed the row for being documented. That is the same defect class as OWN-014's first probe and as the check:phantom tombstone in the same PR — a scanner that does not strip comments cannot tell a rule from an explanation of the rule.
