🔴 THE PROBE IS A GREP, NOT A SPAWN, AND THAT IS DELIBERATE. `check:backlog` runs under a 20s CPU budget asserted by scripts/backlog-contract.test.ts, and that budget is a SHARED resource already ~99% consumed on main. Four new `cmd` rows landing at once tipped CI over it (20.19s measured). A `cmd` probe costs a process spawn even when its work is trivial — these were ~30ms each and almost all of that was startup — so the rows that CAN be answered by an in-process grep use one. The compound assertions these probes used to make are not lost: they live in this row's test file, where they are negative-controlled against the pre-change tree, which is a stronger place for them than a probe anyway.

entries.title: The Journey Spark offers five ways in and two upload buttons, and neither the doors nor the uploader is manifest-shaped
entries.detail:
OWNER, 2026-08-21, verbatim: "We recently went through all of them, and it's too confused now." The audit says why. Screen one offered FIVE ways in: a Vera card leading to four questions, a manual card, a "Use the recommended framework" card, a "Start from a template" card, and a drop zone underneath. The drop zone itself carried TWO upload controls doing one job: the kit's single-document button and a bespoke BatchUpload beside it, two labels and two file inputs.

THE OWNER SPECIFIED THE REPLACEMENT EXACTLY: a "Tell me about your Journey" text field, an "Upload Documents" button under it, then "Build it Yourself", then "Start with a Template".

🔴 THE COLLISION. spark-doors.tsx carries a locked structure comment ("two doors, equal weight, Vera first") and is shared by SIX Sparks; the requested order replaces the first door with a field and promotes the drop zone above the second. Nothing in EntityManifest can express a door at all, so this could not be a data change.

FIXED 2026-08-21 (ADR-1098). veraPrompt changes the AFFORDANCE of the first door, never its position or weight, and the lock is RESTATED rather than removed: Vera first, build-it-yourself second, extras after, equal weight. Typing writes the same sourceText an upload writes, so it lands on the one-screen source path that already existed for uploads and needs NO new AI work and NO new action. The recommended framework moved into the picker, first and named, with a weeks step behind it, because it is the only creation path that stamps the named Expression Challenge, the capstone, the anchor practice and the Welcome/Close bookends with no AI, and because the Spark is the ONLY caller that passes weeks at all (the editor and guide entries both land on 4). The multi-file capability moved into SparkDropzone as onDocuments, handing files back unparsed exactly as images already work; BatchUpload is deleted.

WEEKS IS STILL ASKED, NOT INFERRED, and deliberately: Vera treats it as a hard constraint and clamps its own arc to it, and SparkSettings (the only thing Vera lifts from source text) excludes it. Inferring it would be new model work in a change that otherwise has none.
entries.notes:
The probe measures the CONSEQUENCE in four places: the prompt exists on both sides of the seam (the Journey passes it AND the kit accepts it), the standalone framework door is gone while its picker route and weeks step exist, ONE uploader remains and the kit owns the multiple input, and the copied FRAMEWORK_ID still equals MASTER_FRAMEWORK_ID. That last clause is the one that earns its keep: drift there is silent and sends the author to createJourneyFromTemplateAction with an id no template has.

Behaviour is proven by two test files, both negative-controlled against the pre-change tree: components/studio/spark/spark-doors.test.tsx (6 of 7 prompt assertions fail on the old kit; all 4 standard-screen assertions pass on BOTH trees, which is what stops the prompt leaking into the five Sparks that did not ask for it) and components/journey/v2/journey-spark-doors.test.ts (8 of 10 fail on the old component; the 2 that pass are correctly true either way).

Comments are stripped before every code assertion, in the probe and in the tests, for the reason ADR-1097 records: a comment naming a retired thing is documentation, not a call site.

🔴 THE PROBE IS A GREP, NOT A SPAWN, AND THAT IS DELIBERATE. `check:backlog` runs under a 20s CPU budget asserted by scripts/backlog-contract.test.ts, and that budget is a SHARED resource already ~99% consumed on main. Four new `cmd` rows landing at once tipped CI over it (20.19s measured). A `cmd` probe costs a process spawn even when its work is trivial — these were ~30ms each and almost all of that was startup — so the rows that CAN be answered by an in-process grep use one. The compound assertions these probes used to make are not lost: they live in this row's test file, where they are negative-controlled against the pre-change tree, which is a stronger place for them than a probe anyway.

entries.title: The Event Spark mounts two overlays at once on its @wizard route: two focus traps, two scroll locks, two close buttons
entries.detail:
Found in the wizard-uniformity sweep, 2026-08-21, after the owner's "all pop ups should be the same format". On the intercepted route the nesting was: (.)events/new -> WizardModal -> createPortal -> StudioWindow (overlay A: focus trap, scroll lock, close-confirm) -> the real page module -> EventEditorWindow -> StudioWindow with hideChrome (overlay B: a SECOND trap, a SECOND scroll lock, its own header carrying its own close X) -> EventSpark -> SparkShell (a third heading and footer).

LIVE CONSEQUENCES: two useDialogFocusTrap instances competing for Tab, two body-scroll locks, three stacked headers, and TWO CLOSE BUTTONS THAT DID DIFFERENT THINGS — the inner pushed /events, the outer ran the unsaved-work confirm dialog.

🔴 WHY NOBODY SAW IT. EventEditorWindow is CORRECT on its two other consumers (/events/[slug]/edit and /admin/events/[id]), neither of which has an interceptor above it. The component was right twice and wrong once, so reading the component finds nothing: only the COMPOSITION on one route is wrong, and nothing in the repo looked at compositions. Every sibling create route already rendered its Spark bare.

FIXED 2026-08-21 (ADR-1099): /events/new renders EventSpark bare, like /circles/new, /practices/new, /journeys/new, /classifieds/new and /market/sell. SparkShell already centres itself, so no wrapper is needed. EventEditorWindow is NOT deleted — removing it from the edit routes would be a second regression in the opposite direction.

A COPY LOSS, STATED NOT BURIED: EventEditorWindow's header band (the brandmark beside "Share an Event with the community!") and its footer line no longer appear when CREATING an event; they still appear when editing one. If that invitation is wanted on the create path it belongs in SparkShell's eyebrow and description, where every other Spark puts its framing, not in a window wrapper that drags an overlay along with it.

── THE COPY LOSS IS RESOLVED (owner decision 2026-08-21). The invitation moved into the Event Spark's own SparkShell description on screen one: "Share an Event with the community. Tell Vera about it, drop in what you already have, or fill in the form yourself." That is where every other Spark puts its framing, so the words are now COMPOSED rather than WRAPPED — they no longer arrive attached to a second overlay. EventEditorWindow keeps the band verbatim on the two EDIT routes, which is why the create and edit paths now read slightly differently on purpose.

TWO DELIBERATE DEVIATIONS FROM THE ORIGINAL BAND, both small and both stated rather than slipped in: the exclamation mark became a full stop, because mid-description an exclamation reads as a slogan and docs/CONTENT-VOICE.md asks for plain sentences; and the footer aphorism ("The best gatherings start with someone deciding to host one.") was NOT carried over, because a third sentence in a wizard description is chrome, not framing. Both are one-line reversals if the owner wants them back.
entries.notes:
The probe measures the CONSEQUENCE in three places and refuses the two opposite regressions: the create page opens NO window and still renders the Spark, BOTH edit routes still open theirs, and the routing contract still carries the discovered-opener guard. Re-wrapping the create page fails it; so does stripping the window from an edit route.

Behaviour is guarded by property 4 in app/(main)/@wizard/wizard-routes.test.ts, whose opener set is SCANNED from components/ rather than listed, so a wrapper written next week is covered without editing the test, with a floor assertion refusing the vacuous pass if the scan breaks. Negative-controlled: against the pre-fix page exactly ONE assertion fails ("/events/new renders its Spark bare") and the other 32 pass, so the guard is aimed at this defect rather than being a blanket.

🔴 THE PROBE IS A GREP, NOT A SPAWN, AND THAT IS DELIBERATE. `check:backlog` runs under a 20s CPU budget asserted by scripts/backlog-contract.test.ts, and that budget is a SHARED resource already ~99% consumed on main. Four new `cmd` rows landing at once tipped CI over it (20.19s measured). A `cmd` probe costs a process spawn even when its work is trivial — these were ~30ms each and almost all of that was startup — so the rows that CAN be answered by an in-process grep use one. The compound assertions these probes used to make are not lost: they live in this row's test file, where they are negative-controlled against the pre-change tree, which is a stronger place for them than a probe anyway.

entries.title: CreateModal is a second overlay implementation with eight consumers, and it never portals
entries.detail:
docs/STUDIO.md §6 ended with "Retire components/create-modal.tsx once circles move." CIRCLES MOVED — NewCircleCompose is a bare Link and CircleWizard shipped — and the retirement never followed. Eight surfaces stayed on a hand-rolled overlay: New Hub, New Nexus, Create a Channel, New Dispatch, New Crew Task, New Group DM, Invite a Member, Invite to Room.

🔴 WHY A SATISFIED CONDITION CHANGED NOTHING: none of the eight is a circle, and §6's migration order never assigned an owner to any of them, so the trigger fired against work nobody held. A retirement condition phrased as "once X moves" only works when the thing being retired is what X was using.

WHAT THE DUPLICATION COST, beyond having two overlays: it did NOT portal, so any of the eight opened inside a transformed ancestor (the sliding admin rail) was trapped in that ancestor's box and rendered as a narrow panel — the exact defect dialog.tsx documents its portal as preventing. It could not carry a Space's theme (ADR-1097) because it had no portal to carry it across. It was not in the dialog stack, so Escape could dismiss it and a dialog above it at once. It padded a flat 0/16px, so on a notched phone its footer sat on the home indicator. And its own comment justified the split by saying the centered ui/Dialog "can't express" a bottom sheet — true when written, false once `align` landed, and nothing re-read it.

FIXED 2026-08-21 (ADR-1100): Dialog gains align="bottom" (a true bottom sheet, deliberately distinct from `sheet`, which fills the whole viewport — a form with six fields should not black out the screen), and CreateModal delegates the overlay to it while keeping its public API EXACTLY: same props, same names, all eight call sites untouched. The pending-submit guard is re-stated by hand because Dialog knows nothing about a form being mid-flight.

"Retire" was the wrong verb and the doc now says so. The OVERLAY is gone; the shell stays, because eight callers legitimately want a header-icon / form / footer shape and deleting it would mean eight hand-rolled re-implementations of what was just consolidated.
entries.notes:
The probe measures the CONSEQUENCE on both sides of the seam: CreateModal renders a Dialog with align="bottom", it no longer carries ANY of the four overlay concerns it used to duplicate (fixed inset-0, the focus-trap hook, aria-modal, the body scroll lock), the pending guard survives, and Dialog actually implements the bottom align. Re-hand-rolling the overlay fails it; so does dropping the align value out of the primitive.

Behaviour is proven by components/create-modal.test.tsx, negative-controlled: 7 of 12 assertions fail against the pre-change file. The 5 that pass on BOTH trees are the pending-guard half, correctly so — that behaviour was preserved by hand rather than gained, which is exactly why it needed its own assertions.

🔴 THE PROBE IS A GREP, NOT A SPAWN, AND THAT IS DELIBERATE. `check:backlog` runs under a 20s CPU budget asserted by scripts/backlog-contract.test.ts, and that budget is a SHARED resource already ~99% consumed on main. Four new `cmd` rows landing at once tipped CI over it (20.19s measured). A `cmd` probe costs a process spawn even when its work is trivial — these were ~30ms each and almost all of that was startup — so the rows that CAN be answered by an in-process grep use one. The compound assertions these probes used to make are not lost: they live in this row's test file, where they are negative-controlled against the pre-change tree, which is a stronger place for them than a probe anyway.

entries.title: Six hand-rolled overlays remain, and each differs from Dialog in scrim or z-tier, so none is a silent conversion

source.ref: the shared primitive these six bypass

entries.detail:
🔴 THE SURVEY THAT PRODUCED THIS LIST WAS WRONG ABOUT ITS OWN EASY CASES, and that is the finding worth keeping. An overlay audit on 2026-08-21 sorted 28 modal-shaped overlays into "trivially convertible / needs a decision / must not convert" and put 12 in the first bucket. It sorted on GEOMETRY (items-end vs items-center) and never read scrim colour or z-tier. Verified one by one against Dialog's z-[80] + bg-ink/60 + backdrop-blur-sm, SEVEN candidates yielded exactly ONE true no-op:

  invite-launcher       z-[80]  bg-ink/60  blur-sm   EXACT MATCH -> converted (align="sheet")
  vera-lightbox         z-[60]  bg-ink/60  blur-sm   scrim ok, tier 60 -> 80
  invite-friend-button  z-[80]  button scrim         tier ok, scrim is a click-target element
  capture-launcher      z-[70]  bg-ink/70  blur-sm   tier 70 -> 80, scrim lightens
  chores-overlay        z-[70]  bg-ink/70  blur-sm   tier 70 -> 80, scrim lightens
  teaser-gate           z-50    bg-ink/40  blur-2px  tier + scrim both change
  induction             z-50    bg-ink/40  no blur   tier + scrim change, blur appears

A GREP ALONE WOULD ALSO HAVE BEEN WRONG. teaser-gate and invite-friend-button look scrimless on the `fixed inset-0` line because their scrim is a SIBLING element (an absolute div, and a click-to-dismiss button respectively). Reading the line is not reading the overlay.

SO THERE IS NO SWEEP HERE, only six individual judgments. A z-tier is a claim about what may appear above what (vera-lightbox at z-[60] sits BELOW the modal tier deliberately, so a Dialog can open over it), and a scrim opacity is a design choice (trophy-celebration, excluded from this row, uses a LIGHT bg-canvas/80 wash because it is a celebration, not a modal). Converting on autopilot would darken screens and reshuffle stacking with nobody having decided to.

WHAT IS AT STAKE IF THEY STAY: every one of the six lacks a portal (so the sliding admin rail can trap it), lacks the Space theme (ADR-1097), sits outside the dialog stack, and pads no safe area. Five of the six set aria-modal="true" with no focus trap at all, which tells a screen reader the page behind is inert while Tab walks straight out of it. ── SEQUENCED 2026-08-24 into W6 beside PROG-DAWN3, the other mechanical sweep. It was filed after the 2026-08-20 slate was ruled and sat in no wave. ── ✅ CLOSED 2026-08-24 (ADR-1110). All six converted. THE ROW WAS RIGHT ABOUT THE COUNT AND WRONG ABOUT TWO THINGS, both in the direction of understating it. (1) 'Five of the six set aria-modal with no focus trap' is FOUR — components/teaser-gate.tsx and the induction preview end-state have NO dialog role at all: no name, no modal semantics, nothing. The row's sentence hid the two worst cases inside a claim about the other four. (2) 'vera-lightbox's z-[60] is deliberate so a Dialog can open over it' is FALSE — nothing in that subtree opens a Dialog, and z-[60] is the tier Dialog ITSELF abandoned (its own comment records why: at z-[60] a modal renders BEHIND the z-[70] mobile admin sheet while still locking scroll). Inheritance, not intent. THE TIERS AND THE SCRIMS ARE DIFFERENT KINDS OF CHANGE and are labelled as such rather than swept together: every tier move (50/60/70 -> 80) is a BUG FIX (none carried a justifying comment, none hosts a nested dialog, and two mount from app/(main)/layout.tsx on every route including /admin where they tied with the admin sheet), while three scrim moves onto bg-ink/60 are DECLARED design changes argued in each file. Dialog gained ariaLabelledBy, without which the conversion would have silently RENAMED two dialogs — invite-friend-button is the sharpest: its aria-label said 'Invite a friend' while its visible heading read 'Invite a friend, earn Zaps', so a screen-reader user heard a different name than a sighted member read. EQUIVALENCE PROVED rather than asserted: the same jsdom harness ran before and after, dumping <body> per overlay and diffing — every panel's inner markup is byte-identical, and every delta is enumerated per file. Mutation-proven five ways, each mutant re-hand-rolling that file's ORIGINAL overlay under the name Dialog so only the overlay regresses (6/7/8/7/6 failures). ⚠️ ONE CONSEQUENCE STATED: Dialog portals, so it renders nothing during SSR, and the LIVE-016 a11y test used renderToStaticMarkup and went red — the ASSERTION is untouched, only the render moved to a real client render. A test passing against static markup was, for that component, no longer testing what it claimed. THREE MORE OVERLAYS FOUND that the 2026-08-21 audit never listed, filed as LIVE-102 rather than folded in.

verify.cmd: node -e "const fs=require('fs');const files=['components/teaser-gate.tsx','app/join/(induction)/induction.tsx','components/sidebar/invite-friend-button.tsx','components/feed/capture-launcher.tsx','components/onboarding/vera-lightbox.tsx','components/onboarding/chores-overlay.tsx'];const bad=[];for(const f of files){if(!fs.existsSync(f)){console.error('missing: '+f);process.exit(79)}const t=fs.readFileSync(f,'utf8');if(t.indexOf('<Dialog')<0)bad.push(f+' no longer renders a Dialog');if(/fixed inset-0 z-\\[?[0-9]/.test(t))bad.push(f+' hand-rolls a fixed inset-0 overlay again')}if(bad.length){console.error(bad.join('; '));process.exit(1)}process.exit(0)"

entries.notes:
OPEN, and the probe reports NOT DONE because all six still hand-roll `fixed inset-0`. Closing it does NOT require converting all six: if the owner decides one should keep its own tier or scrim, that decision gets recorded here and the file drops out of the probe's path list with the reason attached. What the row refuses is the third option — leaving them unconverted and undecided.

components/invite/invite-launcher.tsx is deliberately NOT in the list: it was the one exact match and is already on Dialog. components/practice/claim-practice.tsx and components/create-modal.tsx are likewise done (ADR-1100). trophy-celebration is excluded because its z-[100] lightbox tier and bg-canvas/80 celebratory wash make it a deliberate difference rather than a pending conversion.

entries.title: toggleMembership makes no policy decision, so a member can grant themselves the paid tier
entries.detail: FOUND 2026-08-24 by a full-tree security sweep, then RAISED from med to high by a production read the finder could not take. toggleMembership (app/(main)/upgrade/actions.ts:25) establishes WHO the caller is (auth.getUser) and is correctly self-scoped, but never asks WHETHER a member may change their own tier right now. It writes profiles.membership_tier free<->crew through the ADMIN client with no billingLive() gate, while its sibling startSupporterContribution in the same file gates on billingLive() at :170. The only thing hiding it is a client-side conditional render (app/(main)/upgrade/page.tsx:215); upgrade-toggle.tsx statically imports the action and page.tsx statically imports the component, so Next registers the action id at build time and it stays POST-able whichever branch renders. NOT LATENT: billingLive() = billingEnabled() && billing_live (lib/pricing/settings.ts:213); loadPricingFlags reads platform_flags (:186) where billing_live = true; and production logs show live-mode Stripe calls against acct_1TdurHPhyalyRPP1. MEASURED BLAST RADIUS 2026-08-24: select membership_tier, count(*) from profiles -> crew 40, free 16. Sixteen members can POST one server action and take the paid tier for nothing. The money half is real because BOTH payout paths read the STORED tier to pick the take-rate rung (lib/billing/tickets.ts:383-387, lib/commerce/checkout.ts:75-82 via memberNetworkTakeRateBps) — free 10%, crew 8%. WHY THE GATE MISSED IT: check:authz matches auth.getUser as a GUARD and passes the file; identity is not authorization, and the gate's own header says gate CORRECTNESS is out of scope. FIX: add the sibling's gate at the top of toggleMembership. At launch, delete the action with its button in the same change — an orphaned 'use server' export is a live POST endpoint. ── CLOSED 2026-08-24: the gate is in place at the top of toggleMembership, above every read and write, and app/(main)/upgrade/actions.test.ts pins both halves — refuses with NO tier write when billingLive() is true, still toggles while billing is off.

verify.note: Bounded to toggleMembership's own body: the match may not cross the next top-level export, so the sibling action's billingLive() cannot satisfy it. In-process rather than a cmd probe, so no shell quoting can break it (it did) and it costs no extra node process.

entries.title: The outbox retry policy is error-blind, and it dropped 359 emails in one afternoon
entries.detail: FOUND 2026-08-24 by reading notification_queue in production. Nothing recorded this: no row, no ADR, no doc. THE DATA: the table holds 379 'done' (healthy, latest 2026-08-24 13:00, so the drain works today) and 359 'failed', every one created between 2026-07-17 16:00 and 17:43, all kind='email', all at attempts = max_attempts = 5, all carrying the same last_error: [email] send failed: {"statusCode":429,"message":"You have reached your daily email sending quota.","name":"daily_quota_exceeded"}. THE MECHANISM: nextRetry (lib/queue/outbox.ts:36-42) decides retryability from the ATTEMPT COUNT ALONE and never inspects the error. With BACKOFF_BASE_MS = 60_000 (:26) and max_attempts = 5, all five attempts land inside ~15 minutes, against a quota that resets DAILY. So a daily_quota_exceeded is not merely likely to dead-letter every queued email — it is guaranteed to. The queue drained itself into the dead-letter state in 1h43m. WHO PAID: 356 of the 359 were one bulk campaign to 356 distinct recipients; the other three are the real damage — two welcome emails to genuine new members and one event-claim invite. Bulk and transactional mail share one queue with no priority or quota separation, so a campaign starved the welcomes. WHY NOBODY SAW: the code dead-letters loudly (console.error at :128, comment says it 'needs operator attention (ADR-043)') and an operator surface exists with one-tap requeue (components/widgets/marketing/deliverability-dead-letters.tsx). But nothing pages: grepping lib/observability, scripts/ and .github/ for dead-letter references returns zero. Pull-only, and for five weeks nobody pulled. This is the AGENTS.md rule exactly — every fail-safe needs a gate that notices it fired. FIX (this row covers parts 1-2 only): 1. Classify before counting — a 429/rate-limit/quota error is retryable on a TIME axis, so push run_after past the window and do NOT increment attempts. 2. Separate bulk from transactional so a campaign can never starve a welcome. PART 3 (a gate that pages on a dead-letter spike) is already scoped inside DEF-HARDEN and stays there. PART 4 (requeue the three transactional rows, leave the five-week-stale campaign) is an operator action on live data — OWN-042. ── CLOSED 2026-08-24 (parts 1-2; part 3 stays in DEF-HARDEN, part 4 in OWN-042). PART 1: retryDelayFor (lib/queue/outbox.ts) classifies the error first and returns whether the attempt counts. A daily quota waits until the next UTC midnight and spends NO attempt; a generic 429 waits 15 minutes and spends no attempt; a provider Retry-After wins over both, floored at 1 minute and capped at 24 hours. Everything else is nextRetry byte for byte, dead-letter semantics untouched. Free deferrals are bounded by WALL-CLOCK AGE off created_at (the only clock the table already has, so no migration): 72h for a quota, 1h for a rate limit, after which the same error falls back to attempt counting and can dead-letter. PART 2: a lane (transactional | bulk) rides in the payload jsonb; the campaign fan-out and the nurture drip declare bulk, everything else is transactional by default, and a pre-lane campaign row still reads as bulk from its campaign_id tag. The drain runs transactional first within a batch and, on the first quota refusal, parks the rest of the bulk lane without calling the provider. The fan-out also drips its run_after at 10/min so it cannot fill the claim window. NOT DONE, and stated plainly: claim_outbox_jobs is 'order by run_after asc' and lane-blind, so an ALREADY-backlogged bulk queue can still sit in front of a welcome at CLAIM time. Closing that needs a lane/priority column plus a new ORDER BY in the RPC, i.e. a migration, which this row did not write.

verify.note: Measures the DEFECT, not the fix. The row originally specified grep-present "retryDelayFor", which passes the moment the NAME exists — the shape-not-truth failure four ADRs name, and the implementing agent said so unprompted. This greps for the drain line that made the decision from the attempt count alone. Behaviour is pinned by 22 tests in outbox.test.ts, including the 2026-07-17 case end-to-end: five drains of 429 daily_quota_exceeded never dead-letter, never write attempts, and each land within 10s of the next UTC midnight.

entries.title: Blocking is not enforced on friend requests, so a blocked member keeps a channel
entries.detail: FOUND 2026-08-24 by a full-tree security sweep. sendFriendRequest (app/(main)/people/friend-actions.ts:45-88) resolves the caller from the session, so there is no IDOR, but it never consults isBlockedBetween — while SIX sibling contact-initiating paths do: app/(main)/messages/actions.ts:53,138,202, lib/messages/scoped-dm.ts:344, lib/comms/bulk-dm.ts:126, app/(main)/events/[slug]/social-actions.ts:101, app/(main)/market/service-actions.ts:109. The loop is closed by two deletes: blockUser DELETES the friendship row (lib/blocking.ts:31-33), leaving a clean slate for a fresh 'pending' insert, and declineFriendRequest deletes it again (:132-136, comment: 'so the requester can try again later'). So block -> request -> notification -> decline -> repeat, indefinitely, each cycle writing a notifications row addressed to the person who blocked them. The profile page's own guard is ONE-DIRECTIONAL — hasBlocked(myProfileId, profileId) asks 'did I block them' (app/(main)/people/[handle]/page.tsx:194) — so the BLOCKED viewer sees a normal FriendButton (:388) and is not even hidden client-side. VERIFIED there is no other layer: no wrapper (four client components call it directly), NO middleware.ts anywhere in the repo, no DB trigger and no RLS (supabase/migrations/20240301000000_blocked_users.sql states enforcement is app-code only), and no block filter in lib/notifications/. This is exactly the contact channel ADR-036 shipped blocking to close ('required for a public beta and for App Store review'). FIX: one line matching the six siblings, plus the same treatment for inviteToRoom (app/(main)/messages/rooms/actions.ts:278), which today relies only on an accepted-friendship check that a pre-block friendship could have satisfied. ── CLOSED 2026-08-24. One line matching the six siblings, plus friend-actions.test.ts pinning that a blocked pair writes NO friendships row and NO notifications row (the notification is the actual harm). ── ONE CLAIM IN THIS ROW WAS REFUTED WHILE FIXING IT: the row said inviteToRoom (app/(main)/messages/rooms/actions.ts:278) needed the same treatment because 'a pre-block friendship could have satisfied' its accepted-friendship check. It could not. blockUser (lib/blocking.ts:31-33) deletes the friendship row unconditionally on the canonical pair with no status filter, so after a block there is no row at all and the invite path already throws. Blocking IS enforced there, transitively. The asymmetry is worth keeping: the same unfriend-on-block CLOSES the invite path (which requires a friendship to exist) and OPENS the request path (which requires one to be absent). No gate was added to inviteToRoom — a guard that can never fire reads as coverage it does not provide (ADR-970). ── UNVERIFIED, NOT CHASED: blocking deletes the friendship but does NOT remove existing room_members rows, so a blocked pair already sharing a group room appears to stay in it together. That is a separate question from this row and wants its own measurement before anyone writes code.

verify.note: Passes when the friend-request path consults the block list, like its six siblings.

entries.title: listPublicSpaceCircles admits only active, so a Space with forming Circles shows none
entries.detail: FOUND 2026-08-24 in the delta audit of the 30 PRs since the last full scan, and CONFIRMED LIVE against production the same day. listPublicSpaceCircles hard-filters .eq('status', 'active') on all three of its arms (lib/circles/store.ts:431 owner path, :445 listed path, :509 inside myCirclesInSpace), where every other public circle reader admits forming too: lib/nearby/map-pins.ts:218 and lib/channels/programs.ts:123 use .in('status', ['forming','active']), lib/circles/remix.ts:120 the same, and lib/people/associations.ts:116 carries a local LISTABLE_CIRCLE_STATUS of ['forming','active','inactive']. app/(main)/admin/actions.ts:235 creates circles with status defaulting to 'forming', so the operator path produces exactly the rows this reader hides. CONSEQUENCE: a Space whose Circles sit at forming gets no Circles tab at all (lib/spaces/profile-nav.ts:81 gates on presence.circles, which flows from this reader), a 'Circles 0' hero stat (lib/spaces/profile-stats.ts:58), and a 'No circles yet' empty state on a page its own manage console lists rows on. NOT HYPOTHETICAL: select status, count(*) from circles on prod azsqfeonabsbmemvddqd, 2026-08-24 -> forming 2 circles in 1 space, draft 3 in 1 space, active 2 in 2 spaces. A real Space's Circles tab is suppressed right now. ATTRIBUTION, because it matters: LIVE-083 is honestly done — its probe proves the unlisted/access visibility fix it was about. This is a NEW adjacent defect from that same change, where the fix for one visibility axis over-narrowed a different one, and LIVE-083's probe structurally cannot see it. FIX: replace the three .eq('status','active') calls in these two functions with .in('status', [...LISTABLE_CIRCLE_STATUS]) against one exported constant. NOT widened to map-pins/programs/remix this pass: those are already behaviourally correct, and map-pins.test.ts:109 asserts the string literal, so adopting the constant there is a separate mechanical change. ── CLOSED 2026-08-24. LISTABLE_CIRCLE_STATUS = ['forming','active'] now lives in lib/circles/visibility.ts, next to the two axes it is repeatedly confused with, and all three circles reads in store.ts use it. Four tests in store.test.ts pin it: forming lists beside active, draft and archived still do not, the owner path agrees so preview matches the manage console, and the viewer's own forming circle still resolves. CORRECTION TO THIS ROW'S OWN COUNT: it said three .eq('status','active') sites at :431,:445,:509 and the file holds nine. Six of the other seven are on memberships / space_members / space_memberships / journey_runs and are correct as written (an ACTIVE MEMBERSHIP is a real thing); only the three named were on circles. The test harness also had to learn that PostgREST ANDs multiple .in() calls — its fake builder kept one slot, so with two .in() clauses it would have silently dropped the status filter and passed a tree that filtered on neither. NOT WIDENED: map-pins / programs / remix already admit forming and were left alone; map-pins.test.ts:109 asserts the string literal, so adopting the constant there is a separate mechanical change.

verify.note: TABLE-SCOPED on purpose. The first draft of this probe was bounded by function markers and would have demanded changing .eq(status, active) on MEMBERSHIPS, which is correct code on a different table. This one matches only a query chain rooted at from(circles), so it fires on a real regression anywhere in the module and never on the six legitimate membership/run filters. Proven with three controls: passes now, fires when one circles filter is restored, silent when only the memberships filters remain.

entries.title: ADR-1093’s Stripe throw-guard reached one billing surface of two
entries.detail: FOUND 2026-08-24 in the delta audit. Commit bb4a690 added the viaStripe() wrapper to every Stripe reach in app/(main)/settings/billing/actions.ts with the note 'Never let one of these throw again.' The sibling file — modified in the same range — was left bare: 5 viaStripe uses on the member surface, ZERO on the Space surface, with three raw awaits at app/(main)/spaces/[slug]/settings/billing/actions.ts:43 (createSpaceBillingPortal), :55 (updateOperatorSeats) and :86 (createSpaceLoadoutCheckout). Neither callee catches: lib/billing/space-plan-checkout.ts:100 calls stripe.billingPortal.sessions.create with no try, and the loadout path calls stripe.checkout.sessions.create the same way; both return string|null only for GATE misses (no key, no customer, plan not sellable), never for a throw. NOT THEORETICAL: a StripeInvalidRequestError is exactly what production threw on /settings on 2026-08-20 ('You must complete your platform profile to use Connect...' and 'Please review the responsibilities of managing losses...'), which is the incident ADR-1093 was written about. On the Space surface such a throw escapes the action and trips the error boundary, replacing the whole /spaces/<slug>/settings/billing page — plan, seats and portal — rather than showing an inline error on the card that asked. FIX: lift viaStripe out of the member actions file into a shared module and wrap all three call sites. ── CLOSED 2026-08-24. viaStripe moved out of the member actions file into lib/billing/via-stripe.ts and all three Space call sites wrapped. The seam that stops this recurring is lib/billing/via-stripe.test.ts: a source-shape test that holds BOTH surfaces to the rule at once, so a fourth Stripe reach added to either file without a wrapper fails there rather than in production. Proven as a real control, not one that passes by existing — the regex matches the pre-fix line and not the post-fix one. Log labels are now prefixed by surface (settings/billing …, spaces/billing …) since the file no longer implies which page threw.

verify.note: Passes when the Space billing surface carries the same throw-guard as the member surface.

entries.title: A rejected chat send loses the draft and leaves the bubble reading as sent
entries.detail: FOUND 2026-08-24 in the delta audit. send() (components/chat/use-support-chat.ts:93) has no try/catch around persist(), and both callers consume it with a bare .then(): support-chat-widget.tsx:299 and live-chat-bridge.tsx:34. isError(r) only covers the action RETURNING an ActionResult failure. A Next.js server action REJECTS on a network drop or an unhandled server error — the most likely failure for a visitor-facing widget. On that path the promise rejects before 'return false', so the .then callback never runs and the draft is gone (the exact loss the new JSDoc claims it fixed: 'they now put the draft back on false'), the optimistic bubble is never removed so the visitor sees their message as sent, setError never fires so no banner appears, and the rejection is unhandled. Same shape one line up at :57: loadHistory().then((r) => { ...; setLoading(false) }) with no .catch, so a rejected history read leaves the panel on 'Loading...' forever. The file currently contains ZERO catch blocks. FIX: wrap the body of send in try/catch — drop the optimistic row, set a real error, return false — and add .catch(() => setLoading(false)) to the loadHistory chain. Both callers then need no change. ── CLOSED 2026-08-24. send() now wraps persist() in try/catch and handles a REJECTION exactly as it handles a returned failure: the optimistic row is dropped, a readable error is set, and it returns false, so the draft-restoring .then in both callers runs on the network-drop path too. Neither caller changed. The loadHistory chain gained a .catch that clears loading and sets an error, so a rejected history read ends the "Loading…" state instead of pinning it. Two fallback strings live at the top of the file for the failures the server never gets to describe. Proven by components/chat/use-support-chat.test.tsx (5 tests): the two rejection cases fail against the pre-fix file, the happy path and the returned-ActionResult-failure path pass both before and after.

verify.cmd: node -e "const fs=require('fs');const S='components/chat/use-support-chat.ts',T='components/chat/use-support-chat.test.tsx';if(!fs.existsSync(S)||!fs.existsSync(T))process.exit(79);const s=fs.readFileSync(S,'utf8'),t=fs.readFileSync(T,'utf8');const code=s.split(String.fromCharCode(10)).filter(x=>x.trim().indexOf('//')!==0&&x.trim().indexOf('*')!==0).join(String.fromCharCode(10));const bad=[];const p=code.indexOf('await persist(');if(p<0)bad.push('persist() call not found - re-read this probe');else if(code.slice(Math.max(0,p-200),p).lastIndexOf('try')<0)bad.push('the await persist() call is not inside a try: a REJECTED persist leaves the optimistic bubble reading as sent, loses the draft and never returns false');const c=code.indexOf('.catch(');if(c<0)bad.push('the loadHistory chain has no .catch: a rejected history read pins the panel on Loading');else if(code.slice(c).indexOf('setLoading(false)')<0)bad.push('the .catch never clears loading');if(t.indexOf('Promise.reject')<0)bad.push('no rejection test in '+T);if(bad.length){console.error(bad.join('; '));process.exit(1)}process.exit(0)"
verify.note: Three conditions, all measuring the DEFECT. The first version checked only that the word catch appeared ANYWHERE in the file, so it still passed against a source with send()'s try/catch removed — the loadHistory .catch alone satisfied it. It now requires the `await persist(` call itself to sit inside a try, verified as a control in both directions.

entries.title: An uncapped Circle sorts last under "Most room"
entries.detail: FOUND 2026-08-24 in the delta audit, confirmed by reading both functions. roomIn (app/(main)/spaces/[slug]/(profile)/circles/page.tsx:315-320) returns 0 when member_cap is absent, but cap <= 0 means NO CAP, which isOpenToJoin fifteen lines above (:299-303) correctly reads as always-joinable (return cap <= 0 || ...). So under ?sort=open ('Most room') every uncapped Circle sorts BELOW a capped one with a single seat left — the exact opposite of the function's own docstring, which says an uncapped circle is 'treated as roomy but never infinite'. Uncapped is the default for a new Circle, so this is the common case, not the edge. FIX: return a named constant expressing the docstring's own rule (roomy but not infinite) for the uncapped case, and unit-test sortCircles with one uncapped circle against one capped circle at cap-1. ── CLOSED 2026-08-24. The three pure helpers (roomIn, sortCircles, isOpenToJoin) moved out of page.tsx into a colocated sort.ts, because while they sat in the route file they could not be unit-tested — which is exactly what this bug cost. Seven tests now pin it, including the docstring rule in both directions: an uncapped Circle beats a nearly-full capped one, AND a genuinely emptier capped Circle still beats the uncapped one, so "roomy but never infinite" is a measured claim rather than a comment.

verify.note: Measures the DEFECT, not the fix: this is the exact expression that returned zero room for an uncapped Circle. A grep-present for the new constant would pass by existing, which is the shape-not-truth failure. Proven as a control: the pattern matches the pre-fix line and not the post-fix one. The behaviour itself is pinned by sort.test.ts, which runs in CI.

entries.title: The /spaces/:slug/community 308 can now land on a permanently cached 404
entries.detail: FOUND 2026-08-24 in the delta audit. next.config.ts:318 redirects /spaces/:slug/community -> /spaces/:slug/circles with permanent: true. The previous destination (/spaces/:slug) resolved for any visible Space. The new destination notFound()s on two conditions the old one did not: app/(main)/spaces/[slug]/(profile)/circles/page.tsx:96 (space.type === 'root') and :100 (the circles function switched off). Because this is a 308 the browser caches it, so an operator who turns the Circles function off converts a previously-working bookmark — and every already-sent notification link — into a permanently cached 404. Leave the :93 !space notFound() alone — a missing Space is a real 404. ── CLOSED 2026-08-24. Both soft cases (root Space, circles function off) now redirect to the Space root instead of 404ing; the missing-Space case stays a notFound(), because that is a real 404. The gate comment in the page header now states why, naming the cached-308 interaction that makes a 404 here permanent rather than transient.

entries.title: The two circle-claim Zap awards carry no daily cap
entries.detail: FOUND 2026-08-24 by a full-tree security sweep, then settled against production. claimCircle (app/(main)/circles/[slug]/claim-actions.ts:13-56) verifies the caller is real and the circle is is_demo, then sets host_id: myId. There is no check that the caller ever visited, joined or was offered that circle, and the id is a client argument — this is the documented ADR-1048 flow, so the CLAIM is intended. The reward side-effect is not: each claim calls awardZapsForAction(myId, 'circle_start') (:78) and, with a practiceId, 'circle_activate' (:79). recordEngagementEvent is idempotent per circle; the Zap award is not. MEASURED 2026-08-24: select action_type, zaps_amount, daily_cap, is_active from zap_config -> circle_start 100 Zaps daily_cap NULL active, circle_activate 40 Zaps daily_cap NULL active. So enumerating demo circle ids farms 140 Zaps a time with no ceiling. OWNER LANE because the cheapest correct fix is a config write to live data (set daily_cap on the two rows), which an agent must not make unilaterally; the alternative is a code change binding the claim to a demo circle the caller is actually a member of. Either arm closes this. ── CODE ARM LANDED 2026-08-24 (owner chose BOTH arms), BUT NOT THE ONE THIS ROW PRESCRIBED, AND THE ROW WAS WRONG. It proposed binding the claim to a demo circle the caller is actually a member of. That would BREAK the feature: docs/DEMO-SYSTEM.md's Claim-this-Circle flow (ADR-1048 Phase 2) is that a signed-in real member VIEWING a demo circle sees the banner and claims it, and ClaimCircle renders from the circle layout for any viewer. Membership is not part of the flow, so requiring it would gate out every honest claimer to stop a farmer. WHAT WAS ACTUALLY WRONG is the REWARD, not the claim: recordEngagementEvent is idempotent per circle and the Zap award is not, so enumerating ids collects 140 Zaps a time. A per-profile rate limit closes exactly that — rateLimitOk('circle:claim', myId, 3, '1 d') in app/(main)/circles/[slug]/claim-actions.ts — because claiming three sample circles in one day is already far past honest use, while a member genuinely starting circles does it over weeks. It neither touches the documented flow nor under-rewards a real host, which a once-per-member award would have. THE OWNER HALF IS STILL OPEN: set daily_cap on the circle_start and circle_activate rows in zap_config. The two halves are independent on purpose — neither relies on the other, so the belt survives if the braces are ever loosened. This row stays OPEN until the config write lands. ── 🔴 THE OWNER HALF WAS INERT, AND NOBODY KNEW UNTIL 2026-08-24. This row had been asking the owner to 'set daily_cap on the circle_start and circle_activate rows' since it was written. THAT CONFIG WRITE WOULD HAVE DONE NOTHING. lib/zaps.ts awardZapsForAction selected `zaps_amount, is_active` and handed off to an unconditional insert; the string `daily_cap` appeared ZERO times in the file, while /admin/gamification let an operator set one and even validated it carefully (a present-but-invalid cap is REJECTED rather than silently becoming NULL, precisely so an operator's throttle is never quietly dropped). The Gem path read it correctly all along. So this row's remaining ask was not merely open — it was UNACHIEVABLE, and would have CLOSED FALSELY had the owner performed it. That is the cheapest kind of row to get wrong and the hardest to notice, because doing the work would have produced no error and no visible change. ── ENFORCEMENT LANDED AND APPLIED 2026-08-24 (ADR-1109). awardZapsForAction now reads daily_cap and delegates the check AND the insert to award_zaps_atomic — the Gem RPC's shape, per-(profile, action) advisory xact lock, UTC day boundary, one serialized section, NULL cap = uncapped, fails CLOSED on an RPC error with a tagged Sentry capture. Proved against a REAL Postgres (20 pgTAP assertions) plus an 8-session concurrency run: 1 ledger row with the lock, 8 without — the Gem incident reproduced on the Zap function before it shipped. Migration 20270322000000 APPLIED to production and the ledger repaired to that version (630 rows against 630 files); verified from the catalog: anon false, authenticated false, service_role true, security definer, search_path pinned. ⚠️ THE OWNER ACTION IS NOW REAL AND STILL OUTSTANDING: set daily_cap on circle_start and circle_activate at /admin/gamification. Both reach the ledger through awardZapsForAction, which IS the capped path, so the write now bites. ⚠️ SCOPE, so it is set with open eyes: the cap binds on awardZapsForAction only. awardZaps (caller-computed amount, no config row) still inserts directly, and 186 of 199 practice_logged rows go through it — an uncapped row still CONSUMES the day's allowance, and reverseZaps debits under a different action_type so un-logging does not return it. This row closes on the code, which is what it could control; the config write is tracked in OWN-040.

verify.evidence: Code arm done (per-profile claim rate limit, 3/day). ENFORCEMENT arm done AND APPLIED 2026-08-24 (ADR-1109): migration 20270322000000 is live in production, ledger repaired to 630/630, grants verified from pg_proc (anon false, authenticated false, service_role true). Before it, a daily_cap write on ANY zap_config row was inert, so this row's owner half could not have worked and would have closed falsely. Both circle actions run through awardZapsForAction, the capped path, so the remaining config write now has an effect — moved to OWN-040 as an owner-config item rather than holding this row open, because the code half is what this row could control and it is complete.

entries.title: Decide what happens to the 359 dead-lettered emails
entries.detail: The operator half of LIVE-091. 359 rows sit in notification_queue at status='failed' from the 2026-07-17 quota exhaustion. The operator surface (components/widgets/marketing/deliverability-dead-letters.tsx) already offers a one-tap requeue, so no code is needed. THE DECISION: 356 of the 359 are one bulk campaign now five weeks stale and almost certainly should NOT be re-sent; the other three are transactional and arguably should be — two welcome emails to genuine new members who never received one, and one event-claim invite. Requeuing the transactional three is a live send to real people, so it is the owner's call, not an agent's. Note the ordering: fixing LIVE-091 first is what stops a requeue from re-running the same failure. ── OWNER RULED 2026-08-24 'requeue the 3 transactional only', AND THEN THE RULING'S PREMISE DID NOT SURVIVE THE DATA, SO NOTHING WAS SENT. The ruling was made on my characterisation that the three were 'worth sending late'. Measured before touching anything, that is false for all three. (1) The claim invite is for 'Exquisite Beasts: Night of the Soul', starts_at 2026-07-18 — FIVE WEEKS PAST. Sending it invites a host to claim an event that already happened. (2) The welcome to IshAset Lumi goes to a member with 239 engagement events who was active on 2026-08-20; a 'Welcome to Frequency' five weeks after they joined and while they are actively using the product reads as broken software, not as hospitality. (3) The welcome to David is the only one where the mail was genuinely missed and never substituted — he joined 2026-07-17, recorded 5 events, left after about three hours and never came back — but a five-week-late 'Welcome' to someone who has gone is a RE-ENGAGEMENT email wearing a welcome's clothes, and it should be written as one rather than replayed. NOTHING WAS REQUEUED. Sending is outward-facing and irreversible, and the justification for it evaporated on inspection; an agent executing it anyway on a ruling made from a wrong summary is the failure mode this list exists to prevent. WHAT THIS ROW NOW NEEDS is a smaller decision than the one it asked: either mark all three handled and leave them as history, or write David a real re-engagement note that does not pretend to be a welcome. The 356-row campaign is unchanged and still should not be sent. NOTE the underlying defect is fixed either way: LIVE-091 shipped, so a requeue can no longer re-run the 2026-07-17 quota failure. ── CLOSED 2026-08-24: OWNER RULED 'don't send those emails, clear it all out'. All 359 rows deleted from notification_queue (the 356-recipient campaign and the 3 that had been called transactional). The queue is now 379 done, 0 failed, 0 pending. NOTHING WAS SENT, which is the right outcome on the evidence: the claim invite was for an event five weeks past, one welcome was addressed to a member with 239 engagement events who was active four days ago, and the other was to a member who left after three hours — a five-week-late 'Welcome' to any of them reads as broken software rather than hospitality. The DLQ sitting at ZERO is now a usable baseline: any non-zero dead-letter count from here is new, which is exactly the signal DEF-HARDEN's alerting half needs and could not have had while 359 stale rows sat in front of it.

verify.evidence: Deleted 2026-08-24 on the owner's ruling; verified after: notification_queue is 379 done, 0 failed, 0 pending. Future sends verified healthy the same day: 20 emails drained successfully in the trailing 14 days, most recent 2026-08-24 13:00, and LIVE-091's error-aware retry is deployed in e4e44123c.

The acceptance is explicitly scale-bound and says so in the entry: at 23 active members 10 Auth connections is not the constraint, and it re-opens if the instance is resized or sign-in latency reaches the SLOs. Accepting a finding is only honest when the reason is written down and carries its own expiry.

entries.title: Two campaign senders, two reliability postures: one queues, one sends inline
entries.detail: FOUND 2026-08-24 while fixing LIVE-091, and it is the reason that fix does not reach as far as it looks. LIVE-091 said 'bulk and transactional mail share one queue', which assumes all bulk mail IS queued. It is not. lib/email-studio/send.ts fans a campaign out through the OUTBOX — durable, retried, and now lane-tagged so it can never starve a welcome. lib/spaces/email.ts sendSpaceCampaign sends campaigns INLINE via sendRawEmail, with no outbox row at all: no durability, no retry, no lane, and no dead-letter surface. So a Space campaign that hits the same daily quota that dropped 359 emails on 2026-07-17 does not get deferred and does not get recorded — it just fails, and nothing holds the message. The LIVE-091 lane work cannot reach that path by construction. THE DECISION: route sendSpaceCampaign through enqueueEmail with lane 'bulk' like its sibling, or state deliberately why a Space campaign is allowed to be best-effort while a platform campaign is durable. Two senders with different reliability postures and no recorded reason is the thing to fix either way. ── CLOSED 2026-08-24 by the ROUTE arm (owner ruling). sendSpaceCampaign now enqueues each recipient onto the durable outbox with lane 'bulk' and a dripped run_after off one fan-out clock, exactly like its sibling lib/email-studio/send.ts. The inline sendRawEmail call is gone, which also settles the contradiction that made this a finding: lib/email.ts's own header states 'the spine: queue all email, never send inline (ADR-026)', and this was the one campaign sender violating it. THE RECONCILIATION QUESTION THAT MADE ME DEFER THIS TURNED OUT TO BE ALREADY ANSWERED BY THE SCHEMA. The blocker looked like recordSend writing status 'sent' + resend_id per recipient, which cannot be true at enqueue time. But outreach_sends_status_check already permits queued | sent | delivered | bounced | complained | failed | suppressed — the DB was designed for this async lifecycle all along and only the TypeScript union was narrower. So a campaign row is now 'queued' with no resend_id, the delivery webhook moves it on, and NO MIGRATION was needed. The ledger id still equals the tracking token's send id, so opens and clicks resolve unchanged. Cap accounting is unchanged and still honest: it counts a job we have COMMITTED to send, which is what a fresh countTodaySends will also see. Tests: the suite's mock was re-pointed from sendRawEmail to enqueueEmail (the seam moved, the assertions did not), and the ledger assertion now pins the queued lifecycle including the deliberate ABSENCE of a resend id — asserting one there is precisely what would let this test pass against an inline send it no longer does. 83 files / 1,215 tests green across lib/spaces, lib/queue and lib/email-studio.

verify.note: Passes when the Space campaign sender goes through the durable outbox like its sibling. Re-pointed 2026-08-25: the 08-24 close enqueued the generic 'email' kind, whose handler DISCARDS the provider id -- so 'the delivery webhook moves it on' was impossible (webhooks match on resend_id), campaign rows stranded at 'queued', and per-Space bounce suppression was blind. Campaigns now enqueue the dedicated kind whose drain handler (runSpaceCampaignEmail) writes resend_id + 'sent' back to the ledger row; the old /enqueueEmail/ pattern matched the broken shape.

entries.title: check:og-trace read from a local build is not evidence, and it just cost an alarm
entries.detail: FOUND 2026-08-24. A parallel session reported check:og-trace FAILING with '16 card-rasterising routes ship without sharp', cards silently serving ~1.7MB instead of ~151KB. RE-MEASURED AGAINST PRODUCTION AND IT IS NOT TRUE: the postbuild of dpl_4RwDvdMkY1kAJYyR77Zmx5zfDZLC (sha 16c3cf7, the same commit) printed '✅ check:og-trace — sharp ships to all 16 rasterising route(s), and to 67 other function(s) by segment inheritance (budget 100). 414 functions carry none of it.' The '16' is the same number in both readings: the COUNT OF RASTERISING ROUTES, not the count of starved ones. THE REAL HAZARD, which is worth a row: this gate reads .next/server/**/*.nft.json, and its verdict is only as good as the artifact underneath. With NO .next it is honest — it prints 'Run pnpm build first' and exits. With a LOCAL build whose trace shape differs from Vercel's it can report starved routes that are not starved in the deploy, and the failure message talks about Apple Mail timing out, so it reads as urgent. AGENTS.md already says the artifact is gated in postbuild, not CI, because CI never builds — that rule needs to extend to READING the gate: a local run is a smoke test, the production postbuild is the evidence. FIX: teach the gate to say so when it cannot tell it is running against a production artifact, and note it in DEPLOY-SAFETY.md. NOT diagnosed further here: reproducing the local trace shape needs pnpm build, which hangs this box, so WHY a local build traces differently is unmeasured and must not be guessed at. ── CLOSED 2026-08-24. The gate now checks VERCEL=1 and, when it is not in a Vercel build, prints that its verdict is a smoke test rather than evidence — and repeats that beside the red starved-route block, which is exactly where the false alarm gets read and escalated. Proven with two controls in a throwaway artifact: the notice fires on a local read and is silent under VERCEL=1, and the escalation line appears attached to a genuinely starved route. The no-.next path was already honest (it refuses to answer) and is unchanged. NOT diagnosed: WHY a local build traces differently from Vercel is still unmeasured, because reproducing it needs pnpm build, which hangs this box. The gate now says it cannot tell, which is the honest state; it does not guess.

verify.note: Greps for the sentence a reader actually sees next to a red starved-route block, which is where the false alarm was read. My first probe for this row matched the word "postbuild", already present in the file, so it passed on arrival — caught by check:backlog on the same run that added it.

entries.title: StreakMeter's frozen day state has no live producer, so the kindest branch never renders
entries.detail: Found 2026-08-24 while re-testing PROG-DAWN2's StreakMeter half. StreakMeter paints three day states — done, missed, and FROZEN (info-teal + snowflake, the 'life happens' pause that says an absence is not a failure). The frozen branch has ZERO live callers, and the code says so itself: components/sidebar/game-stats-dock.tsx:451-453 comments on it, because DockData.last7 is typed boolean[], so every freeze arrives as `true` and paints as `done`. The kindest branch of the component's emotional contract is unreachable in production. This is DATA PLUMBING, not an API change: the tri-state has to survive from lib/practice-streak.ts through components/sidebar/right-sidebar.tsx:154 into the dock, which means widening last7 off boolean[]. Kept separate from PROG-DAWN2 because that row was about widening the primitive's API and this is about feeding it — and because it touches the rail's data assembly, which is a different blast radius. ── ✅ CLOSED 2026-08-24, the same day it was filed. The tri-state now survives end to end: lib/practice-streak.ts gained frozenDaysFrom(meta, anchor) and streakDayRun(anchor, logged, frozen) returning StreakDay[]; components/sidebar/right-sidebar.tsx builds last7 from both sets; DockData.last7 is StreakDay[] rather than boolean[]. So the frozen branch — info-teal and a snowflake, the branch that says an absence is not a failure — can reach a member for the first time since StreakMeter shipped. VERIFIED BY MUTATION rather than by assertion, and by me rather than by the agent that wrote it: disabling frozenDaysFrom turns 7 tests red across lib/practice-streak.test.ts. The row's own stated close condition was 'a render test asserting the dock CAN emit a frozen day', and that test exists (components/sidebar/game-stats-dock.test.tsx) — it drives the REAL producers over a real profiles.meta shape and counts the rendered frozen dots, so it goes red if the plumbing is unwired anywhere along the path rather than passing on a hand-made prop. 44 tests green across practice-streak, the dock, the sidebar and streak-meter. ⚠️ NOTE ON PROVENANCE: the agent implementing this was killed by a connection error mid-write-up, after the code landed but before it produced its proofs. The implementation was therefore verified independently before this row was closed, rather than closed on a report that was never finished.

entries.title: /the-community lost its PillarNav cross-link when its coded body was retired

entries.detail: Found 2026-08-24 while retiring the-community's coded body (LIVE-006), and DELIBERATELY NOT smuggled into that change.
