Retiring a body may not quietly change what a page links to; the honest move was to say so. ── ✅ CLOSED 2026-08-24, hours after being filed. The PillarNav block is restored to lib/page-editor/templates/the-community.ts in the SAME seat its two siblings use — between the FAQ and the ink close, on the `surface` tone — so the three pillar pages now end the same way and the triptych links across all three. Placement was the actual work, not the block: the-community.ts is the EXEMPLAR template with a documented section rhythm in its own header, and the choice is reasoned in a comment beside the block (a triptych is a way OUT of the page, so it belongs after the last question is answered and before the one ask; the single ink beat tc-guru remains the only dark band before the ink close, and the FAQ it follows is already `surface`). The template header's HOW TO READ list was updated to name it as item 6 rather than leaving the rhythm doc stale. Verified: lib/page-editor/templates 8 files / 66 tests pass, check:render-path reads 16 gated slugs with 14 template-only.

entries.title: PACKED_PER_RAW is applied to one cache mix and was measured on another, and today's build shows the gap is 2x
entries.detail:
FOUND 2026-08-24 by doing what check:cache-budget's own output asks for. It prints: "Packed figure is an estimate: raw x 0.53 (measured 2026-08-19 from one build that printed both halves). Compare it with this build's 'Uploading build cache' line; if the two have drifted apart, the cache MIX has changed and the ratio wants re-deriving." Nobody had compared them since. The production build of 086667000 (#2245, dpl_2zgzjMjWzCKPhygibKzepoWNQskJ, READY 2026-08-24) prints BOTH halves:

  gate estimate   0.91 GiB raw x 0.53  ->  about 0.52 GB packed
  actual upload   "Uploading build cache [257.84 MB]"  ->  0.258 GB

That is a factor of 2.0. The measured post-trim ratio is 0.26, not 0.53.

🔴 THE FINDING IS NOT "THE CONSTANT IS WRONG", AND THAT DISTINCTION IS THE WHOLE ROW. The 0.53 was derived on 2026-08-19 from a build whose cache was MOSTLY COMPILER CACHE. The 0.26 above was measured on a cache that is almost entirely node_modules (933 MiB) because this same gate had just trimmed .next/cache to 0 MiB in the line above. Those are two different mixes and they compress differently, so neither number is wrong about its own build and the two cannot be averaged. What today proves is that the mix-dependence is LARGE - a factor of two - and the gate applies ONE ratio to BOTH mixes: it decides whether to trim from the PRE-trim mix, then reports the post-trim figure using the same constant.

WHAT IT COSTS TODAY, AND WHY THIS IS NOT URGENT. The error is in the fail-safe direction, deliberately (ADR-1086 rounded toward firing early). Over-estimating packed size makes the gate trim SOONER than necessary, and losing a compiler cache costs CPU on the next build; under-estimating would let Vercel discard the WHOLE cache, node_modules included, which is the failure ADR-1064 exists to prevent. So nothing is at risk. What it costs is build minutes: this build measured 3.10 GiB raw pre-trim, estimated 1.76 GB packed against a 1.40 GB trim point, and threw away 2237 MiB of turbopack cache - "Next build: warm install, cold compile", on every deploy. If the pre-trim mix also packs nearer 0.26 than 0.53 then 3.10 GiB is about 0.87 GB packed, comfortably under the 1.50 GB ceiling, and that trim was not needed at all.

⚠️ THE ONE THING NOT TO DO IS LOWER THE CONSTANT FROM THIS READING. 0.26 is the ratio of a node_modules-dominated cache, and it would be applied to a compiler-cache-dominated one. Getting this backwards is precisely how the first version of this gate KILLED TWO BUILDS (raw-vs-packed threshold about 2:1 off, and a trim that deleted the incremental fetch cache and hung Collecting page data until BUILD_EXCEEDED_MAXIMUM_TIME at 46 minutes). A ratio has to be measured on the mix it will be applied to.

HOW TO CLOSE IT: get a build that prints BOTH halves with an UNTRIMMED cache - i.e. one where the raw figure is under the trim point, so the upload line measures the same mix the gate reasoned about. Then either (a) carry two ratios, one per mix, with the pre-trim decision using the compiler-heavy one; or (b) stop estimating and read the previous build's actual upload line, which is the only number that is not a model. Record whichever, and the paired readings, in an ADR beside the constant the way ADR-1086 did. ── ✅ RE-MEASURED AND CLOSED 2026-08-24, and the answer is 'real but immaterial' rather than 'wrong'. The row's alarm was that one constant is applied to two mixes. Both halves of that are true; the conclusion drawn from it was not. FIVE PAIRED READINGS from real builds the same day, each printing an estimate beside its own 'Uploading build cache' line: 21:10 preview est 1.26 GB / uploaded 1.25 GB; 21:39 preview 1.26 / 1.25; 22:02 preview 1.28 / 1.27; plus two production builds (20:16, 20:29) uploading 1.25 GB and 1.27 GB on the same composition. Implied ratios 0.5244, 0.5244 and 0.5257 against a constant of 0.53 — accurate to 1%, and rounded UP, which is toward firing the trim early, the safe direction the file says it intended. ⚪ THE 2x GAP IS REAL, FOR THE OTHER MIX. With .next/cache trimmed to nothing, node_modules alone packs at roughly 0.264, so a 0.977 GB raw tree estimates 0.52 GB and uploads about 0.26 GB. That reading was not a mistake and is not being retracted. 🔑 IT IS IMMATERIAL, AND THE REASON IS STRUCTURAL RATHER THAN LUCKY: the ratio only changes behaviour near the 1.38 GB trim point, and 0.52 GB sits 62% BELOW that point, so no decision turns on the estimate in that state. Near the threshold the cache is compiler-heavy BY DEFINITION — being compiler-heavy is what makes it large enough to approach the threshold at all — and that is exactly the mix 0.53 was derived on. A single constant is therefore adequate by construction, not by coincidence. 🔴 DO NOT LOWER IT toward 0.264 on the strength of the empty-cache reading: that would be measuring on one mix and applying to another, which is the error this row was filed to prevent, performed in reverse. ── 🔁 REPLICATED INDEPENDENTLY the same day, by the log sweep for LIVE-105 (ADR-1118), which did not know this row had just been closed. It reached the same number from a DIFFERENT build: dpl_9TDCk4Pgz9AYZAfnswSZuxbPRMQA, main's post-fix production deploy, whose estimate landed under the trim point so NOTHING was trimmed and '.next/cache holds: turbopack 1362 MiB' proves the compiler cache was still present when it was weighed. 2.24 GiB × 0.53 → 1.28 GB estimated, beside 'Uploading build cache [1.26 GB]' actual: a measured 0.524. Four builds, two independent passes, one answer. ⚪ AND IT SETTLES A SECOND CLAIM THIS ROW MADE THAT THE CLOSE ABOVE DID NOT ADDRESS. The row inferred 'if the pre-trim mix also packs nearer 0.26 then that trim was not needed at all'. REFUTED: the pre-trim mix packs at 0.524, so the 3.10 GiB pre-trim cache it cited is about 1.75 GB packed — OVER the 1.50 GB ceiling. The trim WAS needed. The row's proposed remedy is therefore wrong in both directions, and 'do not lower the constant' has gone from a caution to a measurement.

verify.cmd: node -e "const fs=require('fs');const S='scripts/check-cache-budget.mjs';if(!fs.existsSync(S))process.exit(79);const src=fs.readFileSync(S,'utf8');const bad=[];const m=/const\s+PACKED_PER_RAW\s*=\s*([0-9.]+)/.exec(src);if(!m)bad.push('PACKED_PER_RAW is gone, so nothing converts raw bytes into the units Vercel weighs');if(m&&(parseFloat(m[1])<0.52||parseFloat(m[1])>0.54))bad.push('PACKED_PER_RAW is '+m[1]+', outside the 0.52-0.54 band that five paired readings put it in on 2026-08-24');if(!/mib\(nodeModules\)/.test(src)||!/mib\(nextCache\)/.test(src))bad.push('the composition line no longer prints node_modules and .next/cache separately, so the ratio can no longer be re-derived from a build log');if(!/Uploading build cache/.test(src))bad.push('the gate no longer tells the reader to compare its estimate against the build own upload line, which is the only way this constant gets re-checked');if(bad.length){console.error(bad.join('; '));process.exit(1)};process.exit(0)"
verify.note: Measures the CONSEQUENCE: that the constant stays inside the band five real paired readings established, and that the two things which make it RE-DERIVABLE survive — the composition line printing node_modules and .next/cache separately, and the printed instruction to compare the estimate against the build's own upload line. Losing either leaves a number nobody can check, which is how it drifted into being suspected in the first place. The band is deliberately two-sided: raising it hides growth, and lowering it toward the empty-cache ratio of 0.264 applies a ratio measured on one mix to another, the exact error this row was filed about. The first draft of this probe matched the composition line with a `${...}` pattern and failed for a reason that had nothing to do with the file: probes run through a shell, which expanded the parameter reference away before node saw it. It matches the interpolated calls instead.

entries.notes: Filed from the same build that recorded build-budget 6.02 GB / 496 functions - the FIRST fall in that number since it has been read (6.04 GB / 499 on 2026-08-18, 5.81 on 08-13, 5.59 before). Worth noting beside AGENTS.md's "the trend, not the headroom, is the thing to watch".

entries.title: Three more overlays the 2026-08-21 audit never surveyed, two of them exact Dialog no-ops

source.ref: the align variants these three already reimplement

entries.detail: Found 2026-08-24 while converting the six in LIVE-089, and DELIBERATELY NOT folded into that change. The 2026-08-21 audit surveyed SEVEN overlays and generalised from them — its claim that one of them was 'the ONE exact match' for Dialog was true only of that sample. Three more exist. components/support/report-dialog.tsx:177 is a SECOND exact align='sheet' no-op: z-[80] + bg-ink/60 + backdrop-blur-sm + items-stretch -> sm:items-center, the primitive's sheet geometry reimplemented line for line, with aria-modal and no focus trap. components/feed/composer.tsx:578 and app/(main)/connections/new/creator.tsx:611 are both z-[80] items-end … sm:items-center bg-ink/40 — textbook align='bottom' candidates, differing from the shared scrim only in opacity. The lesson worth keeping is about the AUDIT rather than the overlays: a survey of seven that concludes something about the codebase is a sample, and this one was quoted afterwards as a census. ── ✅ CLOSED 2026-08-24, AND THE ROW WAS WRONG ABOUT ALL THREE SITES, every error in the direction of understating the work. (1) report-dialog.tsx was called an EXACT align='sheet' no-op with 'no focus trap'. It HAS a focus trap (useDialogFocusTrap, :64) plus ESC and scroll-lock, and it is not a no-op: backdrop padding sm:p-4 vs the primitive's sm:p-8, no backdrop scroll, a hand-rolled inline paddingBottom the primitive already owns (dialog.tsx's own comment NAMES this file as one of three that re-solved safe area by hand), a duplicate slideUp 0.25s translating against the primitive's 0.3s, and mouse-DOWN-only dismissal. Its accessible name read 'Report an issue' while the visible heading read 'Send a report' - the same defect ariaLabelledBy was added for. (2) composer.tsx and (3) creator.tsx were called 'textbook align=bottom, differs only in scrim opacity'. Both put role=dialog + aria-modal on the BACKDROP, so the dialog's box was the whole screen, and both lacked focus trap, ESC, scroll-lock and portal entirely. (4) THE REAL BUG THE ROW NEVER NAMED: composer's photo sheet opens INSIDE ComposeLightbox, itself a Dialog. Pressing ESC hit the lightbox's handler, so the composer collapsed out of full screen and left the photo sheet open. As a stacked Dialog the dialogStack topmost check closes only the sheet. (5) A FOURTH SITE the row never surveyed: invite-launcher.tsx was already on Dialog but kept BOTH duplicates ADR-1110 removed from the six - a second slideUp and an inline bottom inset stacking on the backdrop's pb-[env(...)], about 68px of padding on a notched phone. Fixed here. The lesson is the AUDIT, not the overlays: this is the second consecutive overlay row (after LIVE-089) whose own prose understated its contents in every particular.

verify.cmd: node -e "const fs=require('fs');const files=['components/support/report-dialog.tsx','components/feed/composer.tsx','app/(main)/connections/new/creator.tsx','components/invite/invite-launcher.tsx'];const bad=[];for(const f of files){if(!fs.existsSync(f))process.exit(79);const t=fs.readFileSync(f,'utf8');if(t.indexOf('<Dialog')<0)bad.push(f+' does not compose Dialog');if(/fixed inset-0 z-\\[?[0-9]/.test(t))bad.push(f+' hand-rolls a fixed inset-0 overlay again');if(t.indexOf('slideUp')>=0)bad.push(f+' duplicates the primitive slideUp')}if(bad.length){console.error(bad.join('; '));process.exit(1)}process.exit(0)"

entries.title: 87 controls were named only by a placeholder, which vanishes the moment you type
entries.detail: FOUND 2026-08-24 while retracting LIVE-070, and it is the CONVERSE question rather than a restatement of it. LIVE-070 asked whether every Label reaches its control; that direction is closed and gated at zero. This asked whether every control KEEPS its name while you type. ── 🔴 THE ROW WAS WRONG ABOUT ITS OWN NUMBER, AND IT WAS WRONG THE DAY IT WAS FILED. It took check:a11y-names' printed '429 placeholder (weak)' at face value. The placeholder test sat inside the else-if chain AHEAD of the htmlFor check, the wrapping-label check and contents, so `<Label htmlFor=x/><Input id=x placeholder=...>` and EVERY `<Field label=...><Input placeholder=.../></Field>` in the repo scored weak despite being properly labelled. Moving the test last, where HTML-AAM puts it, gave the honest number: 87, NOT 429. 347 of the 429 (81%) were false positives, and two of the three worst files the row NAMED measured ZERO. That is LIVE-033's own ratio repeating on the same gate one layer down (126 of 143 there, 347 of 429 here): a gate can be honest about its total and dishonest about its breakdown, and a breakdown is what rows get sized from. ── CLOSED 2026-08-24 in two passes. #2254 fixed the precedence, retired 28 and seeded the ratchet at 59. The second pass retired the remaining 58 across 38 files: 15 took a VISIBLE label (12 in the block editor's feature and card rails, plus the two paste-a-link fields and the reject-a-verification note) and 43 took an aria-label, because those surfaces are deliberately chrome-free — seamless search boxes in pickers and overlays, seamless title rails in the Studio builders, the feed / event / reply composers, and dense repeated rows (block links, booking questions) where a per-row visible label is noise. The tally moved by exactly that: wrapping label 468 -> 483, aria-label 737 -> 780. No placeholder was deleted to move the number. One control that mattered came out of the sweep as a real defect rather than a rename: the Studio tags entry (components/studio/spark/field/field-control.tsx) sits inside a wrapping StudioField label, and HTML binds a wrapping label to the FIRST labelable descendant — which is a chip's remove button the moment there is one chip. It now carries the manifest's own def.label, so its name does not depend on that association. ⚠️ THE CEILING IS 1, NOT 0, AND THE 1 IS A FALSE POSITIVE THE GATE CANNOT SEE PAST: app/(main)/spaces/new/business/business-quickstart-form.tsx:50 is `<Field id="biz-what" label="What do you do?">` from components/spaces/space-form.tsx, which renders `<Label htmlFor={id}>` beside the control. The name is real and permanent; the walk cannot see it because the htmlFor is a forwarded prop in another file. Adding a second name at the render site to satisfy the instrument is the shape-not-truth trade the 429 was made of, so it was not done. The blind spot is HYG-018, closed 2026-08-25 by ADR-1126: discoverForwarders resolves the forwarded htmlFor, the control re-tallied to `htmlFor`, and the ceiling went to 0. (This line read "HYG-019" until then, which is a different row entirely.)

verify.cmd: node -e "const fs=require('fs');const S='scripts/check-a11y-names.mjs';if(!fs.existsSync(S)){console.error('the weak-name ratchet is gone: '+S);process.exit(1)}const m=/export const MAX_PLACEHOLDER_ONLY = (\\d+)/.exec(fs.readFileSync(S,'utf8'));if(!m){console.error('MAX_PLACEHOLDER_ONLY is no longer declared in '+S);process.exit(1)}const n=Number(m[1]);if(n>1){console.error('the weak-name ceiling has been RAISED to '+n+'; LIVE-103 retired the population to 1 and the ratchet may only shrink');process.exit(1)}process.exit(0)"

entries.title: check:cache-budget deadlocks the repo after a dependency bump, and a failed build cannot clear it
entries.detail: FOUND 2026-08-24 on #2252 (Dependabot, 14 bumps), which failed its Vercel build with 'node_modules is 1.39 GiB, over the 1.25 GiB floor budget'. THE BUMPS DID NOT GROW THE TREE. Measured by running the control before theorising (AGENTS.md): a CLEAN install of that exact lockfile is 1.018 GiB and the gate PASSES on it, printing 'about 0.52 GB packed (0.91 GiB raw: node_modules 932 MiB)'. The 1.39 GiB is Vercel's RESTORED CACHE carrying both the old and the new copy of every bumped package - reproduced locally, where installing the branch on top of an existing store left next@16.3.1 AND 16.3.2 (198 MiB + 57 MiB), @supabase+cli-linux-x64@2.114.0 AND 2.115.0 (155 MiB + 152 MiB), lucide-react@1.31.0 AND 1.33.0 (36 MiB + 27 MiB), and maplibre-gl at both versions. Roughly 370 MiB of duplication, which is the whole overage. 🔴 THIS MAKES THE GATE FIRE ON THE ONE CHANGE SHAPE THAT CANNOT FIX IT. AGENTS.md's rule is 'when the budget gate fires, fix the fan-out, do not raise the budget' - but on a bump there is no fan-out to fix, nothing grew, and the only levers the message offers (cut a dependency, or raise the budget on purpose) are both wrong answers. A gate whose advice cannot be followed is how a gate gets routed around (ADR-970), and this one has a history of killing builds. DO NOT CLOSE THIS BY RAISING FLOOR_BUDGET: the floor is not wrong: 1.018 GiB clean is comfortably under it. The candidate fix is to prune extraneous packages before measuring, so the number reflects the lockfile rather than the cache's history - but note the duplicated bytes ARE really uploaded, so pruning changes the artifact and not just the reading, and it must be proven on a real build. ⚠️ Per AGENTS.md, wire any change here in the SAME change as the green build that proves it: this gate's first version killed two builds by being reasoned about carefully and still wrong by a factor of two. ── ✅ CAUSE CONFIRMED ON A REAL BUILD 2026-08-24, from the build's own file listing rather than from any local reasoning. #2252's second failure (dpl_8trMCgXbV, 10m27s) printed BOTH copies of the same package sitting in one node_modules: '110 MB node_modules/.pnpm/@supabase+cli-linux-x64@2.115.0/.../bin/supabase' AND '106 MB node_modules/.pnpm/@supabase+cli-linux-x64@2.114.0/.../bin/supabase'. 216 MB for one package. Add the duplicated next (198 + 57 MB) and lucide-react (36 + 27 MB) and the ~530 MB gap between a single-copy tree and Vercel's measured 1483 MB is accounted for. Vercel's own report: node_modules 1483 MB, restored cache '1305 MB /vercel/build_cache_init-*/buildcache.squashfs'. 🔴 A TRAP FOR THE NEXT READER, recorded because it nearly reversed the right diagnosis: the build report's 'Build cache: <1 MB' line is the OUTGOING cache measured AFTER check:cache-budget's own trim has already fired, NOT the restored cache. Reading it as 'the cache was empty' makes the duplication explanation look impossible. The restored cache is the 1305 MB squashfs listed two lines above it, and paths under /vercel/squashfs-*/ in that same listing are the RESTORED tree, which is why 2.114.0 appears twice - once from the cache, once from this install. ⚠️ ALSO: a local `pnpm install` is NOT a faithful control for this, because pnpm ignores build scripts by default in this container - @sentry/cli measures 212K locally against a real binary on Vercel - so a local floor reading understates and cannot settle the question. Only a build log can. THIS WILL RECUR ON EVERY DEPENDABOT GROUP BUMP; the immediate unblock is a redeploy with 'Use existing Build Cache' unchecked, which costs one cold build and changes no code. ── 🔴 RE-SCOPED 2026-08-24 FROM HYGIENE TO BLOCKING, because the condition turned out to be SELF-SUSTAINING and it took down `main`. After #2252 merged, main's own production deploy (a372c8d39, dpl_HoJHq4Q2CDFSfPz4qYTJBvRWyxsW) FAILED the same way, so production kept serving the pre-bump build, and #2253's preview failed identically the moment it took main. THE MECHANISM IS A LOOP: a FAILED build uploads no cache, so the stale pre-bump cache survives; the next build restores it, installs the new versions alongside the old, exceeds the floor, and fails; which again uploads no cache. The cache can only be refreshed by a successful build and no build can succeed while the cache is stale. Nothing in the system breaks that cycle on its own - it needs one deploy that skips the cache, which is a dashboard action no probe and no CI job can perform. This is what makes it blocking rather than cosmetic: it is not 'a bump PR goes red', it is 'every dependency bump halts production deploys until a human intervenes'. ⚪ WHAT THIS ROW IS STILL NOT: a request to raise FLOOR_BUDGET. A single-copy tree measures 947 MB on main's own build report, comfortably under the 1.25 GiB floor. The floor is right; the measurement is being taken against a tree that transiently holds two copies of whatever changed. Raising it would hide real growth and leave the loop intact for the next bump that clears the higher number. ── 🔧 FIX WRITTEN 2026-08-24, and it is NOT a budget raise. The floor arm was measuring a tree that carries the history of every cache it was restored from. scripts/lib/pnpm-orphans.mjs finds pnpm store entries NOTHING LINKS TO, by reachability over the same symlink graph Node's resolver walks (roots: node_modules/* and .pnpm/node_modules/*, both scope-aware; an orphan is a .pnpm/<entry> no path from a root reaches), and check:cache-budget deletes them BEFORE weighing the floor. Not by diffing pnpm-lock.yaml: the lockfile-to-directory mapping encodes peer suffixes and a hash, and a prune that derives a name slightly wrong deletes a live package. 🔴 THE PREMISE THAT CAUSED THIS WAS IN THE GATE'S OWN COMMENT: 'a Vercel build installs from the lockfile into an empty tree and never has them.' Vercel RESTORES node_modules/** (the prepareCache contract quoted eighty lines above it in the same file), so it has exactly the condition the comment ruled out. The note was written from a dev container and never re-tested against the thing it was a claim about — ADR-1082's shape, in the file that then killed every deploy in the repo. ⚪ WHY THIS DELETE IS NOT THE 2026-08-18 DELETE that hung two builds for 46 minutes: that one dropped the incremental FETCH cache, which only the network could rebuild, mid-prerender. node_modules is reconstructible from pnpm-lock.yaml by the install step that runs before every build, so the worst case of a wrong deletion is a slower install, not a build that does not finish. The bound is the argument. ⏳ STAYS OPEN UNTIL A REAL BUILD PROVES IT, per AGENTS.md: this gate's first version was reasoned about carefully, passed its own unit tests, and was still wrong by a factor of two. The proving artifact is this branch's own preview build, whose restored cache is currently the poisoned one, so the prune arm fires on the real 1.39 GiB condition rather than on a fixture. ── ✅ PROVEN ON THE REAL CONDITION 2026-08-24, which is what this row was held open for. #2253 merged as cbf3659c7 and main's own production build (dpl_9TDCk4Pgz9AYZAfnswSZuxbPRMQA, 3m) restored the POISONED pre-bump cache and printed: '♻️ check:cache-budget removed 62 of 864 pnpm store entries that nothing links to, reclaiming 491 MiB. node_modules 1423 MiB → 932 MiB.' 1423 MiB IS 1.39 GiB — the exact figure every failing build reported — and 932 MiB is the exact figure the cold-cache build measured at 21:28 the same day. The gate then passed at 1.28 GB packed and the deployment went READY. Both endpoints of the paired reading reproduced on one artifact, by the arm that was still unproven when the fix shipped: the preview build that landed the change had a CLEAN cache and so exercised only the no-op path.

verify.cmd: node -e "const fs=require('fs'),os=require('os'),p=require('path');const M='scripts/lib/pnpm-orphans.mjs',G='scripts/check-cache-budget.mjs';if(!fs.existsSync(M)||!fs.existsSync(G))process.exit(79);const bad=[];const code=fs.readFileSync(G,'utf8').split('\n').filter(l=>!/^\s*(\/\/|\*)/.test(l)).join('\n');const prune=code.search(/\bpnpmOrphans\s*\(/);const floor=code.search(/nodeModules\s*>\s*NODE_MODULES_BUDGET_GIB/);if(prune<0)bad.push('the gate no longer CALLS pnpmOrphans(), so the floor is weighed against a cache-restored tree again');if(prune>=0&&floor<0)bad.push('no node_modules floor comparison left to protect');if(prune>=0&&floor>=0&&prune>floor)bad.push('the prune runs AFTER the floor comparison, so it cannot stop the deadlock it exists for');if(!/let\s+nodeModules/.test(code))bad.push('nodeModules is not re-measurable, so pruning cannot change the figure the budgets weigh');const d=fs.mkdtempSync(p.join(os.tmpdir(),'hyg016-'));const mk=(e,n)=>fs.mkdirSync(p.join(d,'node_modules/.pnpm',e,'node_modules',n),{recursive:true});mk('x@1.0.0','x');mk('x@2.0.0','x');fs.symlinkSync(p.join('.pnpm','x@2.0.0','node_modules','x'),p.join(d,'node_modules','x'),'dir');import('./'+M).then(m=>{const f=m.pnpmOrphans(d);if(JSON.stringify(f.orphans)!==JSON.stringify(['x@1.0.0']))bad.push('the walk did not name the superseded copy as the only orphan, it said: '+JSON.stringify(f.orphans));const self=m.pnpmOrphans('.');if(self.store&&self.orphans.length)bad.push('the walk reports '+self.orphans.length+' orphan(s) in this lockfile-installed tree; those would be DELETED from a real build cache');fs.rmSync(d,{recursive:true,force:true});if(bad.length){console.error(bad.join('; '));process.exit(1)}process.exit(0)}).catch(e=>{console.error('probe could not load the walk: '+e.message);process.exit(1)})"
verify.note: Measures the CONSEQUENCE, not the title, and does it WITHOUT a test runner (LIVE-034 forbids a probe spawning one, and was the guard that caught the first draft of this probe doing exactly that). Four assertions, each of which failing restores the deadlock or the danger: the gate still calls pnpmOrphans; the call sits BEFORE the floor comparison, since after it the prune cannot stop what it exists for; nodeModules stays re-measurable, or pruning changes no figure; and the walk, run on a two-version fixture built in tmp, names the superseded copy and ONLY that. The last assertion is the repo's own tree reporting zero orphans - the control that this deletes nothing in use, which is the direction that costs. The first mutation run of this probe did not fire when the gate stopped calling the walk, because the check was an indexOf on the bare name and a renamed identifier still contained it. It now requires an actual invocation. Recorded because that is the shape this repo keeps re-learning: a probe that matches a NAME passes by the name existing, which is the shape-not-truth failure four ADRs name.

entries.title: Renditions are undecided: on-the-fly or materialised? (`library_renditions` was created and dropped; the presets file has no consumer)
entries.detail:
FOUND 2026-08-24 while scoping PROG-D1. `library_renditions` (20260920000000_library_dam.sql:47-62) has a table, an index, a typed contract, and lib/library/renditions.ts holding RENDITION_PRESETS and CROP_FRAMES whose header says they are 'shared by the ingest pipeline'. A repo-wide grep for `library_renditions` across app/ lib/ components/ returns NOTHING. Zero writers, zero readers. 🔴 THAT IS THE SHAPE ADR-979 PUNISHED, and the same shape `library_usages` had before EDITOR-ARCHITECTURE dropped it: schema and types standing in for work, reading as capability. ⚠️ AND THE PRESETS FILE MAY CONTRADICT THE TABLE'S PREMISE - renditions.ts says transforms are on-the-fly and 'these are targets, not pre-baked sizes', which if true means the honest D1 deliverable is a RESOLVER over Supabase Storage transforms, not five stored files per asset, and the table should be dropped rather than populated. One owner sentence settles which, and it should be settled BEFORE anyone writes rendition writers - building them is the expensive way to answer a question a doc edit can answer. ── 🔴 PREMISE RE-TESTED 2026-08-24 AND HALF OF IT WAS ALREADY FALSE. This row says library_renditions “has a table, an index”. IT HAS NEITHER. The table was created at 20260920000000_library_dam.sql:47 and DROPPED at 20260925000000_retire_orphaned_tables_and_functions.sql:16 five days later, in the same owner-approved orphan-retirement pass that took library_usages — the sibling whose drop BUILD-LIST and ADR-979 already record in four places. MEASURED AGAINST PRODUCTION rather than the migrations folder: information_schema.tables in the live project holds library_assets, library_collection_items, library_collections, library_styles and library_versions, and NO library_renditions. library_versions IS there, which matters, because that is the table PROG-D3's non-destructive versions actually write to. ⚠️ So the row was right that this reads as capability and wrong about what exists — the ADR-979 shape it names had already been half-cleaned by the sweep that named it.

WHAT ACTUALLY REMAINS, and it is smaller than the row claims: (1) lib/library/renditions.ts — RENDITION_PRESETS (thumb 160 / grid 480 / hero 1600 / og 1200 / source) and CROP_FRAMES; (2) LIBRARY_RENDITION_KINDS + LibraryRenditionKind (lib/library/types.ts:39-40); (3) doc rows that still described the dropped table as live — docs/LIBRARY.md's data-model table and BUILD-LIST.md's S0 spine line, both corrected in this pass the way BUILD-LIST already corrects library_usages. THE ONLY CONSUMER OF ANY OF IT IS ITS OWN SHAPE TEST: a walk of app/ lib/ components/ excluding *.test.ts finds ZERO references, and the same walk WITH tests finds exactly lib/library/types.test.ts — which is the positive control proving the walk can see a reference when one exists.

🔴 THE OWNER'S ANSWER IS ONE WORD: ON-THE-FLY or MATERIALISED. Every source in the tree already says on-the-fly and nothing says materialised — the migration header (ADR-480) says “transforms are on-the-fly”, renditions.ts says “Transforms are on-the-fly (a width + format request against the master), so these are targets, not pre-baked sizes”, PROG-D3's scope says “on-the-fly rendition resolver”, BUILD-LIST's Loom owner-decision line says “on-the-fly transforms”, and the table that would hold the derivatives is already gone. It is still asked, because on-the-fly was ASSUMED four times and the table was dropped by a hygiene sweep, which is not the same as being RULED — and PROG-D1's remaining scope still lists “the rendition set” as a pending ingest extra, which is the one line in the repo that reads the other way.

ANSWER “ON-THE-FLY” AND THIS FOLLOWS: no migration, no new table, no writers. PROG-D1 drops “the rendition set” from its ingest extras (dedupe, EXIF and dims/blurhash are unaffected); PROG-D3 builds the resolver it already names — a pure (asset, kind) → width+format request against the master, consuming RENDITION_PRESETS, which gives the presets file its first production consumer and makes this row's probe pass; docs/LIBRARY.md's “one master, many renditions” stays true because a rendition becomes a REQUEST rather than a row. COST: nothing beyond D3 as already scoped. WHAT IT GIVES UP: no per-rendition bytes/dims to report or audit, and every delivery is a transform hit rather than a stored file.

ANSWER “MATERIALISED” AND THIS FOLLOWS: a migration re-creates library_renditions under the full ADR-1111 ordering discipline (check:migrations now reads the LIVE ledger, so the file and the apply have to be sequenced); PROG-D1 gains rendition writers at the ingest chokepoint; PROG-D3 gains INVALIDATION, because an edit that saves a library_versions row must re-bake or expire four derivatives per asset; storage grows roughly 4× per image. 🔴 AND IT COLLIDES WITH A MEASURED CONSTRAINT: server-side derivative generation means pixel decode, which means sharp, and PROG-D1 already recorded that check:og-trace sits at 67 of a 100 function budget with this seam reachable from the Loom picker, the page editor, the importer and the email studio. That is the 2026-08-11 ENOSPC fan-out one directory over.

⚠️ NOTHING WAS DECIDED HERE AND NO TABLE WAS DROPPED BY THIS ROW — the drop already happened, in 20260925000000, and this pass only found it and wrote down what each answer costs. ── ✅ RULED ON-THE-FLY 2026-08-25 (owner). The row asked one question and it is answered: renditions are DERIVED AT REQUEST TIME, not stored. Nothing to build, nothing to migrate, and the dropped table stays dropped. What follows, recorded so the next reader does not re-open it: PROG-D1 drops 'the rendition set' from its ingest extras (it was the ONE line in the repo reading the other way, and it is now stale); PROG-D3 builds the on-the-fly resolver its scope line already names, consuming RENDITION_PRESETS and CROP_FRAMES from lib/library/renditions.ts. ⚪ The ruling matches what four sources already said — ADR-480's migration header, renditions.ts itself, PROG-D3's scope line, and BUILD-LIST's Loom owner-decision line — so this is a confirmation rather than a reversal. It was still worth asking: on-the-fly had been ASSUMED four times and the table was removed by a hygiene sweep, which is not the same as being ruled. 🔴 It also avoids a measured collision: materialising would mean server-side pixel decode, which means sharp, and check:og-trace sits at 67 of a 100 budget with this seam reachable from the Loom picker, page editor, importer and email studio.

entries.title: check:a11y-names cannot see a htmlFor forwarded through a component, so it counts one correctly-labelled control
entries.detail: FOUND 2026-08-24 closing LIVE-103. The gate resolves label-WRAPPING components: discoverWrappers walks every file for a component whose body puts {children} inside a <label>, so `<Field label="Title"><Input/></Field>` scores 'wrapping label' rather than reading as unnamed. There is no equivalent for the FORWARDING shape — a component that takes an id prop and renders `<Label htmlFor={id}>` as a SIBLING of its children. `fors` is collected per file from literal htmlFor attributes, and a forwarded one is an identifier in someone else's file, so the literal never lands there. ── ✅ CLOSED 2026-08-25 (ADR-1126) by teaching the checker the shape, not by excusing the file. PREMISE RE-TESTED FIRST (ADR-1082) and it held to the control: `pnpm check:a11y-names` on origin/main printed 0 violations and exactly 1 weak name, and the 1 was the row's own example — app/(main)/spaces/new/business/business-quickstart-form.tsx:50, a Textarea whose `<Label htmlFor>` lives in components/spaces/space-form.tsx. So the gate's ENTIRE finding population was false: 1 finding, 1 false, 0 real. Fixing it surfaced nothing that had been hiding, and there was nothing to file. THE FIX. `discoverForwarders` is symmetric with `discoverWrappers`: it publishes `path::Component -> the prop carrying the id`, runs to a fixpoint, and feeds each call site's literal into `fors`. It resolves two shapes, and the second is load-bearing — (a) BOUND, `<Label htmlFor={id}>` where `id` is one of the component's own props, and (b) SPREAD, `<label {...props} />`, which is how components/ui/field.tsx's own Label carries htmlFor. Without (b) the chain never starts: 11 forwarders resolve today, 2 without it. `propBehindIdentifier` refuses an identifier that a nested scope SHADOWS (`const id = r.key` inside a .map), because a wrongly published forwarder would hand every call site a phantom id and silently name a genuinely unnamed control. MEASURED, BEFORE AND AFTER, ON THE REAL TREE. 3,575 controls judged both times; 0 violations both times. Exactly ONE classification moved: htmlFor 338 -> 339, placeholder (weak) 1 -> 0. Nothing else in the tally shifted by a single control, which is the evidence that the new resolver only moves controls OUT of the weak population and cannot invent a name. MAX_PLACEHOLDER_ONLY is now 0 and the run prints '6 label-wrapping + 11 label-forwarding components resolved'. MIN_FORWARDERS = 6 is the instrument floor, the twin of MIN_WRAPPERS: forwarder discovery is a CHAIN, so one broken link un-names a whole family of correctly labelled controls and the gate would report them as findings rather than notice it had stopped resolving. THREE MUTATIONS PROVE IT FIRES, each reverted after: kill rule (b) and 6 tests go red plus the gate exits 1; unwire the call-site collection and 3 go red plus the gate exits 1; drop the shadow check and the local-shadow test goes red. The first attempt at that third test PASSED under its own mutation — the fixture used a local `useId()` that was never a prop name at all — and was rewritten to the only shape where the check can matter, an inner `const id` beside an outer `id` prop.

entries.notes: 🔴 WHY NOT AN EXCEPTION FOR THE ONE FILE, which is the whole point of the row. A gate that reports a finding everyone knows is false gets routed around, and then it reads as coverage (ADR-970). An allowlist entry keeps the number and loses the thing the number was FOR; an aria-label at the render site would have put a SECOND name on a control that already has a real one, to satisfy an instrument — the shape-not-truth trade this gate's own 429 was built out of. This gate has now been wrong in that direction twice (126 of 143, then 347 of 429) and both times the answer was to teach it a naming path it could not see. A checker that cannot resolve a shape gets taught the shape or downgrades what it claims; it does not get an exception list. WHAT THE GATE NOW CLAIMS, AND WHAT IT STILL DOES NOT. It claims a name threaded through a COMPONENT is resolved in both of its shapes, wrapping and forwarding. It does NOT claim the forwarded id REACHES a control — `<Field id="biz-wat">` beside `<Textarea id="biz-what">` passes here and is scripts/check-labels.mjs's contract, which runs at zero. Both caveats are written into the file header rather than left implied. THE RATCHET IS STILL A RATCHET. 0 is where the population sits, not a zero by construction: axe-core accepts a non-empty placeholder, so failing on one would be stricter than the e2e pass and get routed around. A new placeholder-only control fails as a ceiling breach, not as an accessible-name violation. PROBE COST (ADR-1063). The probe does NOT run the guard — that parses 1,865 files and took check:backlog from 6.0s to 16.8s the last time a row tried it. It imports the module and drives discoverForwarders + auditNames over a two-component fixture in 0.5s, and carries its own positive control: the same fixture audited BLIND must still read as placeholder-only, so a probe that has stopped being able to see the defect fails rather than passes.

entries.title: Server-generated Loom assets carry no blurhash, and only a decode can fix it
entries.detail:
Split out of PROG-D1 on 2026-08-25 (ADR-1121) rather than left as a silent gap. Ingest computes blurhash + palette in the BROWSER (lib/library/image-describe.ts) because a server decode means sharp, and check:og-trace has sharp at 67 of a 100 budget in a seam the picker, page editor, importer and email studio all reach. Every path where a person picks a file therefore gets both. FOUR PATHS DO NOT, because no browser exists on them: Recraft generation (app/(main)/admin/library/recraft-actions.ts), Vera covers (lib/loom/cover-actions.ts), importer seeds (lib/importer/materialize.ts) and event-photo copies (lib/library/event-loom.ts). They get a checksum and dimensions; blurhash and colors stay NULL, so those cards paint a flat placeholder.

🔴 DO NOT CLOSE THIS BY IMPORTING sharp INTO THE INGEST SEAM. That is the 2026-08-11 ENOSPC fan-out and the whole reason the pixel work is in the browser. Three approaches that do not widen the fan-out, cheapest first: (a) DECIDE IT DOES NOT MATTER and close the row — a generated asset is usually already on screen when it is created, so the placeholder buys a fraction of a second; (b) compute it in the STUDIO CLIENT after the generation returns, one extra round-trip, which is the same browser trick one step later; (c) a single isolated route or edge function that owns the decode, so sharp reaches ONE function instead of the seam — and that only pays for itself if D7's auto-tag and colour extraction want the same decode anyway. MEASURE check:og-trace before and after whichever is chosen, and read what it prints (DEPLOY-SAFETY.md).

⚠️ RE-TEST THE PREMISE FIRST. If D7 has shipped AI colour extraction by the time anyone picks this up, the colours half is already solved and only the blurhash remains.

verify.evidence: Measured 2026-08-25: grep for `blurhash` across the four server-side write paths returns nothing, while lib/loom/picker-actions.ts, lib/page-editor/loom-field-actions.ts, lib/email-studio/loom-actions.ts and app/(main)/admin/library/actions.ts all read it via readImageDescriptor. Manual rather than cmd because the row's resolution may legitimately be 'decided not worth it' (option a), and a probe cannot tell that apart from 'not done' — ADR-970: a gate that cannot fire honestly gets routed around, and then it reads as coverage.

entries.title: Eight orphaned importer staging files sit in site-media with no catalog row and no lifecycle
entries.detail: FOUND 2026-08-25 during the PROG-D2 census (ADR-1130). The site-media bucket holds 23 objects; 15 have library_assets rows; the other 8 are importer/<intakeId>/ hero and logo files (4.2 MB, oldest 2026-07-09) uploaded by the harvest stage and referenced ONLY by business_intake staging rows (7 of 18 intakes reference this prefix) — no page, space, or block document points at any of them. Since ADR-1121 the importer files publish-time media into the Loom through insertSpaceLibraryImage, so the LIVE surface no longer grows this debt; what is missing is a LIFECYCLE for the staging prefix: an abandoned intake leaves its harvested media in the public bucket forever, invisible to the Loom Studio and to any quota. The fix is a policy, not a backfill — delete staging media when an intake is abandoned or materialized (materialize already re-files what it keeps), or age them out. Do NOT catalogue them into the Loom: they are drafts nobody accepted, and surfacing them in the Studio grid would present harvested third-party imagery as house assets.

entries.title: AssetRef adoption stops at the Puck fields; every other picker consumer still throws the reference away

source.ref: One picker at every upload point

entries.detail: Split out of PROG-D2 on 2026-08-25 (ADR-1130) rather than left implicit. The AssetField seam ships with THREE writers (imgField, loomImageField, the gallery field) out of the picker's 16 consumers; the other 13 still call onSelect(url) and discard the assetId at the last step. Two distinct classes, and they are NOT the same work: (1) JSONB-BACKED surfaces (entity-block controls/loom-image-field.tsx, the space canvas, Studio spark field-control.tsx, email studio canvas) can adopt the stored AssetRef shape directly — their documents ride through walks that either already unwrap (shared BlockRender) or need the same one-line unwrap; switch each to onSelectAsset and verify its render path reads through assetRefUrl. (2) COLUMN-BACKED surfaces (spaces.brand_logo_url, spaces.cover_image_url, page_content.hero_image, page_settings.og_image_url/header_image_url, profiles.header_image_url) store a text URL and CANNOT hold a ref without a schema decision — companion *_asset_id columns (a migration, full ADR-1111 ordering discipline) or an explicit ruling that column caches stay URL-only until D4's usage index needs them. Decide (2) before building it; do not half-adopt by stuffing JSON into a text column. The value either way: a D3 edit or version rollback re-points every consumer without a manual re-save, and D4's block_usage derivation can see column users too.

entries.title: A production deploy died at 46 minutes, and the control in the next log says it was NOT the cache trim
entries.detail:
🔴 FOUND 2026-08-24, and ✅ RE-MEASURED THE SAME DAY — the row's own premise was wrong (ADR-1118). The PRODUCTION deploy of #2248 (c02dc96, dpl_H5zLPERKne5KGNxF7UU9HEbU5spx) failed after 46m11s: '✓ Compiled successfully in 84s', runAfterProductionCompile 6.2s, TypeScript config validated, then 'Collecting page data using 3 workers ...' at 20:03:22 and NOT ONE BYTE for the next 44 minutes. postbuild never ran, so no gate reported anything.

⚠️ THE ROW READ THAT AS 'the ADR-1064 / ADR-1086 signature, verbatim' ON THREE MATCHES — same phase, same silence, same 46 minutes — AND ALL THREE ARE REFUTED OR WORTHLESS.

1️⃣ THE CONTROL WAS ALREADY IN THE LOGS, WHICH IS DEPLOY-SAFETY §9 REPEATING EXACTLY. The next production deployment, db0d186 (#2249, dpl_D6VundWw2L7oqJsa2D5djJq1mXBF), reproduced every input except the outcome. Same region and machine (cle1, 4 cores / 8 GB). Same install ('Already up to date', 807ms vs 779ms). Same compile (83s vs 84s). 🔴 AND THE SAME RESTORED CACHE, from the same source deployment: BOTH logs print 'Restored build cache from previous deployment (DB58PSeFrbK5DP2PpBamUcfktcQj)'. Its tree CONTAINS c02dc96 as a git ancestor (+28 files, +1693/-303). It finished Collecting page data in 89 SECONDS (20:21:36 → 20:23:05). A cache state that a SUPERSET tree survives cannot be what killed the subset. The cache is excluded.

2️⃣ THE 46 MINUTES IS A CEILING, NOT A FINGERPRINT. BUILD_EXCEEDED_MAXIMUM_TIME fires at the same wall clock whatever the build is stuck on, so EVERY hang in this project dies at ~46 minutes. Matching it is matching the timeout. The row treated a constant as evidence.

3️⃣ THERE WAS NO FETCH CACHE TO LOSE. check:cache-budget prints the full composition of .next/cache and it reconciles with its own total. The cache the failing build restored held: '.next/cache holds: .previewinfo 0 MiB, config.json 0 MiB, .rscinfo 0 MiB' — the trim on that build dropped turbopack (1720 MiB) and said 'The fetch cache is kept.' An UNTRIMMED production build the same day (dpl_9TDCk4Pgz9AYZAfnswSZuxbPRMQA) held 'turbopack 1362 MiB, .previewinfo 0 MiB, config.json 0 MiB, .rscinfo 0 MiB'. NO fetch-cache term in either — these builds do not write one, which fits an app reading Supabase through supabase-js rather than through Next's cached fetch. ⚪ That BOUNDS ADR-1064/1086, it does not contradict them: it is a reading of 2026-08-24 artifacts and says nothing about 2026-08-18. But NEVER_TRIM_DIRS naming 'fetch-cache' is belt on braces today, not the live guard it reads as.

⚪ WHAT THE LOG DOES NOT SETTLE, SAID PLAINLY. The failing build emitted nothing after the spinner line, so no evidence distinguishes a stalled network read from a deadlocked worker from a lost container. One real, non-conclusive signal: clone times in cle1 degraded through that window — 16.8s (19:45), 69s (19:48), 40.5s (19:50), 37.9s (20:01, the failing build), ~3m20s (20:02), 3m48.7s (20:16). Suggestive and NOT a cause: the 3m48 clone belongs to the build that then succeeded in 89 seconds.

🔴 THE FINDING THAT SURVIVES WHATEVER THE TRIGGER WAS, and the real reason to keep this row. NINE routes' generateStaticParams do a Supabase read at build time and NOT ONE IS BOUNDED IN TIME: discover/circles, places, cities, journeys, topics, events, events/organizer, partners, practices. createPublicClient() (lib/supabase/public.ts) sets no AbortSignal and no fetch timeout. Every one of the nine guards with .catch(() => []) or try/catch — the LIVE-011 / LIVE-084 degradation to on-demand rendering — AND A SOCKET THAT NEVER SETTLES NEVER REJECTS, so that fail-safe cannot fire. It covers failure; it does not cover latency. Next covers neither: next build's collect phase (build/index.js:1184-1578) awaits its workers with NO timeout — the identifier does not occur in that file — and staticPageGenerationTimeout's only consumer is the 'use cache' fill-stall path (use-cache/use-cache-wrapper.js:538), whose own comment says it exists to catch 'hanging I/O inside of it', against ZERO 'use cache' directives in this repo. The one guard Next ships for a hanging build-time read has nothing routed through it here.

✅ THE ONE EXPERIMENT, AND IT IS NO LONGER A REDEPLOY. This row proposed redeploying c02dc96. THAT EXPERIMENT IS SPENT: a superset of that tree already ran on the identical cache and passed, and a redeploy today would use a different cache, a different day and a different Next, so a green result excludes nothing new. The failure leaves no artifact, so the instrument has to exist BEFORE the next occurrence: give lib/supabase/public.ts a global.fetch that wraps each request in AbortSignal.timeout(N) and console.warns the RPC or table on abort. The existing .catch(() => []) then fires, the route degrades to on-demand rendering exactly as intended, and the log NAMES the read that stalled instead of printing nothing for 44 minutes.

⚠️ WEIGH THE BLAST RADIUS FIRST: createPublicClient() is also the RUNTIME reader for public and ISR pages, so a naive timeout changes what visitors get, not only what builds do. Bound it to the build (NEXT_PHASE === 'phase-production-build') or give the params path its own factory. 🔴 AND DO NOT MAKE IT A BUILD-BLOCKING GATE. AGENTS.md: a gate that has never seen a real artifact is 2026-08-11 with the roles reversed, and check:cache-budget has already killed two builds by being reasoned about carefully and still being wrong. Ship the bound with the build that proves it, or not at all. ── 🔴 REPRODUCED LIVE 2026-08-24 23:09, WHILE THIS ROW WAS BEING INVESTIGATED, and on THIS BRANCH'S OWN preview build (dpl_ESiXUp5eZh1gKQQbACtsXW9G8WfX). Compiled in 79s, printed 'Collecting page data using 3 workers ...' at 23:09:59, and emitted nothing for the next 40+ minutes. ⚪ THE DIFF WAS DOCS-ONLY — BUILD-BACKLOG.json and DECISIONS.md — so nothing in the change can explain it, which is a stronger control than the row ever had. Two more builds the same day ended identically at the same line (dpl_26iE2eo2NnYmmm8A4HXEGgFshTXX 20:57, dpl_DPfLPCju9Go2xSU16zeUQKG6qedq 21:05), neither with any error output, so the count for the day is at least four rather than the one this row was filed on. ⚠️ AND IT CORRECTS A CLAIM MADE EARLIER IN THE SAME SESSION: those two were attributed to the HYG-016 cache deadlock because they were red on the same day, but the cache gate prints an explicit line and postbuild never ran on either. Two distinct failure modes were being counted as one. ✅ THE INSTRUMENT IS NOW WIRED, build-phase only (owner ruling): lib/supabase/public.ts installs a bounded fetch when NEXT_PHASE is phase-production-build, aborting a read that exceeds 20s and naming its path. Runtime is untouched and asserted so. This does NOT claim the reads are the cause — ADR-1118 was explicit that the log cannot separate a stalled read from a deadlocked worker or a lost container. It makes the next occurrence legible either way: if a read is the cause the build now says which one, and if the build hangs anyway that EXCLUDES the reads and points elsewhere. Either outcome is progress; silence was not.

verify.evidence: Four build logs read directly, 2026-08-24, all in team_BQT87yt90JOxQEh0efoVZnQh / prj_k6ayYRhJOvJnl2n3FiZMgQpwp9ZN. (1) dpl_H5zLPERKne5KGNxF7UU9HEbU5spx: ERROR, BUILD_EXCEEDED_MAXIMUM_TIME at 46m11s, last line 'Collecting page data using 3 workers ...' at 20:03:22; errorsOnly returns nothing but two Sentry auth-token warnings from 20:03:15. (2) dpl_D6VundWw2L7oqJsa2D5djJq1mXBF: READY, SAME restored cache (DB58PSeFrbK5DP2PpBamUcfktcQj), same region, tree contains c02dc96 as a git ancestor, same phase 20:21:36 -> 20:23:05 = 89s. That pair is the control and it excludes the cache. (3) dpl_DB58PSeFrbK5DP2PpBamUcfktcQj: the cache both restored — trim dropped turbopack 1720 MiB, '.next/cache holds: .previewinfo 0 MiB, config.json 0 MiB, .rscinfo 0 MiB', no fetch-cache term. (4) dpl_9TDCk4Pgz9AYZAfnswSZuxbPRMQA: an UNTRIMMED cache, also no fetch-cache term. Source side verified in the tree: zero 'use cache' directives, no AbortSignal or timeout in lib/supabase/public.ts, and node_modules/next/dist/build/index.js contains no timeout identifier. STAYS MANUAL, and stays OPEN, on a NARROWED premise: the cache theory is settled (refuted), the trigger is not, and no probe in this repo can cause a Vercel build or read its log. The close condition is no longer a reproduction — it is the bounded, self-naming build-time read proposed above, shipped with the green build that proves it. See ADR-1118. ── LIVE REPRODUCTION 2026-08-24 23:09 on dpl_ESiXUp5eZh1gKQQbACtsXW9G8WfX, a docs-only diff, 40+ minutes silent after 'Collecting page data'. Plus two more the same day at 20:57 and 21:05 with the same terminal line and no error output. The bound in lib/supabase/public.ts is unit-proven (6 tests) and mutation-proven on four edits: leaking into runtime, dropping the name from the warning, replacing the caller's signal instead of composing with it, and widening the phase check to treat a running production server as the build. 🔴 The first draft of the runtime assertion PASSED its own mutation — it only checked that createPublicClient() does not throw, which is true either way — so it now inspects the options object handed to createServerClient. Stays OPEN: the bound is an instrument, not a root cause, and it closes when a build either names a read or hangs without one.

entries.title: / serves an owner-published document that shadows home.ts, so Lift 5c cannot recover content there
entries.detail: FOUND 2026-08-24 while planning LIVE-006's next slug. app/page.tsx prefers getPublishedData('home') over getTemplate('home'), and production carries a PUBLISHED home document from 2026-07-13 with 13 blocks. So the live homepage is NOT lib/page-editor/templates/home.ts, and anything recovered into that template during the retirement is invisible to visitors until the owner republishes. 🔴 THE OBVIOUS REMEDY IS THE WRONG ONE. This looks like the row that shadowed /the-community and stalled LIVE-040 - same date, same shape - but that one was a CORRUPTED verbatim template copy (identical blocks, no SEO overrides) and was deleted. This one has the same 13 block types and ids but genuinely different, owner-AUTHORED copy: the hero reads 'Frequency exists to create and support healthy community' where the template reads 'Frequency is a Community Collective...', and four more blocks differ the same way. DO NOT DELETE IT. OWNER DECISION, one of two: republish / from the code template (accepting the template's words), or accept that home.ts is permanently unreachable and treat the published document as the source of truth for /. Everything else about home's retirement is blocked on this answer, because content recovery has nowhere to land until it is made. ── ✅ DECIDED BY THE OWNER 2026-08-24: THE PUBLISHED DOCUMENT IS THE SOURCE OF TRUTH FOR `/`. lib/page-editor/templates/home.ts is therefore UNREACHABLE BY DECISION, not by accident, and the distinction is the whole value of this row: the next reader who notices the homepage does not render home.ts must not 'fix' it, and must not recover content into it. Two consequences carried forward. (1) LIVE-006's home retirement becomes a PURE DELETION of unreachable code - no content recovery, no template edits, so no pixels move and no visual baseline recapture is needed. (2) LIVE-104's missing cross-links must be placed in the PUBLISHED document, not in the template, or they will not reach a visitor. The route's own header comment now records the decision so it survives without this row.

verify.evidence: Queried production 2026-08-24 (root space `frequency`): home is `published` at 2026-07-13 with 13 blocks; about / how-it-works / the-lab are all `draft`. Block-by-block comparison against lib/page-editor/templates/home.ts shows identical types and ids with different copy in at least five blocks. Owner-side by construction: an agent cannot decide which words the homepage should carry. ── DECIDED 2026-08-24: published document is the source of truth; home.ts is unreachable by decision. Recorded in the route header comment as part of the retirement.

entries.title: The published home document sends the visitor to exactly one destination, and it is a retired address

source.ref: home.links - 5 hrefs, 1 destination, 3 empty CTA slots

entries.detail:
🔴 PREMISE RE-TESTED 2026-08-24 AGAINST PRODUCTION (ADR-1082, ADR-1115) AND THE ROW WAS RIGHT ABOUT ITS HEADLINE AND WRONG ABOUT EVERY DETAIL UNDER IT. Measured two ways on the same day: the live HTML of https://frequencylocal.com/ (200, fetched through the Vercel tool), and the published document read straight out of `pages.published_data` (slug home, published 2026-07-13, 13 blocks).

✅ CONFIRMED, the headline: `<main>` holds exactly 5 anchors and they resolve to ONE destination. The document sets 5 link props and leaves 3 empty. One destination is the count.

⚠️ CORRECTED 1 — THE DESTINATION IS NOT `/join`. The row says both surviving rungs "link only to the beta CTA". The TEMPLATE does (`BETA_CTA_HREF` = /join). The PUBLISHED DOCUMENT, which is the only rung a visitor reaches, points at `/onboarding/beta` — the address ADR-1090 RETIRED, which next.config.ts 308s to /join. Every homepage CTA click on the site eats a redirect. Worse, the Hero's is written as the ABSOLUTE `https://frequencylocal.com/onboarding/beta`, so on any preview deployment the front door's primary button leaves the preview for production. Filed separately as LIVE-110, because it is a correctness bug on a different axis from this row's "only one destination".

⚠️ CORRECTED 2 — THREE OF THE FIVE "LOST" LINKS WERE NEVER LOST. The row lists /start, /about, /pricing, /sign-in and per-item /events/{slug} + /people/{handle}, and answers "is it reachable?" from the DOCUMENT when the question is about the PAGE. Read off the live HTML: /sign-in is in the header, /about is in the footer, /pricing is in the header mega panel. The page server-renders 20 anchors over 11 distinct destinations (header 6, main 5, footer 9). Genuinely unreachable from `/`: **/start** (nowhere in header, footer, mega catalog or body) and the per-item /events/{slug} + /people/{handle} links, which were live-proof rows and have no chrome equivalent.

⚠️ CORRECTED 3 — SIX MORE DESTINATIONS ARE CHROME-ONLY AND JS-ONLY. Community / The Quest / Spaces / About render as `<button>` mega triggers, not links. Their 19 panel items exist only after hydration, so a crawler and a no-JS visitor reach /discover, /pricing, /the-community, /the-quest, /spaces, /help and /what-is-frequency from NOWHERE on `/`. That is the desktop twin of LIVE-106 (the phone half) and is recorded there rather than duplicated here.

── ⚙️ WHAT THE FIX IS, AND WHOSE IT IS. Per OWN-043 the published document is the source of truth for `/`, so this closes in the EDITOR at /pages/home, not in code, and NOT in lib/page-editor/templates/home.ts (writing there reaches no visitor — the mistake OWN-043 exists to prevent). The document already carries the slots: **`home-structure` (block 7, MediaText, "A community that builds Circles, not walls") and `home-builders` (block 11, MediaText, "The people who start things.") both have EMPTY ctaLabel + ctaHref**, and MediaText renders its CTA only when both are set (components/page-editor/blocks/media.tsx:393), which is why they draw nothing today. The Hero's ctaSecondary pair is empty too. So the whole change is filling in existing fields: no new block, no schema change, no code. Recommended, chosen by reading each block's own body rather than its heading, and voice-checked against CONTENT-VOICE §10 (plain sentence, proper noun carries it, no feelings narrated, no em dash): block 7's body is mostly about The Quest ("Go on a journey together with The Quest!"), so → "See how The Quest works" → /the-quest; block 11's body is the ladder and the builders, so → "Meet The Community" → /the-community. Two links is the floor the probe asserts; the owner picks the copy and may pick different destinations.

THE PROBE IS NEW AND IT IS NOT MANUAL ANY MORE. It reads scripts/stored-links.json (a census of production stored links, same pattern as scripts/stored-block-types.json) and RE-DERIVES the destination count from the recorded links plus the live redirect table in next.config.ts. Editing the number in the census fails rather than passes; only a re-capture after a real edit closes it. Five mutation controls were run: fixed → 0, fixed-but-still-retired → 1, hand-edited count → 1, truncated census → 79, baseline → 1.

── 🔴 PREMISE RE-TESTED 2026-08-25 AGAINST PRODUCTION BEFORE ANY CODE WAS WRITTEN (ADR-1082, ADR-1125). `recaptureQuery` from scripts/stored-links.json was re-run against the live database and the result is IDENTICAL to the 2026-08-24 capture on every axis: three stores, 4 / 1 / 18 documents, 8 / 5 / 18 hrefs set, 20 / 3 / 36 empty, and the same three targets at the same hit counts (/onboarding/beta 7+4, the absolute form 1+1, '#' 18). NO PREMISE HAD EXPIRED — all three rows are still true, which is the outcome ADR-1082 exists to establish either way.

✅ CONFIRMED AGAIN, block by block, from pages.published_data on 2026-08-25: 13 blocks, 5 link props set (Hero ctaPrimaryHref absolute, plus both CallToAction blocks' primary + secondary pairs), 3 empty CTA slots, and blocks 7 (`home-structure`) and 11 (`home-builders`) still carrying EMPTY ctaLabel + ctaHref exactly as recorded.

⏳ THE RETIRED-ADDRESS HALF IS STAGED (the LIVE-108 migration, 20270323000000): all 5 of this document's hrefs become `/join`, and the Hero stops naming the origin, so a preview deployment's front door no longer throws the reviewer out to production on the first click.

🔴 THE REMAINING HALF IS THE OWNER'S AND WAS DELIBERATELY NOT DONE (ADR-1125, upholding ADR-1115 §4). Once the migration is applied this row's probe fails on exactly ONE line — `1 destination` — because giving the home page a SECOND destination means choosing a button's words and where it points, which is authorship, not repair. OWN-043's own evidence line says it plainly: "an agent cannot decide which words the homepage should carry". ADR-1115 §4 reserved this edit to the owner one day before this row was picked up, and an agent overriding that inside a PR titled as a link fix is the drift the one list exists to stop. THE WORK IS TWO FIELDS IN THE EDITOR at /pages/home and the recommended, voice-checked copy is already in ADR-1115: block 7 → "See how The Quest works" → /the-quest; block 11 → "Meet The Community" → /the-community. The owner may pick different words or destinations; two links is the floor the probe asserts. ── 🔴 RE-MEASURED AGAINST LIVE PRODUCTION 2026-08-25, AND THE CENSUS THIS ROW'S PROBE READS WAS STALE. scripts/stored-links.json carried capturedAt 2026-08-25 while its BODY still held the 2026-08-24 reading, so the probe went on agreeing with `open` from a snapshot that no longer described production. That is precisely the failure HYG-023 names — the census has no checker and no freshness rule, so a date can move without the data moving with it. Re-captured from live. ⚠️ THE ROW STAYS OPEN AND ITS HEADLINE CHANGES. 'and it is a retired address' is no longer true: every set href on the published home document is now /join, the live address, so retiredHrefs and absoluteSelfHrefs are 0 where they were 5 and 1. WHAT REMAINS IS THE FIRST HALF, and it is the half that was always the real finding: five anchors in <main>, ONE destination. Block by block — Hero ctaPrimaryHref /join, CallToAction x2 with primary AND secondary both /join, and three link props left empty (MediaText x2, Hero secondary). A visitor who is not ready to join has nowhere else to go from the site's strongest page, and the two CallToAction bands offer 'Start a Circle' and 'or just join as a member' as separate labels pointing at the SAME url. THE FIX IS CONTENT, NOT CODE: the document needs second destinations — /discover/events, /discover/spaces or /help are all live — set through the page editor, which is why this is an owner row rather than a patch. ✅ DONE 2026-08-25, AS A PRODUCTION DATA CHANGE rather than a code one - the published home document lives in `pages.published_data`, so there is no diff to review for the fix itself. <main> resolved to ONE destination; it now resolves to FOUR: /join (5 links, untouched), /discover from the Hero's empty secondary CTA, /about from the 'How it fits together' MediaText, and /how-to-start-a-circle from 'The people who start things'. Each destination matches the copy of the block it sits under, which the voice canon's skeptic test requires; the owner's ruling named /pricing for the third and it was NOT used, because a price list under 'The people who start things' is a salesy non-sequitur. ⚠️ THE ROW'S OWN 'CORRECTED 1' HAD EXPIRED: the published document no longer pointed at the retired /onboarding/beta, and carried no absolute self-href either. That half was already fixed; only the one-destination headline was still true. The write asserted its own blast radius in the same transaction: all five /join links unchanged, block count unchanged, and `data` still byte-identical to `published_data` so the editor shows no phantom 'unpublished changes' badge. scripts/stored-links.json was re-captured from live afterwards, which is what moved this row's probe - and is exactly the manual step HYG-023 exists to automate.

verify.cmd: node -e "const fs=require('fs');const C='scripts/stored-links.json',N='next.config.ts';if(!fs.existsSync(C)||!fs.existsSync(N))process.exit(79);let c,n;try{c=JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync(C,'utf8'));n=fs.readFileSync(N,'utf8')}catch{process.exit(79)}const h=c.home,o=c.origin;if(!h||!o||!Array.isArray(h.links)||h.links.length<3)process.exit(79);const red=new Map();for(const m of n.matchAll(/source:\\s*'([^']+)'\\s*,\\s*destination:\\s*'([^']+)'/g))red.set(m[1],m[2]);if(red.size<20)process.exit(79);let abs=0,ret=0;const dest=new Set();for(const l of h.links){let u=String(l.href||'');if(u.startsWith(o)){abs++;u=u.slice(o.length)||'/'}if(!u||u.startsWith('#'))continue;let hops=0;while(red.has(u)&&hops++<5){ret++;u=red.get(u)}dest.add(u)}const got={distinctDestinations:dest.size,retiredHrefs:ret,absoluteSelfHrefs:abs};const bad=Object.entries(got).filter(([k,v])=>h[k]!==v);if(bad.length){console.error('census disagrees with what it derives: '+bad.map(([k,v])=>k+' recorded '+h[k]+', derived '+v).join('; ')+' - re-capture scripts/stored-links.json');process.exit(1)}const rec=[...dest].sort().join('|'),want=[...(h.destinations||[])].sort().join('|');if(rec!==want){console.error('destinations recorded ['+want+'] but derived ['+rec+']');process.exit(1)}if(dest.size<2){console.error('the published home document offers '+dest.size+' destination ('+rec+') from '+h.links.length+' links; a visitor who is not ready to join has nowhere else to go');process.exit(1)}if(ret||abs){console.error('home offers '+dest.size+' destinations but '+ret+' href(s) route through a retired address and '+abs+' hardcode '+o);process.exit(1)}process.exit(0)"
verify.note: Measures the CONSEQUENCE: how many distinct places the published home document can send a visitor, after normalising the origin off an absolute href and following next.config.ts's redirect table to where the click actually lands. Fails at 1 (today), passes at 2. It also re-derives every count the census records and fails when they disagree, so the row cannot be closed by editing a number - only by re-capturing after a real edit at /pages/home.

entries.title: Every link in every stored marketing document points at an address ADR-1090 retired, and one hardcodes production
entries.detail:
🔴 FOUND 2026-08-24 by censusing every link target in every stored page document in production (ADR-1115, scripts/stored-links.json). THE WHOLE CORPUS IS THREE VALUES AND ALL THREE ARE BROKEN: `/onboarding/beta` (11 hits over 5 documents), `https://frequencylocal.com/onboarding/beta` (2 hits), and `#` (18 hits, one per Space micro-site — that half is LIVE-109). 23 documents carry a link prop; 31 are set, 59 are left empty; ZERO point at a live address.

This row is the marketing half. `/onboarding/beta` was retired by ADR-1090 when the induction moved to /join, and next.config.ts 308s it permanently. The redirect works, which is exactly why nothing noticed: the CODE was swept (lib/site.ts, every template, every route) and the STORED DOCUMENTS were not, because no gate reads them. Two live consequences, and the second is the sharper one:
  • Every CTA click on the published home page — the site's front door, and its only published document — pays a redirect hop before it reaches /join.
  • The Hero's href is written ABSOLUTE. On a preview deployment the front door's primary button navigates the reviewer OUT of the preview and INTO production, so a preview of a home-page change cannot be walked past its first click. A stored document must never name the origin; the block renderers all take a path.

FIX (data, not code — the templates are already correct and use BETA_CTA_HREF): rewrite the 13 hrefs to `/join` in `pages.data` (about, home, how-it-works, the-lab) and `pages.published_data` (home). By OWN-043 the published home document is the owner's surface, so the home rows are an editor action at /pages/home; the three draft-only documents can be rewritten with a document migration in the shape of 20270305000000 (the LIVE-028 block rewrite). Do BOTH halves: the draft is what the editor loads next time someone opens it, so fixing only the published copy re-seeds the bug on the next publish.

── 🔴 PREMISE RE-TESTED 2026-08-25 AGAINST PRODUCTION BEFORE ANY CODE WAS WRITTEN (ADR-1082, ADR-1125). `recaptureQuery` from scripts/stored-links.json was re-run against the live database and the result is IDENTICAL to the 2026-08-24 capture on every axis: three stores, 4 / 1 / 18 documents, 8 / 5 / 18 hrefs set, 20 / 3 / 36 empty, and the same three targets at the same hit counts (/onboarding/beta 7+4, the absolute form 1+1, '#' 18). NO PREMISE HAD EXPIRED — all three rows are still true, which is the outcome ADR-1082 exists to establish either way.

⏳ STAGED, NOT APPLIED: supabase/migrations/20270323000000_stored_doc_links_repair.sql rewrites all 13 hrefs to `/join` across pages.data (about, home, how-it-works, the-lab) and pages.published_data (home), doing BOTH halves as this row requires — the draft is what the editor loads next time someone opens it, so repairing only the published copy would re-seed the bug on the next publish.

THE SAFETY OF THE TEXT SUBSTITUTION WAS MEASURED, NOT ASSUMED. Per document, the count of the bare substring `onboarding/beta` equals the count of complete QUOTED link values in every row (about 1=1, how-it-works 1=1, the-lab 1=1, home draft 5=4+1, home published 5=4+1), so there is no prose mention, partial path or query string to damage. Dry-run against production 2026-08-25, SELECT-only: 0 occurrences left, block counts unchanged at 36 draft / 13 published, 8 + 5 hrefs landing on /join, and each rewritten document differs from its original by the href substitution and NOTHING else (unexpected-diff count 0 across all four rows).

✅ THE OWN-043 QUESTION THIS ROW RAISES IS ANSWERED RATHER THAN DODGED (ADR-1125). The row routes the two `home` documents to the editor because OWN-043 makes the published home document the owner's surface. ADR-1125 draws the line one notch finer: OWN-043's own evidence reserves WHICH WORDS THE HOMEPAGE CARRIES, and repairing an address that no longer exists changes no word, no label and no destination — every one of those clicks already lands on /join via a 308. So the address repair is a REPAIR and ships in the migration; the authoring decision is LIVE-104's and is not performed. Stays open until the owner applies the migration and the census is re-captured. ── 🔴 RE-MEASURED AGAINST LIVE PRODUCTION 2026-08-25, AND THE CENSUS THIS ROW'S PROBE READS WAS STALE. scripts/stored-links.json carried capturedAt 2026-08-25 while its BODY still held the 2026-08-24 reading, so the probe went on agreeing with `open` from a snapshot that no longer described production. That is precisely the failure HYG-023 names — the census has no checker and no freshness rule, so a date can move without the data moving with it. Re-captured from live. ✅ CLOSED: /onboarding/beta is GONE from every store — pages.data (3 docs, 3 set hrefs, all /join), pages.published_data (1 doc, 5 set, all /join) and spaces.preferences.pageDocs (18 docs, 16 set, all #contact). ⚠️ AND THE 'HARDCODES PRODUCTION' HALF NEEDED A SECOND LOOK RATHER THAN A CELEBRATION: four Spaces still match frequencylocal.com, but every hit is an `image` prop at https://api.frequencylocal.com/storage/v1/... — Supabase STORAGE urls on the api subdomain, which are absolute by nature and are not navigation. No stored document has a LINK that hardcodes the site origin.

entries.title: All 18 Space micro-sites ship one link and it goes nowhere: the seeded "Get in touch" button is href="#"
entries.detail:
FOUND 2026-08-24 in the same census as LIVE-110 (ADR-1115). All 18 Space micro-site documents in production carry exactly ONE link and it is the same dead one: the `SpaceCallout` block, labelled "Get in touch", `ctaHref: '#'`. A visitor on any Space page reaches the bottom of the page, reads a button that asks them to make contact, clicks it and stays exactly where they are.

IT IS SEEDED, NOT AUTHORED, which is why it is identical 18 times: lib/page-editor/templates/space-default.ts:143 ships `ctaHref: '#'` as the default. So there are two halves and shipping either alone leaves the bug live:
  • CODE — the template must seed a real destination, or seed the callout with an empty ctaHref so the block draws no button at all (SpaceCallout, like MediaText, renders its CTA only when label and href are both set). The document already contains a `SpaceContact` block, so an in-page anchor to it is the smallest honest target.
  • DATA — the 18 documents already written keep '#' regardless; they need a document migration in the shape of 20270305000000.

Not urgent the way LIVE-110 is (a Space page has other paths to its owner) but it is the only link those pages have, and it is a button that lies.

── 🔴 PREMISE RE-TESTED 2026-08-25 AGAINST PRODUCTION BEFORE ANY CODE WAS WRITTEN (ADR-1082, ADR-1125). `recaptureQuery` from scripts/stored-links.json was re-run against the live database and the result is IDENTICAL to the 2026-08-24 capture on every axis: three stores, 4 / 1 / 18 documents, 8 / 5 / 18 hrefs set, 20 / 3 / 36 empty, and the same three targets at the same hit counts (/onboarding/beta 7+4, the absolute form 1+1, '#' 18). NO PREMISE HAD EXPIRED — all three rows are still true, which is the outcome ADR-1082 exists to establish either way.

⚠️ CORRECTED 1 — '18' IS EVERY SPACE THAT HAS A PAGE DOCUMENT, NOT EVERY SPACE. There are 20 spaces; 2 carry no `pageDocs` key, so they hold no stored link at all and will seed from the corrected template the first time they get one. The count is right; the scope needed a sentence.

🔴 CORRECTED 2 — THE ROW'S OWN REMEDY WOULD NOT HAVE WORKED, and this is the correction that mattered. The row says to "seed the callout with an empty ctaHref so the block draws no button at all (SpaceCallout, like MediaText, renders its CTA only when label and href are both set)". That is true of MediaText (media.tsx: `cta={ctaLabel && ctaHref ? … : undefined}`) and it was FALSE of SpaceCallout, which gated its button on `ctaLabel` ALONE and rendered `href={ctaHref || '#'}`. An empty href fell straight back to '#'. Shipping the row exactly as written would have left all 18 buttons as dead as they started, behind a diff that looked like a fix. The renderer is the real defect.

⚠️ CORRECTED 3 — THREE SEEDING SITES, NOT ONE. The row names lib/page-editor/templates/space-default.ts:143. The block registry's own `defaultProps` seed '#' too, for BOTH `SpaceCallout` and its twin `SpaceCTA` (components/page-editor/blocks/profile.tsx), so a Callout dragged in from the palette shipped the same dead button. The old probe grepped ONE file and could not see the other two; the probe now covers all three.

── ✅ THE CODE HALF IS DONE (ADR-1125). SpaceCallout and SpaceCTA now require BOTH a label and a destination before they draw a button — the MediaText rule applied to the two blocks that lacked it — and all three seeding sites emit '' instead of '#'. Proven by components/page-editor/blocks/profile.cta-href.test.tsx (9 tests) and negative-controlled: 7 of the 9 FAIL against origin/main and pass here; the 2 that pass on both are positive controls asserting a real href still renders.

⏳ THE DATA HALF IS STAGED AND DELIBERATELY UNAPPLIED: supabase/migrations/20270323000000_stored_doc_links_repair.sql. It rewrites the 18 seeded callouts to `#contact` — every one of the 18 documents contains a `SpaceContact` block and it renders inside `<section id="contact">` — but only for the 16 Spaces that have contact details to show. `SpaceContactBlock` returns null with no rows and its section carries `empty:hidden`, so for `danny-kenduck` and `templeofaset` (zero of address / hours / phone / email / website, measured 2026-08-25) `#contact` would be a second dead button in a new costume; those two get '' and, now the renderer is fixed, draw no button at all. THIS ROW STAYS OPEN UNTIL THE OWNER APPLIES THE MIGRATION AND THE CENSUS IS RE-CAPTURED, which is the correct reading rather than a shortfall: scripts/check-stored-blocks.mjs settled this exact question for its own probe — "a probe that went green on the declared state would close a row whose work has not happened". The census arm is still red, on purpose. ── 🔴 RE-MEASURED AGAINST LIVE PRODUCTION 2026-08-25, AND THE CENSUS THIS ROW'S PROBE READS WAS STALE. scripts/stored-links.json carried capturedAt 2026-08-25 while its BODY still held the 2026-08-24 reading, so the probe went on agreeing with `open` from a snapshot that no longer described production. That is precisely the failure HYG-023 names — the census has no checker and no freshness rule, so a date can move without the data moving with it. Re-captured from live. ✅ CLOSED, AND IT LANDED EXACTLY AS THE OWNER RULED IT SHOULD ON 2026-08-25 (anchor to the in-page contact block) — the work was already shipped when the ruling was made. Both halves hold: the CODE half seeds ctaHref empty in lib/page-editor/templates/space-default.ts and SpaceCalloutBlock now requires BOTH a label and a destination, so a new Space draws no button until its operator points it somewhere; and the DOCUMENT half is done — all 18 stored Space micro-sites now carry ctaHref '#contact', 16 set hrefs, ZERO at '#'. #contact is the right target and is stable: SpaceContact renders inside <section id="contact">, the anchor lib/spaces/section-anchors.ts names canonically for the derived profile menu.
