entries.title: Editor E0 task 9: upgradeLayout enters the read path
entries.detail:
lib/entity-blocks/node-tree.ts ships upgradeLayout - pure, total, idempotent, deterministic, and proven over the 37 frozen production shapes in scripts/entity-layout-corpus.json (ADR-1129). Nothing calls it. Task 9 calls it at the top of parseEntityLayout, which is EDITOR-E0 §1.5's stated safe halfway point: every reader becomes node-shaped and nothing is written.

What to expect, so it is not mistaken for a bug:
  • layout-equal.ts is a BYTE comparison and powers the 'unpublished changes' badge, so every Space reads dirty exactly once. Harmless, but it will be noticed.
  • layout-equal.test.ts:94-111 asserts on the SOURCE TEXT of actions.ts, so it fails on any rename.
  • upgradeLayout is deliberately MORE permissive than parseRows in one way - it preserves a block type the registry no longer knows (ADR-978), leaving legality to sanitizeRows / resolveRows, which run after. Keep that property; do not 'fix' it by dropping unknown types at the upgrade.
  • EntityLayout gains the node shape here; the sibling content/style maps are NOT removed until task 11.

Not a migration. All five stores are opaque JSONB and §1.6 rules a SQL transform out (the transform needs the registry, and SQL does not have it). ✅ DONE 2026-08-25. `parseEntityLayout` calls `upgradeLayout(raw)` at the top and attaches the result as a read-path-only `EntityLayout.nodes`. 🔴 TWO OF THIS ROW'S OWN NOTES WERE WRONG, both re-measured before the work: (1) `layout-equal.ts` is NOT a byte comparison - it was rewritten to compare the RENDER (`layoutRenderKey` -> `resolveRows` + content + style) and its own header calls the byte version 'THE BUG THIS EXISTS FOR'; and (2) the 'unpublished changes' badge does not go through `parseEntityLayout` at all - it compares raw `profileLayoutDraft` vs `profileLayout` on the stored preferences (owner-space-layout-preview.tsx). So NO Space reads dirty, not even once. The row's prediction should not be looked for. (3) The section reference was also off: §1.5/§1.6 are in docs/EDITOR-E0.md, not EDITOR-ARCHITECTURE.md. ⚠️ THE REAL HAZARD WAS ELSEWHERE AND IT IS ORDERING: `upgradeLayout` returns NON-NULL for every object, so attaching `nodes` before the emptiness gate makes `parseEntityLayout` never return null - disarming `?? starterEmailLayout()` on two LIVE email send paths, which would compile an empty body. The gate runs first and a test pins it. A second test pins that `sanitizeEntityLayout` (the WRITE path) never carries `nodes` through, which caught a real mistake during this very change. A third pins the ADR-978 divergence: `rows` drops a de-registered type and `nodes` preserves it, on purpose.

entries.title: Seven block renderers still draw a button at '#' when the operator leaves the destination blank
entries.detail:
FOUND 2026-08-25 while working LIVE-109 (ADR-1125). The 18 dead Space buttons had a root cause one level below the seed the row blamed: `SpaceCalloutBlock` gated its button on `ctaLabel` alone and rendered `href={ctaHref || '#'}`, so an operator who typed a label and left the link box empty got a button that went nowhere — and blanking the seed could not have removed it. That is fixed for `SpaceCallout` and its twin `SpaceCTA`. THE SAME SHAPE SURVIVES IN SEVEN MORE PLACES, all in components/page-editor/blocks/design.tsx (lines 200, 203, 496, 514, 526, 623, 711), and four of them say so in their own comments: "a missing link falls back to '#' until the operator sets one".

⚠️ NOT ALL SEVEN ARE THE SAME BUG, WHICH IS WHY THIS IS A TRIAGE ROW RATHER THAN A SWEEP. Three (496, 514, 526) sit behind `safeHref()`, so '#' is ALSO what an unsafe url degrades to — a deliberate stored-XSS fallback that must not be removed, only separated from the empty-field case. The other four (200, 203, 623, 711) are the plain LIVE-109 shape. Two further sites in profile.tsx (290, 2349) are NOT in scope: their href comes from live identity data, not an authored text field.

LATENT TODAY, NOT LIVE, and said plainly so the row is not read as an outage: the census (scripts/stored-links.json) records no '#' target in either marketing store, so no stored marketing document trips this today. It is one blank field away in the editor, on any of the seven.

THE DURABLE FIX IS AN EDITOR ONE and belongs with the PROG-E series rather than here: a link field that offers the page's real anchors and routes instead of a free-text box cannot be left in a state that renders '#'. This row is the interim — make the renderers decline to draw a button they cannot point anywhere, the way MediaText, SpaceCallout and SpaceCTA now do. ── ✅ CLOSED 2026-08-25 (ADR-1147). Six renderers in components/page-editor/blocks/design.tsx now require BOTH a label and a destination, and the seventh was a FALSE POSITIVE worth recording: the card title link at ~496 already sat inside `safeHref(card.href) ? …`, so its `|| '#'` was DEAD CODE the type checker forced rather than a route any visitor could reach. It is gone too, so the site stops reading as a seventh instance. ⚠️ THE THREE BEHIND safeHref() ARE NOT A SEPARATE CASE, which is what made this a triage row: '#' is ALSO what an unsafe url degrades to there, and withholding the link is the correct answer to BOTH — a blocked destination and a missing one are equally not somewhere to send someone. One wrapper bug went with it: `hasActions` counted LABELS, so withholding every button still drew the empty mt-8 action row and left a gap under the copy; it now counts buttons that will actually render. components/page-editor/blocks/design.cta-href.test.tsx adds 11 arms, the twin of the profile file from ADR-1125, including an UNSAFE-url arm proving the two cases converge. Mutation-proven three ways.

Comment lines are stripped first so prose describing the defect cannot hold the row open. Reads 7 today; passes at 0. The three safeHref() sites must be RESOLVED rather than deleted: '#' is also their stored-XSS degradation path, so the fix separates 'unsafe url' from 'empty field' instead of dropping the fallback.

entries.detail:
SPLIT OUT OF PROG-P4 2026-08-25 (ADR-1127), because it is the half that CHANGES WHAT RENDERS. 24 files still compose IndexTemplate with no hero band: app/(help)/help/page.tsx, app/(help)/help/[category]/page.tsx, /circles/templates, /crew/leaderboard, /drafts, /housing/roommates, /lead/training-library, /market/manage, /messages, /orders, /partners, /partners/collaborators, /partners/join, /search, /spaces/[slug]/journeys, /spaces/[slug]/loom, /spaces/[slug]/manage/circles, /spaces/[slug]/podcasts, /spaces/[slug]/practices, /spaces/operating, /support, /discover/partners, /discover/practices, /discover/practices/pillar/[slug].

Adopting is mechanically one line each (`const hero = await resolveIndexHero(route)` + `{...hero}`), but it is NOT a no-op the way PROG-P5's detail adoption is: resolveIndexHero always returns heroOverlay: true, so an unmapped route gets a LARGE GRADIENT BAND and the page's h1 moves onto it. Contrast detail-hero.ts, whose unmapped tail is 'none' — an adoption there is invisible until the section is mapped. So each of the 24 needs an INDEX_HERO_DEFAULTS row FIRST, classifying it discovery (large + a section cover) or utility (short + the gradient), per the short/large product decision already written into that map.

Three things to settle in that PR, not here:
  (a) Whether the index ladder should grow a 'none' tail like the detail one, so adoption can be staged. If it does, this row shrinks to adding map rows.
  (b) The /spaces/[slug]/* tab pages (5 of the 24) sit INSIDE a Space profile that already has its own hero above them; a second band may be wrong there regardless of size.
  (c) Visual baselines move on every surface adopted. Expect pr-compare diffs and re-baseline deliberately.

entries.detail: PULLED OUT OF HYG-010 2026-08-25: it sat inside a clause about 'menu polish' and it is a feature, not a badge. ADR-860 asked for three things and TWO AND A HALF have shipped: syncMenuFromDefaults is the non-destructive re-check (lib/menus/actions.ts:459), identity rides `synced_default_keys` (20260801140000), and LIVE-107 added scripts/maintenance/menu-drift.mjs on the weekly sweep. What is still missing is the half that faces a PERSON: nothing in components/admin/menu/ shows an operator, per item, whether it is SYNCED (matches the code default), EDITED (label/subheading/gating diverged), RETIRED (its href is in synced_default_keys with no live row, so the inserts-only sync will NEVER resurrect it) or MISSING (a new default the next sync will inject). 🔴 A WEEKLY CI JOB IS NOT A SUBSTITUTE, and LIVE-107 is the proof rather than the refutation: the mislabelled 'Spaces directory' row was created BY AN OPERATOR IN THIS EDITOR, and the person who created it had no way to see that the row they were editing had left its default behind. A weekly job tells a maintainer afterwards; a drift column tells the author at the moment of the edit. Why it is S and not XS: the classification is a pure function of (resolved menu, defaultMenu(surfaceKey), synced_default_keys), but the third input is DB state the 900-line client editor does not receive, so the fix threads a prop from the server page as well as rendering the state. Do the derivation in lib/menus/ where it can be tested without a browser, and reuse menu-drift.mjs's comparison rather than writing a second one that can disagree with it.

Merging deploys to production (AGENTS.md), and a NOT NULL that finds an unexpected row fails the migration and the deploy with it — so this wants its own PR, re-counting the untenanted rows immediately before it goes, not a line in somebody else's diff. entries.detail:
FOUND 2026-08-25 by PROG-DAWN3 slice 1 (ADR-1119), and found the only way it could be — by a sweep moving pixels and CI mostly not noticing. Slice 1 changed 37 sites; EXACTLY ONE of them rendered on a surface the visual suite watched (the event approval controls, mounted by the space console), and that one produced 4 real failures. The other 36 moved with nothing looking at them, so the run's '140 passed' was never evidence the sweep held still.

THE CAUSE WAS STRUCTURAL. test/e2e/visual.spec.ts took its surfaces from test/e2e/surfaces.ts, which parsed EDITABLE_PAGES out of lib/page-editor/data.ts at run time plus one hand-maintained extra ('/discover'). EDITABLE_PAGES exists to say WHICH PAGES THE PAGE EDITOR MAY EDIT, so the camera pointed wherever an unrelated product decision happened to point it. Measured 2026-08-25: ZERO '/admin' literals in the file, i.e. no operator surface in the product was visually watched at all.

── CLOSED 2026-08-25 (ADR-1128). The visual suite now has its OWN list, coverageSurfaces(), with three inputs: the parsed EDITABLE_PAGES routes (the parse was never the bug — Lift 5c conversions must keep joining automatically, so it stays as ONE INPUT), the public extras, and OPERATOR_PATHS — seven /admin routes chosen by CENSUS, not by taste. scripts/visual-surface-census.mjs is committed so the argument re-runs. Measured on the tree AFTER slice 1 landed, so these are live numbers and not pre-sweep ones: 99 of the repo's 463 frozen raw-button-bg sites (21.4%) and 518 of its 1,799 raw <button> tags (28.8%) live in app/(main)/admin/** + components/admin/**, and the seven picked routes hold 47/98 and 256/481 of what all 92 static admin routes can be credited with — 48% of the operator raw-button-bg and 53% of its buttons for 7.5% of the routes, at ~1.5 minutes of added runner time per pixel-moving PR. The share is stable under a sweep: slice 1 retired 43 sites repo-wide and the operator share of raw <button> did not move off 28.8%, which is what makes this structural rather than a snapshot.

THE MEASUREMENT HAD ITS OWN TRAP AND THE ADR RECORDS IT: a FULL transitive import closure credits fourteen unrelated admin routes with the same 71 debt-bearing files, because a registry deep in the graph imports most of the product. An import is not a render, so the census basis is deliberately shallow (route directory + two import hops) and every number is stated as an UPPER BOUND.

WHAT WAS CUT, NAMED RATHER THAN TRUNCATED SILENTLY: the other 85 static admin routes (368 captures, ~18 min/PR, for the remaining 51 sites), every dynamic route (no stable seeded id survives a new preview hostname — the app-room failure), the seeder/demo consoles, and the @a11y + overflow suites (an operator surface with no a11y-baselines.json row is held to $defaultMax, so widening those needs its own seeded capture — HYG-027).

🔴 NOT MERGEABLE UNTIL THE BASELINES ARE CAPTURED ON A RUNNER: e2e-manual.yml → workflow_dispatch → base_url=<preview>, capture_shell ✔, update_baselines ✔ writes the 28 admin* PNGs. The operator surfaces ride the SAME PW_STORAGE_STATE as the member shell (no second auth path); what they need on top is the /admin role floor, and whether the e2e account clears it is the subject of HYG-027.

entries.title: The stored-links census has no checker and no freshness rule, so its two probes carry duplicated inline logic
entries.detail:
FOUND 2026-08-25 while working LIVE-104/108/109 (ADR-1125). ADR-1115 modelled scripts/stored-links.json on scripts/stored-block-types.json and copied the census but NOT the instrument around it. The block census has scripts/check-stored-blocks.mjs (integrity floors, a pure classifier, loud degradation, a `--probe` mode) plus scripts/check-stored-blocks.test.ts driving it against broken fixtures, so the DETECTOR is proven to fire rather than assumed to. The link census has neither. Three consequences, all live in the tree today:

  • THE LOGIC LIVES IN THE ROWS. LIVE-104's probe is ~1.5 KB of `node -e` that parses the census, parses next.config.ts's redirect table, follows redirect chains and re-derives four counts. LIVE-108's re-implements the same census walk and the same redirect parse. Two copies, written in JSON string escapes, where neither can be unit-tested and a fix to one silently misses the other.
  • THE DETECTOR IS UNPROVEN. Its arms have been exercised by hand — mutation controls are recorded in ADR-1115 and ADR-1125 — which is better than nothing and is exactly the manual ritual check-stored-blocks.test.ts exists to replace.
  • THERE IS NO FRESHNESS RULE. `capturedAt` is written but nothing reads it, so a census months behind production reads exactly like one taken this morning. The block census at least asserts the field is PRESENT. ⚠️ Stated rather than glossed, because it does not go away: neither census can see a document written AFTER its capture date — only a credentialled re-capture can, and this repo has no credentialled CI job. A freshness rule cannot fix that; it can only stop a stale reading from passing quietly as a fresh one.

THE WORK: lift the shared walk into scripts/check-stored-links.mjs (census I/O, integrity floors, the redirect-table parse, the classifier), give it a test that drives it against broken fixtures, and reduce both row probes to a `--probe` call. Do NOT weaken what those probes currently assert while doing it.

verify.cmd: node -e "const fs=require('fs');const S='scripts/check-stored-links.mjs',T='scripts/check-stored-links.test.ts',B='docs/BUILD-BACKLOG.json';if(!fs.existsSync(B))process.exit(79);const miss=[];if(!fs.existsSync(S))miss.push(S+' does not exist: the census has no instrument, only two hand-rolled row probes');if(!fs.existsSync(T))miss.push(T+' does not exist: the detector is unproven');let b;try{b=JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync(B,'utf8'))}catch{process.exit(79)}const rows=(b.entries||[]).filter(e=>e.id==='LIVE-104'||e.id==='LIVE-108');if(rows.length!==2)process.exit(79);for(const r of rows){const c=(r.verify||{}).cmd||'';if(/next\.config/.test(c)&&!/check-stored-links/.test(c))miss.push(r.id+' still re-implements the census walk and the redirect-table parse inline ('+c.length+' chars of node -e) instead of calling the shared checker')}if(miss.length){console.error(miss.join('\n'));process.exit(1)}process.exit(0)"
verify.note: Measures the CONSEQUENCE — the shared instrument exists, it has a test, and the two row probes actually CALL it instead of each carrying a copy of the census walk and the redirect-table parse. A file that merely exists does not close it: the probes must stop re-implementing next.config.ts parsing inline. Exits 79 if the backlog or the two rows cannot be read, so 'I could not look' never spells the same as 'I found nothing'.

entries.title: listing_saves: superseded by SCAN-508 — the retirement was correct and the callers came later
entries.detail:
FOUND 2026-08-25 04:14 UTC while running the migration finale, and the premise CHANGED once it was measured. A ledger row `20270327000000 restore_listing_saves` appeared in production between 04:00 and 04:14, applied from OUTSIDE the session driving the merge queue, with no file in supabase/migrations and none on any of the 20 most recently pushed branches. Because ledger-parity computes inParity as repoOnly === 0 AND ledgerOnly === 0, that one orphan row turned check:migrations red on NINE open branches at once, none of them for a reason their own diff could explain.

🔴 THE RETIREMENT WAS WRONG, and that is the finding. 20260925000000_retire_orphaned_tables_and_functions.sql dropped public.listing_saves as an orphan -- 'no reader, no writer'. It has BOTH, and they are reachable: lib/listings/index.ts declares saveListing / unsaveListing / listSavedListingIds against `listing_saves`, and app/(main)/housing/[id]/edit/actions.ts exports saveListingAction and unsaveListingAction over them, with app/(main)/housing/[id]/page.tsx batching listSavedListingIds for the browse grid. So from 2026-09-25 until tonight's restore, a member hearting a housing listing was writing to a table that did not exist. Nobody filed it, which says the path is cold in practice -- but it was live code against a missing table, not dead code.

WHO restored it is still unknown: the owner was asked on 2026-08-25 and answered that it was not them. The repair direction was chosen from the live catalog rather than from the row -- the table EXISTS (profile_id, listing_id, created_at; composite PK; both FKs cascade; RLS with one policy, listing_saves_self, FOR ALL on profile_id = private.get_my_profile_id(); 0 rows), so deleting the ledger row would leave a fresh replay without a table production has. 20270327000000 reconstructs it field-by-field off the live catalog, idempotent, and scripts/table-grants.txt carries its `authenticated` verdict.

THE WORK: (1) write the ADR recording the un-retirement and AMEND 20260925000000's 'orphaned' claim, which production and the code both contradict; (2) decide whether the saves feature is wanted -- if yes it needs a test so the table cannot be retired out from under it again, and if no, the honest end state is retiring the CODE first and then the table in a new higher-versioned migration; (3) audit the REST of 20260925000000: if it was wrong about this table it may be wrong about its siblings, and that is the cheap check to run now.

⚠️ DO NOT close this by deleting the ledger row, and do not edit 20270327000000 -- it describes an apply that already happened. ── ✅ CLOSED 2026-08-25 AS SUPERSEDED BY SCAN-508 / ADR-1144, AND THIS ROW'S HEADLINE WAS WRONG. It says 'THE RETIREMENT WAS WRONG, and that is the finding'. It was not. The local clone was SHALLOW (71 commits) so nothing here could order the events; git fetch --deepen=500 reaches 681 and settles it: 20260925000000 landed 2026-07-07 (#1606) verifying 0 code references, and lib/listings/index.ts gained its four .from('listing_saves') sites on 2026-07-27 (#1967), TWENTY DAYS LATER. The EFFECT this row describes is real and was real — a member hearting a housing listing wrote to a table that did not exist — but the diagnosis is backwards: a feature was built on an already-dropped table, so it never worked rather than having broken. The 'WHO restored it' question is answered too: the restore was deliberate and correct, recorded in 20270327000000 and explained in the AMENDED note now carried by 20260925000000. Two rows described one thing and one of them asserted something the other disproves; the one list keeps the accurate one.

verify.evidence: Superseded by SCAN-508 (done) and ADR-1144. Timeline established from git after `git fetch --deepen=500`: retirement migration first appears 2026-07-07 in #1606; the listing_saves call sites first appear 2026-07-27 in #1967. Production: public.listing_saves exists with 0 rows and 1 policy. SCAN-508's probe is the live one — it holds the AMENDED note in the retirement migration and the throw-path tests in lib/listings/saves.test.ts.

entries.title: The operator surfaces have no a11y ratchet rows, and the e2e account may not clear the /admin role floor

verify.cmd: node -e "const fs=require('fs');const F='test/e2e/a11y-baselines.json';if(!fs.existsSync(F))process.exit(79);const j=JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync(F,'utf8'));const keys=Object.keys(j.surfaces||{}).filter(k=>k.startsWith('/admin'));if(keys.length===0){console.error('the a11y ratchet holds 0 operator rows, so the seven /admin surfaces the visual suite watches are still held to $defaultMax and cannot join the a11y matrix');process.exit(1)}process.exit(0)"

entries.detail:
FILED 2026-08-25 by ADR-1128, which deliberately left both halves out of its own change.

HALF ONE — THE A11Y RATCHET. ADR-1128 added seven /admin routes to the VISUAL suite only. a11y.spec.ts and overflow.spec.ts still read publicSurfaces()/appSurfaces(). A surface with no row in test/e2e/a11y-baselines.json is held to $defaultMax (0 serious+), so adding the operator routes there without first SEEDING the ratchet would fail pull requests on debt that predates them — exactly what update-a11y + capture_shell exists to prevent. The seed is a dispatch: e2e-manual.yml → base_url=<preview>, capture_shell ✔, update_a11y ✔. The probe measures the consequence: at least one '/admin' key in the ratchet.

HALF TWO — THE ROLE FLOOR, AND IT WAS MEASURED RATHER THAN CALLED UNCHECKABLE. requireAdminFloor() (lib/admin/guard.ts) admits platform staff (web_role admin/janitor) or a team_members staff role that sees an admin group, and redirects everyone else to /feed. PW_MEMBER_EMAIL is an owner-held secret, but its CONSEQUENCE is readable: test/e2e/a11y-baselines.json carries '/spaces/danieltyack/manage' rows, so the e2e account manages that Space, and exactly two profiles do — danieltyack (web_role janitor, clears the floor) and awesomepossum (web_role none, does not). Repo-wide only danieltyack and moderation hold a staff web_role and team_members holds one row. So the outcome is one of two and the first capture run settles it in one line of the job summary: if the seven /admin rows appear under 'Still unphotographed', the account is the second one and the fix is a single grant (web_role='admin', or a team_members staff role that sees an admin group). Until then operatorDenialReason() skips those tests WITH THE CAUSE NAMED and shell-reporter.ts lists every one of them on every run — loud, never silent.

entries.title: Vercel builds intermittently stall at 'Collecting page data' for tens of minutes, and merging deploys to production

source.ref: the cold-compile path a trim leaves behind — NOT established as the cause

entries.detail: FOUND 2026-08-25 05:26-05:36 UTC while driving the merge queue. Preview build dpl_DYMk7sVcpW8n7xCfupmUmbtbnjqB (#2285, efad250) printed 'Collecting page data using 3 workers ...' at 05:26:05 and emitted NOTHING for the next 10 minutes, against a control that did the whole build in 2m10s. Three builds hung the same way earlier the same night. 🔴 WHY THIS IS LIVE AND NOT HYGIENE: main is protected and merging DEPLOYS, so the same stall on a production build is a production deploy that never lands. ── WHAT IS ESTABLISHED, from the two builds' own logs. They are the SAME BRANCH one docs-only commit apart, so the code is not the variable: (a) ca95b0a restored cache 8erA4jNs, compiled in 46s, finished 2m10s, green; (b) efad250 restored cache 92GM6pY7 — the build whose postbuild had just trimmed .next/cache/turbopack (1621 MiB) — compiled COLD in 113s, then stalled. The cold compile is expected and documented ('Next build: warm install, cold compile'); it costs CPU by design. The STALL is at a later stage and is NOT explained by it. ── 🔴 THREE HYPOTHESES TESTED AND RULED OUT, recorded so nobody re-runs them: (1) NOT the ADR-1064/ADR-1086 fetch-cache deletion. check-cache-budget.mjs protects it — NEVER_TRIM_DIRS = ['fetch-cache','images'], the trim walks only COMPILER_CACHE_DIRS = ['turbopack','rspack','webpack','swc'], an OVERLAP assertion refuses to trim if the lists ever meet, and check-cache-budget-trim.test.ts reconstructs the old bad trim. The gate's '.next/cache 0 MiB' line is not a deleted fetch cache: the 'holds:' line shows the directory contained only .previewinfo, config.json and .rscinfo, so there was no fetch-cache directory to lose. (2) NOT database saturation, which WAS the proven cause of the ~02:40 incident: measured mid-stall at 34/60 connections, 1 active, 0 blocked, no lock waits. (3) NOT build concurrency, the other proven cause: efad250 was the only build running. ── WHAT IS NOT KNOWN: the cause. The leading untested hypothesis is memory pressure — the builder is 4 cores / 8 GB, page data prerenders ~330 routes across 3 workers, and a cold compile denies them every warm module cache; a hung build never reaches the 'Build system report' line that would print 'No memory or disk space problems detected', so absence of that line is not evidence of health. NEXT STEP for whoever picks this up: correlate hung builds against whether their restored cache had been trimmed (the Vercel log's 'Restored build cache from previous deployment (<id>)' line gives the lineage for free), and if the correlation holds, test the memory hypothesis by raising the builder or lowering worker count before touching the trim. Do NOT 'fix' check:cache-budget on this row's suspicion alone: its trim is proven correct by mutation test, and breaking it re-opens the 1.50 GB ceiling that killed two builds. ── 🔴 AMENDED 2026-08-25 05:46: THE CACHE-LINEAGE CORRELATION IS FALSIFIED. When this row was filed, three builds were consistent with 'restored a trimmed cache -> stalls'. A direct control killed it: theme/p5-adoption was re-pushed as 71c9913c5, Vercel restored THE SAME trimmed cache (92GM6pY7 — branch-scoped restore, so the re-push could not escape it), the build cold-compiled exactly as efad250 had, and then COMPLETED — 'Build Completed in 2m', READY in ~2m50s, finishing with 'Uploading build cache [1.26 GB]'. Same branch, same cache, same cold compile, opposite outcome. So the trimmed cache does NOT cause the stall, and the 'branch is trapped on a poisoned cache' reading that followed from it is wrong too — the trap does not exist, because a build on that very cache succeeded and replaced it. FOUR hypotheses are now dead (fetch-cache deletion, DB saturation, build concurrency, cache lineage), and the stall stands as an UNEXPLAINED TRANSIENT: one occurrence, not reproducible on demand, no known trigger. 🔴 DO NOT re-run the four dead hypotheses, and do not treat the cold compile as the fault: it is documented, intended, and costs CPU only. The honest next step is not a fix but an OBSERVATION: this needs a second occurrence before it can be diagnosed at all, so what would actually help is capturing whether a stalled build ever reaches BUILD_EXCEEDED_MAXIMUM_TIME and what its 'Build system report' says — a hung build never prints that line, which is why the memory hypothesis below remains untested rather than untrue. ── 🔴 CORRECTION 2026-08-25 06:16, and it retracts this row's own advice: RETRY IS NOT A RELIABLE WORKAROUND. The row said so on the strength of #2285, which stalled once and went green on its first retry. #2283 then stalled THREE TIMES IN A ROW on the same branch — dac3a9d96 (05:51, terminal error captured), 0f294a89d first attempt, and 0f294a89d again after a re-push — so the earlier sentence described a coin flip, not a fix. Occurrence rate on the night: 4 of ~16 preview builds. ── WHAT THE THREE #2283 FAILURES ADD: they were NOT all cold compiles (81s, 77s and 113s across the set, against a 46s warm control), NOT all concurrent with another build (one ran alone), and NOT cache-lineage bound (#2285 succeeded on the very cache #2283 keeps failing on). The one thing every failure shares is the stage: page-data collection, 3 workers, dying without output. 🔴 APPLICATION CODE IS RULED OUT, and this is the cleanest evidence in the row: PR #2287 is DOCS-ONLY — two files, docs/BUILD-BACKLOG.json and AGENTS.md, zero code, zero dependencies — and its build stalls identically (0942e50, 11m+ at page data). A build with no code change cannot be crashed by code, so every application-level lead dies with it, including the astronomy-engine one #2283 invited. ── THE REMAINING ASYMMETRY, worth a look but NOT yet a cause: in the same window, builds on a branch based on OLD main (claude/frequency-codebase-audit-vii214, base 10c2f0b3) went READY in 2m54s and 3m29s, while every branch based on TONIGHT's main stalled. That points at something that entered main during the 11-PR merge run rather than at any one PR's diff — but main's own production build after #2285 (591bcc1) went READY in 2m6s, which argues against it, so the asymmetry is unexplained rather than damning. The concrete lever remains worker count or builder size. ── ✅ CARRIED OVER FROM THE HANDOFF BRANCH, and it is the most diagnostic fact in this row: THE STALL IS NOT A STALL. Established at 06:01, BEFORE the 06:16 correction above, and folded in here on 2026-08-25 08:5x when the two records were reconciled. The #2283 build was allowed to run to its natural end — the one thing no earlier occurrence had done — and it did not time out silently, it FAILED with a real error: `Error: The file "/vercel/path0/.next/routes-manifest.json" couldn't be found`, emitted at 23:01:36 UTC against 'Collecting page data using 3 workers ...' at 22:51:47. So the ~10 minutes of silence is not a hang: page-data collection DIES, produces no routes-manifest.json, and Vercel only surfaces it after its own wait. That reframes the row — the thing to explain is a CRASHING collector, not a blocked one, and 'it hung' was the wrong question for four hypotheses in a row. 🔴 IT ALSO MAKES THE MEMORY HYPOTHESIS THE LEADING ONE and is consistent with every observation: the builder is 4 cores / 8 GB, page data prerenders ~330 routes across 3 workers, a worker killed by the OOM reaper writes nothing and prints nothing, and the 'Build system report' line that would say 'No memory or disk space problems detected' is only reached by builds that COMPLETE — which is exactly why every healthy build shows it and no failing one does. NEXT STEP, concrete: reduce the page-data worker count (or raise the builder) and see whether the rate goes to zero. The misconfigured-distDir causes Vercel's own error text suggests are ruled out by the same commit and config building green on a retry. ── ⚠️ FIFTH OCCURRENCE 2026-08-25 08:12, on the meta-scan split: dpl_9WWrdz7onHuhx32cisXkTXeUmHtL (#2289 split/b-seo, 571aac085) compiled normally in 78s and then sat at 'Collecting page data using 3 workers ...' from 08:12:57 with no further output. It matters for the rate rather than the diagnosis: the SAME session's other three split branches built green (#2288, #2290, #2291 all READY), so it is still intermittent and still not branch-, code- or cache-bound. Running total on the two sessions: 5 of ~20. The workaround that worked here was not a retry but a re-push carrying a main merge, which is a new build rather than a re-run of the same one. ── 🔴 SIXTH OCCURRENCE 2026-08-25 11:17, AND IT IS THE FIRST ON PRODUCTION — THIS ROW'S OWN PREDICTION CAME TRUE. dpl_7Dbat8ebPxAkzpWrpC8sx1nAWiYg is the PRODUCTION build of 2f4b1cd93, the merge commit of #2287, and it is in state ERROR. Compiled successfully in 84s, completed runAfterProductionCompile in 83s, printed 'Collecting page data using 3 workers ...' at 11:17:42 and emitted nothing further. postbuild never ran, so that build produced NO gate readings. CONSEQUENCE, which is the part that matters: production is serving ee1aacf99 and main's HEAD IS NOT DEPLOYED. The row opened by arguing it was LIVE rather than hygiene because 'the same stall on a production build is a production deploy that never lands' — that is no longer a forecast. ✅ AND IT IS THE CLEANEST CONTROL IN THE ROW, better than the #2287 preview it already cites: 2f4b1cd93 differs from ee1aacf99 — the last GREEN PRODUCTION build, same target, same branch, same builder class — by exactly TWO FILES, AGENTS.md and docs/BUILD-BACKLOG.json, and neither is read by any app or script the build runs (grep across app/lib/components finds only comment prose mentioning AGENTS.md; prebuild is copy-maplibre-worker.mjs alone). Every byte the compiler and the collector see is identical. A build input that cannot differ, succeeding and then failing on the same target, retires 'something about this tree' as a class of explanation, not just the four hypotheses already dead. Running total 6 of ~21. THE NEXT STEP IS UNCHANGED AND NOW HAS A COST ATTACHED: set experimental.cpus in next.config.ts to lower the collector's worker count (Next 16.3.2's getNumberOfWorkers at node_modules/next/dist/build/index.js:369 treats any value differing from the default as a user override; the config does not set it today, so the 3 in the log is Vercel's own modifyConfig choosing for a 4-core builder), or raise the builder. ⚠️ Do NOT wire that from this row's suspicion in a change that cannot observe it: at a ~29% failure rate ONE green build proves nothing, so the change and the reading of its rate belong together. ── ✅ THE GAP CLOSED 2026-08-25 12:36, WITHOUT ANYONE FIXING THIS ROW. The production build of 1386abe6c (#2293) went READY, so production is current with main's HEAD again and the 'not deployed' consequence recorded above is over. It is a data point, NOT a fix: the failure is intermittent by definition, and one green build at a ~27% rate proves nothing about the cause. Running total 6 of ~22. ⚠️ TWO THINGS THAT BUILD PRINTED AND A FAILING ONE NEVER DOES. (1) 'Build system report • No memory or disk space problems detected' — exactly as this row predicts, that line is reached only by a build that COMPLETES, so its presence here is not evidence against the memory hypothesis and its absence on the six failures is not evidence for it. It stays untested. (2) postbuild ran all four gates, which a failing build never reaches: build-budget 6.67 GB / 498 fns (83%), og-trace 69/100, shell-weight 1011 KB / 21 chunks (72%), cache-budget 1.28 GB predicted against 1.27 GB actually uploaded — a THIRD paired reading, accurate to 1%, on the same mix as the c8b5ee97 exact one. 🔴 ONE NEW OBSERVATION WORTH THE NEXT READER'S TIME: this build took NINE MINUTES ('Build Completed in /vercel/output [9m]') against the 2m-2m50s controls this row quotes throughout, and still finished. So slowness at this stage is not itself the failure, and a build sitting quiet for several minutes is not yet a stalled one — which is worth knowing before anyone cancels another and destroys the evidence.

verify.evidence: Vercel dpl_DYMk7sVcpW8n7xCfupmUmbtbnjqB (theme/p5-adoption, efad250): 'Restored build cache from previous deployment (92GM6pY7KcpiE47fmp3AH3LRZ8tz)', 'Compiled successfully in 113s', then 'Collecting page data using 3 workers ...' at 05:26:05 with no further line for 10+ min. Control dpl_AEAZN7As5zEBLceQMDQmjjYo5Cgc (hyg/visual-coverage-surfaces, ca95b0a): 'Restored build cache from previous deployment (8erA4jNsESPA6Fnj3sjYXzr71EA7)', 'Compiled successfully in 46s', READY in 2m10s. Trim recorded in dpl_92GM6pY7KcpiE47fmp3AH3LRZ8tz postbuild: 'drops compiler caches instead: .next/cache/turbopack (1621 MiB)'. Live DB mid-stall: 34/60 conns, 1 active, 0 blocked. FALSIFYING CONTROL: dpl_9JHKUk5Q9q2nzHQaT3qwdxfeTqVW (theme/p5-adoption, 71c9913c5) 'Restored build cache from previous deployment (92GM6pY7KcpiE47fmp3AH3LRZ8tz)' — the same trimmed cache efad250 pulled — then 'Build Completed in 2m', READY 05:46:17, 'Uploading build cache [1.26 GB]'. TERMINAL ERROR CAPTURED (carried over from the handoff branch): dpl_9y44g2LaSLVACtvhC4BnAzaXhS9T failed at 23:01:36 with 'The file "/vercel/path0/.next/routes-manifest.json" couldn't be found', ~10 min after 'Collecting page data using 3 workers ...' at 22:51:47. The collector dies; it does not hang. FIFTH OCCURRENCE: dpl_9WWrdz7onHuhx32cisXkTXeUmHtL (#2289, 571aac085) compiled in 78s then no output after 'Collecting page data using 3 workers ...' at 08:12:57, while three sibling split branches built green in the same window. SIXTH, AND FIRST ON PRODUCTION: dpl_7Dbat8ebPxAkzpWrpC8sx1nAWiYg (production, 2f4b1cd93, #2287 merge) state ERROR — 'Compiled successfully in 84s', 'Completed runAfterProductionCompile in 83s', 'Collecting page data using 3 workers ...' 11:17:42, then nothing; postbuild never ran. Diff against the last green production build ee1aacf99 is two docs files (AGENTS.md, docs/BUILD-BACKLOG.json), neither read by any build-time code. Production therefore serves ee1aacf99, one commit behind main. GREEN AGAIN: dpl_qfBanV5X4usst8d9jq1KbJ1CLbu7 (production, 1386abe6c, #2293) READY at 12:36 — 'Build Completed in /vercel/output [9m]', all four postbuild gates printed, 'Build system report • No memory or disk space problems detected'. Production is current with main's HEAD again. Rate 6 of ~22.

entries.title: lib/database.types.ts carries a hand-added spotlight_guestbook block — regen from production to prove parity

The debt: nothing has machine-checked that the hand-written block matches what supabase gen types would emit. Next integrator regen (the standing 'regen + drop the untyped admin-handle casts' step BUILD-LIST already names) closes this: run the regen, diff, and mark this row done with the commit as evidence.

entries.title: The guest RSVP door closes ~7-8 hours early: wall-clock-as-UTC compared to now()
entries.detail: MS25 Phase 1. capture_guest_rsvp gates on v_event.starts_at <= now(), but starts_at stores the event's WALL-CLOCK as UTC parts (lib/time/zone.ts convention): a 7pm PT event reads as 19:00Z, so from ~noon PT every guest submission is silently rejected while the anti-oracle receipt still says ok - the guest believes they RSVP'd. Members face no such gate. Fix is one SQL function change resolving the stored wall-clock through events.time_zone before comparing. BLOCKED on the migration freeze; apply the moment it lifts.

verify.cmd: node -e "const fs=require('fs');const f='supabase/migrations/20270328000000_guest_rsvp_zone_aware_gate.sql';if(!fs.existsSync(f)){console.error('the zone-aware gate migration is missing');process.exit(1)}const s=fs.readFileSync(f,'utf8');if(!/at time zone/.test(s)||!/pg_timezone_names/.test(s)){console.error('the gate does not resolve the event zone, or does not validate it');process.exit(1)}"
verify.note: Measures the CONSEQUENCE: a migration exists that resolves the stored wall clock through the event's own zone AND validates the zone name (the unvalidated form raises on the anon door). Applied to production 2026-08-25 with the ledger reconciled to the filename; verified beforehand that zone-aware and naive comparisons agreed on all 20 future events and that zero rows carry an unknown zone.

entries.title: A pre-existing membership row makes Join a permanent 'try again'
entries.detail: MS25 Phase 1. joinCircle plain-inserts against UNIQUE(profile_id, circle_id); a 23505 conflict (already-active member re-tapping Join, or a dormant row) returns 'Could not join this circle. entries.title: Rule how pending-approval seats interact with capacity and the waitlist
entries.detail: MS25 Phase 1. The approval-gate fixes exposed a design tension nothing has ruled on: a pending (unapproved) seat holds status 'going' and consumes capacity (lib/events/capacity.ts:27-38), and promoteFromWaitlist promotes a still-pending waitlist row into a confirmed seat. Either behavior may be intended; neither is recorded. One ruling, then a small code follow-through if it changes. ── ✅ RULED AND CLOSED 2026-08-25 (ADR-1148). OWNER RULING: APPROVAL GATES THE SEAT. A pending request does NOT consume capacity; only an approved (or ungated) 'going' seat counts, and on approval a full event sends the person to the waitlist. That matches content/help/groups/events.md verbatim — 'A full event still sends approved people to the waitlist. Approving says yes, you are welcome, not there is room' — which was only true if approval, not the request, consumes the seat. THE DEFECT IT REMOVES: twenty unapproved REQUESTS could fill a twenty-seat event the host had not said yes to, and the host could then not approve anyone, because their own event read as full. THREE PLACES, kept in lockstep because they answer the same question: getCapacityInfo (lib/events/capacity.ts), the paged fallback in lib/events/going-counts.ts, and the event_going_counts RPC (20270333000000_going_counts_exclude_pending.sql, applied; ledger repaired to the repo version, 641 ⇄ 641). AND PROMOTION NO LONGER BYPASSES THE GATE: promoteFromWaitlist took the oldest waitlist row whatever its approval state, so a still-pending request could be lifted into a confirmed seat by someone else's cancellation — approval granted by timing rather than by the host. ✅ approval_status is NOT NULL DEFAULT 'none' (verified on production), so a plain <> 'pending' is COMPLETE rather than merely careful, and a null branch would suggest a state the column cannot hold. ⚠️ MEASURED BEFORE CHANGING: 0 gated events, 0 pending rows, 'none' the only value present — so this changes no current count and closes the rule before the first gated event exists. lib/events/capacity.test.ts adds 5 arms that assert THE FILTER IS SENT rather than that a number came back, because the bug was never in the arithmetic; mutation-proven both ways.

verify.cmd: node -e 'const fs=require("fs");const cap=fs.readFileSync("lib/events/capacity.ts","utf8");const strip=function(t){return t.split("\n").filter(function(l){return l.trim().indexOf("//")!==0}).join("\n")};const c=strip(cap);const n=(c.match(/neq\(.approval_status., .pending.\)/g)||[]).length;if(n<2){console.error("lib/events/capacity.ts applies the pending filter "+n+" time(s), expected 2 - the going count AND the waitlist pick both need it, or an unapproved request holds a seat or is promoted past the host");process.exit(1)}const gc=strip(fs.readFileSync("lib/events/going-counts.ts","utf8"));if(!/neq\(.approval_status., .pending.\)/.test(gc)){console.error("lib/events/going-counts.ts lost the pending filter, so the paged fallback disagrees with the RPC and the Has-open-spots facet depends on whether a migration was applied");process.exit(1)}const mig=fs.readdirSync("supabase/migrations").filter(function(f){return /exclude_pending/.test(f)});if(!mig.length){console.error("no migration excludes pending from event_going_counts; the server-side count still lets an unapproved request fill an event");process.exit(1)}const sql=fs.readFileSync("supabase/migrations/"+mig[0],"utf8");if(!/approval_status\s*<>\s*.pending./.test(sql)){console.error("the migration exists but its function body no longer excludes pending");process.exit(1)}'
verify.note: Measures the CONSEQUENCE in all three places that answer 'how many seats are taken': both filters in capacity.ts (the count AND the waitlist pick), the paged fallback, and the RPC's own body. Comment lines are stripped first, so the prose explaining the rule cannot satisfy the probe that enforces it.

entries.title: Twenty other reads still count a pending request as an attendee
entries.detail: FOUND 2026-08-25 while closing SCAN-105, by measuring the NEIGHBOURS of the read being fixed rather than stopping at it — the habit that found SCAN-211. SCAN-105 settled the CAPACITY question: a pending request does not hold a seat. It deliberately did NOT touch the other ~20 sites that filter `.eq('status','going')`, because they answer a different question and each needs its own answer. THE LIST, grouped by what they drive: NOTIFICATIONS — app/api/cron/event-reminders (x2), lib/events/cancellation.ts, lib/digest.ts, app/api/zap-prompt. Should someone the host has not approved get a reminder for an event they may not be attending, or a cancellation notice? ATTENDANCE + REWARDS — lib/achievements.ts, lib/onboarding/founder-tasks.ts, lib/events/connectors.ts, lib/events/matching.ts. Does an unapproved request count toward an achievement or a connection suggestion? OPERATOR/AI READS — lib/ai/poster-observer.ts, lib/ai/event-blurb.ts, lib/events/poster-quality.ts, app/(main)/admin/events/load-posted.ts, lib/spaces/tickets.ts (x3), lib/events/store.ts. ⚠️ THE HONEST POSITION IS THAT THESE ARE NOT ALL THE SAME BUG, which is why this is a triage row rather than a sweep and why it was not smuggled into SCAN-105: a cancellation notice probably SHOULD reach a pending requester (their request is moot either way), while an achievement probably should not. Latent today at 0 gated events. Rule each group, then apply. ✅ RULED AND CLOSED 2026-08-25 (ADR-1152). 🔴 THE ROW'S OWN ENUMERATION WAS WRONG IN THREE WAYS, all caused by its grep matching only the literal `.eq('status', 'going')`. (1) event-reminders is x1, not x2 — the RECIPIENT read was already fixed alongside SCAN-105; only the warm-proof count was open. (2) lib/spaces/tickets.ts x3 is a FALSE POSITIVE: it queries space_ticket_rsvps, a different table with no approval_status column, so the 'fix' would have errored. (3) It MISSED eight sites that filter in JS or in SQL, and two of those were the highest-impact findings in the whole row: `enforce_event_rsvp_capacity()` still counted requests as seats — answering SCAN-105's question the OLD way one layer BELOW the app, so getCapacityInfo said '1 spot left' and the trigger silently rewrote the member's RSVP to waitlist — and it never fired at approval time at all, making rsvp-depth.ts's comment 'the capacity trigger still applies' false for the whole life of the feature. `event_calendar_feed` leaked a hide_address venue to an unapproved requester, through the exemption 20270331000000 granted it on the premise 'every row in it is an event the subscriber is ATTENDING' — a premise approval-gating falsified. Both defects were REPRODUCED against production before the fix: the trigger demoted a third pending request on a two-seat event with zero seats taken, and the feed returned '123 Secret St'. Twelve sites ruled wrong and fixed; the host queue, cancellation notices, the member's own digest and RSVP badge, host-facing reach, the dispatch audience and the GDPR export were ruled CORRECT and deliberately left alone.

../,"the calendar social-proof count disagrees with the /events cards again"],["app/api/cron/event-reminders/route.ts",/neq\(.approval_status., .pending.\)/,"the reminder email prints a going count the rest of the product stopped believing"],["lib/achievements.ts",/neq\(.approval_status., .pending.\)/,"an achievement can be minted from a request the host never approved"],["lib/onboarding/founder-tasks.ts",/neq\(.approval_status., .pending.\)/,"a rewarded founder task completes on a single pending request"],["lib/events/matching.ts",/neq\(.approval_status., .pending.\)/,"people you know are going counts friends who are not going"],["lib/ai/event-blurb.ts",/neq\(.approval_status., .pending.\)/,"Vera states a known-going count that includes unapproved requests"],["lib/events/connectors.ts",/neq\(.approval_status., .pending.\)/,"a connection is suggested from a request the host may decline"],["lib/ai/poster-observer.ts",/neq\(.approval_status., .pending.\)/,"anti-farming evidence admits self-minted pending rows"],["lib/events/poster-quality.ts",/neq\(.approval_status., .pending.\)/,"poster quality counts an RSVP the host never acted on"]];for(const t of need){if(!fs.existsSync(t[0])){console.error("missing "+t[0]+": "+t[2]);process.exit(1)}if(!t[1].test(fs.readFileSync(t[0],"utf8"))){console.error(t[2]+" ("+t[0]+")");process.exit(1)}}'

The two migrations carry behavioural controls of their own that drive a real gated event and assert what each row becomes, so this probe checks the predicate is present and those controls do the proving. Sites ruled CORRECT (the host queue, cancellation notices, the member's own digest and RSVP badge, host reach, dispatch audience, GDPR export) are deliberately absent.

entries.title: Vera's dispatch is keyed on the UTC day, so it rolls over at 5pm Pacific

source.ref: dispatchDay(); read by lib/vera-dispatch.ts, app/api/zap-prompt/route.ts, app/(main)/on-air/dispatches/page.tsx

entries.detail: DONE 2026-08-25. PREMISE RE-TESTED AND IT HELD: todayUTC() was still at line 43 and still used at line 230. The key now comes from dispatchDay() = dayInZone(new Date(), HOME_TZ), exported from the leaf module lib/on-air/dispatch-day.ts so there is exactly ONE mint. IT IS A LEAF DELIBERATELY: defining it in lib/vera-dispatch.ts (where it started) would have dragged lib/ai/complete.ts -> lib/ai/client.ts, which VALUE-imports the Anthropic SDK, into the Zap route bundle - the AGENTS.md fan-out rule, and a contradiction of that routes own header saying it has no AI dependency. THE ROW UNDER-COUNTED THE READERS: two other surfaces derived the same key with their own toISOString().slice(0,10) and would have silently disagreed with the new one. app/api/zap-prompt/route.ts backs the most-tapped button in the app and looks up todays cached Dispatch by day - left as it was it would have missed every Dispatch after ~5pm Pacific and fallen back to the template line; it now imports dispatchDay. Its nudge-line hour had the same 5pm bug (getUTCHours put the tonight copy on screen 9am-4pm Pacific and never in the evening) and now reads the community hour via zoneOffsetMinutes. app/(main)/on-air/dispatches/page.tsx labels Today/Yesterday against the same imported function, and its 5-paragraph comment explaining why the label had to stay UTC is replaced (it was honest when written; SCAN-106 moved the key and the label together, which is what it asked for). COMMUNITY DAY, NOT MEMBER DAY, deliberately: lib/member-day.ts exists and is right for practice_logs.logged_for, which MEASURES a members own behaviour. This is a DELIVERY key under UNIQUE (profile_id, day) with no zone column stored beside it, so it must mean the same thing on every read forever. profiles.home_timezone is NULLABLE and MUTABLE (written from the browser by app/(main)/timezone-actions.ts), so a member-keyed day changes meaning between two reads minutes apart - unset zone mints under UTC (leaving this bug unfixed for exactly those members), the client then persists America/Los_Angeles, and the next session that evening finds no row and mints a SECOND Dispatch; travel does it in reverse and SKIPS a day. dayInZone(now, HOME_TZ) is a pure function of the instant. SHIPPING NOTE, unchanged from the original row and deliberately NOT papered over: members served in the 5pm-midnight Pacific window before the deploy can be minted one extra Dispatch, and (second-order, not in the original row) that orphaned tomorrow-keyed row will replay as tomorrows instead of a fresh one. Both one-time, copy valid either way. A dual-key read was rejected as permanent code for a one-day transition.

verify.cmd: node -e "const fs=require('fs');const Q=String.fromCharCode(39);const K='lib/on-air/dispatch-day.ts';const F=['lib/vera-dispatch.ts','app/api/zap-prompt/route.ts','app/(main)/on-air/dispatches/page.tsx'];if(F.some(f=>!fs.existsSync(f)))process.exit(79);const strip=s=>s.replace(/\/\*[\s\S]*?\*\//g,'').replace(/^\s*\/\/.*$/gm,'');const C={};for(const f of F)C[f]=strip(fs.readFileSync(f,'utf8'));const bad=[];if(!fs.existsSync(K))bad.push(K+' is missing, so there is no single place the dispatch day key is minted');else{const k=strip(fs.readFileSync(K,'utf8'));if(!/export\s+function\s+dispatchDay\s*\(/.test(k))bad.push(K+' exports no dispatchDay(), so there is no ONE key every reader can share');if(!/dayInZone\s*\([^)]*HOME_TZ/.test(k))bad.push('the dispatch day key is not minted with dayInZone(..., HOME_TZ), so it is not the community calendar day');if(/toISOString\(\)\s*\.slice\(\s*0\s*,\s*10\s*\)/.test(k))bad.push(K+' still mints a day key from the server UTC calendar day');if(k.indexOf('lib/ai/')>=0)bad.push(K+' is no longer a leaf, so importing the key drags AI deps into the hot Zap route');}for(const f of F){if(/toISOString\(\)\s*\.slice\(\s*0\s*,\s*10\s*\)/.test(C[f]))bad.push(f+' still mints a dispatch day key from the server UTC calendar day');if(!/\bdispatchDay\b/.test(C[f]))bad.push(f+' reads the dispatch day without importing dispatchDay, so its key can drift from the one rows are minted under');}if(C['lib/vera-dispatch.ts'].indexOf('eq('+Q+'day'+Q+', day)')<0)bad.push('lib/vera-dispatch.ts no longer filters vera_dispatches on the minted day, so nothing ties the key it mints to the rows it reads');if(bad.length){console.error(bad.join('; '));process.exit(1)}process.exit(0)"
verify.note: Measures the CONSEQUENCE across ALL THREE readers of vera_dispatches.day plus the module that mints it: the key comes from one exported dispatchDay() built on dayInZone(..., HOME_TZ), nobody re-derives it from the server UTC calendar day, and the minting module stays a LEAF (no lib/ai import) so the hot Zap route can share the key without the AI SDK. Comments are stripped first so a note quoting the old expression cannot pass or fail it. Verified to FAIL on the pre-fix tree.

entries.title: Answer the reconstructed listing_saves migration's open question, and amend the 2026-09 retirement claim it contradicts
entries.detail: MS25 Phase 0. That migration file was reconstructed from live state by the session running the merge queue (#2276) after the 2026-08-25 meta-scan applied the restore to production ahead of its file, which turned check:migrations red on every open branch until the reconstruction landed. Its header records what it could not establish and asks for two things. Both are answerable now. (1) WHY: the restore was DELIBERATE. 20260925000000 dropped listing_saves on the claim '0 code references', and that claim was false - lib/listings/index.ts holds four live .from('listing_saves') sites (saveListing / unsaveListing / listSavedListingIds / listSavedListings) reached from components/marketplace/save-listing-button.tsx on the /housing index and detail pages. Every path failed SAFE (the write discarded its error, the reads fell back to an empty set), so the heart flipped and silently reset on reload, and the saves tests mock the client so nothing caught it. THE READER THAT NEEDS THE TABLE is that button. (2) The retirement claim in 20260925000000 is contradicted by production and wants amending in place - not by editing the reconstructed file, which correctly describes an apply that already happened. An ADR recording the restore + the false-orphan lesson belongs with it. ✅ CLOSED 2026-08-25 (ADR-1144). 🔴 AND THIS ROW'S OWN ANSWER WAS WRONG, which is the finding. It asserted the retirement claim 'was false'. It was TRUE. The local clone was SHALLOW - 71 commits - so the order could not be read; `git fetch --deepen=500` reaches 681 and settles it: 20260925000000 landed 2026-07-07 (#1606) verifying 0 code references, and lib/listings/index.ts gained its four .from('listing_saves') sites on 2026-07-27 (#1967), TWENTY DAYS LATER. So the defect is the mirror of a bad retirement: a feature was built against a table that had already been dropped, and it NEVER WORKED - the heart flipped on click and reset on reload from the day it shipped, which is also why the restored table holds zero rows. TWO INDEPENDENT REASONS NOTHING CAUGHT IT, and both generalise. (1) IT COMPILED: db() in lib/listings/index.ts returns createAdminClient() typed as a bare SupabaseClient with NO Database generic, so the generated types - which were CORRECT, having dropped the table - were never consulted. A typed client would have failed the build that introduced the calls. (2) IT WAS SILENT: the writes discarded their error, the reads fell back empty, and lib/listings/saves.test.ts drove a stub whose resolve() hardcoded error: null, so it could not produce a database error of ANY kind. #2288 had already fixed half of it by making the writes throw - but that branch shipped with no test, because the stub could not reach it. This change gives the stub an error channel and adds the three arms (save throws, unsave throws, the reads still fail safe), each mutation-proven. The amendment lands in 20260925000000 as a NOTE rather than a retraction, since its premise held on the day it was written. The other five tables in that sweep were re-checked: zero .from(...)/.rpc(...) sites across app/, lib/ and components/. ⚠️ THE GENERAL HAZARD IS THE UNTYPED HANDLE, NOT THE SWEEP: '0 references' is a fact about one day, and nothing stopped a later branch from writing against the dropped table.

verify.cmd: node -e 'const fs=require("fs");const R="supabase/migrations/20260925000000_retire_orphaned_tables_and_functions.sql";if(!fs.existsSync(R)){console.error("the retirement migration is gone: "+R);process.exit(1)}const r=fs.readFileSync(R,"utf8");if(r.indexOf("listing_saves")<0){console.error("the retirement migration no longer mentions listing_saves; re-point this row");process.exit(1)}if(r.indexOf("AMENDED")<0||r.indexOf("20270327000000")<0){console.error("the retirement migration still stands alone, with no note that listing_saves was later restored - the two files contradict each other again");process.exit(1)}const S="supabase/migrations/20270327000000_restore_listing_saves.sql";if(!fs.existsSync(S)){console.error("the restore migration is gone: "+S);process.exit(1)}const t=fs.readFileSync("lib/listings/saves.test.ts","utf8");if(t.indexOf("const errors: unknown[] = []")<0){console.error("the saves stub lost its error channel, so it can no longer produce a database error and the throw branch is untestable again");process.exit(1)}if(t.indexOf("errors.shift()")<0){console.error("the stub declares an error queue but no longer reads it");process.exit(1)}if(!/rejects\.toThrow\(\/saveListing failed\//.test(t)||!/rejects\.toThrow\(\/unsaveListing failed\//.test(t)){console.error("the write helpers lost their throw-path tests - the branch #2288 added would ship uncovered again");process.exit(1)}const i=fs.readFileSync("lib/listings/index.ts","utf8");if(!/throw new Error\(.saveListing failed/.test(i)||!/throw new Error\(.unsaveListing failed/.test(i)){console.error("a write helper went back to swallowing its error, which is how a dropped table no-opped every save invisibly");process.exit(1)}'
verify.note: Measures the CONSEQUENCE on both halves. The record half: the retirement migration carries an AMENDED note naming the restore file, so the two stop contradicting each other. The code half: the stub still HAS an error channel and still READS it (a declared-but-unused queue would be the same blind spot wearing a disguise), both write helpers still have throw-path tests, and both still throw. Mutation-proven: reverting either helper to swallow its error, or making a read throw, turns it red.

entries.title: The beta referral contest is removed: the owner ruled there is no contest
entries.detail: FOUND 2026-08-25 while re-deriving SCAN-502's index, by classifying the dead functions instead of counting them. lib/beta/referral-contest.ts exports runContestSweep, whose own doc reads 'Catch up the contest tally: record any newly-activated referrals and any Circles that have crossed the starter threshold since the last run. Idempotent + bounded, so it is safe to run on a schedule. No-op when the contest flag is off.' It has ZERO callers anywhere in the tree, and none of the 27 crons declared in vercel.json is a referral-contest path. So the catch-up never happens: referrals that activate outside whatever inline path records them, and Circles that cross the starter threshold, are never added to the board. ⚠️ WHAT IS NOT ESTABLISHED, and wants an owner ruling rather than a patch: whether the contest is meant to be live at all. The function no-ops when betaReferralContestEnabled() is false, so wiring a cron is safe either way — but wiring a schedule for a contest the owner has parked would be building on a decision nobody made. THE FIX IF IT IS LIVE: an /api/cron/referral-contest route wrapped in withCronHeartbeat, plus its vercel.json entry — the same shape as the 27 that exist. THE FIX IF IT IS NOT: delete the sweep, and say so, so the next dead-export pass does not re-find it. ── 🔴 CORRECTED WITHIN THE HOUR, BEFORE THIS ROW SHIPPED, AND THE CORRECTION MATTERS MORE THAN THE ROW. The sentence above says the catch-up never happens; an earlier draft of it, and the PR body that carried it, went further and said THE CONTEST NEVER TALLIES. That is FALSE, and I wrote it by reading one function's callers instead of its siblings'. BOTH RECORDERS ARE WIRED INLINE: recordReferralActivation is called from lib/qr/referral.ts:121 inside releaseReferralReward, which /api/cron/referral-release runs on a schedule that DOES exist; and recordCircleStarterMilestone is called from app/(main)/circles/actions.ts:233 on a membership change. So the contest tallies fine on the happy path, and the board is not empty. WHAT IS ACTUALLY MISSING is the SAFETY NET: runContestSweep exists precisely because someone expected the inline hooks to miss cases — an activation that arrives without passing through releaseReferralReward, or a circle that crosses ten actives by a path that does not run that action — and nothing re-checks for those. Severity drops from 'a feature does not work' to 'a reconciliation pass nobody runs', which is a real but much smaller gap. ⚠️ THE LESSON IS THIS SESSION'S OWN, TURNED ON ME: I classified a dead export by reading its doc comment and its own caller count, and did not check whether its siblings covered the same ground. ADR-1145 says a doc comment is not evidence of a caller; it is equally not evidence of ABSENCE of one elsewhere. ── ✅ CLOSED 2026-08-25 BY OWNER RULING: there is no beta referral contest. That settles the fork this row named, and it settles it at the wider scope, because the whole feature was provably inert: platform_flags.beta_referral_contest was FALSE, beta_referrals held 0 rows, reward_grants held 0 beta_contest.* grants, and app/(main)/referral/page.tsx called notFound() while the flag was off, so no member could reach it. REMOVED: lib/beta/referral-contest.ts (423 lines) and its test, the /referral route (page + its copy-link client component, which nothing else imported — components/spaces/invite-form.tsx has its own local CopyLink), the recordReferralActivation call in lib/qr/referral.ts and the recordCircleStarterMilestone call in app/(main)/circles/actions.ts, three now-pointless vi.mock lines in the circles tests, and a stale cross-reference in lib/zaps.ts. ⚠️ THE TABLE IS DELIBERATELY LEFT: public.beta_referrals (0 rows) stays for now, because the repo's own sequencing — stated in 20260925000000's header about commerce_variants — is drop the WRITE, deploy, THEN drop the table. Doing both in one change is exactly the shape ADR-1144 was written about. Filed as SCAN-511.

verify.cmd: node -e 'const fs=require("fs");const gone=["lib/beta/referral-contest.ts","lib/beta/referral-contest.test.ts","app/(main)/referral/page.tsx","app/(main)/referral/copy-link.tsx"];for(const f of gone){if(fs.existsSync(f)){console.error("the beta referral contest is back: "+f+" - the owner ruled on 2026-08-25 that there is no contest");process.exit(1)}}const walk=function(dir,out){for(const e of fs.readdirSync(dir,{withFileTypes:true})){if(["node_modules",".next",".git","dist","build",".vercel","coverage"].indexOf(e.name)>=0)continue;const fp=dir+"/"+e.name;if(e.isDirectory())walk(fp,out);else if(/\.(ts|tsx)$/.test(fp))out.push(fp)}return out};const files=walk(".",[]);if(files.length<2000){console.error("the walk found only "+files.length+" files - it is not descending, so a clean result would prove nothing");process.exit(1)}const hits=[];for(const f of files){const s=fs.readFileSync(f,"utf8");if(/referral-contest|recordCircleStarterMilestone|recordReferralActivation|betaReferralContestEnabled|getContestLeaderboard/.test(s))hits.push(f)}if(hits.length){console.error("contest code returned in: "+hits.join(", "));process.exit(1)}'
verify.note: Measures the CONSEQUENCE — the feature is gone and stays gone. Four named files must not exist, AND no .ts/.tsx anywhere may mention the module or any of its four exported entry points, so a re-add under a new filename still fails. Carries a 2,000-file walk floor: without it, a walk that stopped descending would report a clean tree and pass by not looking (ADR-970).

entries.title: Drop public.beta_referrals now that the contest writes have deployed

source.ref: owner ruling 2026-08-25, no beta referral contest

entries.detail: SCAN-510 removed every reader and writer of public.beta_referrals when the owner ruled there is no beta referral contest. The TABLE was deliberately left behind in that change, and this row is the second step. 🔴 WHY IT IS TWO STEPS AND NOT ONE: the repo's own sequencing rule, stated in 20260925000000's header about commerce_variants — 'drop the write + column, deploy, THEN drop the table'. Dropping a table in the same change that removes its callers is precisely the shape ADR-1144 was written about: there, a drop and its code moved out of step and a feature silently never worked for a month. Here the order is deliberate. PRECONDITION: SCAN-510's removal must be DEPLOYED to production first — confirm the production build carrying it went READY, then land a drop migration. The table held 0 rows and 0 beta_contest.* reward_grants when the ruling was made, so nothing is lost. Also drop the beta_referrals block from lib/database.types.ts in the same pass by regenerating, rather than hand-editing (see HYG-031 for why hand-edits there rot). ✅ DONE 2026-08-25. PRECONDITION CHECKED RATHER THAN ASSUMED: SCAN-510 shipped in #2297 and its PRODUCTION deployment read READY on the Vercel deployment list (target=production, ref=main), so no running code could reference the table when the drop landed. The table held **0 rows** immediately before the drop, so the owner's 'export then drop' option was moot rather than declined. lib/database.types.ts had its beta_referrals block removed in the same pass. ⚠️ NOT a full regen: no SUPABASE_ACCESS_TOKEN is available in this container and the repo has no regen script, so the alternative was routing ~16k lines of generated types through an agent's context. The block removed is one contiguous, visible declaration, and the FULL regen-from-production remains HYG-031's job, which is what that row exists for.

The first version only checked that a FILENAME matched /beta_referrals/ and /drop/i, which an empty file passes.

entries.title: eslint warnings were never ratcheted, so the two that existed could never be the last two
entries.detail: MS25 close-out. Verifying merged main turned up two eslint warnings and, behind them, the reason there were exactly two: `pnpm lint` was bare `eslint`, with no --max-warnings, so a warning has NEVER failed the required `lint` job. Zero warnings was a state nobody was holding, not a floor. BOTH WARNINGS WERE REAL DEFECTS, not noise. (1) app/(main)/events/admin-actions.ts declared a `PlaceTimeRow` type nothing referenced, under a heading claiming when/where lived in its own admin module, `event-place-time-module`. No such module exists and none ever did for events: `place` is a spine slot only `circle.placeAndTime` fills (lib/admin/modules/registry.ts), and an event edits its when/where in event-settings-module.tsx against lib/studio/entities/event.ts. The type was a strict subset of EventAdminRow kept in step with it by nobody - a second declaration of the same row shape, which is the drift class the Studio contract exists to prevent. Type deleted, heading corrected to describe the one live thing under it (readRsvpWindow). (2) lib/qr/client-download.ts fell back to `window.location.href = <relative /api/qr URL>` when client-side rasterisation failed. The rule that flagged it was right to flag it and WRONG IN ITS REMEDY: it suggests router.push(), which at an /api route client-navigates and downloads nothing. A code download is a file fetch, so it wanted an <a download> all along - and the anchor is strictly safer, because assigning location unloads the page and depends on the server's Content-Disposition to bring the member back, so a missing header dropped them on a raw PNG instead of on the code they were downloading. THE RATCHET IS THE ACTUAL FIX: --max-warnings=0 added to the lint script CI already runs as a required context, proven green on the merged tree BEFORE wiring (0 errors, 0 warnings) and proven to FIRE by a mutation - a re-added unused `DeadShape` type turned it red at exit 1. The first mutation attempt used `_Unused` and did not fire, because the rule exempts /^_/; recorded because a control that cannot fail reads as coverage (ADR-970) and this one nearly shipped as exactly that. ADR-1142 records it, including the half that turned inward: this row's own probe was written in the safer single-quoted style and check:backlog REFUSED IT, because its quote rule counted double quotes unconditionally - blind to a bare single quote inside a single-quoted body, and rejecting the very style its own failure message recommends. The rule now derives the hazard from the quote that OPENED the body, with all four cases pinned in backlog-contract.test.ts.

").filter(function(l){return l.trim().indexOf("//")!==0}).join("
")};const cd=strip("lib/qr/client-download.ts");if(cd.indexOf("location.href")>=0){console.error("lib/qr/client-download.ts touches location.href again -- a code download is a file fetch, not a navigation; use the <a download> helper");process.exit(1)}if(cd.indexOf("clickDownload(")<0){console.error("the <a download> helper is gone from lib/qr/client-download.ts");process.exit(1)}const aa=strip("app/(main)/events/admin-actions.ts");if(aa.indexOf("PlaceTimeRow")>=0){console.error("PlaceTimeRow is back in the events admin actions -- an unreferenced subset of EventAdminRow, for a module that does not exist");process.exit(1)}if(aa.indexOf("function readRsvpWindow(")<0){console.error("readRsvpWindow is gone -- it was the one live thing under that heading, so its removal means the section went wholesale");process.exit(1)}'
verify.note: Probes the RATCHET, not the tree: --max-warnings=0 in the lint script AND ci.yml still running `pnpm lint` under a job named exactly `lint` (the context branch protection requires). That is the consequence - the ratchet is what holds the tree at zero on every future PR, so re-running eslint here would cost minutes and prove only today. The two instance arms are paired positive/negative, so deleting a file wholesale fails instead of passing. ⚠️ IT STRIPS COMMENT LINES FIRST, and must: the fix's own comments name `PlaceTimeRow` and location.href verbatim to explain why they are gone, so a naive grep would flag its own explanation. ⚠️ AND IT IS `node -e` UNDER SINGLE SHELL QUOTES with indexOf rather than regex. The first version used double quotes and escaped regex classes, the escaping mangled the -e argument, node fell through to reading stdin, and the probe HUNG - which check-backlog correctly scored `unprovable` rather than passing. It sat in the unprovable bucket looking like coverage. Same family as the SCAN-210 probe that carried a double quote.

entries.title: /events loader: serial settings cluster + counting RSVPs by fetching every row
entries.detail: DONE 2026-08-25. HALF THE ROW HAD ALREADY EXPIRED. (a) THE SERIAL SETTINGS CLUSTER WAS FIXED BEFORE THIS ROW WAS WORKED, by #2290 (922febc66, Meta-scan phase 3) - the four awaits the row cites at :350/:370/:382/:388 are real, but they are the PRE-#2290 file; the current loader already gathers all five reads (resolvePageContent, eventsListingHorizonDays, demoModeEnabled, viewerHidesDemo, getSeriesDisplayConfig) into one Promise.all. Confirmed by running the new probe against 922febc66^, where all five arms fire, and against HEAD, where none do. Nothing to do; the probe now guards it against regression. (b) THE RSVP COUNT WAS REAL AND WAS WORSE THAN A PERF ROW. The loader pulled every going row for up to 3 x SERIES_WIDE_READ = 1,500 events to tally integers in JS, and PostgREST caps a response at max_rows (1,000) SERVER-SIDE, which neither service_role nor .limit() escapes - so past 1,000 going rows in one listing the counts silently under-reported with no error, flipping the Has open spots facet ON for a full event and mis-ordering the Most going sort. Now lib/events/going-counts.ts: prefers a grouped-count RPC, chunks ids 500 at a time so a full response can never be a truncated one, and FAILS SAFE to the original tally - now PAGED with .range() over the PK - whenever the RPC is absent or errors. A partial RPC result is discarded rather than merged, so it can never double-count. 13 unit tests in lib/events/going-counts.test.ts, including a fake client that reproduces the max_rows cap. THE MIGRATION IS WRITTEN AND UNAPPLIED: supabase/migrations/20270329000000_event_going_counts_rpc.sql (owner applies). The fallback is what makes merging it before the apply safe. OTHER .in() READS IN THE SAME WAVE, MEASURED: myRsvpRows is safe by the event_rsvps_event_profile_uniq constraint (<=1 row per event per profile); circlesRows is bounded by distinct hosting circles (theoretical only); tierRows is STILL EXPOSED - active ticket tiers scale as events x tiers with no bound, so past 1,000 the trailing events silently lose their From  price stat. That last one is out of this rows scope and is documented in the loader, needing its own row.

entries.title: The leaderboard Consistency widget fans out ~36 queries for 12 mates
entries.detail: MS25 Phase 3. mateIds.map(getPracticeStreak) - each call resolves the member day (serial profiles read) then a 2-query wave, so 12 mates cost ~36 queries plus a follow-up profiles read per render. Batch: one profiles .in() for zones, one practice_logs .in() for the window, then derive per-mate in memory - derivePracticeStreak is already pure. CLOSED 2026-08-25. Two batched reads (one profiles .in() for zone + meta + name, one windowed practice_logs .in()) replace ~36 round trips, and the per-mate streak is DERIVED through the same pure functions the reader uses — memberDay, frozenDaysFrom, derivePracticeStreak, isResting — so the rules are called, not restated. The logs read is chunked (MATE_LOG_CHUNK) because PostgREST truncates at max_rows=1000 and practice_logs is unique on (profile_id, practice_id, logged_for), not on the day: one .in() over twelve mates x a 400-day window is not guaranteed to fit, and a truncated response drops the OLDEST rows, which is exactly where a streak walk ends. components/widgets/leaderboard/streak-nudge-wiring.test.ts pins both halves.

Exactly one call is the honest count; derivePracticeStreak proves the mates went the batched way; the row budget proves the window cannot truncate into a shortened streak.

entries.title: Verify-then-add loading.tsx on the hot child routes that block above the shell
entries.detail: MS25 Phase 4. Verify-first, and the verify was most of the answer. The inventory looked for a loading.tsx IN each folder; Next 16 puts the boundary at the SEGMENT — loading.js wraps page.js and every NESTED layout.js below it, never the layout in its own folder. So three of the six named routes were already covered by an ancestor: channels/[id] by app/(main)/channels/loading.tsx, messages/r/[roomId] by messages/loading.tsx, journeys/[slug] by journeys/loading.tsx. A fourth, bare "spaces", is not a route at all — there is no app/(main)/spaces/page.tsx; the index is /spaces/directory. drafts and spaces/directory have no ancestor boundary and need none: both open their own <Suspense> around everything expensive, with only the request-cached caller above it, and no awaiting layout in between. ONE route genuinely blocked: spaces/[slug]. Its (profile) layout resolves the caller, the manage grant, tagline, visibility, follow state, founding badge, capabilities, reviews and the profile nav before rendering a node, with no boundary anywhere between it and app/(main)/layout.tsx {children} — the page own <Suspense> sits UNDER that layout, so it never gets to paint. Added app/(main)/spaces/[slug]/loading.tsx, at [slug] rather than inside (profile) for the same reason circles/[slug]/loading.tsx sits where it does (a file in the layout own folder renders inside it), which also covers the Space owner routes. Role radii and the layout own themable cover token only: check:adoption reads identical on all 18 classes before and after, so literal-radius is NOT raised the way the #2267 route skeletons raised it. No other skeleton added.

verify.cmd: node -e "const fs=require('fs'),B='app/(main)',CHEAP=3;const R=['channels/[id]','messages/r/[roomId]','journeys/[slug]','drafts','spaces/directory','spaces/[slug]/(profile)'];const bad=[];for(const r of R){const parts=r.split('/');const page=B+'/'+r+'/page.tsx';if(!fs.existsSync(page)){bad.push(r);continue}let covered=false,blocking=false;for(let i=parts.length;i>0;i--){const dd=B+'/'+parts.slice(0,i).join('/');if(fs.existsSync(dd+'/loading.tsx')){covered=true;break}const l=dd+'/layout.tsx';if(fs.existsSync(l)&&/[^\w]await /.test(fs.readFileSync(l,'utf8')))blocking=true}if(!covered&&!blocking){const s=fs.readFileSync(page,'utf8');const body=s.slice(s.search(/export default/));const k=body.indexOf('<Suspense');covered=k>=0&&(body.slice(0,k).match(/[^\w]await /g)||[]).length<=CHEAP}if(!covered)bad.push(r)}if(bad.length){console.error(bad.join(String.fromCharCode(44)));process.exit(1)}process.exit(0)"
verify.note: Walks each named route bottom-up to app/(main) and applies the Next 16 rule the row itself got wrong: a segment is covered when a loading.tsx sits at or above it, because that boundary wraps page.js and every NESTED layout.js below it (it does NOT wrap the layout in its own folder). Failing that, no layout on the path may await, and the page must open its own <Suspense> with at most 3 awaits ahead of it. That ceiling is the measured state, and it is what makes the probe measure blocking rather than the mere presence of the word Suspense: the streaming pages read 1 / 2 / 3 awaits before their boundary, while channels/[id] reads 7 before the Suspense buried in its rail, so deleting ANY of the four load-bearing loading.tsx files fails this.
