entries.title: The four commerce sitemap reads cap at 100 rows with no paging
entries.detail: MS25 Phase 2. store/market/housing/classifieds read limit:100 (circles 200) with no follow-up paging. PREMISE EXPIRED THE DAY IT WAS WRITTEN: the row offered two remedies (page it, or record the cap with a threshold that reopens it) and #2289 shipped the second one hours later in the same file — the cap note at sitemap.ts:60-105, named COMMERCE_SITEMAP_CAP / CIRCLE_SITEMAP_CAP constants, and atCap(), which warns per section naming the reader to page. That PR then filed this row as open anyway. Paging is genuinely out of reach from here and the note proves it per reader (three clamp server-side, classifieds takes no offset, circles is an RPC SQL ceiling), so the ONLY thing missing was a gate that notices the fail-safe fired. Added: four tests in app/sitemap.test.ts that drive the real route. They pin the warning at the cap, the silence one row below it (a positive control, so silence means not-at-cap rather than never-warns), and the invariant that makes a silent regression possible — the shared constant must equal the clamp the readers enforce, because raising it would leave the three clamped verticals returning 100 while atCap compared against the bigger number and never fired again. Mutation-checked: silencing the warn, raising the constant to 500, and dropping one atCap wrap each fail the suite.

verify.note: Measures the fail-safe, not the words: atCap must exist, warn on >= cap, be wired into all five capped sections, and COMMERCE_SITEMAP_CAP must still equal the clamp the three commerce readers enforce. Raising the constant without teaching a reader to page fails here.

entries.title: One trim sweep over the ~154 lib modules carrying dead exports
entries.detail: MS25 Phase 5. RE-SCOPED 2026-08-25 by an exact-identifier index over the whole tree (the original number came from a token-presence scan, which under-reports by construction). Two findings changed the row. (1) THE ORIGINAL SCAN MISSES .mts: lib/help/drift.ts and lib/ai/autodoc.ts scored fully dead and are both LIVE, consumed by scripts/help-drift.mts and scripts/help-autodoc.mts. Any sweep that skips .mts/.cts/.cjs/.yml deletes live code — this is the load-bearing correction. (2) ~85% of the row is not deletable: of 860 dead value exports across 707 lib modules, 734 are used INSIDE their own file, so the sweep for those is dropping the `export` keyword, not deleting. Only 126 are declaration-only. Exactly one module is fully dead — lib/help/drift.ts — and that one is the false positive above. So this is an API-surface trim plus a small delete list, not the M-sized code sweep the row described. A ranked 15 is scoped (each with all four searches clean), with three flagged for a ruling before touching, not a sweep: lib/verticals/registry.ts, lib/nav/admin-rail.ts and lib/admin/modules/spine.ts are registry/menu-adjacent — a parallel rail registry with no consumer is a MENU-CONTRACT finding in its own right. Two items carried over from SCAN-501: useEditMode().toggle (no caller since EditModeButton went) and offersPeriod (internal-only now; unexport, and its own test updates with it). Excluded on purpose: lib/profile/spotlight-flags.ts belongs to SCAN-501. ── ⚠️ RE-DERIVED AND RE-CLASSIFIED 2026-08-25 (ADR-1145). The index is now a committed, documented report — scripts/maintenance/dead-exports.mjs — rather than a number in a row, so the next reader re-runs it instead of trusting this sentence. Reading: 6,137 files walked, 5,765 consumers (INCLUDING .mts/.cts/.cjs/.mjs/.yml/.json/.md/.sql), 1,213 lib modules, 7,688 attributable exports, 1,343 dead outside their own file, 45 DECLARATION-ONLY. 🔴 AND THE ROW'S FRAMING NEEDS A CORRECTION: 'an API-surface trim' is only two thirds true. Classifying the 19 unreferenced lib FUNCTIONS by hand splits them three ways, and only one third is safe to delete blindly. (a) BUILT BUT NEVER WIRED: runContestSweep (lib/beta/referral-contest.ts) documents itself 'idempotent + bounded, so it is safe to run on a schedule' and NONE of the 27 crons in vercel.json calls it, so the beta referral contest never tallies. Deleting it removes a finished feature; filed as SCAN-510. (b) GENUINELY RETIRED WITH A STALE DOC: spaceTrailingProcessedCents still cites ADR-552 for the "you'd have saved $X" upgrade nudge, but billing-body.tsx records that ADR-811 RETIRED that nudge. The code is dead and its own comment advertises a feature that no longer exists — which is exactly how it reads as a gap when it is not. (c) CONVENIENCE WRAPPERS, the majority: dropping the `export` keyword is the whole change. ⚠️ THE GENERAL LESSON, and it is the same one SCAN-508 landed on from the other side: a doc comment is not evidence of a caller. Two of the three categories are indistinguishable from their comments alone.

The 19 unreferenced lib functions were classified by hand into built-but-unwired (1, now SCAN-510), retired-with-a-stale-doc (1) and convenience wrappers (the rest). The 2026-08-25 token-presence output is superseded.

entries.title: Route chunks have no weight gate: the shell gate's documented blind spot
entries.detail: MS25 Phase 5. check:shell-weight watches the app shell's eager JS and named admin fingerprints, but a heavy library statically imported by a route-level client component (SCAN-302's react-markdown) is invisible to it. A small fingerprint gate over the member hot-route chunks (feed/events/circles/messages) closes the class, not just the instance. CLOSED 2026-08-25 as ARM C of check:shell-weight, and it is a FINGERPRINT arm, never a budget: from each member hot route page.tsx (feed/events/circles/messages — page, not layout, because the layout IS the shell Arms A/B already measure) it walks the static import graph, marks everything below the first `use client` boundary as client code, and fails if a NAMED heavy module is statically imported inside that subtree. What it can prove without a build is the half a build cannot prove cheaply: a static import below a client boundary is not code-split by any bundler setting, so "statically reachable" IS "in that route first-load JS". dynamic() and bare import() are not static edges and are correctly invisible. It CANNOT see bytes or a chunking change — only Arms A/B can, and only on the artifact. Reading on the real tree: 0 leaks, 668 client modules walked across the four routes, 2 detector controls firing. IT LIVES IN THE CI HALF (scripts/check-shell-weight.test.ts), NOT in postbuild, for two reasons: main() only runs on Vercel, i.e. after the merge, and a filesystem-only arm has no reason to wait for a build; and in postbuild it broke the artifact arms own mutation fixtures, which run the script from a cwd that is deliberately not this repo, where its controls do not exist. Teaching it to skip when the source tree is absent would have given it a way to pass without looking (ADR-970). Two controls keep it honest: two REAL client files that genuinely import a heavy library today, and a 150-module walk floor against 668 measured. Proven by mutation: a static react-markdown import added to components/feed/post-replies.tsx turns it red and names the chain feed/page.tsx -> feed-list.tsx -> post-card.tsx -> post-replies.tsx.

Not `vitest run`: LIVE-034 forbids a probe that spawns a test runner, and this way costs 0.2s instead of 1.9s. A grep for the words in the title would pass by existing.

entries.title: Every public event advertised a start time seven hours early to search and answer engines
entries.detail: FOUND 2026-08-25 by driving the real builders and reading their OUTPUT rather than their source. `events.starts_at` stores the WALL CLOCK as UTC parts (lib/time/zone.ts), and eventSchema published it raw. Measured against production: `breathe-connect-expand-2026-08-27` starts 6:30pm Pacific and its Event node said `2026-08-27T18:30:00Z`, which every consumer reads as 11:30am. All five upcoming public events were wrong, and so was the /events ItemList. This is SCAN-101 on the SEO surface — the same convention read as an instant, which in SQL closed the guest RSVP door before lunch. CLOSED: lib/time/zone.ts gains eventIsoWithOffset, which keeps the host wall clock and attaches the zone offset AT THAT INSTANT, and both builders use it. Its own test found a defect while being written — reading the offset independently disagreed with eventInstant by an hour inside the spring-forward gap — so the offset is now derived from eventInstant own answer and the two cannot disagree by construction. THREE ASSERTIONS IN lib/jsonld.test.ts WERE PINNING THE BUG and were updated. ⏳ FOLLOW-UP: public_events / public_event_by_slug do not return time_zone, so the /discover pages fall back to the community zone. Correct for 61 of 61 events today; widening those RPCs is the durable fix.

entries.title: The /events ticket-tier read truncates at max_rows, so trailing events silently lose their from-price
entries.detail: FOUND 2026-08-25 while closing SCAN-303, by measuring the OTHER .in() reads in the same loader rather than stopping at the one the row named. PostgREST caps a response at max_rows (1000, supabase/config.toml) SERVER-SIDE: service_role does not escape it and .limit() does not raise it. Active ticket tiers scale as events x tiers and are bounded by neither, so past 1,000 rows the trailing events silently lose "From $X" — the same truncation class as ADR-962 (CRM import dedupe), ADR-969 (QR capture counts) and SCAN-303 itself, which is now the FOURTH occurrence. The other two reads in that loader were measured and are safe: myRsvpRows is bounded by event_rsvps_event_profile_uniq (at most one row per event per profile) and circlesRows by the number of distinct hosting circles. FIX: the same shape SCAN-303 used — chunk the input well under the cap, or aggregate in the database, and fail safe. ✅ CLOSED 2026-08-25. Premise re-tested first (ADR-1082): the read was still a single unbounded .in(), and production carried 2 active tiers on 1 event against 60 published events — so this is the first of the five caught BEFORE it fired rather than by its consequence. 🔴 CHUNKING THE INPUT WOULD NOT HAVE FIXED IT, and that is the difference from SCAN-303: that RPC returns at most one row per id, so 500 ids bounded the response. Tiers are many-per-event, so 500 ids at 5 tiers each is 2,500 rows and truncates just the same. The response had to be bounded AT THE SOURCE, so the fix is an AGGREGATE — event_tier_price_summary (20270332000000, applied, ledger repaired to the repo version, 640 to 640) returns exactly one row per event carrying the three things the label needs: tier_count, min_priced_cents and has_flexible. lib/events/tier-prices.ts prefers it and falls back to a PAGED read folded locally, so the migration was safe to merge unapplied. A SECOND INSTANCE OF THE SAME SHAPE was found while wiring it: lib/spaces/content-data.ts ran its own raw .in() for the Space card. It was bounded — listEventsForSpace caps at 24 — but only loosely, since 24 events at 42 tiers each still reaches 1,000, and a bound that depends on nobody building a long ticket ladder is not a bound. Both surfaces now share the helper, and eventPriceLabel was RETIRED rather than left as a second definition of the label. ⚠️ THE MIGRATION'S OWN PROBE CAUGHT TWO OF MY ERRORS BEFORE ANYTHING LANDED, both applies failing atomically with no function, no ledger row and no probe rows left behind: a fixture built on pricing_mode 'sliding' (the schema allows fixed/free/pwyc/sliding_scale/donation), and a grant that revoked from PUBLIC only — Supabase's ALTER DEFAULT PRIVILEGES (ADR-959) grants EXECUTE to anon and authenticated as NAMED roles, so both must be named in the revoke. That is the ADR-964 shape one level over: there it was column grants nobody narrowed, here a function grant that arrives pre-opened. 27 tests, four of them mutation-proven to fire, including an 8-case arm pinning the new path against the RETIRED implementation preserved verbatim as an oracle.

entries.title: Scoped rooms and three USING(true) tables admit anon with no identity check

source.ref: the authenticated verdicts the gate cannot verify

entries.detail: FOUND 2026-08-25 in the final security pass, and filed rather than fixed because both need a policy decision rather than a patch. (1) `rooms_read_public_or_member` admits `visibility IN (circle, hub, nexus, outpost, channel)` with NO identity check at all, and room_messages / room_members carry the same channel branch. Live: anon reads the one channel room metadata; messages and members return 200 [] rather than 42501, so only EMPTINESS is withholding them today — and room_messages is in the realtime publication. (2) dispatch_poll_votes, spotlight_top_friends and listing_comments have `USING (true)` with the anon grant intact; poll votes carry (profile_id, option_id) on member-only dispatches. Latent at 0 rows, which is exactly when it is cheap to fix. ⚠️ THE MEASUREMENT THAT MATTERS: of the tables verdicted `authenticated`, 65 were PROVEN to filter anon against real data, and 72 more are empty and therefore prove nothing. These findings live in that second group, which is the group table-grants.txt says the gate cannot verify. The other side is clean: 79 of 79 `internal` tables fail closed with 42501. ── ✅ RULED AND CLOSED 2026-08-25 (ADR-1149). OWNER RULING: TIGHTEN BOTH. 20270334000000 applied; ledger repaired to the repo version and verified as an EXACT BIJECTION by hash, not just by count (642 ⇄ 642, md5 e870925394181ea1cd8d0a2c48c7abac on both sides). ROOMS: the three scoped branches now require an authenticated caller; `visibility = 'public'` stays open to anon and membership still grants what it always did. Identity rather than membership, deliberately — browsing a circle's rooms before joining is a plausible flow and there is no data to say whether it is used, so this row closes the anon hole rather than redesigning room visibility. THE THREE TABLES: poll votes scope to your OWN vote, top friends to the OWNER's rows, listing_comments to `authenticated` (it is public-adjacent community content on public listings, so owner-scoping would be wrong rather than merely strict; what it stops is a signed-out bulk enumeration). ✅ WHY IT WAS FREE, AND THE CHECK THAT MADE IT SAFE: every application reader of all three tables goes through createAdminClient(), which bypasses RLS entirely, so those policies served NO application path — they only widened what the publishable anon key could ask PostgREST for. The rooms side is the same: the one non-admin reader (app/(main)/messages/popover-actions.ts) already calls auth.getUser() and scopes to the caller's own memberships. That question is not a formality — 20270330000000 nearly shipped as a blanket table revoke until app/discover/events/_data.ts turned out to be the ONE anon reader of 245 sites. ⚠️ AND A SECOND PASS WENT FURTHER THAN THE POLICIES: anon's SELECT GRANT was revoked on all five tables that have no anon path, because a policy the caller misses returns 200 [] — the very shape this row criticised ('only EMPTINESS is withholding them') — while removing the grant makes the same refusal arrive as 42501. public.rooms KEEPS its anon grant on purpose, or the public branch would go with it. VERIFIED AS ROLE ANON AFTER: rooms 1 → 0 readable (the channel room is now withheld, and that is the policy rather than emptiness), messages/members/poll votes/top friends all 0. ✅ CLOSED 2026-08-25 by 20270334000000 + 20270335000000. Production now holds ZERO anon SELECT grants across all six tables and retains all six for authenticated. The follow-up migration exists because the first one spared public.rooms on an unmeasured premise; db-tests failed its positive control and no anon reader of rooms turned out to exist (ADR-1150).

The last two matter because the FIRST version of the positive control asserted an absolute grant ("anon lost SELECT on public.rooms"), which db-tests failed on a fresh apply - see ADR-1150. A control stated as a difference is true in every environment; one stated as an absolute is only true in the one it was written against.

entries.title: #2286 (the 2026-08-25 meta-scan) is unmerged, conflicts with main, and is a second agent's in-flight draft

source.ref: the add/add conflict against main's copy of the same version

entries.detail: HANDOFF 2026-08-25 from the merge-queue session that landed #2274, #2276, #2277, #2278, #2279, #2280, #2281, #2282, #2284, #2285 and #2283. #2286 is the ONE open PR that session did not land, and it is blocked on ownership rather than on code: it is a DRAFT belonging to a different agent that was still pushing to it during the queue run (its head moved three times: 44153f2e -> 09e793e8 -> b5908fe8). Pushing a merge commit into a branch another agent is actively rewriting risks colliding with them, so the queue session deliberately did not. ── ITS CONFLICT IS UNDERSTOOD AND CHEAP: two files. (1) docs/BUILD-BACKLOG.json — #2286 adds 30 SCAN-* rows; a 3-way merge by row id resolves it with no losses (measured: base 223 / ours 253 / theirs 225 -> 255 entries, 0 duplicate ids, no both-sides row edits). (2) supabase/migrations/20270327000000_restore_listing_saves.sql — an add/add where BOTH SIDES ARE FUNCTIONALLY IDENTICAL: same table, same PK, same two FKs, same covering index, same private.get_my_profile_id() RLS policy. Main's copy is already merged AND already applied to production, so keep MAIN's file; the only thing worth taking from #2286's copy is its comment block, which answers the question main's copy leaves open (see LIVE-123's sibling finding below). 🔴 DO NOT re-derive the listing_saves provenance: #2286 established it. 20260925000000 dropped public.listing_saves claiming '0 code references', and that claim was FALSE — lib/listings/index.ts holds four live call sites (saveListing / unsaveListing / listSavedListingIds / listSavedListings) reaching the UI through components/marketplace/save-listing-button.tsx and the /housing pages. Every path failed SAFE (the write discarded its error, the reads fell back to 'nothing saved'), so from 2026-09-25 until the restore, hearting a housing listing wrote to a table that did not exist and the heart silently reset on reload. No gate noticed because the saves tests mock the client. NEXT STEP: decide who owns #2286, then resolve those two files and land it, or close it and re-file its 30 SCAN rows. ── ✅ CLOSED 2026-08-25, and NOT by merging #2286. That branch reached 112 changed files, and ci.yml's PR-size gate fails anything over 40 unless the title carries [sweep] — owner-directed after a 215-file PR killed production deploys for a day (ADR-1002). [sweep] is reserved for a single-purpose mechanical change where every file takes the same one edit, which a branch carrying four high-severity fixes, an SEO round, a speed round, an a11y round and an orphan sweep is not. So it was split by backlog row, which is the remedy the gate's own message names: #2288 (phase 1, correctness), #2289 (phase 2, SEO/GEO), #2290 (phase 3, speed + a11y) and #2291 (phase 4, hygiene). Four branches off main with DISJOINT paths, each carrying only the rows it closes, each run through the full battery on its OWN branch rather than on the tree it was carved from. That last part earned itself twice: it surfaced two cross-slice dependencies the combined branch could never have shown (two Spark modules importing a FieldError from another slice, and a route-chunk gate that stays red until the slice fixing its instance lands). This row's own conclusions were both confirmed and used: the listing_saves migration kept MAIN's copy, and the provenance it recorded was not re-derived. #2286 itself is closed as superseded, not merged. ADR-1140 §5 records the decision.

Split by path with disjoint sets; each verified on its own branch (tsc, eslint, full vitest suite, all 24 contract guards, check:backlog) before push.

entries.title: Every agent hand-resolves the same two ledger-doc conflicts, because the fold tooling is never committed

source.ref: the file half of the conflict; no committed tool folds it or DECISIONS.md

entries.detail: FOUND 2026-08-25 by driving eleven PRs through the queue in one session. EVERY open PR appends to the tail of docs/DECISIONS.md and adds rows to docs/BUILD-BACKLOG.json, so EVERY merge to main re-conflicts EVERY other open PR on those exact two files — and on nothing else (verified with `git merge-tree --write-tree` across all remaining branches: the conflict set was those two paths, every time, with zero code conflicts). The queue session hit this eleven times and resolved it eleven times by hand or by throwaway scripts, and this is at least the second session to do so. ── THE TWO RESOLUTIONS ARE MECHANICAL AND ALWAYS THE SAME. DECISIONS.md: both sides append ADR entries at the tail, so keep main's block first and the branch's after (theirs-then-ours), then `node scripts/check-adr.mjs` proves it. BUILD-BACKLOG.json: a 3-way merge BY ROW ID — for each id, if ours == base take theirs, if theirs == base take ours, if both changed STOP and report rather than guess; emit in main's order and append ids only this branch has. Both are ~30 lines. 🔴 THE JSON HALF MUST NOT BE HAND-EDITED: doing so has already produced an invalid file (a dropped `},{` between two rows) and a duplicated row id in this repo's history, each costing a CI round. 🔴 AND IT MUST NOT SILENTLY PICK A WINNER when both sides edited one row: that case is real (HYG-020 was edited on both sides in this session, main holding it `open` and the closing PR holding it `done`) and it needs a human, so the tool must exit non-zero and name the id. Write it to reproduce byte-identical output (the repo file has NO trailing newline; json.dump(indent=2, ensure_ascii=False) plus no final write matches it exactly) or the diff becomes unreviewable. ── ✅ CLOSED 2026-08-25: scripts/maintenance/fold-ledger-docs.mjs shipped in #2291, and it obeys both 🔴 rules above. It refuses when both sides edited the same row and NAMES the id, which is not theoretical — this very branch is the case: main and the handoff both amended LIVE-123, the tool stopped, and a human folded it (main 06:16 spine, plus the terminal-error finding main was missing). It also gained a CI half, scripts/maintenance/fold-ledger-docs.test.ts, and writing that test found three real defects: a trailing newline docs/BUILD-BACKLOG.json does not have (one byte, but it costs a spurious last-line hunk on every branch that merges after), a duplicate row id arriving on EITHER side being silently swallowed by new Map() — which would have resolved a conflict by losing a row — and an unguarded main() that shelled out to git on import. The byte-fidelity rule this row wrote down was itself recorded backwards in the tool header; the file was measured with od -c to settle it.

Deleting the ledger row would be the lie in the other direction — a fresh `db reset` would then not create functions production has. entries.detail: Raised by the autodoc bot on #2283 and carried on OWN-045 until that PR landed. #2283 derives and STORES a full natal chart from the birth date and matches on it natal-first, so "We work out your sun sign from your birth date and use that" is now inaccurate. The PRIVACY half of the sentence ("your birth date itself is never shown to anyone") stays true, and no chart is ever returned by an RPC, so the fix is to correct what is computed without weakening the privacy claim. On voice per docs/CONTENT-VOICE.md: plain sentences, no em dashes, never narrate the reader's feelings. ── ✅ ALREADY TRUE WHEN THE ROW WAS FILED, and the probe is what said so on its first run — the ADR-1082 rule paying for itself again, this time within a minute. The article does NOT carry the sentence the autodoc bot flagged: content/help/connecting/matching-and-romance.md:18 already reads "Your chart is worked out, never shown. We build a birth chart from your birth date and use it to spot quiet overlaps. Nobody sees your birth date or your chart, and nobody gets a breakdown of the score." That is accurate for what #2283 computes AND keeps the privacy claim intact, which is exactly the shape the fix was supposed to take. The row is kept rather than deleted because the advisory was real when raised and the probe is worth keeping pointed at the sentence: if a future edit reintroduces a sun-sign-only claim, this goes red.

verify.cmd: node -e "const s=require('fs').readFileSync('content/help/connecting/matching-and-romance.md','utf8');if(/Only your sign is used/.test(s)){console.error('the article still claims only the sun sign is used');process.exit(1)}"
verify.note: Probes the sentence that would be false, not the row title. It passed on its first run, which is how the row was found to be already closed. Re-point it if the article is restructured rather than edited in place.
